#### Diagrams: draw.io and Visio (N47)

Amends §7's routing, §16.6's label-capable list and §16.26's setup-report scrub. Supersedes the refusal of
`.drawio` and `.vsdx` (2026-10-08 triage D9.d, whose reasons were effort, not harm). `Registry.default`
routes `.drawio .vsdx .vsdm` to `diagram-stdlib` (`agentsync.convert.diagram.DiagramConverter`) under any
policy and with or without an OCR engine: it reads no picture, and a Visio label is read (below), so unlike
`.msg` it stays registered under a label rule and the `without_ocr` and `without_speech` registries hold
it too. It uses the standard library only: no new dependency.

- **Page.** One WHOLE unit: per diagram page a `## <page name>` heading (a Visio background page adds
  ` (background page)`), one `- <text>` line per shape with text in the file's order (a group's members
  after the group; lines inside a shape joined by ` / `; each line through `_escape_line`), then
  `Connections:` and one `- <from> -> <to>: <label>` line per connector with a labelled end or a label
  (`(no text)` for an end without text). A page with no text reads `[no text on this page]`; a diagram
  with no text at all is the `empty-output` stub. The title is empty, so the page takes the file's name;
  the summary is `draw.io diagram: N page(s); pages: …` or `Visio drawing: …`. Pictures, shape data,
  links and layer names are not read; a Visio shape with no `<Text>` of its own shows its master shape's
  text (§16.48 "PDF pictures and diagrams"); text on a hidden layer is read like any other.
  Amended 2026-10-20, §16.144 W27: a diagram with no text is a page too, `[no text on this page]` under each
  page's heading, and one with no pages reads `[empty diagram: no pages]` (emitter 1.3.0).
- **draw.io.** `<mxfile>` with `<diagram>` pages, each a `<mxGraphModel>` or compressed (base64 of raw
  deflate of the URI-encoded XML), or a bare `<mxGraphModel>`. A shape's text is its `value` (a
  `UserObject` or `object` wrapper's `label`, its `%name%` placeholders filled in when the wrapper says
  `placeholders="1"`: §16.48 "PDF pictures and diagrams"). A label is HTML only when `html=1` is one of the cell's
  `;`-separated style items, as draw.io renders it: then `<br>` and block tags (`<div>`, `<p>`, `<li>`,
  `<tr>` and the like, open or close) are line breaks, table cells are spaces, other tags are dropped and
  entities decoded; without `html=1` the label is plain text, angle brackets and all. A tag holds no `<`
  after its first: a `<` with another `<` before its `>` is a character (`p99 < 80ms <b>now</b>` reads
  `p99 < 80ms now`), which also keeps each tag pattern linear in the label's length (a label of 200,000
  unclosed `<` is read in well under a second, where rescanning from every `<` took most of a minute). A
  vertex whose parent is an edge is that edge's label. A cell without an id is no edge's end.
- **Visio.** `visio/pages/pages.xml` gives the order and names; each page part is found through its
  relationship, whether its target is relative (`page1.xml`) or absolute (`/visio/pages/page1.xml`). A
  `Connect` row whose `FromCell` starts `Begin` or `End` gives a connector's ends, and a connector is not
  listed as a shape; other glue (a callout's control handle, `PinX`) leaves the shape a shape. A shape
  without an `ID` is no connector's end, and each shape shows its own text whatever its `ID` (two shapes
  without one, or sharing one, are two lines). A package without `visio/pages/pages.xml` is `conversion
  failed: not a Visio drawing`.
- **Bounds.** No XML part is inflated past 32 MiB, no `.drawio` file is read past 128 MiB, and no file's
  inflated XML passes 128 MiB in all: past any of them the file is a `conversion failed: diagram … too
  large` stub, which the report counts under `conversion failed` (that prefix is matched before `too
  large`). Malformed XML, another XML document under the name, or a broken compressed page is a
  `conversion failed` stub whose reason holds no text of the file: for malformed XML it is `<part> is not
  well-formed XML: <expat's fixed wording for the error code>: line L, column C`, or `… its encoding is not
  supported` for an encoding declaration Python cannot decode, never the parser's own message (that can
  name an undefined entity or the declared encoding). Entity expansion is bounded by expat's
  amplification limit (a billion-laughs file is a `not well-formed XML` failure); external entities are
  never fetched.
- **Labels.** `.vsdx` and `.vsdm` join `policy.OOXML_SUFFIXES`, so a Visio drawing is screened like any
  Office file (an excluded label refuses it, `refuse_unlabelled` refuses an unlabelled one, a name whose
  bytes are not a ZIP is `not-ooxml`) and, through `cycle._LABEL_CAPABLE`, is re-screened when the policy
  changes. Routing it without that would convert a drawing the policy excludes, so the two land together.
  `canonical.OOXML_SUFFIXES` is not changed: a `.vsdx` or `.vsdm` is hashed by its bytes. A `.drawio`
  carries no sensitivity label (plain XML, like `.xml`), so label rules do not apply to it.
- **Report.** `_PATH_IN_LOG_RE` gains `drawio` and `vsdm` (`vsdx` was already in it), so a fetch warning
  naming a diagram at a source's top is `<path>`; the per-suffix scrub test now covers 40 suffixes
  (**amended 2026-10-12, §16.55:** 41 since `.potx`, §16.48 R85). The
  three suffixes stay in `_REFUSED_TYPE_LIST`: a stub can be older than its converter.
- **Old stubs.** An existing `no converter for .drawio` or `.vsdx` stub becomes a page with no operator
  step: on this Mac through the re-read pass (§16.27), online-only through the work queue under the byte
  budget. So does a `no converter for .vsdm` stub. `.vsd`, stencils and templates are still refused.

Amended 2026-10-11 by §16.48 (R86): `.vsdm` is routed with `.vsdx` (routing, labels, report, old stubs and
the extensions tuple below); it was refused here.

Amended 2026-10-11 by §16.48 (R86, part b): a Visio shape with no `<Text>` shows its master shape's text
("Page" said a master's default text was not read); the version below is `1.1.0`.

Amended 2026-10-11 by §16.48 (R86, part d): a draw.io object with `placeholders="1"` has its label's
`%name%` placeholders filled in, or with `placeholder="<name>"` shows that attribute's value instead of its
label ("draw.io" read the label as written); the version below is `1.2.0`.

Version: `1.2.0+python-<x.y.z>`; options `max_page_bytes`, `max_part_bytes`, `max_total_bytes`.

`test_a_visio_callout_glued_to_a_shape_stays_a_shape`, `test_a_diagram_that_cannot_be_read_fails_bounded`,
`test_a_drawio_file_past_the_total_is_not_parsed`,
`test_a_connector_with_one_end_does_not_borrow_a_shape_without_an_id`,
`test_a_drawio_html_label_of_unclosed_tags_is_read_in_linear_time`,
`test_a_drawio_bracket_that_opens_no_tag_is_a_character`,
`test_a_visio_shape_keeps_its_own_text_whatever_its_id`,
`test_a_diagram_parse_failure_reason_holds_no_text_of_the_file`), `tests/test_policy.py`
(`test_a_visio_drawing_is_screened_for_labels_like_any_office_file`), `tests/test_cycle.py`
(`test_a_diagram_stub_from_before_its_converter_is_read_once_as_a_page`), `tests/test_convert_core.py`
(the route set and the counts: 11 converters, 13 with an engine, 11 under a label rule),
`tests/test_convert_determinism.py` (three diagram inputs) and `tests/test_setup_report.py` (the scrub).
`build_drawio` and `build_vsdx` in `tests/test_convert_builders.py` write both formats from nothing.

#### The speech line says the helper is built (`convert/speech.py`) (H13)

With the helper built and a model folder missing, the probe's detail is `the speech helper is built; the speech
models are not placed: <folder>/ and <folder>/`, so the installer's line, doctor and `status` read
`speech: off (the speech helper is built; the speech models are not placed: ...)`, and each cycle's INFO log
reads `speech is off: the speech helper is built; ...`. The clause is printed only after `ocr._look` returned a
helper that exists, passed the trust check and answered `--version` from the pinned FluidAudio commit, so it is
true whenever it is printed, on a re-run that kept an earlier helper as well. The state stays `off`; the
installer's exit status, install.log and doctor's severity are unchanged, and no new state word is added. This
changes the detail that section 16.37 recorded as "unchanged" for B11's ticker: 16.37 is the dated record of
what v10 printed, this is the current contract. Why: the B11 and B12 rehearsals and the v10 corporate run read
minutes of `helpers: building the speech helper` ending in `speech: off (...)`, the same word a switched-off run
prints, and could not tell the build had succeeded.

#### A run a signal stopped names the signal (`convert/ocr.py`, `convert/speech.py`, `convert/pandoc.py`) (H12)

`subprocess` reports a child a signal stopped as the negative signal number. `ocr._ended` reads it at
`ocr._run_helper`, `ocr._compile`, `speech._step` and pandoc's runner and words it `stopped by SIGKILL (signal
9)`, the phrase `scripts/install.sh`'s `rc_meaning` uses; a number that names no signal reads `stopped by signal
N`. (**amended 2026-10-11, §16.47 R81:** `rc_meaning` used only the `stopped by SIG...` stem, for 129, 130 and
143; it now words every other signal's exit, 128 + N, as `stopped by SIG<NAME> (signal N)`, and doctor's git and
pandoc probes and the report's probes word subprocess's negative code the same way.) A crash's own signal (`ocr._CRASHES`: SIGILL, SIGTRAP, SIGABRT, SIGFPE, SIGBUS, SIGSEGV, SIGSYS) adds the
line the tool printed on stderr (`ocr._plain`), because that line is why it stopped: `the OCR helper was stopped
by SIGTRAP (signal 5): main.swift:9: Fatal error: no frames`. Any other signal came from outside and drops what
the tool printed before it. `speech._step` passes stderr only, never stdout, which is SwiftPM's progress. pandoc
passes nothing, since its stderr can quote the document: `pandoc was stopped by SIGKILL (signal 9)`. The two
build sites add the next step: `swift build was stopped by SIGKILL (signal 9); scripts/install.sh tries the build
again on its next run` and `swiftc, building the OCR helper, was stopped by SIGTERM (signal 15); scripts/install.sh
tries the build again on its next run`; a helper run adds none, because the next cycle runs it again. The speech
build's floor check refuses only on the check's own non-zero answer (a reason that starts `git merge-base failed
(exit `). A check that ran out of time, that a signal stopped, or that does not run (`git merge-base does not
run: ...`) keeps its own reason. A non-negative exit keeps its wording byte for byte. Why: the v10 rehearsal read
`speech: not built (swift build failed (exit -9): Building for production...)`, and a killed floor check was
stored in `<helper>.failed` as "does not descend from the build floor", which was false.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.138 V68: both build sites name the installer by its path (`skill.INSTALL_SH`), `...;
~/src/agent-context-sync/scripts/install.sh tries the build again on its next run`, and `ocr._plain` keeps that one
path when it reads the `<helper>.failed` marker back, where it takes every other path out.
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.144 W50: a crash's line is shortened, with an ellipsis, so the whole reason fits the 200
characters `ocr._plain` keeps when it reads the marker back (`ocr._signal_reason`).

#### The speech build's proxy (`convert/speech.py`; amends section 16.35, which builds as section 16.25 does) (H10)

The speech build's `swift` and `git` run in `ocr._env()` plus whichever of the shell's `HTTPS_PROXY`,
`HTTP_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` (either case) are set to a non-empty value (`speech._build_env`,
`speech._PROXY_VARS`). SwiftPM clones FluidAudio with git, which reads them as step 1's git does, and
`~/.gitconfig` (`http.proxy`) still wins in git. `[network] proxy` and `net.resolve_proxy` are not used.
FluidAudio's binary artifact is downloaded by SwiftPM itself, which ignores these variables and uses the macOS
proxy settings (measured 2026-10-10, Swift 6.2.4: with every proxy variable set and no system proxy, the download
went direct). So when a variable that routes an https url through a proxy is set (`HTTPS_PROXY` or `ALL_PROXY`,
either case, `speech._PROXIES`: curl and git ignore `HTTP_PROXY` for an https url, and `NO_PROXY` names none) and
SwiftPM's cache does not hold the artifact, the build first fetches it with `/usr/bin/curl`, which reads them, in
the same environment plus the shell's CA bundle (`speech._seed`, before `swift package resolve`), checks its SHA-256 against `speech.NEMO_SHA256` and only then
renames it into `<cache>/speech/swiftpm/cache/artifacts/` under SwiftPM's own file name, where SwiftPM takes it
("Fetched ... from cache") instead of downloading. A failed fetch or a wrong checksum removes the temporary file
and SwiftPM downloads as before.
The build's `swift` and `git` also get whichever of the shell's `GIT_SSL_CAINFO`, `GIT_SSL_CAPATH` and
`CURL_SSL_BACKEND` are set to a non-empty value (`speech._CA_VARS`): behind TLS inspection these are how the
shell's git trusts the inspecting CA. `swift` and `git` do not get `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR` or
`CURL_CA_BUNDLE`: Xcode's git (libcurl 8.7.1 with LibreSSL) ignores them (measured 2026-10-11 with
`git ls-remote` under `env -i`: each pointed at an empty file still succeeded, while an empty `GIT_SSL_CAINFO`
failed). `/usr/bin/curl` 8.7.1 does read all three (measured 2026-10-11 under `env -i`: `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` or
`SSL_CERT_FILE` at an empty file failed with exit 77, "error setting certificate verify locations", and
`SSL_CERT_DIR` became its CApath), so the seed's curl, and only it, gets their non-empty values
(`speech._CURL_CA_VARS`). `DEVELOPER_DIR`, `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY` and everything else stays dropped. SwiftPM's own binary-artifact download uses the keychain and reads none of these variables. The OCR,
media and speech helpers, and the OCR and media builds, keep `ocr._env()` and never see a proxy or a CA
variable. A failure's reason is SwiftPM's first `error:` line and names no proxy host.

Amended 2026-10-11 by §16.48 (R84): the build passes `GIT_SSL_CAINFO`, `GIT_SSL_CAPATH` and `CURL_SSL_BACKEND`;
`GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY` stays dropped, and `SSL_CERT_*` and `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` stay away from `swift` and `git`, with
the measured reason.
Amended 2026-10-11 by §16.48 (R83): "a Mac whose only route out is a proxy set in the environment still cannot
build the helper" is replaced by the curl fetch that seeds SwiftPM's cache with the checked artifact.
Amended 2026-10-11 by §16.48 (R84, R83): "stays dropped ... would claim a trust they do not give" no longer holds
for curl: the seed's `/usr/bin/curl` reads `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `SSL_CERT_DIR` (measured) and
gets them; the fetch's trigger is `HTTPS_PROXY` or `ALL_PROXY`, no longer `HTTP_PROXY`.

#### A cited commit is on the trunk (`tests/test_deploy_pack.py`) (N38)

A hex word in `tests/`, `src/`, `scripts/`, `launcher/`, `probes/`, `README.md` or this file that names a commit
of this repository names an ancestor of `HEAD`. `test_a_cited_commit_is_on_the_trunk` checks it with
`git cat-file --batch-check` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor`. A commit the clone does not hold names nothing
there, so a depth-1 CI checkout asserts nothing; the check bites in the clone that still holds a stale object,
which is the clone a rebase leaves behind. `docs/plans/` and `docs/research/` are not scanned: they are dated
records of branch work and name branch commits on purpose. Why: `tests/test_config.py`, `tests/test_publish.py` and `README.md` line 23 each cited the pre-rebase twin of a
trunk commit, which a fresh clone cannot resolve; they now cite `e49e212`, `a0e0542` and `d3b7883` (same subject,
same author date, same content at the cited path).

### 16.43 Setup prompt v11 (2026-10-11, wave B13 lane F)

Every prompt-wording item of B13 ships as one version, v11 (operator ruling 2026-10-10, "build everything").
Each was designed, then checked by a skeptic; where the skeptic corrected the designer, its version is the one
built. `PROMPT_VERSION` and `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT` are 11 and the issue form's placeholder is `v11`. v11 moves no
step, so it has no entry in `PROMPT_LAYOUTS`. A saved v10 copy is stopped at step 1 like every older copy
(§16.28). None adds a command, flag, installer option, config key or friction kind.

#### Setup prompt v11 (amends §16.14, §16.22, §16.28 "One round", §16.30, §16.36 "Setup prompt v10" and §16.37; README, `scripts/install.sh`, `agentsync.setup_report`)

- **Step 1's Xcode and git stops log their error** (H1; amends §16.22 and §16.37). Both stops say "go to step
  3's report", and before it: "log the failed command as a step 1 error if ~/src/agent-context-sync exists". A
  step that is not a number (`preflight`) gives the line no step column, so neither reader would open an attempt
  on it; hence "a step 1 error". A Mac with no checkout has nothing to log with, and step 3 says setup stopped
  before the code was downloaded. `parse_friction` already reads that line as a header-less attempt, which the
  Summary judges "failed at step 1" (§16.22). `friction_earlier_end` now ends an attempt at the same line, a
  step 1 `error` more than `NEW_SESSION_GAP` (600 s) after an end line, so section 3 does not send again a
  patch the attempt before it reported (§16.30); a stopped copy's end line still never counts. The §16.37 "no
  attempt was started since" note stays: it still covers an old copy and an agent that did not log. The friction
  log's awk readers (`friction_attempt_stopped`, `friction_close_attempt`, `friction_earlier_end`) run under
  `LC_ALL=C`: a line that is not UTF-8 aborted macOS awk in a UTF-8 locale, and a stopped copy then read as not
  stopped. The report registers proxies set in git's config files (`proxy =` in `~/.gitconfig`,
  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config`, `/etc/gitconfig`, and the `.git/config` of the checkout agentsync was installed
  from and of `~/src/agent-context-sync`), read as files with no git process, as `<proxy-N>`: the logged git
  error names that proxy (`Could not resolve proxy: <host>`). At the stop itself the old checkout's code runs
  (the pull failed), so the companion and the proxy rule protect every later report, not that first one. The
  shell fallback report does not read git's config yet. **SUPERSEDED (2026-10-11, §16.40):** the shell
  fallback's `redaction_pairs` reads the same git config files (`~/.gitconfig`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config`,
  `/etc/gitconfig`, its own checkout's `.git/config` and `~/src/agent-context-sync/.git/config`) and registers
  each proxy host with a dot. **Amended (2026-10-12, §16.46 "Proxies" R42/R67, §16.47 R110):** the shell also
  registers a proxy host with no dot (a generic word such as proxy or wpad only where a URL names it, any other
  host as a whole word), and both reports, the Python one above included, read a linked worktree's git config
  (`<common dir>/config` and `<git dir>/config.worktree`) besides `.git/config`.
- **Step 3's second no-report case names both of step 1's version checks** (H2; amends §16.36 "Step 3 names the
  two stops with no report"). It reads "when step 1 stops because this prompt is not the installer's (either
  check: the --version line does not end with this prompt's number, or the command says so)". In step 1's one
  command the two checks fire together: both read `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, and `--log-start` has refused a
  mismatched copy since v8. The gap is an agent that runs the parts one at a time and stops at `--version`. That
  leaves no stopped attempt, so `friction_attempt_stopped` cannot catch a `--report-only` after it, which
  re-renders the last real session's report into `bring-back.md` and prints `bring back:` and the issue link.
  "The --version line" names no line when `--version` never ran: at the Xcode and git stops the command ends
  before it, and those stops still end with the report. The number is not written out, so step 3 has nothing to
  bump.
- **The finish names one NEXT line** (H3; amends §16.14 and §16.36). "the last NEXT: line printed before the
  report, or "none", and under it each WAITING ON YOU: line the same command printed". v10's "the last NEXT: or
  WAITING ON YOU: line of the loop" had several candidates; the v10 rehearsals read it two ways (on a new Mac the
  draft-baseline wait alone, with no NEXT; on a set-up Mac the NEXT with both waits). "Before the report" leaves
  out the report's own `NEXT:`; `install.sh --log` prints none. The report's Loop line already lists every wait.
  **Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J66 (by §16.72 H6):** since v16 the item adds "(also "none: waiting for your folder answer"
  while you wait for my folder answer in step 1; the folder list's NEXT: line is not a step for me)": at the
  folder wait no report runs, so "before the report" pointed at nothing.
  **Amended 2026-10-14, §16.82 K19:** since v18 the clause covers the folder wait only ("... in step 1: there, the
  NEXT: line that leaves the folders to choose is not a step for me)"); at the list's exit-3 stops (OneDrive not
  signed in, no folders synced yet) its NEXT is the person's step and is the one named.
- **Step 2's NEXT does not count toward the loop** (H4; amends §16.28 "One round"). "Step 2's NEXT: line does not count, even when it
  already said "session done": step 2's sync downloaded nothing, so run this loop's sync at least once." On a
  re-run, loop rules 5, 9 and 10 can end the installer's `NEXT:` in "session done". Step 2's sync is
  `--materialise-budget 0` and online-only files are a note, never rule 3, so the loop's plain syncs are the
  session's only downloading syncs. The budget-0 round starts once this loop's `NEXT:` line has said "session
  done". The installer's `NEXT:` is unchanged (K02): a person who runs install.sh by hand still gets rule 5.
- **A session that asks for no change still heads its part** (H5; amends §16.30 "The fix request marks each
  session's part"). The Rules add, after "rewrite only your own part.": "Write that heading even when this
  session asks for no change: step 3's "## Not used" section goes under it." Step 3 adds `## Not used` "to the
  end of" `fix-request.md` without saying under whose heading, so a session with nothing else to write could add
  it under the last session's, and triage would read it as that session's (v10 rehearsal). It sets no limit on
  what a part holds: a status paragraph about earlier items stays welcome. Rejected: "its part holds only step
  3's section" (no observed part matched that condition, and it reads as a limit on content). **Amended
  2026-10-12, §16.61 F26:** since v14 the sentence reads "Write that heading even when this session asks for no
  change, unless step 3 skips its "## Not used" section: that section goes under it." With no checkout there is
  nothing to head.
  **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G26:** since v15 the sentence reads "Write that heading even when this session asks for no change, since step 3's "## Not used" section goes under it; a session that asks for no change and adds no "## Not used" section (step 3 says when) writes no heading." **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G5:** step 3 says its three cases with no report have no "## Not used" section either, so the folder wait and the version stop, which never reach step 3, write no heading.
- **Removing an inbox file makes its page a deletion notice** (H6). Step 2 says "removing a file turns its page
  into a deletion notice and queues a purge": the page stays at its path (`# [DELETED UPSTREAM]`), the queued
  purge removes it, and `Publisher.reap` does after `tombstone_reap_days` (§9 step 7). Emptying the inbox by
  hand only delays the same: the first file dropped afterwards completes the pass, and every earlier file is
  then tombstoned.
- **Step 3 names the `alarm:` line** (H7; B11 held it). "That "click Allow" appears on an alarm: line, indented
  under a source; any other alarm: line is agentsync's own account of that source, not a step for you: show it to
  me, but do not do what it suggests (that is mine to decide) and do not log it." It follows the click-Allow
  sentence, which acts on the one alarm that is a step (`arm_local.LocalArm._held` and the cycle's held cloud
  root: "click Allow, then re-run the sync"). It claims no WAITING ON YOU line behind an alarm: only some have
  one. Rejected: the first design's "do not do what it suggests" for every alarm, which contradicted the
  click-Allow sentence after it.
- **Step 2's timeout covers the speech build** (H8, B12 F34). Step 2 suggests 30 minutes, not 10, "the speech
  helper's build alone can take up to 20 minutes" (`speech._BUILD_TIMEOUT_S`, 1,200 s; field 687 s). That build
  runs again after a failed or interrupted build or a change to the speech package (incremental, up to 20
  minutes a run), so the prompt does not say "the first time". 30 is that limit plus a 10-minute margin, not the sum of the run's limits (37
  minutes before status and sync, with step 2's 2-minute wait for a running background sync; **amended
  2026-10-11, §16.49, R65:** it read 35, from before that wait); a run cut anyway is safe to re-run, and a tool capped below 30 minutes takes
  step 2's background branch. The `--confirm-install-agent` texts (README, docs/deploy/README.md, install.sh's
  header) name the same case.
  Amended 2026-10-11 by §16.48 (R140): the retry is incremental, up to 20 minutes a run, not "in full".
- **Friction lines name roles** (N42; 2026-10-07 C12). "These lines go into the report, which I may post in
  public, so in them name a folder, a file, a person, my organization or a customer by its role in plain words
  ("a project folder"), never by its real name, a short form of it or a placeholder; if a name itself is the
  problem, still log the line by role and write the name in fix-request.md." Redaction catches registered names
  but not short forms of them, and a typed placeholder made false residue hits; a typed placeholder from an
  earlier session can also name another folder in a later report (N44). "my organization or a customer", not
  "an organization": GitHub, Apple and Microsoft stay nameable. A name that is the problem still gets its line,
  because a `question`, `click` or `approval` line counts in the outcome. C12 rejected "role or placeholder";
  this rule says "never a placeholder".
- **A go-ahead or an answer given in the chat is a `question`** (N43; 2026-10-07 U4; amends §16.30 "Not done, by
  choice"). The kind reads "in the chat, you asked me something other than which folders to sync, or I gave you
  a go-ahead or an answer other than my folder answer or telling you I clicked something; log a question and my
  answer to it as one line, and my go-ahead as a question line of its own even when you also log what it allowed
  as a deviation". The agent's own questions count as in v10, an announced Allow is never logged and any other
  click has its `click` line, so word of a click is never a second line; a go-ahead and the workaround it allowed
  are two lines. Not `approval`: a counted approval prints "1 approval" and drops "approvals: not observable" for
  tools whose approvals are not seen. Not `deviation` alone: no count reads it. Field rates before and after v11
  are not comparable on this point.
- **Fix-request names carry a role that tells the folder apart** (N44; amends §16.22's "by its role or by the
  report's placeholder"). "name a folder, a file or a person by a role that tells it apart from the others on
  this Mac, adding the setup report's placeholder if it has one ("the folder of scanned invoices (<folder-2>)"),
  not by its real name, unless the name itself is the bug. Placeholder numbers can change from one report to the
  next; the role does not." A report numbers placeholders in registration order: in `_build_redactor`,
  configured CloudStorage components, then the listing, then configured folders elsewhere; in the shell
  fallback, the run's `--source-local` folders, then sources.toml, then install.log. An added folder, a listing
  past its 3 s bound or a fallback report therefore renumbers between two reports, step 2's and step 3's of one
  session included, while `fix-request.md` outlives every report. "a project folder" tells no folder apart: the
  prompt has the person sync project folders. Not changed, because each would make things worse:
  content-derived placeholders (a short hash of a low-entropy name can be confirmed from the public report, and
  `<folder-N>` is pinned); a persisted name-to-number map (a new file of real names); one sorted order (a
  configured CloudStorage folder would lose its number when the listing fails); registering folders outside
  CloudStorage before the listing (its fuzzy variants would stop being redacted); the fallback's folders last
  (the number would look reliable without being reliable). **Amended (2026-10-11, §16.46 R135):** `<org-N>`
  differs between the two reports as well: the shell fallback numbers the CloudStorage entries in glob order
  (a repeated organisation takes no number, §16.47) and never reads `graph.tenant` or SharePoint site hosts. A one-word organisation is
  redacted as a whole word wherever it stands (`Microsoft` in `Microsoft Graph`) on purpose, since that fails
  closed; no common-word exemption is made. **Amended (2026-10-12, §16.58 F92):** not for a one-word value that
  is a word the report prints; see §16.46 "Kept as they are".

#### Outside the prompt

- **The IT request names every install download** (H9, B12 C1; read §16.35's "The build fetches FluidAudio from
  github.com" with this). `docs/deploy/it-request.md`'s "What leaves the Mac" has an "Installation downloads"
  bullet: uv and its Python from `astral.sh`, `releases.astral.sh` and `github.com` (`astral.sh` has redirected
  to `releases.astral.sh` since at least 2026-10-10); FluidAudio's git fetch from `github.com`, pinned; the prebuilt
  `NemoTextProcessing` xcframework FluidAudio links (87 MB, checksum-pinned in FluidAudio's manifest, served from
  `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, so an allowlist of `github.com` alone blocks it and the speech helper is
  then not built, which nothing else needs). `[convert] recordings = false` skips both speech downloads; the
  helpers step runs before `sources.toml` exists, so a new Mac needs that file written before installing.
  `test_it_request_names_the_speech_build_downloads` ties the page to `Package.swift`'s pin through
  `FLUIDAUDIO_BINARY_TARGETS`: a new pin fails it until FluidAudio's binary targets at that commit are re-read.
- **A friction time is the second of the call that wrote it** (N40). `setup-feedback.md` section 1 says each
  friction time is the UTC second of the `install.sh` call that wrote the line (`friction_cmd`,
  `friction_close_attempt`), not the moment of the event, so lines logged together share it and the file's order
  is the order they were logged; section 4's rules read those times. Docs only.

### 16.44 Round 3: purge (2026-10-11, wave B13 round 3 lane A)

Round 3 lane A of B13 (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 2"): items R49, R64, R91, R93, R95 and R96
are built; R123 and R124 are kept not built, with the reasons below.

#### A kept upstream deletion is a note, not a wait (`agentsync.governance`, `agentsync.loop`, `agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.cycle`; amends §16.38)

`governance.partition_purges(state_paths, queue=None)` splits the queue (the file, or the entries passed) into the
entries a `purge --queue` would run and the ones it keeps queued, each with its reason. It reads the manifest
once and judges every entry with `_kept_why`, the rule `run_purge_queue` applies before each entry (a fresh read
per entry there, since an earlier purge of the run changes the manifest), so the display and the run cannot
differ. A manifest it cannot read (a schema from a newer build, a SQLite error) is logged and leaves every entry
runnable, as before. `KEPT_PURGES` is the text after the kept count: ``upstream deletion(s) stay queued while
their file is listed again; once the file is gone, they wait for `agentsync purge --queue` like any queued purge``
(**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.50 Q45:** was `...; they run on their own once the file is gone`, but nothing runs
them: the rewrite runs only from `purge --queue`).

- The loop's wait and its `governance.purge_queue` check count only the runnable entries and appear only when
  there is one; the kept ones add the note `K <KEPT_PURGES>` (a note, not a wait).
- `status`: `queued purges: N (...)` counts only the runnable entries; a separate line `queued purges kept: K
  <KEPT_PURGES>` follows.
- doctor `governance.purge_queue`: WARN with its fix (or the `yours: see WAITING ON YOU` note) only when a runnable
  entry exists, its detail ending `; K <KEPT_PURGES>` when there are kept ones too; with only kept ones, INFO, ok,
  detail `K <KEPT_PURGES>`, no fix.
- STATE.md's `## Queued purges` counts only the runnable entries in its waiting line and adds `- K <KEPT_PURGES>`.
- `purge --queue` exits 0 when every report is verified or not run and every entry left on the queue is a kept
  upstream deletion; its last line is then `N queued purge(s) run; K stay queued while their file is listed`. With
  any other entry left: `N queued purge(s) run; M still queued`, plus ` (K of them while their file is listed)`
  when some are kept, exit 1. The dry run's count (`N queued purge(s) previewed`) counts only the entries it
  previewed, not the ones it reports as not run.

Why: an entry kept because its file is listed again exits 1 on every run and clears nothing, yet the loop's
`WAITING ON YOU` line, status and doctor's WARN told the operator (or an agent following the wait) to run it
on every sync while the file existed. The kept entries stay visible, because each is a pending history erasure.
Tests: `tests/test_cli.py::test_purge_queue_keeps_an_upstream_deletion_of_a_live_file_and_does_not_count_it_as_run`,
`::test_a_kept_upstream_deletion_beside_a_runnable_purge_leaves_a_wait_for_the_runnable_one`.

#### A held queue entry gets a report (`agentsync.governance`)

An entry whose purge raises `GovernanceError` stays queued with a `PurgeReport` like a kept one: `items` and
`docs_paths` empty, `remote` "not run", `not_run` and its one note `stays queued: <why>`. For a hold
(`HoldActiveError`) the why is the error's text, which names the hold's scope, reason and owner and no item; for
any other `GovernanceError` it is the fixed `the purge failed; the log has the error` (a git failure's text can
name a path or an id), and the full text stays in the log's warning. The entry also joins the run's "stays
queued" list, so a later verified purge in the run that covers it does not drop it. Why: a held entry printed
nothing on stdout while a kept one printed its reason; the preview is where the operator reads why an entry
stays. Tests: `tests/test_cli.py::test_purge_queue_skips_a_held_source_and_keeps_it_queued`,
`::test_purge_queue_dry_run_previews_a_held_source_and_writes_nothing`,
`tests/test_governance.py::test_purge_queue_runs_and_keeps_held_requests`.

#### A queued entry an earlier purge of the run did is not run again (`agentsync.governance`; amends §16.38 "A purge by selector takes the queue entries it did off the queue")

When a purge of the run verifies, `run_purge_queue` takes every queue entry it covers (`_covers`), later in the
queue or kept so far after a failed run, as done at that moment: each writes the audit line `{"action":
"purge-covered", "at", "covered_by_sha256" (the covering selector's fingerprint), "reason", "selector_sha256"}`
so an erasure request keeps a record that it was fulfilled, and adds the note `also did the queued <reason> purge
of the same item: taken off the queue` to the covering report (no report of its own, never one with `not_run`,
which would turn the exit code into a failure). A covered later entry is not run. An entry already reported as
kept or held this run is never taken by a later cover. The queue file written after each verified purge leaves
out every covered entry, so a run that stops part-way neither puts one back nor loses its audit line.
Why: the run walked the original queue, so each covered entry cost a full no-op history pass and wrote a second
`purge-summary` that read as an erasure that erased nothing. Test: `tests/test_governance.py::
test_purge_queue_runs_an_entry_an_earlier_purge_of_the_run_covered_only_once`.

#### A taken path spares every worktree's live file; a listed file's outputs row stays (`agentsync.governance`; amends §16.38)

The taken map holds, per path, the identity of the page at that path in every worktree HEAD (it held only the
first HEAD's), and every such identity is spared by the index scrubber; which paths are taken is unchanged. The
purge's row deletion by path keeps an outputs row whose owner is a file the manifest lists that the purge did not
select (`_ManifestTargets.others`); tombstones and depends rows at the path are still deleted by path, and a path
whose HEAD holds no page is still not taken, so history's index lines naming it still go. This removes §16.38's
residual "a live item with an outputs row at the path but no page there in HEAD still loses its row". Why: a
second worktree's live file at a taken path lost its `_manifest` line under a VERIFIED report; and a live row
left without its committed page (a crash between the manifest write and the commit, the tree then cleaned by
hand) was deleted, so the next cycle's repair could not republish the page. Tests:
`tests/test_governance.py::test_purge_keeps_the_manifest_line_of_each_worktree_heads_own_file_at_a_taken_path`,
`::test_purge_keeps_a_listed_files_outputs_row_at_a_purged_path_with_no_page_in_head`.

#### The `PurgeReport` stub lists `not_run`

The §16 stub of `PurgeReport` now carries `not_run: str = ''` after `taken_paths`, as the code has since §16.38.

#### Kept not built

- History and log lines that name a taken path (R123). In history, a CHANGELOG `- A`/`- D` line or an older
  DEPENDS.tsv row naming only the taken path stays: the path is the live page's own name in HEAD, and older
  DEPENDS.tsv pinned hashes also survive in history's topic frontmatter, which a purge never rewrites, so nothing
  new leaks. Scrubbing them would remove the live page's own lines (the defect §16.38 fixed), and doing it only in
  commits before the live item appeared needs time-aware scrubbing per commit for a metadata-only gain. Logs and
  run errors are diagnostics: a line naming the path cannot be told apart between the purged and the live item,
  so scrubbing it is fail-closed. This replaces the reason "logs are regenerated": the scrubbed lines are deleted
  for good.
- A transient quarantine still runs its queued upstream deletion (R124). Treating a quarantined row as listed
  would leave the earlier text in history where that text is what the purge must remove (a credential in the
  name, secret-in-content after a re-screen, encrypted, label policy), and `state_reason` is free text, so a
  narrow allowlist that missed would do the same; a "transient" reason can also be permanent and keep the entry
  queued indefinitely. The cost of running is the file's earlier history only; the next cycle republishes its
  page once the quarantine clears. Pinned by `tests/test_governance.py::
  test_purge_queue_keeps_an_upstream_deletion_of_a_file_that_is_listed_again` and `docs/deploy/data-governance.md`.

### 16.45 Round 3: sync, status and doctor (2026-10-11, wave B13 round 3 lane B)

Wave B13 round 3, lane B: 29 items (`~/.cache/agentsync-bring-back/b13/round2/items/R<n>.md`, lanes in
`round2/lanes.json`). Each item below is built with a test that fails without it, or names why a part is not built.
Items that describe one defect from two or three finders are built once: R37, R50 and R80 (the lock holder); R46,
R47 and R57 (the credential alarm's tail). R144's refusal and R1's `exclude-empty` command are not built (see
each).

**R52, R94, R54: the purge queue preview counts as the run does (`agentsync.cli`).** `purge --queue --dry-run`
counts as previewed only the entries a run would run (an upstream deletion of a live file and a held entry stay
queued), the same count the real run prints; its `M queued` stays the whole queue (a preview leaves it as it is).
**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.50 Q61:** an entry an earlier purge of the run covers is folded into the covering
report in a preview too, as the run folds it, so it is not counted as a preview of its own. `_print_purge` prints a `taken:` line right after its `path:` line in both modes. The `accept-deletions` help line
says a pass that does not list SOURCE in full applies no removal and keeps the breaker. Tests:
`test_purge_queue_preview_does_not_count_a_kept_upstream_deletion_as_previewed`,
`test_purge_marks_a_taken_path_after_its_path_line`,
`test_accept_deletions_help_says_an_incomplete_pass_applies_none`.

**R58: the reviewer's guide reads the preview's last line right.** docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md's Purge queue row
quotes both last lines as the CLI prints them; pinned by
`test_setup_feedback_reads_the_purge_preview_last_line_as_the_cli_prints_it`.

**R46, R47, R57: the credential alarm names the preview first (`agentsync.cycle`).** The credential rescan's alarm
ends with `cycle._PURGE_QUEUE_STEPS` (dated line in §16.38); pinned in `tests/test_credential_rescreen.py`.

**R77: an unreadable once-a-credential record is rebuilt (`agentsync.cycle`).** An unreadable
`secret_once_credential` value is logged (WARNING) and rebuilt from the rows quarantined as a credential plus
`secret_rescreen_waiting`, and the files of queued `DLP_REMEDIATION` purges, then written back at once
(`_Cycle._rebuilt_once`); pinned by
`test_an_unreadable_once_a_credential_record_is_rebuilt_from_the_manifest_and_logged`. The other meta reads that
swallow a bad value (the waiting list, the rules identity) are unchanged: each already falls back to a re-screen,
not to a weaker scan.

**R105: an absent file's pages become deletion notices, and the words say so (`agentsync.cycle`,
`agentsync.cli`).** A local or inbox file absent from two complete passes is tombstoned. Its page stays in the
mirror as a `[DELETED UPSTREAM]` stub until `tombstone_reap_days`. Four messages used to say "removed"; they now
say "deletion notices", plural because an `.eml` tombstones its attachment pages with it. The four messages are the
marking alarm (`N file(s) absent from this complete pass: their pages become deletion notices only if still absent
next pass`), the removing alarm (`N file(s) still absent from this complete pass: their pages are now deletion
notices (deleted upstream; purge queued)`), the sync line (`K turned into deletion notices (deleted upstream)`) and
the status suffix (`· absent N (turned into deletion notices by a later complete pass if still missing)`). `; purge
queued` is printed only when `purge_on_upstream_delete` is on: it is on by default, and `archive = true` turns it
off. `absent_removed` keeps its name. The §16.37 and §16.39 H23 literals are amended in place. Tests:
`tests/test_cli.py` (status suffix, alarm, marking and removing lines, line order),
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_an_exclude_added_while_files_are_absent_retires_only_what_it_excludes` and
`::test_archive_on_upstream_delete_survives_a_head_moved_by_hand` (under archive, no "purge queued").

**R51: a source the run did not select reads `skipped (not in this run)` (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.cli`,
`agentsync.publish`).** The published-page rescan can raise an alarm about a page of a source the run did not list:
`sync --source`, `reconcile --source`, `accept-deletions SOURCE` or `materialise`. That source then gets a line,
which used to read `skipped (-) · INCOMPLETE · cursor held`. `_Cycle._report` now gives its SourceReport
`skipped_reason="not in this run"`. The reason is set only in the frozen report: `_acc` does not set it and
`run_sources` does not record it, so heartbeats and `loop` are unchanged. The sync line prints
`complete`/`INCOMPLETE` and the cursor word only for a source with `pass_kind`. The CHANGELOG prints
`complete`/`INCOMPLETE` only for such a source. A paused, retired or client-less source therefore reads `skipped
(<reason>)` followed by its alarms. STATE.md's `pass: skipped` is unchanged. Test:
`tests/test_credential_rescreen.py::test_a_source_the_run_did_not_select_reads_not_in_this_run_with_no_completeness_word`.
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J51:** `sync --source` does not exist (KISS K13b deleted it on 2026-10-05, before this
text was written; `sync` refuses it with exit 2): the runs that leave a source out are `reconcile --source`,
`accept-deletions SOURCE` and `materialise`.

**R2: an unreadable conversion is counted apart from a failed one (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.cli`,
`agentsync.setup_report`).** The run record adds `converted_unreadable`, the UNREADABLE results among `converted`.
`converted` and `converted_failed` keep their meanings. `SourceReport` carries `unreadable` and
`conversion_failed`. When U > 0, the sync's last line ends ` (of the converted: U unreadable, F failed)`. This
comes after the `converted N, deferred M online-only[, read again R]` words, so install.sh's `SYNC_SUMMARY_RE`, its
awk note and setup-report's `_CONVERTED_LINE_RE` all still match. The Repeat conversions table gets an `of them
unreadable (stub, kept, not retried)` column. When a run it shows has such a file, a note says that the file is in
Quarantine under its stub's class (`encrypted`, `not the type its name says`, `empty`, a `no text` class), never
`conversion failed`. The first-sync clause takes the breakdown from install.out's line of the same sync.
install.log's `converted-N-deferred-M` note has none, since install.sh writes it. Tests:
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_an_unreadable_conversion_is_counted_apart_from_a_failed_one`,
`tests/test_setup_report.py::test_repeat_conversions_part_reads_the_run_records_and_the_cache` and
`::test_first_sync_clause_carries_the_read_again_count`.
Amended 2026-10-12 (§16.58, F8 and F32): setup-report reads the `of the converted: U unreadable, F failed` clause
wherever it stands after the counts (§16.57 F34 puts it after Q28's clause as `; of the converted: ...`).

**R100: a converter library upgrade reopens the re-read (`agentsync.cycle`).** `_Cycle._capabilities` adds `deps`:
the sorted `[name, convert._common._dist_version(name)]` pairs of `cycle._CONVERTER_DISTS` (olefile, openpyxl,
pdfminer.six, pypandoc_binary, pypdfium2, python-pptx). A library that is not installed reads `unknown`. The pairs
use distribution versions only, never a converter's `version()`. A `uv sync` that moves one of these libraries
therefore restarts the scan once, as a new build does. A file in `tried` gets its two attempts again. Amends §16.27
("tried" bullet and "The record" `for` bullet) and §16.39 N4 (its "a dependency upgrade alone ... restarts nothing"
paragraph). Tests: `tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_file_given_up_is_read_again_by_another_build[library]` and
`::test_the_converter_libraries_in_the_re_read_digest_are_dependencies`.

**R59.** §16.37's paragraph on the alarm of a source whose unknown folders are all empty cloud folders now carries
a dated line (`**Amended 2026-10-11, §16.39 N27:**`) that quotes the pointer the code prints, for an inbox as for a

Doc only; the alarm texts stay pinned by `tests/test_arm_local.py`
(`test_zero_child_cloud_dirs_log_at_info_and_the_scan_alarm_names_them`,
`test_an_unreadable_folder_beside_an_empty_cloud_folder_offers_no_exclude`,
`test_an_inbox_empty_cloud_folder_alarm_points_at_the_waits`).

**R103.** An empty source root, plain or cloud, gets one alarm and never an exclude: with files mirrored, the

read: '.' (EPERM: ...)`; EPERM keeps the grant, and EACCES reads `the source folder's own permissions do not let

Amended 2026-10-19, §16.131 U18, U71, U102: `is empty but N files are mirrored` (`1 file is mirrored`).

**R102.** The wait for a local source whose listing a folder blocks (no access, a missing folder or sentinel) is

Amended 2026-10-16, §16.101 N12, N38: the bracket names the cause by the stored kinds (`refused with EACCES`, ...)
and the sentinel only while one is set; `no access, or a missing folder or sentinel` only when no kind is stored.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.115 Q80 (by §16.107 O49): `or a missing sentinel` only when the last walk stored
today's sentinel as missing (`sentinel_missing:<id>`), not whenever one is set.

**R101.** An inbox pass stamps `last_seen_run`, and only that, on the present file rows of the files its walk
withheld as changed within `quiescence_s` or future-dated (`ScanResult.withheld`, stable ids;
`Manifest.touch_withheld`, in the pass's transaction). `Manifest.unlisted_count`, so `loop._missed` and the setup
report's Empty cloud folders count, no longer count such a file, and `unseen_live` never offers it as a deletion
candidate. A withheld file with no row (a new file still being written) stamps nothing, so a file deleted upstream

`tests/test_loop.py::test_an_inbox_file_the_walk_withheld_is_not_in_the_count` (was
`..._is_in_the_count_until_a_sync_lists_it`), `test_withheld_inbox_files_leave_a_real_deletion_in_the_count`.

**R1.** A zero-child folder is unknown, never empty, only in a File Provider domain: its provider folder
(`~/Library/CloudStorage/<provider>`, the first component below a cloud root) carries a File Provider extended
attribute (a real domain root carries `com.apple.file-provider-domain-id`), or the attribute read fails for any
reason (EPERM, ENOSYS off macOS: fail-safe, the old rule). A clean read with no such attribute (a plain folder, as
a rehearsal sandbox's `mkdir` makes) makes a zero-child folder an ordinary empty one, so the listing completes. The
walk reads the attribute once per provider folder per walk (`arm_local._is_domain`, cached in `walk`);
`file_provider_marker` moved from `setup_report` to `materialise` and both import it from there. A zero-child cloud
root with no provider folder above it keeps the rule. Decision 71d3e66ef726 is unchanged. The empty cloud folder
wait now reads `N empty cloud folder(s) keep the listing of <id> incomplete: an empty folder in a cloud folder is
expected and loses nothing, since deletions in <id> are only held until it is excluded, and another sync does not
clear it; if they are meant to be empty, set exclude = [...] ...`. Dated lines in §11 and in the §16.22 rule's
restatement. Not built: the spec's `exclude-empty` command (the CLI command set is frozen). Tests:
`tests/test_arm_local.py` (`test_an_empty_folder_in_a_plain_provider_folder_is_just_empty`, macOS only;
`test_a_provider_folder_whose_attributes_cannot_be_read_keeps_the_rule`), `tests/test_loop.py`
(`test_an_empty_folder_in_a_plain_provider_folder_gets_no_wait`, macOS only). `tests/conftest.py` reads every
provider folder as a domain in-process (autouse `_provider_folders_are_domains`); the R1 tests opt out with
`real_domain_check`, and `file_provider_domain(path)` sets the real attribute for a walk in another process.
**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.51 Q11, Q71:** the wait reads `... loses nothing, but while the listing is incomplete,
deletions in <id> are held, not applied, and another sync does not complete it; if the folder(s) are meant to be
empty, run `~/.local/bin/agentsync exclude-empty <id>` ...`; the command is built (§16.51 Q71).

**Review fixes (R1, R102, R103).**
- R1: `_is_domain` also counts an entry that is not a real folder on lstat (a symlinked provider entry, whose own
  attributes say nothing) as a domain, and the walk keeps the rule for any path with a `..` in it under a cloud
  root. Test: `tests/test_arm_local.py::test_a_provider_folder_reached_through_a_symlink_or_dot_dot_keeps_the_rule`
  (macOS only).
- R1 (pre-existing): `arm_local._cloud_roots` also holds each cloud root's resolved path, so a source stored

  `tests/test_arm_local.py::test_a_home_reached_through_a_symlink_keeps_the_rule`.
- R102/R103: a source whose last walk could not list its root, or found it empty, or could not walk it at all
  (manifest meta `root_unlisted:<id>` = "1", `cycle._ROOT_UNLISTED_META`, written beside `empty_cloud_dirs:<id>`
  only on a change) gets its own wait with no exclude: `the folder of <id> itself could not be listed or is empty
  (an unmounted volume, a sync client that has not filled it yet, or no access; another sync does not clear it):
  mount it or let the sync client fill it, or grant Files and Folders access; to stop syncing it on purpose, set
  state = "paused" in [[source]] id = "<id>" in <sources.toml>`, and its `heartbeat.<id>` check. Every other wait
  is byte-identical. Test: `tests/test_loop.py::test_a_source_root_a_sync_cannot_list_never_offers_an_exclude`.
  Amended 2026-10-17, §16.113 Q6, Q11, Q34: a root that does not exist (stored `unlisted_kinds:<id>` `{".":
  "missing"}`) has its own wait, `the folder of <id> does not exist (...)`.

**R37, R50, R80: an empty-body lock holder is named one way and runs no cycle** (`agentsync.ops.lock`,
`agentsync.ops.doctor`). A held lock with an empty body (install.sh's lockf, a status or doctor `is_held` probe, or
a cycle between its flock and its body write) reads `an unrecorded holder (install.sh while it reinstalls
agentsync, a status or doctor check, or a cycle starting)` in `LockHeldError`'s text, in its `who` (the CLI's
`skipped: lock held by ...` WARNING) and in doctor: one constant, `EMPTY_BODY_HOLDER`, with no pid or time, so
Recent errors still merges the WARNING. A non-empty body that does not parse keeps `an unidentified holder
(unparseable lock body)`. Doctor's held `lock` line adds `(a cycle is running)` only when the body parses as a
cycle's record (`LockInfo.parse`); for any other body it reads `held by <desc>` and reads no holder sidecar, so a
dead cycle's leftover sidecar never yields a `kill <pid>` fix while install.sh holds the lock. N24 and the
install.sh lock bullet carry dated amendments. Tests: `tests/test_ops_lock.py`
(`test_a_holder_with_no_lock_body_yet_is_named_as_unidentified`), `tests/test_ops_doctor.py`
(`test_lock_held_with_an_empty_body_names_no_cycle`).

**R38: status's own fix names no command** (`agentsync.ops.doctor`). A local source's incomplete-listing fix reads
`each WAITING ON YOU line about <id> says what stops the listing and what to do: another sync does not clear it`:
status prints it, so `agentsync status (...)` sent the reader to the command they had just run, and "above" does
not hold in the setup report's Doctor section. N27's "each" and the source id stay; the text has no parentheses,
since the report's fix parser strips one level. §16.39 is amended. Tests: `tests/test_ops_doctor.py`
(`test_heartbeat_states`, `test_heartbeat_incomplete_fix_by_source_kind`), `tests/test_setup_report.py`
(`test_a_wait_the_loop_names_is_yours_and_a_stopped_sync_stays_unexpected`).

**R151: doctor follows the loop's waits instead of re-deriving them** (`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.ops.doctor`).
status reads `loop.next_step` before its checks and passes `NextStep.checks` to `doctor.run_checks(config, ...,
loop_checks=...)` (a keyword; `None`, the default, keeps the old wording). An incomplete listing gets the WAITING
ON YOU fix, or under `AGENTSYNC_NO_NEXT_HINT=1` the note `yours: see WAITING ON YOU`, only when its
`heartbeat.<id>` is among those checks, whatever the source kind (an inbox with empty cloud folders included); any
other incomplete local source reads `agentsync sync; another full walk lists it`, which holds both right after the
exclude line was pasted (no sync since) and after a pass that was not FULL. That first read skips rule 9's count of
the curation queue (`count_queue=False`); `NextStep.checks` depends on neither that count nor the FAILs. status
prints that read's NEXT only when no check failed and its step came before rule 9; otherwise it reads the loop
again exactly as before (`next_lines(fixes=...)`), so NEXT is byte for byte the old one and the queue is counted no
more often than before (rule 1 counts none). The setup report's Doctor section passes no loop checks and keeps the
default. Tests: `tests/test_ops_doctor.py` (`test_heartbeat_incomplete_follows_the_loop_checks`),
`tests/test_loop.py` (`test_status_points_the_heartbeat_at_a_wait_only_while_the_loop_has_it`,
`test_status_next_is_the_loops_with_and_without_a_fail`).

**R78: a fix command quotes a path by what it holds** (`agentsync.ops.doctor`, `agentsync.setup_report`). The docs
repo fixes (`mkdir -p`, `move ... aside`, `git -C ... rm --cached`) and a cloud root's `open ... in Finder once`
print the path through `_shell_path`, never raw, so a space no longer splits it. `_shell_path` keeps `~/'<rest>'`
(or `'<path>'`) for a path with no `'`; a path with a `'` and none of `!$`\"` is `~/"<rest>"` (or `"<path>"`),
still the raw path in one piece for the redaction; any other is spliced with `'\''`, which splits a name holding a
quote for the redaction. Each form reads back as the exact path in sh, bash, zsh and dash. The setup report's
`_HOME_CONTAINER_RE` takes either quote after `~/`, so `~/"Development/<folder-1>"` is no residue hit. Tests:
`tests/test_ops_doctor.py` (`test_shell_path_quotes_by_content_and_every_shell_reads_the_path_back`,
`test_docs_repo_fixes_quote_the_path`), `tests/test_setup_report.py`
(`test_residue_ignores_macos_path_components_and_the_temp_folder_is_redacted`).

**R79: a cache or log folder that holds home is a FAIL, never a chmod target** (`agentsync.ops.doctor`). The
permissions check applies the sync's rule, `cycle._holds_home` (same file, not same spelling; the home folder or
any folder above it): such a `cache_dir` or `log_dir` is neither walked (the person's own entries are not tenant
data) nor named in the chmod, and gets its own FAIL, `config.<key>`: `<key> is the home folder or a folder that
holds it, so agentsync leaves its modes alone`, fix `set <key> in <sources.toml> to a folder of its own, such as
<the default>`. With no chmod target left, `docs_repo.permissions` offers no chmod. Test:
`tests/test_ops_doctor.py` (`test_a_cache_or_log_folder_that_holds_home_is_a_fail_and_no_chmod_target`).

**R144: two sources holding the same files is an advisory, never a refusal** (`agentsync.ops.doctor`,
`agentsync.manifest`). The duplicate refusal stays inbox versus live Graph row (design failure-mode row 24):
between two other sources neither copy is the real one, and stubbing one by an unproven inference would cost its
citations. Doctor adds `sources.shared_content`, an ok (info) line shown only when two live non-inbox sources share
live or dataless files by canonical hash: `<n> file(s) in <a> have the same content as a file in <b>; ...: both are
kept; if one source copies the other, set state = "retired" in its [[source]] block in sources.toml (its pages
become tombstones in one labelled commit)` (**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.50 Q42:** was `removing it from sources.toml
retires its pages`, but deleting the block is refused at the next sync, exit 78, `Cycle._refuse_vanished_sources`,
so the line names the explicit retirement in that refusal's words). One grouped query,
`Manifest.shared_canonical_counts(source_ids)`, which joins each file with the distinct (source, hash) set of the
other sources, never with every copy (a join of copies with copies grows as their product, on every status); no
line before the first sync or when the manifest cannot be read. Tests: `tests/test_manifest.py`
(`test_shared_canonical_counts_pairs_the_given_sources_in_one_query`,
`test_shared_canonical_counts_meets_each_copy_once`), `tests/test_ops_doctor.py`
(`test_two_sources_holding_the_same_files_is_an_info_line`).
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.131 U18, U71, U102: `<n> files in <a> have the same content` (`1 file in <a> has`).

**R75: a background run finds the gitleaks the person's shell finds.** launchd gives a LaunchAgent run the PATH
`/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, so a gitleaks that only a shell PATH reaches (`go install`, MacPorts, `~/bin`) was
missed and every background run scanned with the builtin patterns alone. A run from the shell (`agentsync sync`,
`agentsync install-agent`) now records (`lints.remember_gitleaks`) the path its PATH finds (`shutil.which`'s path,
not the resolved one, so an upgrade keeps it) in `gitleaks-path` in the default state dir; a LaunchAgent run writes
nothing there. `lints._gitleaks()` (`lints.gitleaks_lookup`) uses, in order: the recorded path when it is still an
executable file (`lints.recorded_gitleaks`), PATH, then the fixed places, which now also include `/opt/local/bin`,
`~/.local/bin` and `~/go/bin`. Because both kinds of run read the record first, they use the same gitleaks and
`secret_rules_identity` does not move between them (no rescan from alternating runs). Doctor's `gitleaks` check
WARNs when this shell finds a gitleaks that a LaunchAgent run would not (record, launchd's PATH and the fixed
places all miss), with the fix `agentsync sync`; INFO with no fix when no LaunchAgent is installed; no line
otherwise. Tests: `tests/test_lints.py::test_a_launchd_run_uses_the_gitleaks_a_shell_run_recorded`,
`::test_a_launchd_run_records_nothing_and_a_stale_record_is_passed_over`,
`::test_a_go_install_gitleaks_is_found_on_launchds_path`,
`tests/test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_gitleaks_only_this_shell_finds_is_a_warn_until_a_shell_run_records_it`,
`tests/test_credential_rescreen.py::test_a_sync_from_the_shell_records_the_gitleaks_its_path_finds`.

**R76: the builtin patterns read every page, beside gitleaks.** gitleaks 8.30.1 does not flag a plain `Password:
Welcome123`, and only a file once stubbed as a credential (`builtin_too=`) was read by the builtin patterns as
well, so a copy or move of a stubbed file (a new id) and any new page with a plain password were published on a Mac
with gitleaks. `lints.lint_secrets` now runs the builtin patterns over every page it scans and gitleaks beside
them; `builtin_too=` is removed. In the same version bump, `generic-password` passes over a bracketed hint that
holds a space or is one placeholder word (`(minimum 8 characters)`, `<your password>`, `{password}`, `[redacted]`)
and over a value of mask characters only (`*`, `x`, `.`, `•`, `-`, trailing punctuation allowed: `********,`); a
bracketed value that is neither (`(Welcome123)`, `<S3cr3t!x>`, `{Welcome123}`), a value after a hint (`(min 8
chars) Welcome123`), `Password: Welcome123` and `pwd=Abc12345` are hits. `SECRET_RULES_VERSION` is 2: every install
scans its published pages once more under both changes. Tests:
`tests/test_credential_rescreen.py::test_a_new_file_with_a_password_gitleaks_misses_is_a_credential_stub`,
`::test_a_copy_of_a_credential_stub_under_a_new_name_is_a_stub_too`,
`::test_the_builtin_patterns_read_every_page_when_gitleaks_scans`,
`tests/test_lints.py::test_the_password_pattern_passes_over_placeholders_and_masks`.

**R48: a page rewritten in the run the rules move is checked against its committed text (§16.39 N5).** in the run
the secret-scan rules move, a page the run rewrites (an edit, or a re-read for an emitter or capability change) is
no longer skipped by the published-page rescan. While `secret_rescan_pending` is set,
`_Cycle._scan_rewritten_history` reads, from HEAD, every page the run wrote and every path its changes name (a
rename's earlier path included), with the text sidecars HEAD holds under each, into a private folder under the
staging folder, and scans them with `lints.lint_secrets` as the rescan does. An item whose committed text hits is
recorded; when its page then becomes a credential stub, its cached conversions are deleted and a `dlp-remediation`
purge is queued with the rescan's alarm and WARNING. When the committed text hits but the page the run wrote does
not (an edit removed the key, the file is another stub now, or it was deleted that run), the purge is queued all
the same, with the alarm `a published page matches the secret scan's new rules: the text committed before this run
does; ...`. A key the edit brings in (HEAD text clean) gives the stub alone, with no purge. Tests
(`tests/test_credential_rescreen.py`):
`test_a_page_edited_in_the_run_the_rules_move_still_queues_the_purge_of_its_earlier_text`,
`test_a_page_read_again_in_the_run_the_rules_move_still_queues_the_purge_of_its_earlier_text`,
`test_a_key_the_edit_brings_in_the_run_the_rules_move_is_a_stub_with_no_purge`,
`test_a_key_the_edit_removes_in_the_run_the_rules_move_still_queues_the_purge_of_its_earlier_text`,
`test_a_file_deleted_in_the_run_the_rules_move_still_queues_the_purge_of_its_earlier_text`.

**R74: archive pages are scanned again when the rules move (§16.39 N5).** `[governance] archive` pages are scanned
again when the rules move. Every `archive/` page whose frontmatter says `status: archived`, with the text sidecars
under its `.files/` folder (symlinks skipped), joins the rescan apart from the output pages. A hit deletes the copy
and its sidecars (committed as a deletion), rewrites the item's mirror tombstone without the line naming the copy
when that tombstone is still there, deletes the item's cached conversions and queues a `dlp-remediation` purge
named by the copy's own frontmatter ids, with the rescan's alarm head (`a published page matches the secret scan's
new rules: its archive/ copy is deleted; ...`) and WARNING, naming the source id and the opaque id only. It never
writes a stub for an item its source deleted. §16.39 N5 is amended in place (its archive residual is closed). Test:
`test_an_archive_page_the_new_rules_match_is_deleted_and_queues_a_purge`.

**R144 and R1, the parts not built.** R144's refusal of a duplicate between two non-inbox sources: its verifier
measured that a refusal would stub a source's copy on an unproven inference and cost its citations (only the
advisory above is built). R1's `agentsync exclude-empty <id>` command: the CLI command set is frozen (tests pin
it); the wait's paste line stays the one step, and in a plain folder the turn no longer arises.
**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.51 Q71:** built as the hidden `agentsync exclude-empty SOURCE`; the freeze allowed a
hidden command pinned in §16.10, and no harm was measured. The operator still runs it.

### 16.46 Round 3: report redaction (2026-10-11, wave B13 round 3 lane RA)

Both reports redact alike, and every change below is made in both: `agentsync setup-report`
(`setup_report.Redactor`, `_build_redactor`) and the shell fallback (`scripts/install.sh`'s `redaction_pairs`,
`redact_stream`). Tests: `tests/test_report_redaction.py`, which runs each case through both.

#### This repository's own locator is kept whole (R3, R10, R20, R39)

On a Mac whose full name run together is this repository's public owner, the name's joined forms turned
every copy of the issue link and the source URL in the report body into `github.com/<name>/agent-context-sync`
and counted a name; only the last line, written after redaction, kept it. Both redactors now keep
`github.com/` or `github.com:` and the owner/repo of `ISSUE_URL` (any case, `.git` optional, followed by no
word character or hyphen) as one piece: `Redactor`'s first alternative (with a leading `git@`), and a held
piece in `redact_stream` built from `ISSUE_URL`. Only that owner's: a fork's owner, another host's copy and the
joined name anywhere else stay `<name>`. Holding the bare owner word, or dropping the joined name form, would
leak the name wherever else it is written run together, so neither is done.

#### A second pass leaves a placeholder whole (R69)

The Summary's item lines are redacted twice and a friction log can hold an earlier report's placeholders: a
registered value spelled like a placeholder's word (a folder `Host`, `Folder 1`) turned `<host>` into
`<<folder-1>>`. `Redactor` now tries a placeholder's shape first and keeps it uncounted: a numbered kind with
any number or `N`, an unnumbered kind, `<path>` and the IT request's template fields, the set
`redact_stream` already held. No other bracketed word is held: `<contoso>` with `contoso` registered is
`<<org-1>>`, and a folder named `<Draft>` is matched whole. Holding every `<word>` shape would let a
registered value through inside angle brackets.

#### Unicode case boundaries and accents (R70, R115)

`_tokens` splits a fuzzy value at Unicode case boundaries and skips combining marks, so `CaféPlans` and
`MonÉtude` cover `Café Plans`, `mon-étude` and their NFD spellings; every ASCII split is as before. Each
accented letter of a value matches in NFC, in NFD or without its accent, never the front of an accented letter
(NFD `Cafés` is not cut), and the Redactor keys values without accents (`_bare`), so `Cafe Resume`, `Café
Résumé` and text mixing the two forms share one placeholder. An exact value (a lone name part) gets the same,
with its case kept. An accented value registered after its unaccented spelling keeps that placeholder and is
matched as written too. The shell registers each value's accent-stripped form (combining marks U+0300 to
U+036F). Text that mixes NFC and NFD letters is matched by the Python report only: the shell matches literal
bytes, and a value with k accents would need 2^k pairs; normalising the report instead would need `iconv`,
which stops at a byte that is not UTF-8. The shell registers no CamelCase forms, so R70 has no shell twin.

#### Every part of a full name (R71, R72, R73)

A hyphenated part (`Jean-Luc`) is registered whole and in pieces; an all-capitals part (`DOE`, `LI`) also
capitalised; a two-letter part in each form `short_name` / `_short_word` allows, starting with a capital as
written (a particle such as `de` names no one, in any case). Brackets are stripped innermost first until none
is left (`Jane Doe (Northwind (EU))`), and every pass's words are lone names, written, upper-case and, when
all capitals, capitalised. The shell splits at hyphens as well as commas; upper-cases with `tr` in UTF-8
(`ÅL` for `Ål`; byte-wise where the text is not UTF-8), since bash 3.2 has no `${x^^}`; registers two-letter
forms through `add_forms` (`add_pair` without its 3-character floor, so with their NFC, NFD and `%q` forms); and
its joined forms gain the capitalised words (`Jane Li` for `LI, JANE`).

#### A name logged under UTF-8 and reported under C (R111)

bash 3.2's `printf %q` writes `Café Notes` as `Café\ Notes` under UTF-8 and as `$'Caf\303\251 Notes'` under C.
The shell now also registers a non-ASCII value's UTF-8 `%q` form, and a loose `--source-local` word's, with the
locale set inside the command substitution (bash 3.2 ignores a prefix assignment for a builtin). The C form
needs no pair: `redact_stream` makes every `$'..'` word `<path>` first.

#### Proxies (R4, R27, R42, R67, R68)

- A proxy host with no dot that is one of the report's own words (`_GENERIC_PROXY_HOSTS`, the shell's
  `generic_proxy_host`: proxy, wpad, localhost and the like) is matched only where a URL names it: after `//` or
  `@`, or before `:<port>`. `HTTPS_PROXY`, `network.proxy` and "Could not resolve proxy:" stay. Any other host
  with no dot (`contosogw`) can name the company and is matched bare, as git and curl print it; the shell, which
  skipped every dotless host, now does both (pair flag `t`: not followed by a word character, dot or hyphen).
- The Environment line ends `· proxy in git's config: set (git uses it before HTTPS_PROXY)` or `not set`, from
  `_git_proxy_urls`; the shell prints `- proxy in git's config: …` from the same files (`git_proxy_values`). Set
  or not set only, never the host.
  Amended 2026-10-13, §16.69 H20: then `· URL rewrite in git's config: set (N)` or `not set` (the shell: `- URL
  rewrite in git's config: …`), a count of `[url "<base>"] insteadOf` bases, never a host; each base's host, the
  base after its scheme and user, and its path are registered as `<proxy-N>` after git's proxies.
- The shell fallback prints `- system proxy (scutil --proxy): manual HTTPS yes|no · PAC yes|no · WPAD yes|no`
  from the Enable flags, as `net.py` reads them (a host key can stay while its flag is 0), or `unknown`.
- The LaunchAgent's own proxy, which doctor's `network.proxy.job` line prints where it differs from this
  shell's, is registered: a `ReportHooks.job_proxy` hook (`cli._job_proxy_urls`: `launchctl getenv` for the URL
  variables, never NO_PROXY, then the plist's), called under the report's budget, last so it renumbers no other
  `<proxy-N>`. The shell reads `launchctl getenv` for the same variables.

#### The report's own words

- The Redaction section's "Send it" sentence names only the issue-form fields the last line's link fills,
  read from the link (`issue_link_fields`, against `ISSUE_FIELD_LABELS`, which a test keeps equal to
  `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/setup-report.yml`); a link that fills none opens a blank "Setup report" issue form (R23).
- The shell legend says "a name every OneDrive or Google Drive has, such as Documents, only where it stands as a
  whole word" and "every word bash wrote in its dollar-quote form, which install.log uses for a name with a
  curly apostrophe, an en dash or an accent" (R7).
- `test_headings_redaction_and_runtime` asserts `<library-1>` from install.log's args in the Installer section,
  not from Doctor, which a loaded machine timed out (R45).

#### Kept as they are (R135, R141)

- A one-word organisation is redacted as a whole word wherever it stands (`Microsoft` in `Microsoft Graph`),
  and the shell numbers `<org-N>` in its own order: both fail closed. A common-word exemption would print a
  tenant named like a common word; matching the shell's order would still not match Python's numbers (the
  shell never reads `graph.tenant` or SharePoint hosts), and partly matching numbers would look reliable
  without being so (N44, amended).
  Amended 2026-10-12 (§16.58, F42, F55, F92): whole-word redaction of a value that is a word the report prints
  does not fail closed: the report's template is public, so its placeholder in fixed text reads back as the
  word. Such a one-word organisation is still registered from every entry (no exemption prints it) but matched
  only in folder and domain names; such a folder or library sends the report privately. The full fix is
  redaction where each value is put into a line.
- A short name's joined forms over-redact report words ("Ho, Me" turns "home" into `<name>`). Dropping parts
  under 3 letters from the joined forms reopens the leak of `LiJo`, `li_jo` and a listed-word part (`Me` in
  `Ho Me`), which the joined forms alone cover (§16.40 H20).

### 16.47 Round 3: setup report and installer (2026-10-11, wave B13 round 3 lane RB)

Round 2's rehearsal, review and harvest items for the setup report, the installer and `it_request.py` (lane
RB). Each item names its round 2 id; the spec is the adversarial verifier's corrected fix. Where an item amends
an older section, a dated line sits at that section too.

#### The shell fallback report

- **launchd job ownership** (R6, R16, one defect). `launchctl print` reads the uid's domain, not this HOME's.
  `launchd_foreign` applies `setup_report._background`'s rule: the job is another install's when the plist it
  was loaded from is outside this home folder, or its program or an argument is in another user's or a
  temporary folder. Then the line reads `- loaded, but the job belongs to another install (its plist or
  ProgramArguments are outside this home folder); its runs and exit codes are not this setup's result`, with no
  state, runs or exit code. A job loaded from this home's own plist path whose file is gone stays this setup's:
  `- loaded, but the plist is absent (removed without launchctl bootout; agentsync install-agent repairs it):
  state ...`. The Summary's `- launchd: real` reads `- launchd: not simulated (real LaunchAgents)`. Tests:
  `test_the_shell_report_names_another_installs_job_as_not_this_setups` (the stub's `print` takes
  STUB_LC_PATH and STUB_LC_PROGRAM).
  Amended 2026-10-12 (§16.53, Q5, Q6): every Background runs line starts with its job's label, the reconcile
  job has its own, and the Summary reads `- launchd: not simulated (the real launchctl); <label> plist
  present|absent, ...`.
  Amended 2026-10-13, §16.65 G74: the plist-absent line reads ``(removed without `launchctl bootout`;
  `~/.local/bin/agentsync install-agent` repairs it)``.
  Amended 2026-10-14, §16.75 J5: the Summary line reads `- background sync: <label> plist present|absent, ... in
  this home (Background runs has each job's state)`, or `- background sync: launchd: simulated (no LaunchAgent of
  this setup ran)`.
- **uv's Pythons** (R5): the count skips uv's hidden `.temp` folder (`! -name '.*'`).
  `test_the_shell_report_counts_uv_pythons_without_uvs_hidden_folder`.
- **A repeated organisation** (R44) takes no second `<org-N>`. Only the same bytes are a repeat: the shell
  matcher is case-sensitive (`index`), so a case-insensitive dedupe would leave another spelling unregistered.
  The order stays glob order (§16.46, R135). `test_the_shell_report_gives_a_repeated_organisation_one_number`.
- **A linked worktree's git config** (R110), here and in `_git_proxy_urls`: `checkout_git_configs` and
  `setup_report._checkout_git_configs` resolve `.git` (a directory, or a file with `gitdir: <path>`, relative
  to the checkout), then `commondir` (relative to the git dir), and read `<common dir>/config` and `<git
  dir>/config.worktree` as files. Tests: `test_a_linked_worktrees_git_config_is_read_for_proxies`,
  `test_the_shell_report_reads_a_linked_worktrees_git_config`. A comment inside that process substitution
  carries no apostrophe: `/bin/bash` 3.2 reads one there as a quote, which made the block a syntax error that
  its `2>/dev/null` hid (every proxy pair lost; caught by the H19 test).

#### A stopped copy's report (R17, R18)

`--report-only` for an attempt `--log-start` stopped writes `~/agent-context/setup/stopped-copy-report.md`,
not `setup-report.md`, so the last report that was not stopped keeps its bytes, as `bring-back.md` already did.
Its first line is `> This report is of an attempt that an out-of-date copy of the setup prompt started: do not
send it or bring it back.`, followed by ` The report of the last attempt that was not stopped is
~/agent-context/setup-report.md.` only when that file exists; the line is added after redaction, so it names a
home path only as `~/`. The agentsync report's Send-it paragraph and last-line issue link are untouched. The
NEXT says `do not send it or bring it back` and, only where `bring-back.md` exists, `(<path> was not touched: it
still holds the report of the last attempt that was not stopped)`: never "finished", since a failed attempt's
report writes it too. `test_the_report_of_a_stopped_copy_invites_no_bring_back`. The stop comment and
`docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md` now say which copies still go on to a report (v9 and older, and a v10 copy taken
before its step 3 named the stop; R21).
Amended 2026-10-12 (§16.53, Q10, Q18, Q20): the Send-it line and the last-line issue link are no longer
untouched: the stopped copy's report ends on `Not for sending: see the note at the top of this report.` instead,
and the next report of an attempt that was not stopped deletes the file.
Amended 2026-10-12 (§16.59, F18): the first line reads `> This report is of an attempt that a copy of the setup
prompt that does not match this installer started: do not send it or bring it back.`; "an out-of-date copy" was
false of a newer one.
Amended 2026-10-13, §16.65 G9: the first line and the NEXT read `an attempt started by a copy of the setup
prompt that does not match this installer`; a newer copy's NEXT says `, which is for setup prompt v<N>` after
"this installer" and has at most one bracket after its fix.
