Amended 2026-10-13, §16.70 H18: the bring-back bracket stands after "bring it back", before the fix, and reads
`(<path> was not touched and still holds the report of the last attempt that was not stopped)`; no bracket follows
the fix.

#### Step 2's reinstall (R34, R114, R125)

- The reinstall holds the lock of this run's config and of the config each LaunchAgent's plist names after
  `--config` (PlistBuddy), once each; a busy probe on any of them is the wait. The wait is per lock.
- Not built: building the checkout into a wheel first. Measured at load 500 (uv 0.12.17), it would cut the
  time the environment is missing from about 6 s to about 0.9 s, but uv then records the temporary wheel as the
  install source (`direct_url.json`: `archive_info` instead of the checkout's `dir_info`), and
  `setup_report._installed_from` (the report's install source and checkout facts), `_git_proxy_urls` (that
  checkout's proxy) and `it_request.source_checkout` (its refusal to write inside the checkout) all read the
  checkout from there. Restoring it would mean rewriting a file RECORD hashes, and uv's receipt. A tick in the
  window ends as the next bullet says, and launchd's next interval recovers.
- A locked install that fails and leaves no interpreter (a tick started Python while uv removed the
  environment: "Directory not empty") runs once more under the locks; a second failure says the environment was
  left without its interpreter and to run the command again, not network, proxy or TLS.
- install.log's `step=agentsync` line notes what the script saw: `waited-for-a-background-sync`,
  `wait-ran-out-after-<N>s` or `lock-not-taken-rc<N>`; a run with no wait keeps the line byte for byte. The
  Summary's install.sh line shows that step's note. A sync that starts after the probe is waited for with no
  note.
- The header says a tick in the rebuild ends in SPAWN_FAILED (exit 71) or an import error, and that a run killed
  with SIGKILL during the wait leaves lockf to run the reinstall once the lock frees (R125, kept). The launcher
  is unchanged: an edit would rebuild it, a new TCC identity.
- Tests: the wait, ran-out and free-lock tests (their notes),
  `test_the_reinstall_holds_the_lock_of_the_config_a_job_runs_with`,
  `tests/test_launcher.py::test_install_sh_full_run_is_idempotent` (the reinstall's source is the checkout,
  not a wheel),
  `test_a_locked_install_that_meets_a_half_removed_environment_runs_once_more`,
  `test_the_install_line_says_what_the_agentsync_steps_seconds_held`.

#### The setup report's Summary

- **First sync of an attempt that ran no install.sh** (R19, R28, one defect). The fallback to the newest earlier
  run is named: `(install.log: the install run of <start>, before this attempt; this attempt ran none)`, its
  counts `(install.log: that earlier run; ...)` or `(install.out: an earlier run's; this attempt ran none)`. With
  no earlier sync step it reads `no install.sh run during this attempt (install.log)`. The live baseline clause
  and the Loop line keep their words. `test_an_attempt_that_ran_no_installer_names_the_earlier_run_its_sync_line_reads`.
  Amended 2026-10-16, §16.92 M6 (M22, M38 the same defect): an attempt whose install runs reached no first-sync step
  reads `no install run of this attempt reached its first sync (install.log: the last stopped at its <step> step)` (a
  list-only attempt: `this attempt ran only install.sh --list-folders, no first sync (install.log)`), and
  install.out's counts are its own only under one of its runs' headers; an earlier run's are tagged `(install.out:
  the install run of <start>, before this attempt; ...)`, a headerless file's `(install.out: which run printed it is
  not recorded; ...)`.
- **No install.sh run, no folder question** (R15). An attempt with no run of its own counts no folder question
  and reads `- expected turns: none (no install.sh --list-folders run in this attempt: no folder question and no
  Allow click)`; any run keeps the usual rules and a logged question still counts.
  `test_an_attempt_with_no_installer_run_is_given_no_folder_question`.
- **Approvals with no Agent: line** (R24) are `approvals: not observable`.
  `test_approvals_are_counted_or_not_observable_by_tool`.
- **One timestamp** (R26): `session: one timestamp (<time>), no duration`.
  `test_an_attempt_with_one_timestamp_says_so_on_its_time_line`.
- **One step line** (R107): `its only step line is ...`; two or more `the last of its N step lines is ...`.
- **A gone process** (R131, wording only): `its process is gone: killed, the Mac restarted, or its end line
  could not be written`, since `log_at` drops a failed write. No detection: free space at report time says
  nothing of the earlier write.

#### Other report and doctor lines

- **Empty cloud folders** (R14): `; its last walk listed all T file(s) the mirror holds for it` when none was
  missed.
- **The setup-report warning's quoted time** (R108) is converted to UTC by one regex anchored to `warning:
  agentsync setup-report failed (...): `; it is lazy across the parentheses, because `rc_meaning` can give
  `stopped by SIGTERM (a tool timeout?)`.
- **Signal exits** (R81): `rc_meaning` names every 128 + N as `stopped by SIG<NAME> (signal N)`; doctor's git
  and pandoc probes (`_exit_words`) and the report's probes (`_exited`) word subprocess's negative code with
  `ocr._ended`. `test_a_signal_exit_is_named_by_its_signal`,
  `test_a_probe_a_signal_stopped_is_worded_as_the_converters_word_it`.
- **A .msg or an image under a label rule** (R33). The stored reason stays `no converter for <suffix>` (re-reads,
  stub identity, no label escalation). The page says `a [policy] label rule is set and the label of a <suffix>
  file cannot be read, so its content is withheld (content policy)` and names the route (save as .eml, export
  as a PDF). The report counts such rows as `withheld by label rule` while the rule is on, with a line naming
  those routes. An image is the rule's only where an OCR engine exists (the cycle's `Publisher.images_readable`;
  the report's OCR part reading `ready`): without one no image converter is registered whatever the policy
  says, and the image keeps the `no converter` words and class. `convert.registry.label_withheld_suffixes()` defines the set beside the gates;
  `setup_report._LABEL_WITHHELD` is held equal to it by a test. **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.51 Q27:** the stub's
  summary says it too (`refused: withheld by label rule: ...`).
- **The exclude line** (R8): an allowlist. Agentsync's shipped globs show as written; every other entry is
  `"<path>"` or `"/<path>/"`. The Loop line cuts a path to its last part first (K16b), so a nested
  `"/a/b/"` entry shows there as `"<path>"`.
- **Doctor's fixes name `~/.local/bin/agentsync`** (R12): the purge-queue, compaction and Time Machine fixes are
  built from `loop.BIN`; the report's Loop line keeps stripping paths (K16b).
- **An inbox held by an empty cloud folder** (R53): `loop.empty_cloud_folders_held` (stored empty folders today's
  exclude does not prune, after a FULL pass, not held for a prompt) decides; such an inbox gets the local
  source's status pointer, a note under install.sh. Doctor reads the manifest's stored state and lists no
  folder. `test_doctor_points_an_inbox_held_by_an_empty_cloud_folder_at_the_loops_wait`.
- **The evidence parts' helper lines** (R106) quote the probe's detail, which for a failed build is its reason:
  the docstrings and setup-feedback.md say so instead of "no reason text".

#### Tests (R97, R98)

The stubbed purge waits carry the loop's two-command text (R97). R98: the setup_report content tests run with a
roomy budget (`roomy_budget`; `build_report` reads `TIME_BUDGET_S` at the call); the budget's own wall-clock
bounds are in tests marked `timing`, which conftest skips while the 1-minute load passes 4 per core
(`AGENTSYNC_TIMING=1` runs them); the status progress test asserts the first tick precedes status's lines, not
the last; the friction options' speed is CPU time.

#### Kept, not built

- R127: bracketed tail words stay exact-case (written and upper case). A case-insensitive form would replace
  every lower-case use of a common word in the report's own prose (the verifier's run: "sales").
- R148: section 2 stays the whole fix-request.md and section 3 keeps its "not repeated" line. Sending the patch
  every time restores 165 KB of unredacted names a report; sending earlier parts once needs a delivery record
  the zero-IT Mac cannot have.
- R60 and R132 are contract text only: R60's mark at §16.43's git-config sentence is lane P's SUPERSEDED line
  (ffbb615), and R132's sentence is under "The bring-back sends local work once".

### 16.48 Round 3: converters and speech (2026-10-11, wave B13 round 3 lane E)

Amends §16.42 where each part says so; items are the round 2 harvest's (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`,
"B13 round 2").

#### Outlook messages and decks

**A damaged `.msg` is called damaged (R36; R13 is the same defect).** Amends §16.42 N46 and §16.28's
`quarantine_class` table. A compound file olefile cannot open, or a message whose reading raises past its
root properties stream, was `not-msg (not an Outlook message): <exception type>`: a Python class name in
the person's text, and a claim that an Outlook message with a broken chain is not one. It is now
`DAMAGED_MSG_REASON`, `damaged-msg (a compound file that cannot be read as an Outlook message)`, with no
exception type; the type goes to the `agentsync.convert.msg` log at info (`<name>: the Outlook file cannot
be read: <type>`), so the diagnostic survives. The wording says "a compound file" because a file olefile
cannot open may be a damaged `.doc` or `.xls`. `NOT_MSG_REASON` stays for the two certain cases (no
compound-file magic; no root properties stream). `setup_report.quarantine_class` maps `damaged-msg` to the
new class `damaged`, tried before `not-msg`. The emitter version is 1.0.1, which moves the action key, but
a version change reads nothing again by itself (§16.27): an unchanged file is never converted again. So
`MsgConverter.outdated` (§16.27's list) is true for a stub whose reason starts `not-msg (not an Outlook
message): `, the suffixed form only emitter 1.0.0 wrote, and the re-read pass reads each such row once (a
row settled as `: MemoryError` included). What the re-read writes has no suffix, so the rule ends there.
Until that re-read a row keeps its old reason and `not the type its name says`. Tests:
`tests/test_convert_core.py`
(`test_a_msg_stub_with_an_exception_type_in_its_reason_is_outdated_and_no_other_msg_result_is`),
`tests/test_convert_formats.py`
(`test_a_compound_file_olefile_cannot_open_is_damaged_not_a_python_class`,
`test_a_message_whose_body_cannot_be_read_is_damaged`, `test_not_a_message_is_a_settled_unreadable_stub`),
`tests/test_setup_report.py` (`test_a_reason_is_reported_as_one_of_the_fixed_classes`) and
`tests/test_cycle.py` (`test_a_msg_is_read_and_under_a_label_rule_its_page_becomes_a_stub`, the version).

**A MemoryError while reading a `.msg` fails the pass (R55).** Amends §16.42 N46. `MemoryError` subclasses
`Exception`, so the two broad `except Exception` clauses of `MsgConverter.convert` took it for a fact about
the file and settled it as an UNREADABLE stub, cached. It is now re-raised at both (the olefile open and the
read), and `convert_file` makes it FAILED, uncached, read again on a later pass, as every other converter
does (§16.42 N45). `OSError` is not carved out: olefile reports format damage as `OSError`, so it stays a
settled `damaged-msg`. The machine's `OSError`s inside a read are not: the 8-byte head read was already a
`ConversionError`, and `_PandocRunner.html_to_gfm` now raises one, `cannot write pandoc's temporary files:
<strerror>`, for an `OSError` writing the temporary copy of an HTML body (a full disk, an unwritable
temporary folder). Before, that reached the broad clause and a healthy message was cached as damaged. The
change is shared by `.eml`, Teams and `.html` pages, which made such an error FAILED already. Tests:
`tests/test_convert_formats.py` (`test_memory_error_on_a_msg_fails_the_pass_and_is_not_cached`, the open
and the read; `test_a_full_disk_while_an_html_body_is_copied_for_pandoc_fails_the_pass_and_is_not_cached`).

**A `.msg` that holds MIME text is read as an `.eml` (R87).** Amends §16.42 N46 and §16.27's `outdated`
list. Some tools save mail as RFC 822 text under a `.msg` name; `MsgConverter.convert` raised `not-msg` for
it, which the setup report calls `not the type its name says`. Now, when a file does not start with the
compound-file magic, the converter reads its first 64 KiB (`msg._HEAD_BYTES`) and `msg._rfc822_head`
looks for a header block from the very first line: header lines (`[!-9;-~]+:` then a space, a tab or the
end of the line) or folded continuations of them, ended by a blank line, with at least one of From,
Subject, Date, Message-ID or MIME-Version. When it finds one the file is converted by `EmlConverter` (the
same page an `.eml` of those bytes gets, under `msg-olefile`'s id and version); otherwise it stays
`not-msg`. That version ends `+eml-<the .eml emitter>`: the `.eml` renderer makes the page, so a new `.eml`
emitter is a new action key (a cached MIME `.msg` page is rendered again, as an `.eml` of the same bytes is)
and the page's `converter:` stamp says which `.eml` renderer made it. `_emitter` reads only the leading
three numbers, so `outdated` and the re-read floor still go by the `.msg` emitter. The gate is strict
because `EmlConverter` makes a page of almost anything: a zip or a binary file fails at its first line. The
window is 64 KiB, not the 8 KiB the finding sketched, because a message
routed through many servers can carry more than 8 KiB of headers. The label path does not change:
`MsgConverter` stays unregistered under a `[policy]` label rule (plan D8), so such a file is still the `no
converter for .msg` stub there. (**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.54 Q78:** no longer: under a rule `msg-mime` reads
such a file as an `.eml`; only a binary `.msg` is that stub.) `policy.read_labels` picks the `.eml` label reader by name only, so if MIME
`.msg` files are ever to be read under a rule it must first sniff the same block. The emitter stays 1.0.1
(one bump past main, R36's): a version change reads nothing again by itself, so `MsgConverter.outdated`
is also true for a plain `not-msg` stub from an emitter below `msg._REREAD_BELOW = "1.0.1"`, and
`MsgConverter.outdated_key` (`1.0.1<1.0.1`) puts the floor in what the cycle remembers having looked for.
Each such row is read once; one that is no message stays `not-msg` under 1.0.1 and is not read again.
Tests: `tests/test_convert_formats.py` (`test_a_msg_that_holds_mime_text_is_read_as_an_eml`, CRLF and LF;
`test_a_mime_msg_page_is_rendered_again_when_the_eml_emitter_moves`;
`test_not_a_message_is_a_settled_unreadable_stub`, a zip, binary, a late header, no mail header, a broken
block, no blank line, a blank first line; `test_under_a_label_rule_a_msg_is_the_no_converter_stub`, a MIME
`.msg` under each rule, against a control in its own cache that converts the same bytes to a page),
`tests/test_convert_core.py`
(`test_a_not_msg_stub_from_before_mime_text_was_read_is_outdated_and_one_from_now_is_not`) and
`tests/test_cycle.py` (`test_a_mime_msg_settled_as_not_msg_by_emitter_1_0_0_is_read_once_as_a_page`).

**An attached message is listed under its name (R56).** Amends §16.42 N46. §16.42 said an attached message
is listed as `<its subject>.msg`, but the row's name comes from 0x3707, else 0x3704, else 0x3001, and
Outlook sets 0x3001 on a method-5 attachment to the attached message's subject; so a file Outlook wrote
lists `Contoso kickoff`, not `Contoso kickoff.msg`. `<its subject>.msg` is only the fallback for a storage
with no name, and `attached-message-N.msg` the one after it, which §16.42 left out. The contract is
reworded to the code; the code is unchanged. Appending `.msg` to a name was not built: a name ending
`.rpmsg` would become `.rpmsg.msg` and slip past the IRM name check in `_refuse_protected`, and a suffix test by
`Path.suffix` misreads a dotted subject. Only the listed name is at stake: the type, size, sha256 and the
protection screen do not depend on it. `msg_bytes` takes `display_names` (attachment index to 0x3001).
Test: `tests/test_convert_formats.py`
(`test_an_attached_message_is_listed_under_its_display_name_else_its_subject_dot_msg`: 0x3001, the subject
fallback and the numbered one; `test_msg_headers_body_attachments_like_an_eml` keeps `Original.msg`).

**A label refusal says refused once (R35).** Every label refusal reason starts with `policy.REFUSED_PREFIX`
(`refused: `), and `Publisher._plan_stub` built the stub's summary as `<status>: <reason>`, so a labelled
file's summary read `refused: refused: sensitivity label ... is excluded by [policy]` and its body `did not
convert this source: refused: ...`. That held for all four label refusals (an excluded label, an unreadable
label, no label, an excluded item label). The prefix stays in the reason, because it is what makes a stub a
refusal: `policy.is_refusal_reason` picks the refused stub and its content-policy body, the manifest's
refusal query matches `state_reason LIKE 'refused: %'`, and the setup report classes the prefix as `label
policy`. `_plan_stub` drops it only where it renders: the summary is `refused: sensitivity label ... is
excluded by [policy]` and the body `agentsync did not convert this source: sensitivity label ... is excluded
by [policy].` The frontmatter `reason`, the planned page's refusal and `_sync/QUARANTINE.tsv` keep the
prefixed reason. Tests:
`tests/test_publish.py` (`test_label_refusal_stub_says_refused_once`, the four refusals from
`policy.label_decision` and `policy.screen_item_label`) and `tests/test_e2e.py`
(`test_label_policy_refuses_a_labelled_file_and_converts_the_rest`, which now splits the body at `did not
convert`).

**A PowerPoint template is read as a deck (R85).** Amends §7's routing and the `PptxConverter` stub of
`agentsync.convert.pptx`. A `.potx` was the `no converter for .potx` stub, kept on the reasoning (D9.b of
`docs/research/corporate-bring-back-2026-10-08.md`) that python-pptx raises on a template, so routing it
would turn a quiet stub into a failed conversion. That holds only for routing it as it is: python-pptx
refuses the template main content type (`…presentationml.template.main+xml`), not the parts. So
`PptxConverter.extensions` is `(".pptx", ".potx")`, and for a name ending `.potx` (any case) `convert`, after
`_check_ooxml_container`, copies every zip member into memory and rewrites that type to the deck's
(`…presentationml.presentation.main+xml`) in `[Content_Types].xml` only (`pptx._template_as_deck`); the
staged file is not touched. A `.potx` whose content types do not carry the template type is opened as it is,
and python-pptx's own error stands; a broken zip is still a `ConversionError`; a `.pptx` keeps the old path,
so one carrying the template type still fails. `.pptm` needs nothing: python-pptx accepts the macro main
type. The label screen is unchanged (`.potx` was already in `policy.OOXML_SUFFIXES` and
`cycle._LABEL_CAPABLE`). The emitter version stays 1.0.0: the action key is the converter's id, version,
options and the file's hash, none of which a new suffix moves, so no `.pptx` page is converted again. A
`.potx` stub is read once by the existing `no converter` re-read, as a suffix that has a converter now.
`setup_report._REFUSED_TYPE_LIST` keeps `.potx` (a stub can be older than its converter) and moves it to the
group of suffixes a converter reads. The cost is a second in-memory copy of the package while it opens;
python-pptx holds every part in memory anyway. Tests: `tests/test_convert_formats.py`
(`test_a_potx_template_is_read_as_a_deck`: lower and upper case, the staged bytes unchanged, a `.pptx`
with the template type, a `.potx` with the deck type, a broken zip), `tests/test_cycle.py`
(`test_a_potx_stub_from_before_the_deck_converter_read_templates_is_read_once_as_a_page`;
`test_the_stub_of_an_online_only_file_nothing_converts_is_published_once` now uses `Contoso Deck.pot`, a
suffix nothing claims), `tests/test_convert_core.py` (`test_default_registry_routes_exactly_the_contract_set`;
`test_a_registry_with_an_engine_keeps_the_one_without`, `.potx` among the suffixes OCR reads in) and
`tests/test_setup_report.py`
(`test_the_suffixes_and_keys_the_evidence_goes_by_are_the_codes_own`, `.potx` in `_OCR_DOCUMENTS`;
`test_a_log_line_never_names_a_file_a_converter_reads`, now 41 suffixes).

The report follows the new suffix in two more places, both pinned to the registry by those tests.
`_PATH_IN_LOG_RE` gains `potx`: a file the cycle fetches is a file its warnings can name, so a template at a
source's top is `<path>` in the report, as every claimed suffix is. `_OCR_DOCUMENTS` gains `.potx` as
`deck template`: with an engine the deck converter reads a template's pictures, so the OCR part prints
`- deck template (.potx) files with a page: ...` under the deck line, and such pages count among the files
from before OCR, as a deck's do.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.86 L5: only when a template has a page; otherwise it is named in the one `- no ... file
has a page` line.

#### The speech build and the build watcher

The speech build trusts the shell's CA (R84). `speech._build_env` is `ocr._env()` plus the non-empty values of
`speech._PROXY_VARS` and `speech._CA_VARS` (`GIT_SSL_CAINFO`, `GIT_SSL_CAPATH`, `CURL_SSL_BACKEND`). A Mac
behind TLS inspection whose shell exports one of these clones from the shell; without them SwiftPM's clone of
FluidAudio failed certificate verification and speech stayed off. `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY` and `DEVELOPER_DIR` never
reach the build, and `ocr._env()` is unchanged. Pinned by
`tests/test_speech.py::test_the_build_gives_git_the_shells_ca_and_never_turns_verification_off`.

SwiftPM's own folders live beside the build tree (R90). `speech._compile` makes one owner-only folder
`<cache>/speech/swiftpm` (`speech._SWIFTPM`) and passes `--cache-path <it>/cache --config-path <it>/config
--security-path <it>/security` after the subcommand word to both `swift package resolve` and `swift build`, with
the same values so the build reuses what resolve fetched. On Darwin SwiftPM finds its user-level folders through
Foundation, which ignores `HOME`, so before this the build wrote the real `~/Library/Caches/org.swift.swiftpm`,
`~/Library/org.swift.swiftpm/configuration` and `.../security` whatever `HOME` said (measured on Swift 6.2.4 in a
sandbox that denied those writes; `--cache-path` alone still pointed at the real configuration and security
folders). The folder is made owner-only in the build's `finally`, as the build tree is. A first build no longer
reuses a FluidAudio clone that happens to sit in the user's shared SwiftPM cache. Pinned by
`tests/test_speech.py::test_swiftpm_keeps_its_cache_config_and_security_beside_the_build_tree` and
`test_the_build_resolves_checks_the_floor_pins_the_commit_and_leaves_everything_owner_only`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.102 N18: the flags keep SwiftPM out of the real `~/Library` folders, not out of the whole
home. On Swift 6.2.4, with all three (and `--swift-sdks-path` too), both `swift package resolve` and `swift build`
re-create the account's real `~/.swiftpm/security` symlink (to `~/Library/org.swift.swiftpm/security`): SwiftPM
finds it through Foundation, so `HOME` is ignored, and no flag moves it (measured with a sandbox that kills the
process on a write there). The `~/Library` cache, configuration and security folders are not written. SwiftPM's
lock, `_Users_<login>_.swiftpm.lock`, is in `$TMPDIR`, not in the home.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.108 O69: `CFFIXED_USER_HOME`, Foundation's own home override, which N18 never tried, does
move it: the swift steps get it set to `<cache>/speech/swiftpm/home`, so the `~/.swiftpm` links and the
`<home>_.swiftpm.lock` in `$TMPDIR` are the build's own, with SwiftPM's manifest sandbox on.

Behind a proxy set only in the environment the speech build seeds SwiftPM's cache itself (R83). SwiftPM downloads
FluidAudio's one remote binary target, `NemoTextProcessing.xcframework.zip` from text-processing-rs v0.3.1, with
its own networking, which ignores the proxy variables, so such a Mac could not build the helper. `speech.NEMO_URL`
and `speech.NEMO_SHA256` are pinned next to `FLUIDAUDIO_FLOOR`, copied from FluidAudio's `Package.swift` and
`Package@swift-6.2.swift` at 04e363c (both name the same url and checksum). Before `swift package resolve`, when
one of `HTTPS_PROXY` or `ALL_PROXY` (either case, `speech._PROXIES`) is set and
`<cache>/speech/swiftpm/cache/artifacts/` holds no file for that url, `speech._seed` runs `/usr/bin/curl --fail
--location --proto =https` (a minute below 1 KB/s ends it) under `speech._build_env` plus the shell's CA bundle,
so curl reads the proxy, into a temporary file in that folder. Only a
file whose SHA-256 is `NEMO_SHA256` is renamed to `speech._artifact_name(NEMO_URL)`, the url with every character
that is not a letter or digit made `_`; that name is SwiftPM's internal cache layout, measured on Swift 6.2.4
(the user's own SwiftPM cache holds the zip under that name, and its SHA-256 is the pinned checksum). Any failure
removes the temporary file and SwiftPM downloads as before; SwiftPM checks the checksum again either way. The
fetch counts against the build's twenty minutes. Measured 2026-10-11, Swift 6.2.4: with the seeded file in a
fresh `--cache-path` and `HTTPS_PROXY` pointing at a closed port, `swift package --cache-path ... --config-path
... --security-path ... resolve` printed "Fetched ... from cache" and exited 0. A SwiftPM mirror is not used: it
rewrites urls and does not change the route. curl verifies TLS with its own trust: of `speech._CA_VARS` it reads
`CURL_SSL_BACKEND` (`secure-transport` trusts the keychain), not `GIT_SSL_*`, and it reads `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`,
`SSL_CERT_FILE` and `SSL_CERT_DIR`, which it alone gets (below). Spec correction: the
verifier's fix put `--cache-path` at `<agentsync cache>/speech/swiftpm`; the build uses R90's one folder, whose
`cache/` subfolder is the cache path. Pinned by
`tests/test_speech.py::test_behind_a_proxy_the_build_seeds_swiftpms_cache_with_the_checked_artifact`,
`test_a_wrong_or_failed_fetch_leaves_nothing_and_swiftpm_downloads_as_before`,
`test_without_a_proxy_the_build_fetches_nothing_itself` and
`test_the_seeded_artifact_is_the_one_the_pinned_fluidaudio_names` (a new `FLUIDAUDIO_PIN` is a KeyError there
until its manifest is read again).

The seed's curl trusts what the shell's curl trusts, fetches only behind an https proxy, and leaves no partial
file behind (R84, R83, review of both). `/usr/bin/curl` 8.7.1 reads `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `SSL_CERT_FILE` and
`SSL_CERT_DIR` (measured 2026-10-11 under `env -i`: the first two at an empty file failed with exit 77, "error
setting certificate verify locations", and `SSL_CERT_DIR` at a missing folder became its CApath), and those are
the usual way a shell behind TLS inspection trusts the inspecting CA. Without them the seed's curl failed
verification where the shell's worked, and SwiftPM's direct download failed after it, so the R83 fetch did not
reach the Mac it is for. The curl step alone now runs in `speech._build_env()` plus their non-empty values
(`speech._CURL_CA_VARS`, through `_step`'s `env`); `swift` and `git` still do not get them, since Xcode's git
ignores them. The fetch's trigger is `speech._PROXIES`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `ALL_PROXY` in either case: curl and git
both ignore `HTTP_PROXY` and `http_proxy` for an https url (measured: either at a closed port still fetched
https://github.com directly, while `HTTPS_PROXY` or `ALL_PROXY` there failed to connect), so a shell with only
`HTTP_PROXY` made a direct 87 MB fetch before SwiftPM's own. The build still passes `HTTP_PROXY` to `swift` and
`git` (`speech._PROXY_VARS`). An install stopped by SIGTERM or SIGKILL mid-fetch never runs the seed's `finally`,
and each such run left another random `.seed-*` file of up to 87 MB in the artifacts folder that nothing
removed; `speech._seed` now first removes every `.seed-*` file there, whether or not it then fetches. Two builds
at once would at worst remove each other's temporary file, and that fetch then falls through to SwiftPM's own
download. Pinned by
`tests/test_speech.py::test_the_seeds_curl_trusts_the_shells_ca_and_swiftpm_and_git_never_see_curls_variables`,
`test_without_a_proxy_the_build_fetches_nothing_itself` (its `HTTP_PROXY` and `http_proxy` cases) and
`test_a_fetch_cut_off_mid_way_leaves_no_temporary_file_past_the_next_build`.

A shell that trusts the inspecting CA through git alone, `GIT_SSL_CAINFO`, cloned FluidAudio but fetched the
seed with curl's own bundle and failed verification, since curl ignores `GIT_SSL_*` (R84, R83, lead's
follow-on). The seed's curl now runs in `speech._curl_env()`: the above, plus that file as `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`
when the shell sets neither `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` nor `SSL_CERT_FILE`, so the seed trusts what step 1's git trusts
(measured 2026-10-12 with `/usr/bin/curl` 8.7.1: `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` at an empty file exits 77, at
`/etc/ssl/cert.pem` it fetches). `GIT_SSL_CAPATH` is not mapped: `SSL_CERT_DIR` beside an unusable bundle still
exited 77 in the same measurement. `swift` and `git` never get `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`. Pinned by
`tests/test_speech.py::test_a_ca_only_git_trusts_is_the_seeds_curl_bundle_unless_curl_has_its_own`.

A Ctrl-C while Popen starts a build tool still stops the tool (R89). `ocr._run_build`'s `finally` treated "no
Popen object" as "the tool ended", so a KeyboardInterrupt that landed after the fork but before `proc` was set
(mainly the error-pipe read inside `Popen._execute_child`) told the watcher "done", and the tool ran on to its
end in the watcher's group, which the terminal's Ctrl-C never reaches. Now, with no Popen object, the tool
counts as ended only when nothing is in flight or the exception is OSError (exec failed; Popen has already
reaped the child). Otherwise the watcher is not told "done", so its end-of-input path stops the group, and
`_run_build` also sends `os.killpg(watcher.pid, SIGINT)` at once, so the group is signalled at once rather than
when the watcher wakes, and even while a just-forked child still holds the pipe's write end (it closes its copy
only in `close_fds`, just before the exec). No test pins that direct signal: with it made a no-op, the test
below still passes, through the watcher's end-of-input stop. Only the watcher, which ignores SIGINT, and perhaps
the tool are in that group. One race remains, and it is wider than the join alone: a signal that reaches the
child before it execs the tool is lost. The child joins the group only after the fork, and until the exec it
keeps CPython's C SIGINT handler (on the fork path `_posixsubprocess` restores only SIGPIPE, SIGXFZ and
SIGXFSZ), which records the signal for Python code the child never runs again. Both the direct `killpg` and the
watcher's end-of-input stop can land in that window. Measured by the round 3 review of the R89 fix, with SIGINT sent
to the main thread at a random point 0-4 ms into the tool's Popen: 6 of 115 interrupts that landed mid-Popen
still let the tool finish unwatched, and 17 of 103 with 8,000 extra open file descriptors, which lengthen
`close_fds` after the join, so the loss is after the join, not before it. Not built: a second group SIGINT a
moment later (a watcher that runs `kill -INT 0; sleep 1; kill -INT 0`), which would catch a tool that execed
after the first; unmeasured. The docstring's "a Ctrl-C in the milliseconds Popen takes still leaves it
unwatched" is narrowed to that race, about 1 in 20 interrupts that land while Popen runs.
Pinned by `tests/test_ocr.py::test_a_ctrl_c_while_popen_starts_the_tool_still_stops_it`, which wraps
`subprocess.Popen._execute_child` to raise KeyboardInterrupt after the real call for the tool's argv only. Its
stub tool, which sets its own SIGINT handler as swiftc does, writes `got-int`; before the fix it wrote
`finished-unwatched`.

Ctrl-Z and a tool that ignores SIGINT stay as they are (R130, no code). A Ctrl-Z stops install.sh and Python,
not the tool, which is not in the terminal's foreground group and keeps compiling. Nothing goes wrong as a
result: the tool's input is /dev/null and its output goes to files, and on resume `Popen.wait` reaps a tool that
ended during the pause before it checks the deadline. A tool that ignores SIGINT outlives the group stop,
including one that inherited the ignore from a non-interactive shell's `cmd &` (Popen restores only SIGPIPE,
SIGXFZ and SIGXFSZ). Measured: swiftc and SwiftPM set their own SIGINT handling, so an inherited ignore does not
keep them running; the stub tool in the R89 test sets its handler for the same reason, since a `/bin/sh` tool
cannot trap a signal that was ignored when it started. Not built: having Python catch SIGTSTP and stop the
tool's group. If Python were killed while the tool was stopped, the watcher's SIGINT would stay pending, so
the tool and its compilers would stay stopped indefinitely. That is a worse leak than today's. The `_run_build`
docstring now states both behaviors and that neither applies to swiftc or SwiftPM.

A failed speech build is tried again on every install.sh run, as before (R140, no code). The retry is
incremental, not in full, and this amends §16.43's step-2 bullet, which said "in full": `speech._compile` keeps
`<folder>/build`, so a retry reuses SwiftPM's checkout and build products and runs resolve and build again, up
to 20 minutes (`speech._BUILD_TIMEOUT_S`) a run. That holds after a change to the speech package too: the build
tree is shared across helper hashes, and `ocr._prune` removes only `<prefix>-*` and `.build-*` entries. Not built: a
skip marker. The `<helper>.failed` marker is read only by `probe`, and the frozen CLI has no command to clear
a marker. A one-off failure (a network drop during resolve, a signal, a timeout) would then leave speech unbuilt
for good, and the messages "scripts/install.sh tries the build again on its next run" and "scripts/install.sh
rebuilds it" would no longer be true. What a build that times out costs per run is unmeasured. A later change
keeps retry as the default and never blocks a rebuild because of what an earlier run left behind.
**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.61 F101 (by §16.51 Q71):** the freeze no longer rules out a clear command (§16.51
Q71 built a hidden one, pinned in §16.10's Hidden line), so "the frozen CLI has no command to clear a marker" is no
longer a reason. The decision stands without it. With a marker, a one-off failure (a network drop, a signal, a
timeout) would leave speech unbuilt until someone ran that command. Today's retry needs nothing from anyone, and the
two install.sh messages ("tries the build again on its next run", "rebuilds it") stay true.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.138 V68: both messages now name the installer by its path,
`~/src/agent-context-sync/scripts/install.sh` (`skill.INSTALL_SH`), and keep these words after it.

#### PDF pictures and diagrams

**A picture drawn turned on purpose is read as its lines (R82; amends §16.42 "The other way round").**
With an engine, `PdfConverter` reads every picture the way up the page shows it first, as §16.42 says. A
picture shown a quarter turn from its stored pixels turned by the page's `/Rotate` alone (its own matrix,
or a form around it, turns it a quarter: `pdf._other_way`) has that other way to read it. When the
helper's lines for such a picture run down (`image._direction`: most of the lines' characters are in lines
whose box is more than 1.5 times higher than wide, measured in pixels, the box's width times the image's
width against its height times the image's height, never in the fractions the helper gives), it is read
once more the other way, after every other picture (`pdf._read_other_way`). That reading is kept when its
lines run across by the same measure (more than 1.5 times wider than high); a tie, no lines, lines that run
down again, or a helper failure on it keep the first reading. The lines measured are those the reading
order keeps (`ocr._kept` drops one or two characters read under confidence 0.35), and under 8 characters
of them, less whitespace, decide neither way (`image._DIRECTION_MIN_CHARS`): one glyph's box is taller
than wide, and the helper finds stray marks in pictures with no text (measured with the real helper: a dot
at confidence 1.0 in a turned chart of bars, five digits at 0.3 in a wallpaper). So a picture whose first
reading runs across, holds no text, or holds only such marks (a turned phone photo) costs one helper read,
as before. The picture counts once toward
`ocr_max_pictures`; its second reading is charged its pixels again against `ocr_picture_pixels` (the first
reading stands when they would pass it) and shares the document's OCR time: none is started once that
time is over. `image._PictureText` gains `down`, the digests whose lines run down; the other converters do
not read it. A picture drawn upright on a page whose `/Rotate` alone turns it has no other way here (its
stored pixels turned by the page are the pixels already read) and is read as the page shows it.
`ocr_pdf_rules` is 4; a page already published keeps its reading until its file changes, as with each
earlier bump. Measured with the real helper on an Apple silicon Mac: a table of three rows stored upright
and drawn turned a quarter left read as one line before and as its three rows now.

Tests: `tests/test_convert_formats.py`
(`test_a_picture_stored_upright_and_drawn_turned_is_read_as_its_separate_lines`,
`test_a_picture_stored_on_its_side_and_drawn_upright_is_still_read_once_as_shown`,
`test_a_turned_picture_keeps_its_first_reading_unless_the_other_one_runs_across`, whose "no text" case is
a turned photo that costs exactly one helper read, `test_a_turned_photo_with_stray_marks_costs_one_read`,
`test_a_second_reading_counts_once_against_the_pictures_read`,
`test_a_second_reading_is_charged_to_the_pixel_budget_and_the_time`,
`test_a_picture_only_its_page_turns_is_not_read_twice`, `test_which_way_lines_run_is_measured_in_pixels`,
and `ocr_pdf_rules` 4 in `test_pdf_version_and_options_change_only_with_an_engine`) and `tests/test_ocr.py`
(`test_the_real_helper_reads_a_pdf_picture_stored_upright_and_drawn_turned_as_its_separate_lines`; §16.42's
`test_the_real_helper_reads_a_pdf_picture_stored_on_its_side_the_way_up_the_page_shows_it` still passes).

**A Visio group nested any depth is read (R86, part a).** `diagram._vsdx_shapes` walks a page's shapes with
a stack instead of by recursion: each shape, then its group's members (pushed last first, so they come off
in the file's order), then what follows the group, the order §16.42 "Page" gives. Groups nested past
Python's recursion limit (about 1000) failed as `conversion failed: corrupt Visio package: RecursionError:
…`, though the package was sound; now they convert, so no "nested too deep" wording is needed. Every
drawing that converted before reads exactly as it did and a failed conversion is never cached, so the
converter's version stays `1.0.0+python-<x.y.z>`. A drawing that failed this way keeps its stub until its
file changes: a failed conversion is not retried (§16.28 "The run record"), and `diagram-stdlib` has no
`outdated` rule.

Amended 2026-10-19, §16.138 V74 (by §16.132 U3, §16.138 V65): a failed conversion is now tried again
(`_retries`) in up to 2 later cycles while its row is ERROR, and the stub of one a build before U3 had settled is
given the ERROR verdict once after the upgrade (`Manifest.retry_settled_failures`). So a drawing that failed this
way is converted again in the first syncs after the upgrade, which part a's stack walk reads; one that fails every
time keeps its stub until its file changes. `diagram-stdlib` still has no `outdated` rule.

Tests: `tests/test_convert_formats.py` (`test_a_visio_group_nested_thousands_deep_is_read_in_the_files_order`,
groups 5000 deep with shapes before, inside and after each; §16.42's
`test_a_visio_drawing_is_its_shape_text_and_connections_per_page` still passes).

**A macro-enabled Visio drawing is read like a `.vsdx` (R86, part c; amends §7's routing, §16.6's
label-capable list and §16.42 "Diagrams: draw.io and Visio").** A `.vsdm` is the `.vsdx` package plus a
macro project (`visio/vbaProject.bin`). It lands as one change, because routing it alone would convert a
drawing the label policy excludes and would read it as draw.io XML: `.vsdm` joins `policy.OOXML_SUFFIXES`
(so `policy.screen_file` screens it as it does a `.vsdx`: an excluded label refuses it, `refuse_unlabelled`
refuses an unlabelled one, a name whose bytes are not a ZIP is `not-ooxml`) and through it
`cycle._LABEL_CAPABLE` (a policy change re-screens it); `DiagramConverter.extensions` is
`(".drawio", ".vsdx", ".vsdm")` and `convert()` reads a name ending `.vsdx` or `.vsdm` as Visio;
`setup_report._PATH_IN_LOG_RE` matches `vsd[xm]?`. Only the parts a `.vsdx` has are read (`pages.xml`, its
relationships and the pages, and the label parts): `vbaProject.bin` is never opened and no macro runs.
`canonical.OOXML_SUFFIXES` is not changed. A `no converter for .vsdm` stub becomes a page through the
re-read pass, as §16.42 "Old stubs" says of `.vsdx`. No page any other file had changes, so the
converter's version stays `1.0.0+python-<x.y.z>`.

Tests: `tests/test_convert_formats.py`
(`test_a_macro_enabled_visio_drawing_is_read_like_a_vsdx_and_its_macros_never_opened`), `tests/test_policy.py`
(`test_a_visio_drawing_is_screened_for_labels_like_any_office_file`, now for `.vsdx` and `.vsdm`, with the
not-a-zip refusal and `cycle._LABEL_CAPABLE`), `tests/test_convert_core.py`
(`test_default_registry_routes_exactly_the_contract_set`) and `tests/test_setup_report.py`
(`test_a_log_line_never_names_a_file_a_converter_reads`, 40 suffixes; **amended 2026-10-12, §16.55:** 41 since
`.potx`, R85 above).

**A Visio shape without text of its own shows its master's (R86, part b; amends §16.42 "Diagrams: draw.io
and Visio", "Page").** A shape dropped from a stencil often carries no `<Text>` element: it shows the text of
the master shape it is an instance of, and was missing from the page. Now a shape with no `<Text>` takes that
text. The master is found through `visio/masters/masters.xml` (a `Master` element's `ID` and its `Rel`) and
`visio/masters/_rels/masters.xml.rels` (a target relative to `visio/masters/` or absolute, as for pages).
A shape with a `Master` attribute is an instance: it takes the text of the master's top-level shape when the
master has exactly one (a master of several is instanced as a group whose members name theirs), or of the
shape its own `MasterShape` names. A member inside an instance, at any depth, takes the text of the shape its
`MasterShape` names in the nearest enclosing instance's master; a member with no `MasterShape` (added to the
instance on the page) and a shape naming an unknown master or master shape show nothing. Its own `<Text>`
always wins, and an empty `<Text/>` stays empty: the master's text is never shown over it. A connector's end
is named by the text its shape shows, master text included. The master parts are read only when a shape
needs one (a drawing whose shapes all carry their own text never opens them), each once, and all through
`diagram._part`: they count against the 32 MiB part cap and the 128 MiB total like a page, and past either
the file is a `conversion failed: diagram … too large` stub. A malformed master list, its relationships or a
master is `conversion failed: <the master list | the master list's relationships | a master> is not
well-formed XML: …`, naming no master and quoting nothing of the file. The converter's version is
`1.1.0+python-<x.y.z>`, so a cached reading is not reused; a page already published keeps its reading until
its file changes.

Tests: `tests/test_convert_formats.py` (`test_a_visio_shape_without_text_shows_its_masters_text`, an
instance, an empty `<Text/>`, own text, a group instance's members by `MasterShape`, a master of two
top-level shapes, an unknown master and a connector named by master text;
`test_a_visio_master_is_read_only_when_needed_and_within_the_caps`) and `tests/test_cycle.py`
(`test_a_diagram_stub_from_before_its_converter_is_read_once_as_a_page`, the version read from the module).

**A draw.io placeholder shows its value (R86, part d; amends §16.42 "Diagrams: draw.io and Visio",
"draw.io").** A draw.io object can show its data in its label: `<object label="Owner: %owner%"
owner="Contoso Ops" placeholders="1">` shows `Owner: Contoso Ops`, and was read as `Owner: %owner%`. The
rules are draw.io's own (`Graph.getLabel` and `Graph.replacePlaceholders` in its `Graph.js`), measured from
its source:

- Only an `object` or `UserObject` wrapper with `placeholders="1"` and no `placeholder` attribute is filled
  in; without it (or with `placeholders="0"`) every `%…%` stays as written. A bare `mxCell` holds no data,
  so its `value` is never filled in, whatever attributes it carries.
- A wrapper with `placeholders="1"` and `placeholder="<name>"` does not show its label at all
  (`Graph.convertValueToString`): it shows the attribute `<name>` of itself or of the nearest object around
  it that has one (an empty one included), as written and not filled in, or nothing when none has it, and
  an HTML label (`html=1`) then has its tags read as usual. Without `placeholders="1"` the `placeholder`
  attribute does nothing.
- A placeholder is draw.io's pattern `%(date\{.*\}|[^%{}"'=;]+)%`. Its name is looked up in the object's
  own attributes, then in each object around it in turn (its container, its layer, the diagram's root
  object `id="0"`, by `parent`), the nearest that has the attribute giving the value (an empty one
  included). `%id%` is the cell's id.
- Left as written: draw.io's own variables (`%page%`, `%pagenumber%`, `%pagecount%`, `%date%`, `%time%`,
  `%timestamp%`, `%date{…}%`, `%filename%` and the like, which depend on when and where draw.io shows the
  page), a shape's `%width%` and `%height%` and an edge's `%length%` (measured from the drawing),
  `%label%`, `%tooltip%`, and any name nothing defines.
- A `%` just before a placeholder keeps it: `%%owner%` shows `%owner%`. That is the only escape: `%%`
  elsewhere stays `%%` (`50%% done` is not a placeholder), as in draw.io. The spec's "`%%` is a literal
  percent" was corrected to this by reading draw.io's source.
- It is done on the label as written, before an HTML label (`html=1`) has its tags and entities read, so
  an expanded value is read like the rest of the label (`A &amp; B` reads `A & B`, a `<br>` in a value is
  a line break); a plain label keeps the value as it is.
- Edges are filled in like shapes, and an edge's ends are named by the filled-in text.

Both steps are linear in the file: draw.io's pattern ends a `%date{` at the last `}%` on its line, which is
found once a line rather than once for every `%date{` (the pattern itself took about 100 seconds over
100,000 unclosed `%date{`), and the cells are walked once as their `parent` tree, each attribute name keeping
the values of the objects around the cell, so a lookup costs the same however deep the cell is (walking
to the root for each placeholder did not finish in 5 minutes for 20,000 nested containers). A cell in a
`parent` loop sees only its own attributes. A label without `placeholders="1"` reads exactly as before, but
a drawing with one now reads differently, so the converter's version is `1.2.0+python-<x.y.z>` and a cached
reading is not reused; a page already published keeps its reading until its file changes.

Tests: `tests/test_convert_formats.py` (`test_a_drawio_placeholder_is_expanded_as_draw_io_shows_it`: filled
in, no `placeholders`, `placeholders="0"`, a `placeholder` attribute, the built-ins, the geometry names, an
unknown and an empty value, the `%` escape, `%id%`, an HTML label and a plain one;
`test_a_drawio_placeholder_is_found_on_the_object_then_its_containers`, a container, a layer, the root, an
edge and a bare `mxCell`; `test_a_drawio_placeholder_attribute_shows_that_attribute_instead_of_the_label`,
the attribute found on a container, a value not filled in, a name none has, an own empty value, the
attribute without `placeholders="1"` and an HTML value; `test_a_drawio_placeholder_label_is_read_in_linear_time`;
`test_a_drawio_placeholder_in_a_deep_container_is_looked_up_once`; §16.42's
`test_a_drawio_diagram_is_its_shape_text_and_connections_per_page` still passes).

### 16.49 Round 3: setup prompt v12 and docs (2026-10-11, wave B13 round 3 lane P)

The B13 round 2 items of lane P (specs `round2/items/R<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built). Ten need
prompt text, so the prompt is **setup prompt v12**: `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, `PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's `prompt
v12` and `setup-prompt-compat 12`, the issue form's placeholder and the block's digest move together; a saved v11
copy is stopped at step 1 like every older copy. v12 moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry and is read
with v7's rules. Every other lane of round 3 said it had no prompt words, so v12 carries only these.

**Step 1's git stop** (R22, R29, R32). It read "show me its error (a corporate proxy may need HTTPS_PROXY set)
and go to step 3's report", and nothing told the person what to do once git works. It now reads: show me its
error and tell me "Once git can reach GitHub from a terminal (a corporate proxy may need HTTPS_PROXY set there;
if the error names a proxy, the one in git's own settings, which git config --get http.proxy prints, comes
before HTTPS_PROXY and may point at a network this Mac is not on), start a new session from that terminal and
paste this prompt again", and go to step 3's report. The hint is inside the quoted words, so it reaches the
person. **Amended (2026-10-12, §16.55 Q25):** the parenthetical is now one unconditional sentence, "a corporate
proxy may need HTTPS_PROXY set there; a proxy in git's own settings, which git config --get http.proxy prints,
wins over HTTPS_PROXY, so if git's error names a host other than github.com, check that setting: it may point at
a network this Mac is not on".
- A new session, not the same one: HTTPS_PROXY must be in the environment of the shell the agent runs, and the
  rules forbid editing the shell profile.
- git's `http.proxy` wins over the environment (measured with both set: git used the config value). The setting
  is named for the agent to read, written without backticks so it is no command the block runs; nothing tells
  the agent to change `~/.gitconfig`.
- No report-side `NEXT:` was added: a failed clone has no installer and no report, and after a failed pull the
  report is the old checkout's code.
- "Before going to the report from either of these two stops" followed three cases, the middle one a recovery;
  it now names "the Xcode stop or the other-git-failure stop above".
  **Amended 2026-10-14, §16.85 K65 (by §16.76 J19):** since v17 it names three stops, "the Xcode stop, the
  not-a-checkout stop or the other-git-failure stop above", and logs the error if
  ~/src/agent-context-sync/scripts/install.sh exists, the installer, not the folder, being the condition.

**The step 1 error names the prompt and the agent** (R25). That line is the only one a session writes when step 1
stops before `--log-start`, so its attempt had no header and the Summary, the friction log section and the issue
link said `not stated`. Step 1 now has the line's what-text start "with prompt v12, <agent> and a colon (the same
words as in step 1's command; write no colon inside <agent>)": no quotes, which the friction rule would have the
agent write as `’`, and the block names `--log-start` once, in the command. `parse_friction` reads that prefix
(`_STEP1_STATED_RE`: case-insensitive, any of ` ,:;-` after the number as `--log-start` accepts, quotes around
it tolerated, the agent up to 100 characters and ending at its first colon) only on the
step 1 error that starts a header-less attempt (more than 10 minutes after a finished attempt's end line), puts it
in `Attempt.stated`, and keeps the rest as the line's what-text. `Attempt.said(key)` reads the header first, then
`stated`; `Attempt.version`, `_prompt_version`, the Summary's `agent:` and `prompt:` (marked `(from the step 1
error line)`), the friction section's attempt line, `_turns_line`'s approvals test and `_issue_link` all read
through it. An attempt with a header, or a late line that stays in its attempt, is never read that way, and a line
without the words reads `not stated` as before. Tests: `tests/test_setup_report.py`
(`test_a_header_less_step_1_error_states_its_prompt_and_agent`), `tests/test_deploy_pack.py`
(`test_readme_step1_is_one_command`: the prompt's words are the ones the regex reads).

**Step 2** (R9, R40). "[warn] or WAITING ON YOU: lines about them may predate this session" covered only a Mac
that already runs agentsync, while a new Mac's first sync prints one too (an empty cloud folder, which names a
`sources.toml` edit). Now: "Any [warn] or WAITING ON YOU: line this command prints is mine (on such a Mac it may
predate this session): show it to me and do not do what it says, neither its commands nor its sources.toml
edits." After "run the same command again": "If another sync is running when it reinstalls, it says so and waits
for that sync to end, up to 2 minutes, printing "still running" lines, and then goes on even if that sync has not
ended; that is expected, not a deviation: do not log it." The 2 minutes is install.sh's `REINSTALL_WAIT` default,
which the test reads. **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G37:** since v15 it goes on "its first sync then says
"another sync is still running" and waits for that sync again, up to 10 more minutes, and is skipped ("skipped,
lock busy") if it is still running then. Both waits and that skip are expected, not deviations: do not log
them."
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J66 (by §16.72 H66):** since v16 that first-sync wait is its own sentence, for every run, a
re-run at the same commit included ("If another sync is running when its first sync starts ..., it says "another
sync is still running" and waits for it, up to 10 minutes"), no longer "again, up to 10 more minutes".

**Step 3's report is defined once** (R31): "Step 3's report, where every "go to step 3's report" in this prompt
lands, has two parts, in this order. First, add a "## Not used" section ...; skip this part if
~/agent-context/setup does not exist. Then the report, always, ...". The folder is missing only before step 1's
`--log-start` ran on a new Mac, which has no report either. **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G25:** since v15 "Then the
report, even after a failure (except in the three cases below)".

**The finish** (R11, R30): "the folders this Mac syncs, as full paths (those step 1's list marked [synced] and
those step 2 added; if step 1 stopped before its list, the kind = "local" sources in
~/agent-context/sources.toml that are not paused or retired; never the inbox or another kind = "inbox" folder),
saying which ones this session added, or "none: this Mac syncs no folder" (if setup stopped before step 2, say
at which step)". The folders are
the ones install.sh counts (`synced_folders`: live `kind = "local"` sources), the same N step 1 and step 2 print.
"Every source folder in sources.toml" was not used: it would add the inbox and the person's own inbox folders.
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J66 (by §16.72 H9):** since v16 the finish reads "the kind = "local" sources in
~/agent-context/sources.toml that are not paused or retired, read after step 2 or, if setup stopped before step 2,
as they are (never the inbox or another kind = "inbox" folder), saying which of them this session added: those for
which a run of step 2 this session printed an "added source" line": step 1's `[synced]` marks no longer decide it, so
a list that marked nothing gives no false "none" (§16.72 calls this paragraph §16.36's and §16.43's finish).
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.94 M28: since v20 a sources.toml that does not load is "unknown", not "none".

**Step 1's exception** (R41): "say in your final message that I gave no answer, so no folder was added" (§16.29's
block carries a dated line).

**Not built: the finish's NEXT wording and "(WAITING ON YOU above)"** (R133, keep). "The last command's NEXT"
would read "none" after a failure: the last command before the report is then `install.sh --log`, which prints no
NEXT. The current wording shows the previous command's NEXT, where a re-run starts. The "above" mismatch shows only
when the installer exited 0 and the loop's sync then printed no NEXT; it loses nothing.
**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.51 Q74:** the second half is built: rule 5 says `(see the WAITING ON YOU lines)`,
true above or below.

**Lock holder with no body** (R62; amends §16.39 N24 and §9 step 2 by dated lines). One constant names an empty
body in `LockHeldError.who`, on the stderr line and in doctor; doctor adds `(a cycle is running)` only for a held
lock with a body. Tests: `tests/test_ops_lock.py` (`test_a_holder_with_no_lock_body_yet_is_named_as_unidentified`),
`tests/test_ops_doctor.py` (`test_lock_states`).
**Amended (2026-10-12, §16.45 R50/R80):** the text is now `EMPTY_BODY_HOLDER`'s (§9 step 2), and doctor adds
`(a cycle is running)` only when the body parses as a cycle's record (`LockInfo.parse`); a non-empty body that does
not parse reads `held by <desc>` with no suffix and no sidecar read. Test: `tests/test_ops_doctor.py`
(`test_lock_held_with_an_empty_body_names_no_cycle`).

**Download hosts, checked weekly** (R119). `scripts/download_hosts.py` follows the redirect chains of the speech
build's release file, uv's installer, uv itself (the installer's default `ARTIFACT_DOWNLOAD_URLS`), the Python
3.11 uv installs and PyPI with curl HEAD requests, one hop at a time, and fails when the release file ends off the
host it-request.md names for release files or any hop passes a host the "Installation downloads" bullet does not
name. A server that refuses HEAD is asked for one byte; a chain curl cannot follow is a problem line with curl's
message, and the other chains are still checked. `.github/workflows/download-hosts.yml` runs it weekly and on `workflow_dispatch`, never on a push; it is
outside the gate (CLAUDE.md says why). Test: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py`
(`test_a_weekly_check_follows_the_download_hosts_the_it_request_names`, offline).

**The Python report's two passes** (R43). §16.41 and the `Redactor` sketch said the Python report replaces in a
single pass; its Summary item lines are redacted twice (before they are cut, so a value split at the cut still
matches, then with the whole report). Both carry a dated line that says so and that §16.46 R69 holds a
placeholder whole on the second pass. The inner pass in `_item_line` stays: cutting first could leave a fragment
the whole-report pass no longer knows.

**Docs** (R61, R63, R65, R66, R116): dated markers in §16.36, §16.37 and §16.43 and the corrected H8 sum (37
minutes); data-governance.md covers an Outlook `.msg` under a label rule; setup-feedback.md's friction.md row shows
the current version (`test_setup_feedback_shows_the_current_prompt_version`).

**Not built: placeholder numbers that skip** (R138, keep). Compacting `<kind-N>` numbers by order of appearance
would make a value's number depend on which other values a report mentions, a new cause of renumbering in every
report, and the issue link, the Redaction legend and `fix-request.md` would no longer match the report text. N44's
role-first naming already covers renumbering whatever its cause.

### 16.50 Round 4: purge (2026-10-12, wave B13 round 4 lane A)

Round 4 lane A of B13 (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 4"): the purge queue's words, preview and cost,
the doctor's retirement advice, and two test gaps. Each entry names the finding it builds.

**Q42: the shared-content advice names the retirement the cycle accepts** (`agentsync.ops.doctor`). §16.45 R144's
info line told a person that removing the copying source from sources.toml retires its pages; the next sync refuses
that instead (exit 78, `Cycle._refuse_vanished_sources`: retirement is explicit). The line now ends `if one source
copies the other, set state = "retired" in its [[source]] block in sources.toml (its pages become tombstones in one
labelled commit)`, the refusal's own words, and R144 carries a dated amendment. Tests: `tests/test_ops_doctor.py`
(`test_two_sources_holding_the_same_files_is_an_info_line` now pins the end of the line).

**Q43: telling kept purges apart costs rows + entries** (`agentsync.governance`). `partition_purges` read the
manifest once but resolved each queued entry over every row (`_kept_why` -> `_resolve_read`), and status (three
calls), doctor, the loop and STATE.md on every cycle call it: 1,000 queued upstream deletions over 10,000 rows took
about 15 s a call, and the cycle queues one per confirmed deletion, so a moved folder fills the queue. An entry of
the cycle's shape (`upstream-deleted`, a source id and a stable id, no docs glob) is now judged by lookup: the rows
`_resolve_read` selects for that shape are the queued id and the id it is an alias of, nothing else
(`_kept_listed`), and both paths word the note through one formatter (`_kept_note`). Any other shape still resolves,
with each row's state built once. `run_purge_queue` keeps its fresh read per entry: each purge it runs changes the
manifest. Tests: `tests/test_governance.py`
(`test_partition_purges_judges_a_cycle_entry_by_lookup_as_kept_why_does`, entry by entry against `_kept_why` over
re-keyed, tombstoned, directory, second-source, dataless, quarantined and refused rows;
`test_partition_purges_costs_rows_plus_entries`).

**Q45, Q47: a kept queued purge says it was not run and what runs it** (`agentsync.governance`, `agentsync.cli`).
`KEPT_PURGES` (loop note, status, doctor info line, STATE.md) said the kept entries "run on their own once the file
is gone", and `_kept_why`'s note said the entry "runs once the file is gone again"; nothing runs them, the history
rewrite runs only from `agentsync purge --queue`, and once the file is gone the entry is a queued purge again and the
wait returns. `KEPT_PURGES` is now ``upstream deletion(s) stay queued while their file is listed again; once the
file is gone, they wait for `agentsync purge --queue` like any queued purge`` and the note ends ``an upstream
deletion is not run against a listed file; a later `purge --queue` runs it once the file is gone`` (§16.38's
`_kept_why` text and §16.44's `KEPT_PURGES` text carry dated amendments; the §16 stub carries the new constant).
`_print_purge` printed a report the queue did not run (a kept upstream deletion, a held or failed entry: `not_run`
set) as `NOT VERIFIED · 0 item(s) · ... · remote: not run`, which reads as a purge that ran and left something, and
under `--dry-run` as `dry run · ... would be removed`. It now prints `purge <selector> (<reason>): not run` and the
entry's `note:` lines, in both modes; exit codes, counts and the last line are unchanged, and a purge that ran and
left something still prints NOT VERIFIED. Tests: `tests/test_governance.py`
(`test_kept_purges_note_names_the_run_that_clears_them`,
`test_purge_queue_keeps_an_upstream_deletion_of_a_file_that_is_listed_again`), `tests/test_cli.py`
(`test_purge_queue_skips_a_held_source_and_keeps_it_queued`,
`test_purge_queue_keeps_an_upstream_deletion_of_a_live_file_and_does_not_count_it_as_run`).

**Q87: a dataclass stub lists the code's fields** (`docs/design/CONTRACTS.md`, `tests/test_contracts.py`). The
contract test checked that each public name appears somewhere, not a stub's fields, so `PurgeReport` lacked
`not_run` from §16.38 until §16.44 R64, and two stubs were still short: `Suppressions` of `paths` and `canonical`
(added in prose, §16.12), and `GovernanceConfig` of `archive` (added by a partial block, §16.18). Both stubs now carry
those fields. The first stub of each class in the python blocks under a ``#### `agentsync.<mod>` `` header must list
`dataclasses.fields()` of the class, in order; a later partial block that repeats a class to add a field is not the
stub. There is no allowlist: a field added in code is added to its stub in the same commit. Tests:
`tests/test_contracts.py::test_dataclass_stubs_list_the_code_fields`.

**Q61: the purge queue preview folds a covered entry as the run does** (`agentsync.governance`). `run_purge_queue`
applied `_covers` only when not a dry run, so a preview of a label escalation then an erasure request for one file
previewed two purges (`2 queued purge(s) previewed`) where the run runs one (`1 queued purge(s) run`), against
§16.45 R52's "the same count the real run prints". In a dry run each previewed purge now folds every later entry it
covers into its report with the note `would also do the queued <reason> purge of the same item: the run takes it off
the queue`, and the loop skips those entries, so the CLI's previewed count equals the run's. It writes no audit line
and no queue file, and the queue stays whole. Only the run's "later entry" half applies: a preview presumes each
purge verifies, and the run's "earlier entry" half exists only for an earlier purge that failed. A covering purge
that fails in the real run leaves the later entry to run itself, which a preview cannot know; every preview makes
that presumption. Tests: `tests/test_cli.py::test_purge_queue_preview_counts_a_covered_entry_as_the_run_does`.

**Q83: the real-keychain offboard test does not collide with a sibling gate** (`tests/test_governance.py`). The
login keychain is one per user, outside the isolated HOME, and the test used a fixed service (`agentsync-test`):
`offboard` deletes every item of its service and the test's `finally` deletes fixed pairs, so gates running at once
deleted each other's items (measured: 4 copies at once, 4 of 4 failed). Each run now uses its own service
(`agentsync-test-<8 hex>`) and holds an exclusive `flock` on `/tmp/agentsync-keychain-test-<uid>.lock` across the
add, plan, offboard and cleanup, so no sibling writes the keychain while this run's `dump-keychain` reads it (a
unique name alone left dumps that found none of their own items under concurrent writes). Measured after: 4 copies
at once, twice, 8 of 8 passed, and no `agentsync-test-` item was left. A run killed between add and cleanup leaves
one uniquely named dummy item (`not-a-secret`) that no later run removes. Tests:
`tests/test_governance.py::test_offboard_deletes_real_keychain_items_of_its_service`.

### 16.51 Round 4: sync, status and doctor (2026-10-12, wave B13 round 4 lane B)

Wave B13 round 4, lane B: 17 items (`~/.cache/agentsync-bring-back/b13/round4/items/Q<n>.md`, lanes in
`round4/lanes.json`), each built to its verifier's corrected fix with a test that fails without it. Q14 and Q35
describe one defect and are built once, as are Q34 and Q46. Q48 removes dead code and changes no behavior.

**Q2: the volume line names what it reads (`agentsync.ops.doctor`).** `source.<id>.volume` reads `volume UUID
<uuid>` for every source. The value is `getattrlist` `ATTR_VOL_UUID` of the mount point, the APFS volume's UUID,
for a File Provider domain as for a plain folder; it said `File Provider root UUID` for any path under
`~/Library/CloudStorage`. No consumer matched the old words. Dated line in §15's `agentsync.ops.doctor` reference, after `run_checks`. Tests:
`test_cloud_source_without_sentinel_and_tcc_note`, `test_a_sentinel_the_system_will_not_read_is_its_own_line`.

**Q14, Q35: an ok heartbeat names an incomplete listing (`agentsync.ops.doctor`).** An incomplete pass sets
`last_success_at` too, so below `_INCOMPLETE_RUNS` (3) the line read as a clean full pass while the loop already
printed a WAITING ON YOU line about the source. The line stays `[ok]` and adds `; listing incomplete for the last N
pass(es), deletions held, a warn after 3`; the detail still starts `last success`, so
`setup_report._yours_warn` is unaffected. The threshold and the warn are unchanged. Test: `test_heartbeat_states`.

**Q48: the held-lock line loses a dead branch (`agentsync.ops.doctor`).** The early return on a body
`LockInfo.parse` rejects (an empty one, or a corrupt leftover under install.sh's `lockf`) stays as §16.45 R37
contracts it, reading no sidecar; the `if body else` below it could never take its else. Covered by
`test_lock_held_with_an_empty_body_names_no_cycle`.

**Q49: every runnable fix names the binary by its full path (`agentsync.ops.doctor`, `agentsync.cycle`).**
`~/.local/bin` is not on PATH by design (install.sh installs uv with `UV_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1`), so doctor's fixes
(login, logout, install-agent, sync, status, the run-again and crash texts, gitleaks, permissions, heartbeat,
`add-source`) use `loop.BIN`, as R12 made cli.py's. `_AGENT_STEP_FIXES` matches `{BIN} install-agent`, so the
install.sh doctor step still reads `installed by the agent step below`. `cycle._PURGE_QUEUE_STEPS` uses
`skill.AGENTSYNC_BIN` (cycle cannot import loop), as do cycle's other alarms and STATE.md lines that name a
command (`accept-deletions`, `purge --queue`, `materialise --budget`, `purge`). The tests' `assert_fix_parses`
requires the full path. Tests:
`test_heartbeat_states`, `test_a_launchd_fail_keeps_its_fix_while_the_installer_step_is_pending`,
`test_sg04_label_escalation_queues_a_purge_and_drops_the_cached_plaintext`.

**Q34, Q46: a cloud folder is one by the resolved CloudStorage too (`agentsync.paths`, `agentsync.arm_local`,
`agentsync.ops.launchd`).** A source path is stored resolved, so under a home reached through a symlink (`/tmp` is
`/private/tmp`) only `~/Library/CloudStorage`'s resolved form holds it. `paths.cloud_storage_roots()` is the one
definition (the root and what it resolves to; resolving touches only `~/Library/CloudStorage` and its ancestors,
never a File Provider tree); `is_cloud_path` and `arm_local._cloud_roots` (which adds the account home's) build
on it. `paths.cloud_relative(path)` gives the path relative to the root that holds it, and
`launchd.tcc_prompt_text` takes the provider folder from it: widening `is_cloud_path` alone made it raise
`ValueError` from `relative_to`. `tcc_protected` reads Documents, Desktop, Downloads and Mobile Documents by the
resolved home too. `config.canonical_source_root` stays lexical. Test:
`test_a_home_reached_through_a_symlink_keeps_a_resolved_cloud_source_cloud`. **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.61 F89:**
`canonical_source_root` stops at either form of `cloud_storage_roots()`, so under a linked home it no longer reads
the links inside a File Provider tree.

**Q11: the empty-folder wait names each thing (`agentsync.loop`).** `N empty cloud folder(s) keep the listing of
<id> incomplete: an empty folder in a cloud folder is expected and loses nothing, but while the listing is
incomplete, deletions in <id> are held, not applied, and another sync does not complete it; if the folder(s) are
meant to be empty, ...`. Dated line in §16.45 (R1). Test:
`test_a_folder_a_sync_cannot_list_is_a_wait_and_reaches_rule_4`.

**Q71: `agentsync exclude-empty SOURCE` (`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.config`, `agentsync.arm_local`,
`agentsync.loop`).** A hidden command (§16.10's Hidden line, `CLI_SURFACE`). It reads the empty cloud folders the
source's last walk stored (manifest meta `empty_cloud_dirs:<id>`; no folder is read), keeps those today's
`exclude` does not prune and that hold no mirrored file, and writes all of them, not five a round, as `/<path>/`
beside the configured globs (`arm_local.exclude_globs`, shared with `exclude_advice`). A folder whose glob would
also prune a folder holding mirrored files (a `[` is written as `?`) is left too.
`config.set_source_exclude(config_path, source_id, exclude)` edits that one table's `exclude` as text: an
existing key's whole span (one line or an array over several) becomes one line, keeping a comment after the
value, or the line goes under the table's `id`; the file's line endings (LF or CRLF) are kept. The result must load, read back and change no other key before anything is written; the file is
then replaced atomically with its mode kept. It runs under the cycle's lock, as an interactive sync waits for it.
A folder that held mirrored files is left and counted (excluding it retires its pages past the deletion check).
Nothing left exits 0 with `nothing to exclude`; a refused edit prints the old paste line and exits 78. The clear
case's wait now ends `if the folder(s) are meant to be empty, run `~/.local/bin/agentsync exclude-empty <id>` (it
adds them to that source's exclude in <sources.toml>; an excluded folder is not mirrored if it later gains
files)`; the gone case's line is unchanged. The operator still runs it (README unchanged); decision
71d3e66ef726's rule is unchanged. Dated line in §16.45. Tests: `tests/test_exclude_empty.py`,
`test_a_folder_a_sync_cannot_list_is_a_wait_and_reaches_rule_4`.

**Q74: rule 5 points at the waits without a place (`agentsync.loop`, `agentsync.setup_report`,
scripts/install.sh).** Rule 5 reads `stop: the operator confirms the baseline questions (see the WAITING ON YOU
lines); session done`. install.sh no longer rewrites it (it prints the waits above its NEXT, status below), so the
finish, which lists the waits under the last NEXT, reads true either way. `setup_report._WAIT_NAMED` (was
`_WAIT_BELOW`) matches the new phrase only: `_loop_line` reads the loop live through the `loop_next` hook, never a
logged line. Dated lines in §16.30 (`_stopped_wait`) and at R133. Tests: `test_rule_5_the_operator_confirms_a_draft`,
`test_the_closing_statuss_waits_are_printed_above_its_next`.

**Q9: stubs and tombstones open with the banner (`agentsync.publish`, `agentsync.lints`, `agentsync.policy`).**
A stub's and a tombstone's body is `policy.UNTRUSTED_BANNER`, a blank line, then `# [<STATUS>] <title>`, so every
mirror page body starts with the banner, as this document and data-governance.md say. `lints` accepts a
tombstone in either layout, so one written before this change raises no FRONTMATTER finding. **Amended
2026-10-12, §16.60 F68:** such a tombstone keeps its heading-first layout until it is reaped
(`tombstone_reap_days`, default 180) or rendered again by repair or unarchive; only stubs get the one-time
re-render (Q75). Tests:
`test_deleted_status_needs_a_tombstone_body`, `test_item_label_excluded_by_policy_gets_a_metadata_only_refused_stub`,
`test_f_delete_writes_a_tombstone`.
**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.61 F88:** "every mirror page body starts with the banner" holds for every stub and
tombstone written since this change. Q75's one-time re-render moves the banner to the top of an existing refused or
unreadable stub; a tombstone written before the change (until it is reaped) and an existing credential, path or
redacted stub keep the heading above the banner. The banner is still in the body.
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G68 (by §16.60 F94):** a credential or path stub is rendered again once as well
(`Cycle._stub_again`). Only a redacted stub, and a tombstone written before the change until it is reaped or
rendered again by repair or unarchive, keeps the heading above the banner. Test:
`test_a_credential_or_path_stub_from_an_older_rendering_is_rendered_again_once`. That was round 5's state: since
§16.66 G76 and G77 a redacted stub and an old tombstone are rendered again once too, so none keeps it.
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.73 H54 (by §16.66 G77):** the F68 line's "only stubs get the one-time re-render" no
longer holds: an intact tombstone of a source in sources.toml (a retired one's too) is rendered again once, banner
first (`Cycle._rerender_tombstones`), keeping its title, `source_path` and redaction. Only a tombstone of a source
deleted from sources.toml keeps the heading-first layout until it is reaped. Test:
`test_a_tombstone_from_before_the_banner_came_first_is_rendered_again_once_with_its_own_title`.

**Q27: a withheld file's summary (`agentsync.publish`).** Under a label rule a `.msg` or image stub's summary reads
`refused: withheld by label rule: the label of a <suffix> file cannot be read; save it as .eml to have it
converted` (`export it as a PDF` for an image), not `refused: no converter for <suffix>`. (**Amended 2026-10-12,
§16.60 F33:** for a `.msg` it names `a binary (Outlook-format) .msg file, or of a .msg not on this Mac,`, in
the body too.) The stored reason,
QUARANTINE.tsv, the body and `rendered_sha256` are unchanged. Dated line at R33 (§16.47). Tests:
`test_a_msg_is_read_and_under_a_label_rule_its_page_becomes_a_stub`,
`test_under_a_label_rule_no_image_is_read_and_a_page_from_before_it_becomes_a_stub`.

**Q75: a stub from an older rendering is rendered again, once (`agentsync.publish`, `agentsync.cycle`).** An
unchanged refused row is never planned again, so a stub kept whatever its renderer wrote (`refused: refused:`
before R35; the heading above the banner before Q9). `publish.STUB_RENDER` (2) versions a stub's rendering; the
cycle (`_rerender_stubs`, manifest meta `stub_render`), once per version and only on a run that covers every
live source, re-plans each refused or unreadable stub it can rebuild from stored state alone: a `no converter`
stub from its name, any other from its own page (its full `reason:` and the converter fields of the read that
made it). It never fetches or hydrates a file and skips a credential stub, a path stub and a redacted item. A
page is written only where the plan differs from the intact page; no verdict or count moves. A row that cannot
be planned or written (`PublishError`, `OSError`) keeps its page and is logged; no sync stops on it. The meta key is
written after the last row, so an interrupted run tries again. Bump `STUB_RENDER` whenever a stub's text changes.
**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.60 F63 F94:** `STUB_RENDER` is 3. A `no converter` stub is rebuilt from its stored
reason and output row even when a converter now claims the name (msg-mime claims `.msg` under a rule), and a
credential or path stub from its own page, as any other; only a redacted item is skipped.
Test: `test_a_label_stub_from_an_older_rendering_is_rendered_again_once`.
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.73 H54 (by §16.66 G76):** a redacted item is no longer skipped: the publisher redacts its
re-plan from the stored redaction, as it did the first page, and its title, `source_path` and `redacted-<hash>`
page name stay. Test: `test_a_redacted_stub_from_an_older_rendering_is_rendered_again_once_and_stays_redacted`.

**Q44: policy prose about a password is no credential (`agentsync.lints`).** `generic-password` passes over,
after `:` only, a letters-only value followed by a lowercase word or a number (`_PROSE`: "minimum 12 characters,
...", "contact the Contoso service desk"), and over a lone status word (`_STATUS`: required, unknown, expired,
...). A value followed by a table bar, a bracket, a dash, a capital or a `;` is still a hit
(`| Password: Contoso |`, `Password=Contoso; Database=crm`). No digit or symbol is required, so
`changeme`, `letmein` and `password=Contoso`, which gitleaks misses, stay hits, as does a value with a digit
before more words. Known miss: a letters-only password followed by more words (`changeme until first login`). The
pattern edit moves `secret_rules_identity`, so every install screens again; the scan code is unchanged, so
`SECRET_RULES_VERSION` stays 2. No field install ran the v2 rules (the field Mac's build predates them), so no
false-positive stub or queued purge from them needs undoing. Test:
`test_the_password_pattern_passes_over_placeholders_and_masks`.

**Q16: deletion-notice counts for one file (`agentsync.cli`).** The sync line reads `N page(s) turned into
deletion notice(s) (deleted upstream)`; status reads `· absent N (each becomes a deletion notice on a later
