complete pass if still missing)`. The alarms keep their `N file(s) ... their pages` house wording. Dated lines in
§16.12 and §16.37. Tests: `test_the_sync_line_tells_the_marking_pass_from_the_removing_pass`,
`test_status_counts_the_files_held_between_the_marking_pass_and_the_removing_pass`.

**Q28: which re-reads are also counted as converted (`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.model`).** A
no-converter stub's re-read is the first read of its bytes, so the file is in `converted N` and in `read again R`.
Every count stays (loop.py's sync-again note and the setup report's engine row read the raw `reread` tally);
`CycleReport.read_first` (run tally `reread_first`) counts those reads, and the line adds ` (F of them read for
the first time, also counted above)` after R, with no bare `converted` token for install.sh's awk. Tests:
`test_the_summary_line_counts_the_files_read_again_apart_from_those_converted`,

  `"<path>"`, or `"/<path>/"` for a root-anchored folder. One LC_ALL=C awk reads the line as the Python regex
  does (the first `] in [[source]]` after `exclude = [`; a line cut inside the list is `exclude = [<path>]`)
  and tokenizes the body: `"..."` strings, a backslash escaping the next byte, blanks around a comma. A body

- **One deadline for step 2's wait** (Q39, Q63, one defect). The reinstall holds the lock of this run's config

  retry gets a fresh one), and execs it. No lock is let go between the probe and the hold: the rejected variant,

  README and prompt text are unchanged: they are now true. The header says the wait is "for all its locks
  together". `test_the_reinstall_waits_once_however_many_locks_are_busy` (the first lock freed at 3.8 s, the
  second held, a 4 s wait: the step took 5 s or more without the fix).

### 16.54 Round 4: converters, speech and tests (2026-10-12, wave B13 round 4 lane E)

Items are the round 4 harvest's and reviews' (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 4"). Where a part corrects
§16.48, the correction is stated here and §16.48 is left as it was.

#### Build tools

**The watcher is ready before a tool starts (Q73; corrects §16.48 R89).** The loss R89 measured (a tool that ran
on unwatched after an interrupt mid-Popen) was not the child before its exec. In every lost trial the watcher had
exited -2: `_run_build`'s stop at once (`os.killpg(watcher.pid, SIGINT)`) reached a `/bin/sh` that had not yet
run `trap "" INT`, killed it, and nothing stopped the group when Python ended. `_WATCH` is now
`trap "" INT; echo; read -r said; ...`: the watcher prints one line after its trap, and `_run_build` reads that line
(a pipe, closed at once and never passed to the tool) before it starts the tool. A watcher that dies first raises
OSError, which the build reports as before. With the watcher alive the round 4 verifier measured 0 lost stops in
425 mid-Popen interrupts (with and without 8,000 extra file descriptors), so neither a second group SIGINT nor a
SIGKILL tail is built: on Swift 6.2.4 SwiftPM ends 0.00-0.02 s after a group SIGINT, with no compiler left 5 s
later, and a second SIGINT finds the build already gone; the git calls take milliseconds. Pinned by
`tests/test_ocr.py::test_the_stop_at_once_never_kills_a_watcher_that_has_not_set_its_trap`: a watcher slow to set
its trap and a tool that swallows the first SIGINT; before the fix the watcher died and the tool ran to its end.

**Each tool starts with SIGINT at its default (Q51; corrects §16.48 R130).** R130 left a tool that inherited an
ignored SIGINT from a `cmd &` launch unbuilt because swiftc and SwiftPM set their own handlers. R83 then put
`/usr/bin/curl` (the speech seed) on the same path, and curl sets none: with SIGINT ignored at launch, a curl was
still fetching 2 s after the build's process group was killed, against none with SIGINT at default. When this
process ignores SIGINT, `_run_build` starts each tool through a `preexec_fn` that sets SIGINT back to its default
before the exec; the parent's own disposition never changes, and with SIGINT not ignored no `preexec_fn` is passed
(it makes Popen fork rather than vfork). Only a tool that ignores SIGINT itself now outlives the stop. Pinned by
`tests/test_ocr.py::test_a_tool_started_with_sigint_ignored_still_stops_with_the_build`.

#### The speech build

**The seed's curl trusts and routes as git does, from git's config too (Q52, and Q79 for the CA folder).** §16.48
said the seed's curl trusts what step 1's git trusts; that held only for `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` in the environment. Git
also reads `http.sslCAInfo`, `http.sslCAPath`, `http.sslBackend` and `http.proxy` from its config files, and
SwiftPM's clone used them. `speech._seed` now runs the build's git once,
`git config --type=path --get-urlmatch http https://github.com` (url-scoped values count; a `~` path comes back
expanded), and `_curl_env` maps with git's precedence: the bundle (`GIT_SSL_CAINFO`, else `http.sslCAInfo`) to
`CURL_CA_BUNDLE` unless the shell names a bundle of curl's own; the CA folder (`GIT_SSL_CAPATH`, else
`http.sslCAPath`) to `SSL_CERT_DIR` unless the shell sets one; `http.sslBackend` to `CURL_SSL_BACKEND` unless the
shell sets it; `http.proxy`, which wins over the environment in git, to `HTTPS_PROXY` and `https_proxy`, in curl's
environment and never on argv. The seed also runs when only git's config names a proxy. `http.sslVerify` is never
read. The CA folder: `/usr/bin/curl` 8.7.1 (LibreSSL) ignores `GIT_SSL_CAPATH` (exit 60), and with `SSL_CERT_DIR`
at a hashed folder beside `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` it fetched from a server that folder's CA signed, while github.com
still fetched with it at that folder or at one that does not exist; under `CURL_SSL_BACKEND=secure-transport` it
is ignored, as before. This replaces §16.48's "`GIT_SSL_CAPATH` is not mapped", whose measurement put the folder
beside an unusable bundle. Pinned by `tests/test_speech.py::test_the_seed_trusts_and_routes_as_gits_own_config_does`,
`tests/test_speech.py::test_a_proxy_only_in_gits_config_still_seeds_and_the_shells_ca_wins_over_the_configs`,
`tests/test_speech.py::test_without_a_proxy_in_the_shell_or_gits_config_nothing_is_fetched` and
`tests/test_speech.py::test_a_ca_folder_only_git_trusts_is_the_seeds_curl_folder_unless_curl_has_its_own`.
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G61 (by §16.60 F78):** the query is `git config --type=path --get-urlmatch http
<NEMO_URL>`, the url curl fetches, so a proxy scoped to that path counts as well as a host-wide one. An empty
`http.proxy` is git's way to turn the environment's proxy off: the seed then fetches nothing, even when the shell
sets a proxy, and `_curl_env` drops every proxy variable.

**The person's SwiftPM mirrors and registries reach the build (Q53; amends §16.48 R90).** `--config-path`
replaces SwiftPM's shared configuration folder outright (Swift 6.2.4: a mirror resolved under its own
`--config-path` and was "not found" under another), so since R90 a Mac that reaches GitHub only through a SwiftPM
mirror or registry could not build. Every build copies `mirrors.json` and `registries.json` from the shared folder
(`~/Library/org.swift.swiftpm/configuration`, then `~/.swiftpm/configuration`, found from HOME so a rehearsal
never reads the real one) into `<cache>/speech/swiftpm/config`, owner-only, and removes a copy whose source is
gone. Pinned by
`tests/test_speech.py::test_the_persons_swiftpm_mirrors_and_registries_reach_the_build_and_leave_with_them`.

#### Converters

**A template or drawing saved again unchanged is not changed (Q76).** `canonical.OOXML_SUFFIXES` is now
`policy.OOXML_SUFFIXES`, one list, so H1 hashes `.potx`, `.vsdx`, `.vsdm`, `.dotx` and `.xltx` by their parts; a
save that changes only docProps is touched, not changed. A purge records the H1 of its day (`bytes@1` for these
until now), so `_after_fetch` also checks the fetched bytes' own hash against the purged hashes: a byte-identical
copy of a template purged before stays suppressed. An existing row is changed once (`canonical-method-changed`)
and keeps its pages (H2). Not built: also recording the raw hash at purge time (the round 4 verifier's optional
step; the check at fetch already holds every purge recorded so far). Pinned by
`tests/test_convert_core.py::test_a_template_or_drawing_saved_again_unchanged_hashes_the_same`,
`tests/test_review_fixes.py::test_a_template_purged_under_its_raw_bytes_hash_stays_suppressed` and
`tests/test_review_fixes.py::test_a_template_hashed_as_bytes_before_is_changed_once_and_keeps_its_page`.
**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.60 F72:** a save of these that only changes the label was touched, not changed, so under
a label rule an exclusion it gained left its page up; the label screen now runs on such bytes.

**A template with no slides says what its layouts and master hold (Q77; amends §16.48 R85).** Under
`[empty presentation: no slides]` the page names the layouts (`Layouts: …`) and gives the fixed text of the
masters and layouts in reading order: every shape that is not a placeholder, and a footer placeholder that carries
text; never a title, body, object, picture, date or slide-number placeholder, which hold prompt text or a field.
The title is the first fixed text, else the first layout name, never the marker; the summary adds `N layout(s)`.
The deck emitter's version is unchanged: an `outdated()` rule cannot tell `.potx` pages from `.pptx` ones and would
read every deck again, and no install has written a `.potx` deck page yet (its stubs are read again by the
no-converter rule). Pinned by
`tests/test_convert_formats.py::test_a_template_with_no_slides_says_what_its_layouts_and_master_hold`.
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G61 (by §16.60 F77):** fixed text is de-duplicated a shape at a time, and the title is
the first fixed line that can be a title (never a table row), else the first layout name.
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.73 H54 (by §16.66 G59):** "the deck emitter's version is unchanged" no longer holds:
`pptx._EMITTER_VERSION` is 1.0.1, so cached bytes get the new rendering on a new conversion, while
`PptxConverter.outdated` is unchanged and reads no deck again by itself.
Amended 2026-10-18, §16.121 S48, S57 (by §16.111 Q39): the summary adds `1 layout` or `N layouts`; a page converted
before keeps its `(s)` until it is converted again.
Amended 2026-10-18, §16.126 T62: not only a page converted before: the write-once cache serves a
summary cached before, `(s)` and all, to any page with the same bytes (a copy, a second synced folder, a restored
file) until its action key moves (the bytes, the converter's version as run, or its options) or a reconcile's
cache GC drops it.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.132 U77: a reconcile's cache GC drops a cached summary only once no live page holds its key
(a purge or a label escalation also deletes it), so a copy beside its live original, or in a second synced folder,
keeps the old wording until the key moves; only a restored file whose page was removed meets the GC.

**Under a label rule a `.msg` that holds MIME text is screened and read (Q78; amends §16.48 R87 and §16.47 R33).**
`policy.read_labels` reads a `.msg` whose first `policy.MIME_HEAD_BYTES` (64 KiB) is an RFC 822 header block (no
compound-file magic: `policy.mime_msg`; `policy.rfc822_head` is the one sniff the screen and both `.msg` converters
share) as the `.eml` it is. Under a label rule `.msg` goes to `msg-mime` (`msg.MsgMimeConverter`): such a message is screened as an `.eml` (an excluded label or, under
`refuse_unlabelled`, no label refuses it) and read through the `.eml` converter. A binary `.msg` keeps the reason
`no converter for .msg`, the page's wording and the setup report's count (`NotConvertibleError` in `convert_file`,
under `msg-mime`'s id). `msg-mime` claiming `.msg` makes each existing `.msg` stub a re-read target once; a binary
one gets the same refusal back, and that settles it: a `no converter` refusal counts as lacking, or as a target,
only when the converter now claiming its suffix is not the one that gave it, and a kept stub's output rows take the
converter of its conversion, which no cache row records for a stub. Without that, three binary `.msg` in a row
stopped every other re-read of the cycle (`_REREAD_STREAK`) and each was read again every cycle. Lifting the rule
reads them again through `msg-olefile`. Under a rule a `.msg` is now fetched, since only its bytes say which kind
it is. (**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.60:** the re-read that settles a stub writes no page, so new stub wording reaches
an existing binary `.msg` stub through the stub re-render (F63), not this re-read; and a `.msg` that reading means a
download for is refused by its name again (F73).) Pinned by `tests/test_convert_formats.py::test_under_a_label_rule_a_binary_msg_is_the_no_converter_stub`,
`tests/test_convert_formats.py::test_under_a_label_rule_a_msg_that_holds_mime_text_is_screened_as_an_eml` and
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_binary_msg_stubs_under_a_label_rule_settle_and_never_stop_another_files_reread`. 2026-10-12: §16.48 R87's
`test_under_a_label_rule_a_msg_is_the_no_converter_stub` is replaced by the first two, since a MIME `.msg` under a
rule is no longer the stub.

#### Tests

**A time bound under load (Q59, Q82).** The `timing` marker says what conftest does: a run whose 1-minute load is
above 4 per core skips it, and `AGENTSYNC_TIMING=1` runs it anyway; nothing reruns a test.
`tests/test_install_oneshot.py::test_friction_options_are_fast`, a CPU-time bound that load stretched to
0.27-0.43 s against 0.2 s, is marked `timing`. `tests/test_curate.py::test_the_citation_lint_survives_hostile_pages_and_units`
measures its linear-time bound in CPU time, so its hostile-input checks run on every Mac;
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_held_root_read_ends_in_the_same_click_allow_pass` holds the read for two minutes
against a one-minute bound; `tests/test_setup_report.py::test_a_v8_attempt_is_judged_like_v7_and_a_version_alone_says_nothing_about_the_copy`
and `tests/test_setup_report.py::test_an_empty_cloud_folders_heartbeat_is_yours_through_the_cli` take
`roomy_budget` (with the report budget starved to 0.3 s, both fail without it).

**The IT request names the release the speech build fetches (Q60).**
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py::test_a_weekly_check_follows_the_download_hosts_the_it_request_names` requires the
page's release url to equal `speech.NEMO_URL`, and the hand-copied table of FluidAudio's binary targets is gone:
the archive and release repository are read from that url, and a new pin fails
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py::test_it_request_names_the_speech_build_downloads` against `speech.FLUIDAUDIO_PIN`.

**Bash 3.2 (Q84).** An apostrophe in a comment inside a multi-line `<( )` passes bash 5's `-n`, `/bin/bash` 3.2's
`-n` and shellcheck, then fails at run time ("bad substitution"); in round 3 it dropped every proxy pair.
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py::test_no_apostrophe_in_a_comment_inside_a_substitution` refuses any apostrophe in a
comment inside a multi-line `$(`, `"$(` or `<(` block of `scripts`, `probes`, `launcher` and the review receipts'
scripts (`install.sh`'s one such comment is reworded), and
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py::test_scripts_parse_with_bash_n` parses every `#!/bin/bash` script with `/bin/bash` on a
Mac, which catches the quoted `"$( )"` form bash 5 accepts. An unquoted `$( )` with the same comment parses and
runs under 3.2.

### 16.55 Round 4: setup prompt v13 and docs (2026-10-12, wave B13 round 4 lane P)

The B13 round 4 items of lane P (specs `round4/items/Q<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built). Three need
prompt text (Q8, Q24, Q25), so the prompt is **setup prompt v13**: `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, `PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's
`prompt v13` and `setup-prompt-compat 13`, the issue form's placeholder and the block's digest move together; a
saved v12 copy is stopped at step 1 like every older copy. v13 moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry
and is read with v7's rules. None adds a command, flag, installer option, config key or friction kind.

**The deviation kind names step 1's stop** (Q8). Step 1 says that when the folder question cannot be asked or comes
back unanswered, the agent logs a deviation, stops and waits; the kind list defined a deviation as "you did
something this prompt did not say, or worked around a problem", which a run that followed the prompt then
contradicted. The definition now ends "or stopped to wait for my folder answer as step 1 says", and
setup-feedback.md's `deviation` row says the same. Step 1 and the report's counting (a deviation is agent
friction) are unchanged. Test: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py` (`test_readme_friction_line_format_and_kinds`).

**The finish names bring-back.md only when a report ran** (Q24). Only `install.sh --report-only` writes
`~/agent-context/bring-back.md`, so after a failed clone there is none, and the stop for a copy that is not the
installer's runs no report while an earlier session's file may still be there. The finish's clause now ends "; if
no report ran this session, say "none" for that file instead, and do not point me to an older bring-back.md". The clause is tied
to whether a report ran, not to the clone, so both no-report stops are covered. Test: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py`
(`test_prompt_routes_changes_to_the_source_not_the_checkout`).

**The git stop's proxy hint is unconditional** (Q25; amends §16.49 "Step 1's git stop" by a dated line). "If the
error names a proxy, the one in git's own settings ... comes before HTTPS_PROXY" put a condition on a fact that
always holds, and "the one" could be read as the proxy the error named. The condition was also hard to check: an
unreachable proxy in git's settings fails as `Failed to connect to <its host> port <N>`, without the word proxy
(git 2.54, measured by the verifier), and only an unresolvable one says `Could not resolve proxy`. The quoted words
now state the precedence first and base the check on what git prints: "if git's error names a host other than
github.com, check that setting". The message stays one quote the agent repeats word for word; the agent is not
asked to judge the error, and nothing tells it to change `~/.gitconfig`. Test: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py`
(`test_readme_step1_is_one_command`). **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.61 F24:** "check that setting" is replaced: the
host is a proxy set by git's setting or by the terminal's `HTTPS_PROXY`, `https_proxy` or `ALL_PROXY`.

**Older contract sections, by dated lines** (Q50 and Q64, one defect; Q54, Q56, Q57, Q62, Q70). Each is pinned by a
test in `tests/test_deploy_pack.py` that reads the contract against the code, except Q70's proxy prose:
- §7 routes `.mp4 .m4v .mov` to `recording-av` (§16.34) and `.vtt` to `vtt-turns` (§16.35) by SUPERSEDED lines

- The `quarantine_class` table has a row for `withheld by label rule` (§16.47 R33) and lists `not-msg` and `not a

- §9 step 2 and §16.49 carry §16.45 R50/R80 lines naming `EMPTY_BODY_HOLDER` and saying doctor adds `(a cycle is
  running)` only for a body that parses as a cycle's record
  (`test_every_section_quoting_the_old_empty_lock_body_text_states_the_constant`). §16.45's own "N24 and the

**Docs** (Q58, Q65, Q68, Q69). data-governance.md: only an Outlook-format `.msg` with an encrypted Office attachment

### 16.56 Round 5: purge (2026-10-12, wave B13 round 5 lane A)

Round 5 lane A of B13 (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 5"): the purge preview, exclude-empty's lock,
the absent-file counts and alarms, the doctor's lock line, the retirement advice, the binary's full path in printed
commands, and the contract stub test (`~/.cache/agentsync-bring-back/b13/round5/items/F<n>.md`). Each entry names the
finding it builds; an entry that changes text an older section quotes is that section's dated amendment
(2026-10-12).

**F80: the purge queue preview skips a covered entry before judging it kept** (`agentsync.governance`). §16.50 Q61
said the loop skips the entries a previewed purge covers, but `run_purge_queue` asked `_kept_upstream_deletion`
first: a preview leaves the manifest as it is, so an upstream deletion of a live file queued behind a label
escalation of the same file read both `would also do the queued upstream-deleted purge ...: the run takes it off the
queue` and `purge stable-id (upstream-deleted): not run` / `note: stays queued: ...`, while the run takes it off. A
covered entry is now skipped before the kept check, in the preview and the run alike; in the run the covering purge
has already erased the row the check reads, so only the preview's words change. Q61's "the loop skips those
entries" and `docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md`'s "the entries a run would keep are exactly those with a `note: stays
queued:` line" now hold. Tests:
`tests/test_cli.py::test_purge_queue_preview_does_not_keep_a_covered_upstream_deletion`.

**F64, F100: the absent-file counts name files, and the alarms read right for one** (`agentsync.cli`,
`agentsync.cycle`). `absent_marked` and `absent_removed` count stable ids, which are files (`SourceReport`'s own
comment), but §16.51 Q16's sync line called the second `K page(s) turned into deletion notice(s)`: a removed
workbook of three pages read `1 page(s)` beside `3 change(s)`. Status's `· absent N (each becomes a deletion notice
...)` counts item rows (`Manifest.absent_counts`), files as well. The sync line now prints `M file(s) marked absent`
and `K file(s) removed upstream (their page(s) are now deletion notice(s))`, and status `· absent N file(s) (their
page(s) become deletion notice(s) on a later complete pass if still missing)`. Q16 kept the alarms' "their pages"
wording; for one file that read "their pages ... deletion notices" under a line that said "page(s)". The marking
alarm now reads `N file(s) absent from this complete pass: their page(s) become deletion notice(s) only if still
absent next pass`, the removing alarm `N file(s) still absent from this complete pass: their page(s) are now
deletion notice(s) (deleted upstream; purge queued)`, and the re-read alarm of the same family `... could not be
converted; their page(s) are kept as they were`. This amends the text quoted in §16.12 (status), §16.37, §16.39,
§16.45 R105, §16.51 Q16 and the §16.27 re-read table row; the counts are unchanged. Tests: `tests/test_cli.py`
(`test_the_sync_line_counts_a_removed_file_of_several_pages_as_one_file`, a three-page workbook removed;
`test_the_sync_line_tells_the_marking_pass_from_the_removing_pass`,
`test_status_counts_the_files_held_between_the_marking_pass_and_the_removing_pass`), `tests/test_cycle.py` (the
alarm pins, with the negative pin `are now deletion notice` kept biting).

**F71: doctor's lock line calls only a sync mode a cycle** (`agentsync.ops.doctor`). The held `lock` line added
`(a cycle is running)` to any body `LockInfo.parse` accepts, and it accepts any label, so `exclude-empty` and
`governance` (a purge, uninstall's cleanup) read `held by pid N (exclude-empty) since ... (a cycle is running)`. The
suffix is now `(a cycle is running)` only when the body's label is a cycle's (a `CycleMode` value: poll, reconcile,
dry_run), and `(not a cycle)` otherwise. The empty or unparseable body and the silent-for warning are unchanged.
This amends §16.41, §16.45 and §16.49's "only when the body parses as a cycle's record" and §16.55's "only for a body
that parses as a cycle's record": the body parses and its label is a `CycleMode`. Tests: `tests/test_ops_doctor.py` (`test_lock_held_by_a_non_cycle_names_no_cycle`,
`test_lock_held_by_a_cycle_says_a_cycle_is_running`).

**F97: one retirement advice, and a config the loader accepts** (`agentsync.config`, `agentsync.cycle`,
`agentsync.ops.doctor`). The vanished-source refusal (`Cycle._refuse_vanished_sources`) and doctor's
`sources.shared_content` line wrote the advice out twice, and §16.50 Q42's "the refusal's own words" was held by
nothing: only doctor's copy was pinned. Both also said to set `state = "retired"` alone, which the loader refuses (`a
retired source needs 'retired_reason'`). `config.RETIRE_ADVICE` is now ``state = "retired" and retired_reason =
"<why>" (its pages become tombstones in one labelled commit)``, beside the check it describes; the refusal ends `put
the [[source]] block back with <RETIRE_ADVICE>, or restore it` and doctor's line `if one source copies the other,
give its [[source]] block in sources.toml <RETIRE_ADVICE>`. This amends the text §16.45 R144 and §16.50 Q42 quote.
Tests: `tests/test_config.py::test_the_retire_advice_names_a_source_block_the_loader_accepts` (the advice's own
assignments parse as a retired source),
`tests/test_review_fixes.py::test_removing_a_source_block_is_refused_not_silently_kept_current`,
`tests/test_ops_doctor.py::test_two_sources_holding_the_same_files_is_an_info_line`.

**F70: exclude-empty reads sources.toml again once it holds the lock** (`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.config`).
`exclude-empty` (§16.51 Q71) loaded the config and chose the source before its lock wait (up to 600 s), then built
the new list from that stale `exclude`; `set_source_exclude` re-reads the file but sets this source's `exclude`
before comparing, so a glob added by hand during the wait was written over with no word. The command now loads the
config and looks the source up again once the lock is held: a file that no longer loads prints `exclude-empty <id>:
sources.toml does not load: ...` (exit 78), a source that is gone or no longer local or inbox prints the usage error
(exit 2), both with the lock released. `set_source_exclude` takes `expected` (keyword only: the `exclude` the list
was built from) and, on its own read, refuses with `source <id>'s exclude changed since it was read; run it again`
when that key differs, so the gap between the two reads ends in the refusal path (exit 78, the paste line) rather
than a lost edit. Tests: `tests/test_exclude_empty.py` (`test_an_exclude_edited_during_the_lock_wait_is_kept`,
`test_a_source_removed_or_a_config_broken_during_the_lock_wait_is_reported`,
`test_the_write_refuses_an_exclude_changed_since_it_was_read`).

**F66, F95: printed commands name the binary by its full path, past cli.py and doctor** (`agentsync.governance`,
`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.setup_report`, `agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.config`, `agentsync.graph.auth`,
`agentsync.graph.discover`). §16.51 Q49 moved doctor's fixes and cycle's alarms to the full path, but round 4 added
bare ones and older ones stayed, so `status` printed `~/.local/bin/agentsync purge --queue` on the queued line and
`agentsync purge --queue` in `KEPT_PURGES` right under it; without `~/.local/bin` on PATH the bare form is
`command not found`. F66 and F95 describe one defect and are built once. Every text below that a person is told to run now names
`skill.AGENTSYNC_BIN` (`loop.BIN` in cli.py):
- `governance.KEPT_PURGES`, the §16 stub's and §16.44 and §16.50 Q45's quoted text: `` ...they wait for
  `~/.local/bin/agentsync purge --queue` like any queued purge ``.
- `cycle._RECORDING_STOPPED` (§16.34's stub text, also the stored quarantine reason): `... run
  ~/.local/bin/agentsync materialise on it from a terminal to read it`. The old text stays matched
  (`_RECORDING_STOPPED_OLD`, in `_RECORDING_STOPPED_REASONS` at both places a reason is compared), so a row given up
  before this still reads as a stopped recording; its published stub keeps the old words until it is read again.
  Cycle's owner-only log line names `<bin> status`.
- `setup_report`: exit 77's meaning (`<bin> graph login`), the doctor block's `<bin> status` runs them, the two
  launchd lines' `<bin> install-agent`, the stale-report warning's `<bin> setup-report`, and the IT draft's
  `<bin> it-request --out ...` (the line and its run-again text). Q81's secret-scan fix at `(fix: agentsync sync from
  this shell)` is round 5 lane RA's (F57, F83) and is not changed here.

### 16.57 Round 5: sync, status and doctor (2026-10-12, wave B13 round 5 lane B)

Wave B13 round 5, lane B: 18 items (`~/.cache/agentsync-bring-back/b13/round5/items/F<n>.md`, lanes in
`round5/lanes.json`), each built to its verifier's corrected fix with a test that fails without it. Four pairs
describe one defect and are built once: F1 and F47, F3 and F50, F10 and F41, F12 and F45. Where this section
gives a line's new words, it supersedes the quotes of the old words in §16.22, §16.39 N27, §16.51 Q71 and Q74.

**F1, F47: the draft wait asks for no count it cannot know (`agentsync.loop`).** The skill drafts fewer than 15
questions for a small mirror and the operator then keeps all of them, so the draft baseline's wait reads `... in
<_eval>, keep up to about 10 in questions.md (all of them if there are fewer), correct the answers in answers.md,
and change both files to status: confirmed`. No count is read: the file holds what is left after the operator's
cuts, not what was drafted, and is edited by hand. The prefix `WAITING ON YOU: the baseline questions are a draft`
and the `in <path>, ` part are unchanged, so `setup_report._WAIT_DRAFT` and `_eval_by_name` still apply. Test:
`test_a_small_draft_is_not_asked_to_keep_ten`.

**F10, F41: rule 5 names one wait line or more (`agentsync.loop`, `agentsync.setup_report`).** Rule 5's NEXT
reads `(see the WAITING ON YOU line)` over one wait and `(see the WAITING ON YOU lines)` over two or more, from
the waits it was built with; still no place word (install.sh prints the waits above the NEXT, status below,
§16.51 Q74). `setup_report._WAIT_NAMED` is the shared prefix `(see the WAITING ON YOU line`, matched as a
substring by `_stopped_wait`, so both forms, and an earlier agentsync's `lines)` in a kept install.out, still pick
the draft. Test: `test_rule_5_names_one_wait_line_or_more_by_their_count`.

**F43: the empty-folder wait names the command that lists its folders (`agentsync.loop`).** Since §16.51 Q71 the
wait names `exclude-empty` and no folder, and status prints no folder of the source, so the wait now adds
`` `~/.local/bin/agentsync sync -v` names the folder(s)`` after the exclude-empty sentence, as the gone line
does. The wait keeps a count and never a path (STATE.md and the setup report carry it). Test:
`test_a_folder_a_sync_cannot_list_is_a_wait_and_reaches_rule_4`. **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.63 G13:** the
pointer is now the sync's alarm line, kept in STATE.md, which a plain sync already prints; `sync -v` is named only
for the folders past the alarm's five. **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.68 H12:** the alarm names it, as `(+N more;
\`~/.local/bin/agentsync sync -v\` logs each one)`, and the wait never does.

**F65: one rule for exclude-empty and its wait (`agentsync.loop`, `agentsync.cli`).** `loop._excludable(manifest,
src, below)` splits the empty folders with no mirrored file below them into those `exclude-empty` excludes and
those whose `/<path>/` glob would also prune a folder holding mirrored files (a `[` is written as `?`), which the
command leaves. `_cmd_exclude_empty` and `next_step` both use it (`_folders_holding_files` moved to loop). A
colliding folder gets its own wait: `N empty cloud folder(s) in <id> have a [ in the name, so an exclude of one
would also match a folder whose files are mirrored (...): rename or remove the empty folder(s) in the cloud drive;
`~/.local/bin/agentsync sync -v` names them` (**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.63 G42:** now the alarm line, as the
other empty-folder waits). It never names exclude-empty, which would leave the folder and the
wait for good. The `size` tail goes on the last empty-folder line, as before. `_empty_dirs` and
`empty_cloud_folders_held` are unchanged. Test: `test_a_folder_whose_glob_would_match_a_folder_with_files_is_left`.
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.63 G55:** `_empty_dirs(manifest, src)` returns `_EmptyDirs(stored, below, holding)` from
one walk of the rows, counting a file below a stored folder whose name differs only in case (the glob ignores
case), and `_excludable(found)` takes it; `_folders_holding_files` and the second walk are gone.

**F11, F44: the empty-folder alarm counts its waits and names status by its path (`agentsync.arm_local`).** Each
empty folder lands on exactly one wait (clear, colliding or gone), so with one folder the alarm reads `the
WAITING ON YOU line about <id> says what to do, and `~/.local/bin/agentsync status` prints it`; with two or more
it keeps `each WAITING ON YOU line about <id> ... prints them`. The mixed-cause branch (`for the empty one(s), ...`)
follows the same rule. Status is named by `skill.AGENTSYNC_BIN`, as §16.51 Q49 requires of every alarm that names
a command. doctor's heartbeat fix keeps `each WAITING ON YOU line about <id>`, which is true for any count. Tests:
`test_an_inbox_empty_cloud_folder_alarm_points_at_the_waits`,
`test_an_unreadable_folder_beside_an_empty_cloud_folder_offers_no_exclude`.
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.63 G42:** the waits now name this alarm as where the folders are named, so the alarm
names the wait for the step and no longer sends the reader back for the folders: `the WAITING ON YOU line about
<id> at the end of a sync's output says what to do, and `~/.local/bin/agentsync status` prints it too` (`each ...
prints them too` for two or more). Its comment counts up to three waits per source (§16.63 G57). **Amended
2026-10-13, §16.63 G44:** doctor's heartbeat fix says `the WAITING ON YOU line about <id>` when status knows exactly
one wait names it (`loop.NextStep.wait_counts`, counted per wait, not per check), and keeps `each ...`
otherwise, including the setup report's doctor, which has no count.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.83 K41: with two or more folders the alarm ends `prints each one too`, since any number of
plain empty folders makes one wait line; its comment counts one line per wait kind present, at most three.

**F2: the tcc ok line names no LaunchAgent that is not there (`agentsync.ops.doctor`).** When `agents_wanted` is
false (no plist, no pending agent step) the line reads `cloud roots were listed with this terminal's privacy
grants; background sync is not installed: if it is turned on, its LaunchAgents run <launcher>, which needs its
own grants`. Otherwise it keeps `... the LaunchAgent runs <launcher> and needs its own (the launcher and tcc.*
lines below report it)`. With no launcher found, `<launcher>` is `the signed launcher (agentsync-launcher)`,
never the interpreter: a cloud root always requires the launcher. Tests:
`test_cloud_source_without_sentinel_and_tcc_note`,
`test_the_tcc_note_names_the_lines_below_when_background_sync_is_wanted`.

**F3, F50: the sentinel ok line says what agentsync holds back (`agentsync.ops.doctor`).** The line reads `no
sentinel configured (optional: agentsync already holds back deletions under a cloud folder that is empty or
cannot be listed)`, with agentsync as the subject (the folder read as holding deletions). Outside a File Provider
domain (`arm_local._is_domain` false for the provider folder, the walk's own `in_domain` test, which also treats
a missing provider folder as a domain) the walk reads an empty folder as empty, so the line ends `that cannot be
listed)`. Tests: `test_cloud_source_without_sentinel_and_tcc_note`,
`test_a_plain_provider_folder_holds_back_deletions_only_for_a_folder_it_cannot_list`.

**F69: a Graph delta pass is no incomplete listing (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.ops.doctor`).** Each Graph arm
reports `enumeration_complete` true only on a FULL pass, and the heartbeat counted every DELTA as incomplete, so a
healthy Graph source warned after three deltas with `sync -v` (another delta) as a fix that could not clear it.
For the heartbeat's `consecutive_incomplete` alone, `_after` passes a Graph DELTA pass as listed: provider
tombstones apply on it and absence checks run only on FULL passes, so it holds nothing back. The manifest's
flag and the classifier are unchanged; a FULL pass that stops short still counts. doctor's warn and ok lines say
`deletions held` for a local or inbox source and `files missing from the listing are kept while deletions Graph
reports still apply` for a Graph one (`doctor._held`); a Graph source's fix is `~/.local/bin/agentsync reconcile --source
<id> (a full pass that lists all of <id> clears this)`. Tests:
`test_graph_delta_passes_leave_the_incomplete_count_and_doctor_at_ok`, `test_heartbeat_incomplete_fix_by_source_kind`.
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.63 G54:** the Graph fix is `~/.local/bin/agentsync sync -v (a full pass that lists all of
<id> clears this)` again, as the loop and the doctor paragraph of §16.22 say. Since this change a delta resets the
count, so the warn needs three incomplete FULL passes in a row; those happen only when no cursor is kept or the
drive is not baselined, and then a plain sync is itself FULL. Otherwise a plain sync runs a delta, which clears the
count. reconcile was only an equivalent, explicit FULL. **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.63 G53:** the heartbeat entry's
`enumeration_complete` keeps the pass's own flag; only `consecutive_incomplete` reads a Graph delta as listed
(`write_heartbeat(..., counts_as_listed=)`).
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.107 O51: the fix reads `~/.local/bin/agentsync sync -v; a full pass that lists all of <id>
clears this`, with no bracket of its own inside the line's `(fix: ...)`.

**F34: one parenthesis per subject on the sync line (`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.setup_report`).** With the Q28
clause (`read again R (F of them read for the first time, also counted above)`) the unreadable split follows as
`; of the converted: U unreadable, F failed`, never a second parenthesis beside the first; without it the split
stays ` (of the converted: ...)`. `setup_report._CONVERTED_LINE_RE` reads both, and an earlier sync's
two-parenthesis line, which the old pattern lost after the Q28 clause (the Summary dropped the split). The line
still has one bare `converted` token. Tests:
`test_the_summary_line_counts_the_files_read_again_apart_from_those_converted`,
`test_the_converted_line_parses_with_the_read_again_clause_in_either_form`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.83 K34: the Q28 clause reads `read again R (F of them a first read: a stub whose bytes had
never been read, now in the count above)`; `, read again R` is unchanged.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.87 L16: it ends `..., so also counted as converted)`.

**F35: a re-screen is counted apart (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.model`, `agentsync.cli`).** A [policy] or
secret-rule change forgets the hashes of files already converted (`mark_for_rescreen`,
`mark_quarantined_rescreen`), and the converter runs on the same bytes; that file stays in N (the Repeat
conversions table reads N) and is counted again. `_after_fetch` calls a conversion a re-screen when it is no
capability re-read, the row's stored `content_sha256` was None, the row is no no-converter stub, and it has an
output other than `skipped-dataless` or `tombstone` (a page made from read bytes). The run tally carries
`rescreened` and `rescreened_unchanged` (its page came out the same), and `CycleReport` the same two. The sync
line ends `; re-screened S for a rule change (also counted above, K of them unchanged)`, after every parsed
clause and with no bare `converted`, `deferred` or `read again`, so install.sh's `SYNC_SUMMARY_RE`, its awk and
`_CONVERTED_LINE_RE` read the line as before. Test: `test_a_policy_rescreen_is_counted_apart_on_the_sync_line`.

**F12, F45: the report's Doctor section points at its Loop line (`agentsync.ops.doctor`, `agentsync.cli`).**
`doctor._LISTING_YOURS_NOTE` (`... the WAITING ON YOU lines at the end of this run say whether it still is`) stays
for install.sh's terminal output. The setup report has no end of its run (`--report-only` prints no wait), so
`cli._report_hooks`'s doctor hook swaps in `doctor.LISTING_YOURS_REPORT_NOTE`: `held at its last walk: the
Summary's Loop line says whether a WAITING ON YOU line still holds it`. It promises no line (the report's doctor
calls a local listing yours by the source's kind) and has no parentheses. `setup_report._yours_warn` reads no
note, so the Summary's grouping is unchanged. Tests: `test_the_report_doctor_never_points_at_the_end_of_its_run`,
`test_a_wait_the_loop_names_is_yours_and_a_stopped_sync_stays_unexpected`.

**F49: the added source line names the stored path (`agentsync.cli`).** A folder typed through a link (or `/tmp`
for `/private/tmp`) is stored resolved; `added source '<id>' to <config> (<typed>, stored as <stored>):` names
both when they differ, as the inbox line does (§16.51 Q36). The config path, the colon before the table and the

`test_the_added_source_line_names_the_stored_path_beside_the_typed_one`.

**F96: both forms of the cloud root stop the config-load walk (`agentsync.config`).** The same defect as lane P's
F89, whose fix landed first (c820e3a3, §16.61): `canonical_source_root` stops at either form of

### 16.58 Round 5: setup report (2026-10-12, wave B13 round 5 lane RA)

Wave B13 round 5, lane RA: 25 items (`~/.cache/agentsync-bring-back/b13/round5/items/F<n>.md`, lanes in
`round5/lanes.json`), each built to its verifier's corrected fix with a test that fails without it, or left with a
measured reason. Where an item amends an older section, the amendment is stated here and the older text is read
with it.

**F4: the coding-agent folder line says what happens.** Amends §16.52's Configuration line: `- folders whose name
is made only of coding-agent product words: N under ~/Library/CloudStorage, which this report does not redact, so
the product name in the friction log's Agent: line stays as written; M of the configured source folders, which are
redacted to <folder-N> like any other`, or `could not list ~/Library/CloudStorage` for the count. The line gives no

Amended 2026-10-16, §16.92 M2: `, so the product name ... stays as written` follows only when an Agent: line of the
friction log has a word of a listed folder's name that is not configured, and N counts only those folders (a
configured one is redacted, and never decides the clause).
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.140 W17: when M is not 0 the clause ends `, except as a word of the agent's name in the friction log's Agent: line`.

**F31: one wording for the label rule.** The OCR part's line is `- [policy] label rule: on (no image is read under
one)`, `off` or `not read (<Exc>)`, the Configuration line's words (Q31), with the OCR part's own suffix kept.
Tests: the OCR part tests that pin it.

**F48: the empty-folder link-count clause.** `M materialised-and-empty (K of them still empty on this Mac, by their
link count of 2)`: what the walk found empty and is still empty now, by one lstat. Test: the Empty cloud folders

this Mac, by its link count of 2)` or `(no longer empty on this Mac, by its link count)`.

**F57 (with F83): the secret-scan fix names the full path.** Amends Q81 (§16.52), read with Q49 (§16.51) and Q12:
`(fix: ~/.local/bin/agentsync sync from this shell)`, built from `skill.AGENTSYNC_BIN`. F83's other half,
`governance.KEPT_PURGES`, is lane A's (§16.56). Test: `test_environment_says_what_the_secret_scan_can_use`.

**F61: the joined-word rule covers every fuzzy kind.** Amends Q72 (§16.52): the rule applies to any fuzzy value of
two or more words (name, folder, library or organisation), as the code always did; it is not limited to a full
name. install.sh's `name_forms` applies it to the full name only, because its folder and organisation pairs are
matched only as written and never matched the run-together lower-case word. Test:
`test_a_short_names_joined_form_that_spells_a_report_word_leaves_the_word_alone` (a folder `Set Up`).

**F8, F32: the Summary keeps the sync line's first-read count and its split.** The CLI half, one parenthesis per
subject on the sync's last line, is lane B's F34 (§16.57; this lane leaves cli.py to it). Read with §16.45 R2 and
Q28: setup-report's `_CONVERTED_LINE_RE` reads the head with named groups and keeps the rest of the line, and
`_FIRST_READ_RE` and `_SPLIT_RE` read Q28's first-read clause and the unreadable/failed split from it wherever
they stand, so F34's `(F of them read for the first time, also counted above); of the converted: ...`, an older
install.out's two brackets side by side and a split alone all read the same; before, the split was lost after
Q28's clause and the first-read count was never read (a reader added 1 + 1 for one file). The first-sync clause
puts both in one bracket, `read again R (F of them read for the first time, also in the converted count; of the
converted: U unreadable, X failed)`, the first-read count only when install.out's line has the same converted and
read-again counts, and its source tag names the file: `(install.log; the first-read count and the
unreadable/failed split: install.out)`. install.sh's note is unchanged (no `-first-F` suffix). F8 and F32
describe one defect and are built once. Tests: `test_first_sync_clause_carries_the_read_again_count`,
`test_the_converted_line_parses_with_the_read_again_clause_in_either_form`.
Amended 2026-10-13, §16.64 G34: the clauses have no bracket of their own, so the source tag is the clause's one
trailing bracket: `read again R: F of them read for the first time, also in the converted count; of the converted: U
unreadable, X failed (<source>)`, and a split alone reads `online-only; of the converted: …`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.83 K34: the CLI's bracket reads `(F of them a first read: a stub whose bytes had never been
read, now in the count above)`, the clause `read again R: F of them a first read, of a stub whose bytes had never
been read, also in the converted count`; `_FIRST_READ_RE` reads both wordings.

**F9, F46: the Loop line's order clause in plain words.** Amends Q13 (§16.52): the wait the loop stopped on
still comes first (the 2026-10-07 field report: the loop prints queued purges first and the draft baseline last,
so by place they hid the wait the NEXT line points at); the clause before the others reads `; also waiting, which
the command prints before it:` when the command printed all of them first, or `; also waiting (the command prints
the first K of these before it):` (`the first of these` for one) when it printed only some first. No `wait(s)`,
no numeral for one, and no place word: the others follow on the same line. F9 and F46 describe one clause and are
built once. Tests: `test_an_exclude_line_never_carries_its_folder_names_into_the_report` (with the middle case),
`test_the_loop_line_shows_the_wait_the_loop_stopped_on_not_the_first_one`.

**F20: the Installer section says whose install.out lines it embeds.** The `<details>` summary of the
install.out tail reads `(what the agent saw)` unless the Summary is kept to an attempt with a time and none of that
attempt's run headers is in the lines read: then `(earlier attempts' install.sh output: this attempt ran no
install.sh)` when install.log has no run of the attempt (a stopped copy), or `(... none of this attempt's runs is
in it)` when it has. The test is `_attempt_out_start`, shared with the Summary's `installer output:` line, which is
unchanged. Test: `test_the_summary_counts_the_installer_output_of_the_latest_attempts_runs_only`.

**F37: a run after the attempt's end line is named apart.** Amends the Summary's install line (K-series,
`install.sh: N install run(s) ... during this attempt`) and the time clause: `runs_for_attempt` and every outcome,
retry, first-sync and issue-link input are unchanged (the operator's `--confirm-install-agent` exit 3 then 0 is
still judged with the attempt). When some of the attempt's runs began after its latest `end | finished` line, the
install line reads `N install run(s) (+L --list-folders) for this attempt, K install run(s) [and J --list-folders
run(s)] after its end line (<time>)` (each kind counted apart) instead of `during this attempt`, and the time clause sums only the runs inside it into the step times and adds
`after its end line: install Ns` (or `--list-folders Ns`), so no run is summed beside a session time that does not
cover it. Tests: `test_an_install_run_after_the_attempts_end_line_is_named_apart`,
`test_an_install_run_that_failed_before_the_one_that_ended_0_is_worked_with_help`.
Amended 2026-10-13, §16.64 G32: N and L count only the runs inside the end line, and the line reads `N install
run(s) (+L --list-folders) during this attempt and K install run(s) [and J --list-folders run(s)] after its end line
(<time>)` (`no install run during this attempt and …` when none is inside); "for this attempt, K …" read as one run
more than there was.

**F38: the report install.sh writes says its run time is before its report step.** install.sh's `on_exit`
writes a provisional `end rc=N seconds=S` line, runs the report, and only then logs the report step and the final
end line, whose seconds include the report. A run is provisional only when it is the newest run in install.log,
`AGENTSYNC_REPORT_RUN` names it, it has no `step=report` line, and its end line is the log's last line
(`setup_report._provisional`); its status then reads `exit N after Ss, before its report step` in the Installer
section, the run list and the Summary's install line, and the total reads `(runs with an end line; this run's
report step not counted)`. A `--report-only` report, and any later read, see the final line and are unchanged.
install.sh is unchanged. Test: `test_the_report_install_sh_writes_says_its_run_time_is_before_its_report_step`.

**F39: the doctor line names the checks install.sh's doctor printed that the report's does not.** Read with
§16.39 N16 and Q26 (round 4 left its install.sh half unbuilt). In the attempt's last install run's install.out
lines, the `[warn]` and `[FAIL]` checks printed before the run's first `sync:` or `first sync:` line that the
report's own doctor does not report add `· install.sh's doctor before its first sync (run <id>): N warn not in this
one: <check>, ...`, and the counts are labelled `(K checks, run when this report was written)`. It states the
difference and never a cause ("cleared by its first sync" is not provable: a `--report-only` report can follow
later syncs or an `exclude-empty`). An older run's warns, warns after the sync line and a check the report's doctor
still gives (already under `yours` or `unexpected`) are not named, nor a warn the report reads as expected before
the agents are installed (a LaunchAgent the same run's agent step installs: `(installed by the agent step
below)`); a run whose first sync did not run (`result` not `done`) names nothing; with none, the line is
unchanged. Test:
`test_the_doctor_line_names_the_checks_install_shs_doctor_printed_that_this_one_does_not`.

**F52: an alarm that names agentsync's full path keeps its words.** Amends the install.out tail and Recent
errors scrub (`_scrub_segment`), read with Q49: every path test reads the segment with `~/.local/bin/agentsync`
turned into the bare word and logger names dropped (`_probe`), while the substitutions still run on the original
text, so the output keeps the full path. Before, the binary's `/` read as an item path and the deletion breaker,
secret-scan purge and credential-page alarms became `alarm: ... <path>`, losing the command they name. A segment
that names an item path beside the binary is still `<path>`. Test:
`test_a_sync_alarm_that_names_agentsyncs_full_path_is_kept_whole`.

**F23: a prefixed step 1 error after a header is another session's.** Amends Q21 (§16.52) in
`setup_report.parse_friction` and install.sh's `FRICTION_AWK`: the `prompt vN, <agent>:` prefix is written only
before `--log-start`, which writes the `Attempt:`, `Prompt:` and `Agent:` header, so a session that wrote a header
never writes one. A prefixed step 1 error therefore starts a new header-less attempt whenever the open attempt has a
header (or an `Attempt:` line), whatever the gap and in the same words (probes P8: a finished attempt, the error 2
minutes on; P3b: an open one, 30 seconds on). The version, agent and gap rules now apply only after a header-less
attempt with stated words. In awk, `track()` sets `HD` on every header line Python keeps (`Prompt:`, `Agent:`,
`Outcome:`, `Run:`, a `Prompt:` with no number included), an `Attempt:` line, `restate()` and a new attempt clear it
(Python's empty header), and a stated line after it is new; so
`friction_earlier_end` prints the finished attempt's end time and section 3 does not send its patch again. Tests:
`test_a_prefixed_step_1_error_after_a_finished_attempt_is_reported_as_its_own`,
`test_a_step_1_error_with_another_sessions_words_leaves_an_attempt_with_no_end_line`,
`test_a_header_less_step_1_error_states_its_prompt_and_agent`,
`test_a_prefixed_step_1_error_after_a_headed_attempt_is_another_sessions`,
`test_the_installer_and_the_report_end_a_stopped_attempt_at_the_same_line`,
`test_the_installer_and_the_report_split_the_same_attempts_after_any_header`. (**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G72:** F23 amends §16.28's
`friction_attempt_stopped` rule as well, which a dated line there says. **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G64:** "or an
`Attempt:` line" does not hold alone: `orphan()` returns before that check unless the attempt has a header (a
`Prompt:` or `Agent:` line) or stated words, and `track()` clears `HD` on an `Attempt:` line, so an attempt with an
`Attempt:` line and no header keeps the error (measured with `parse_friction`). `--log-start` writes the three lines
together, so only a hand-written or cut header meets it; setup-feedback.md says "a header". **Amended 2026-10-13,
§16.73 H64:** a header is a `Prompt:`, `Agent:`, `Outcome:` or `Run:` line (`setup_report.FRICTION_KEYS`, and
`track()`'s `HD` in install.sh), as §16.64 G51 says; the last two appear only in a v4 log.)

**F14: bring-back.md fences each file it embeds.** In install.sh's `write_bring_back`, the setup report
(section 1) and fix-request.md (section 2) each sit inside a tilde fence with the info string `markdown`, and the
local-work patches (section 3) inside one with `diff`, each fence longer than any tilde run that starts a line of
what it holds, and at least 10 tildes (`fence_for`, `embed`; a file without a final newline gets one before the
closing fence). Outside the fences the file's only headings are its title and its three numbered sections; the
embedded H1s and H2s no longer outrank or match them. No heading is rewritten, so every embedded byte is kept and
section 2 still compares line for line (the triage rule's dated line). Not a three-tilde fence: the report's own
`~~~text` blocks would close it. Test: `test_the_bring_back_file_fences_each_file_it_embeds`.

**F40: the Configuration counts the source excludes beyond agentsync's own.** Read with Q31's counts-only rule
and Q71 (`exclude-empty`): after the `[policy]` line, `- source excludes beyond agentsync's own: <label> N (K folder
glob(s)), ...; 0 on the other M source(s) (globs not shown; an excluded folder is not mirrored if it later gains
files)`, or `none`, over the local and inbox sources, counting `exclude` entries not in `_SHIPPED_EXCLUDES`; a
folder glob is one that starts and ends with `/` (the form `exclude-empty` writes). A source is named by its
evidence label (`_Labels`); never a glob's text, a folder name or a glob's depth. Once the next walk prunes an
excluded folder, the Empty cloud folders part says `none`, so this line is where the lasting change shows. The

`SHIPPED_EXCLUDES`; a source is `(source N)` by its place). Tests:
`test_configuration_counts_the_source_excludes_beyond_agentsyncs_own`,
`test_the_shell_report_counts_the_source_excludes_beyond_agentsyncs_own`.

**F93: the joined-word rule reads every word the report prints.** Amends Q72 (§16.52): the words a fuzzy value
of two or more words may spell run together are `setup_report.report_words()`, which holds `_JOINED_WORDS` and
every lower-case word of 3 or more letters in the module's own string literals, read from its source when first
asked (docstrings and comments left out: their examples, such as `janedoe`, name what is redacted). A word the
report's text gains is in it with no list to keep. "In Stall" now leaves `install.sh`, `the install log` and
`INSTALL` alone and still redacts `InStall`, `in-stall` and `In Stall`; a non-word join (`janedoe`) is redacted as
before. The bare one-case join is the dictionary word, so leaving it reveals nothing (Q72's reasoning). install.sh's
`name_forms` reads `report_word`: `joined_word` (still equal to `_JOINED_WORDS`) or a word on install.sh's own lines
that are not comments, read from the file itself (`SELF_FILE`; `SELF` is the display form, `~/...` under the home). Tests: `test_a_joined_name_that_spells_any_report_word_leaves_the_word_alone`,
`test_the_shell_report_leaves_any_report_word_a_name_spells_alone`, `test_the_shell_joined_word_list_is_the_reports`.

**F42, F55: a one-word organisation that is a report word is matched only in folder and domain names.** Amends
§16.46 "Kept as they are" (dated line there). Every CloudStorage entry, symlinks and non-folders included, and every
configured path's provider still registers its organisation, so nothing that might name the tenant prints (Q33's
symlink note and the Environment line print every entry). When the organisation is one word and in

which would also match hyphenated prose. F42 and F55 describe one defect and are built once. Tests:
`test_a_one_word_organisation_that_is_a_report_word_is_matched_only_in_folder_and_domain_names`,
`test_a_cloudstorage_entry_named_like_a_report_word_keeps_the_reports_words`,
`test_the_shell_report_keeps_the_word_a_one_word_organisation_spells`,
`test_the_shell_report_sends_a_report_with_a_word_named_folder_privately` (F92's shell half).
Amended 2026-10-13, §16.64 G45 (with G46, G75): `context` mode is for the one-word organisations in
`_CONTEXT_ORG_WORDS` only (link, data, group, shared, issue, report, domain, folder, files, docs, team, work, home,

at interpolation, is a broad change to `_redact_lines`' callers and is not built. The finder's "Send it" example

### 16.59 Round 5: installer and the shell report (2026-10-12, wave B13 round 5 lane RB)

Lane RB of B13 round 5 (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 5"): fourteen items, each built from its
verifier's corrected fix. F5 and F15 are one defect, built once; F16 and lane RA's F7 are one defect in one awk,
built here.

#### The shell fallback report

- **Run ids without their process id** (F5, F15). `strip_run_pids` runs before `redact_stream` and cuts `-<pid>`
  from `run=<YYYYMMDD>T<HHMMSS>Z-<pid>` only, in the Installer tail and in Recent errors alike, as
  `setup_report._PID_SUFFIX_RE` does; the Installer lead-in says "(run ids without their process id)".
  `test_the_shell_report_shows_run_ids_without_their_process_id`.
  Amended 2026-10-16, §16.98 N21: runs started in one second are numbered over the whole of install.log in its order,
  the first keeping the bare stamp (`<stamp>.2`, `.3`), in both readers; `strip_run_pids` is an awk that reads
  install.log first. The Python lead-in adds `, numbered .2 on for runs started in one second` when one is shown.
- **The `--report-only` install.sh line** (F29, F30). No install log reads `no install log (no install run on
  this Mac)`, and the Python report's `- install.sh: no install log` matches it; a log with no install run keeps
  `no install run in the install log`. A last run that started before the friction log's latest attempt began
  (`friction_attempt_begin`: the begin `parse_friction` gives, by `FRICTION_AWK`) reads `no install run during
  this attempt (began <UTC>); the last one, started <UTC>, <exit or no end line>`. Run start against attempt begin,
  never against the run's end. `test_the_shell_report_only_gives_the_last_install_runs_exit`,
  `test_the_shell_report_only_says_the_last_install_run_was_before_this_attempt`,
  `test_failure_before_the_installer_is_the_errors_step`.
- **CloudStorage** (F56). Providers are folders only (`-type d`, the OneDrive count too); symlinks and other
  entries are added as `and N symlink(s)`, `and N other entry(ies)` only when there are any, as
  `setup_report.cloud` counts since §16.53 Q33. `test_the_shell_report_counts_cloud_folders_apart_from_links_and_files`.
- **gitleaks** (F58). The line names the path `remember_gitleaks` recorded in
  `~/Library/Application Support/agentsync/gitleaks-path` first, when it is an absolute executable file, then
  PATH, then the fixed places: `lints.gitleaks_lookup`'s order.
  `test_the_shell_report_names_the_gitleaks_the_secret_scan_can_use`.
- **Source ids** (F6). Every `id` inside a `[[source]]` table of sources.toml is `<source-N>` (N: the table's
  place), a whole word with `-` as no word character, so `exclude-empty <id>` is matched; an id in
  `GENERIC_SOURCE_IDS` (equal to `setup_report._GENERIC_IDS`) is kept unless its path is under CloudStorage.
  The Redaction text names it. `test_the_shell_report_redacts_a_configured_source_id`,
  `test_the_python_report_redacts_a_configured_source_id`, `test_the_shell_generic_source_ids_are_the_reports`.

#### A stopped copy

- **The quoted earlier run** (F16, F7): see the dated line under §16.53's "A stopped copy's report"; the
  earlier run's quoted `NEXT: review ... bring-back.md and copy ...` line goes into the same marker line, which
  reads `(an earlier run's bring-back, issue link and NEXT lines are left out of this report)`.
  `test_the_real_report_of_a_stopped_copy_invites_no_bring_back` seeds install.out with a full run's end;
  `_sends_nothing` holds both writers to no `issues/new`, no `bring back: ` line and no "Read the report before
  sending it".
  Amended 2026-10-13, §16.65 G14: the marker reads `(an earlier run's bring-back and issue link lines are left
  out of this report)` and the NEXT line is kept; install.out never holds a `--report-only` run's NEXT.
  Amended 2026-10-17, §16.115 Q75 (by §16.105 O70): the marker now reads `(earlier runs' bring-back and issue
  link lines are left out of this report)`, since its lines can span runs.
- **A newer copy** (F17). `--log-start` with a version above `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT` reads its own checkout's
  upstream branch and that remote's URL, origin's when there is no upstream (git, read-only, only with the
  developer tools; `newer_copy_fix`). Following main of the canonical repository: the copy came from another
  branch or a fork, so copy it again from the README. Following anything else: point the checkout at main (or
  move it aside so step 1 clones it), then paste the same prompt. Git cannot say: both sentences. An older or
  unnamed copy is told what it was before, word for word. Only stderr names the checkout's path and the remote
  (without user or token); the friction line's fix, read back by `friction_attempt_stopped` for the stopped
  `NEXT:`, says the same without them, since the friction log and install.out reach the report and a fork
  owner's login or a company mirror's host is nothing the redaction knows. The `NEXT:` repeats only a fix of the
  shapes this installer writes; any other text in that column gets the copy-again sentence.
  `test_a_copy_newer_than_the_checkout_is_told_what_fixes_it`.
  **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G15:** the prompt's own stop said "copy the prompt again" at every such stop, so
  when the checkout was the cause the person got two orders on one screen. Since v15 the agent tells the person
  what the error says, in its words, and says to copy the prompt again only when there is no such error.
  **Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J66 (by §16.72 H65):** since v16 it also gives the checkout sentence whenever the error's
  words do not already mention this Mac's checkout, since installers v8 to v14 answer a newer copy with "copy the
  prompt again" alone.
- **Wording** (F18). The note and the `NEXT:` say "a copy of the setup prompt that does not match this
  installer". `test_a_stopped_newer_copy_is_not_called_out_of_date`.

#### Parity of the friction readers (F54)

`FRICTION_AWK` (C locale) and `parse_friction` read a step 1 line's `prompt vN, <agent>:` alike: both drop
straight and curly quotes, lower ASCII letters only, collapse blanks and tabs only, read ASCII digits only
(`_STEP1_STATED_RE` is `re.ASCII`), and read at most 100 characters of agent (awk counts UTF-8 characters). The
header lines too: `Prompt:`'s version in ASCII digits, and a no-break space around `Agent:`'s value trimmed.
`test_the_installer_and_the_report_end_a_stopped_attempt_at_the_same_line` adds nine logs: curly quotes, an
accented capital, no-break spaces, long agents and Arabic-Indic digits.

#### Smaller items

- **`SELF`** (F53): `~/` then the `%q` of the rest, so the slash after the `~` is never inside a `$'..'` that
  bash 3.2 would not expand. `test_a_tilde_command_runs_whatever_bytes_the_checkout_path_holds`.
- **The not-on-PATH note** (F51) says the setup and its NEXT lines call agentsync by its full path,
  `~/.local/bin/agentsync`, the form those lines print. `test_no_shell_profile_advice_and_no_uv_path_hint`.
- **`waited-for-the-lock` alone** (F59): the note a first sync that printed no counts leaves reads ", after
  waiting for another sync to end" in the Summary, its counts from install.out, never the raw token.
  `test_first_sync_clause_says_the_sync_waited_for_another`.

### 16.60 Round 5: converters, .msg stubs and speech (2026-10-12, wave B13 round 5 lane E)

Builds round 5's converter, `.msg` stub and speech items (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 5"). F33 and
F99 describe one defect, as do F63 and F74; each pair is built once.

**A withheld `.msg` says it is a binary one (F33, F99; amends §16.51 Q27).** Under a label rule msg-mime reads the
label of a `.msg` that holds MIME text, so the stub's summary and body now say `the label of a binary
(Outlook-format) .msg file, or of a .msg not on this Mac, cannot be read` (one not on this Mac is withheld unread,
F73). An image's words are unchanged. The stored reason `no converter for
.msg` and the `withheld by label rule` prefix are unchanged (the setup report, re-reads and stub identity key on
them). Pinned by `tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_msg_is_read_and_under_a_label_rule_its_page_becomes_a_stub`.

**A withheld stub names no converter (F36).** Its front matter reads `converter: none@0`
(`convert.NO_CONVERTER_ID` and `convert.NO_CONVERTER_VERSION`, now public) and carries no
`options_hash`, as a withheld image's does; the output row keeps the converter whose refusal settles it (msg-mime
for a binary `.msg`, Q78), which `_lacks` and `_reread_targets` read. Pinned by
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_binary_msg_stubs_under_a_label_rule_settle_and_never_stop_another_files_reread`.

**Every rendering reaches a `no converter` stub (F63, F74; amends §16.51 Q75).** `Cycle._stub_again` returned
`_no_converter`'s result for such a stub, which is None once a converter claims the name, so the one-time
re-render skipped every binary `.msg` stub under a rule; the re-read that follows only moves its key. It now
rebuilds the result from the stored reason and the output row's converter fields whenever the name-only refusal is
None or names another converter than the row: the page gets the current rendering with the hashes the page
already has (a stub made from the name has none, and a later rendering must not differ by them alone), and the
row's converter stays, so a stub made before msg-mime is still read again once and one msg-mime settled is not. `publish.STUB_RENDER`
is 3 (F33, F36). Pinned by `tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_binary_msg_stub_from_an_older_rendering_is_rendered_again_once_under_a_label_rule`
(a stub made before msg-mime, and one msg-mime made).

**Credential and path stubs are rendered again too (F94; amends §16.51 Q75).** Their page is made from the name,
the path, the reason and the hashes alone, so `_stub_again` rebuilds them from their own page as any other stub;
only a redacted item is skipped. The page's own hashes are kept (`mark_quarantined_rescreen` may have cleared the
row's earlier in the same run). Pinned by
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_credential_or_path_stub_from_an_older_rendering_is_rendered_again_once` (also with
the secret-scan rules moved in the same run). So only a redacted stub, and a tombstone until it is reaped, keeps a heading above
the banner; §16.61's F88 line, written beside this, still names credential and path stubs.
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.73 H54 (by §16.66 G76):** "only a redacted item is skipped" no longer holds: a redacted
stub is rendered again once too, its re-plan redacted from the stored redaction, and since §16.66 G77 an old
tombstone as well, so no stub or tombstone agentsync can rebuild keeps a heading above the banner.

**A `.msg` that reading means a download for is withheld by its name (F73; amends §16.54 Q78).** Under a label rule
`Cycle._no_converter` refuses a `.msg` by its name, as before Q78, when it is online-only or a Graph item, unless
`materialise PATH` names it (that asks for the download); a `DatalessRefusedError` on a `.msg` under a rule
publishes that stub in the same run instead of deferring, and the next fetch is tried again as any other.
`_keeps_page` never keeps a `.msg` page under a rule. So a page from before a
new rule does not stay up until the bytes can be fetched. A `.msg` on this Mac is still read, and a MIME one gets
its page. Cost: a MIME `.msg` that lives only on a Graph source is not read under a rule, as an image is not.
Pinned by `tests/test_cycle.py::test_under_a_new_label_rule_a_msg_the_os_will_not_hydrate_is_withheld_at_once`
and `tests/test_cycle.py::test_under_a_new_label_rule_an_online_only_msg_is_withheld_with_no_download`.

**A save that only changes a label is screened (F72; closes §16.11 C15 req 29).** H1 leaves the label parts out
(`docProps/*`, `docMetadata/LabelInfo.xml`), so a label-only save was touched, not changed, and returned before
any screen; since §16.54 Q76 that held for `.potx`, `.vsdx` and `.vsdm` as well as Office documents. Under a label
rule `_after_fetch` now runs `policy.screen_file` on touched bytes of a label-capable name (`_relabelled`) and
converts them when its label refusal differs from what the pages stand for (a label refusal stub's stored reason,
or none for a page). H1, and so purge suppression, is unchanged: folding `policy.label_fingerprint` into H1 would
let a relabelled copy of purged content escape its purge. Pinned by
`tests/test_review_fixes.py::test_a_save_that_only_adds_an_excluded_label_withholds_the_page` (`.potx`, `.vsdx`,
`.pptx`, and lifting the exclusion restores the page) and
`tests/test_review_fixes.py::test_a_purged_template_that_is_relabelled_stays_suppressed`.

**Comments and docs say binary `.msg` (F76).** msg.py's module doc, `cycle._LABEL_CAPABLE`, publish's withheld
comment, setup-feedback.md and a test docstring said `.msg` has no converter under a rule; they now say a binary
one, and that msg-mime reads a MIME one. Dated lines at §16.42 and §16.48 R87; §7's line is §16.61's (lane P
taught the routing test to read a "with a label rule" clause).

**A template's fixed text is de-duplicated a shape at a time (F77; amends §16.54 Q77).** `pptx._fixed_blocks`

renamed `test_a_proxy_git_scopes_to_fluidinference_on_github_routes_the_seed`, and

**Tombstones written before Q9 (F68).** Docs only: such a tombstone keeps its heading-first layout until it is

### 16.61 Round 5: setup prompt v14 and docs (2026-10-12, wave B13 round 5 lane P)

The B13 round 5 items of lane P (specs `round5/items/F<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built). Five need
prompt text (F24 to F28), so the prompt is **setup prompt v14**: `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, `PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's
`prompt v14` and `setup-prompt-compat 14`, the issue form's placeholder and the block's digest move together; a
saved v13 copy is stopped at step 1 like every older copy. v14 moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry
and is read with v7's rules. None adds a command, flag, installer option, config key or friction kind.

**The git stop's proxy hint names every source** (F24; amends §16.55 Q25 by a dated line). "If git's error names a
host other than github.com, check that setting" sent a person whose terminal holds a stale `HTTPS_PROXY` to git's
`http.proxy`, which prints nothing. A stale `HTTPS_PROXY`, `https_proxy` or `ALL_PROXY` fails exactly as git's own
setting does (`Could not resolve proxy: <its host>`, git 2.54, measured by the verifier), so the error alone cannot
tell them apart. The quote now says the host "is a proxy git was told to use, either by git's own setting, which git
config --get-urlmatch http.proxy https://github.com prints and which wins, or by the terminal's HTTPS_PROXY,
https_proxy or ALL_PROXY, which env | grep -i proxy shows". `--get-urlmatch` also prints a proxy scoped to that URL
(`[http "https://github.com"] proxy`), which `--get http.proxy` misses (measured in the lane's review). It stays one
quote for the person; the agent runs neither command. Test:
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py` (`test_readme_step1_is_one_command`).
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G73:** since v15 the host "git was told to use" is "either as a URL rewrite, which
`git config --get-regexp 'url\..*insteadof'` prints, or as a proxy", and the terminal's variables include

command is in code marks, and the person runs them, not the agent.

above also printed `pushinsteadof` keys, which never change a fetch or pull URL.

with no report" by a dated line). "Two cases have no report ... Every other stop still ends with the report" came

**The heading rule has step 3's exception** (F26; amends §16.43 H5 by a dated line). "Write that heading even when

### 16.62 Round 6: purge and cycle alarms (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 6 lane A)

Round 6 lane A of B13 (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 6"): G30, G36, G38 and G58. No command, flag or
config key.

**A label-escalation purge stays queued while its file is published again** (G30; extends §16.44 and §16.50 Q45's
kept upstream deletions). The cycle queues a `label-escalation` purge when a published file becomes refused. Take
the label out of `[policy]` (or the label off the file) and the next sync publishes it again, but the entry stayed
runnable: the loop still waited for `purge --queue`, and running it erased the current page and added the file to
the suppressions, so it never synced again. `governance._kept_why` now judges both reasons in
`governance.KEPT_REASONS` (`upstream-deleted`, `label-escalation`) by the same rule: a row the selector names (the
queued id, or the id it is an alias of) that is live or online-only keeps the entry queued. A refused row is not
listed, so with the rule back the same entry is runnable again, and `enqueue_purge` dedups the one the cycle
queues. Its note reads ``stays queued: the label policy no longer refuses the file and its page is current again
(N row(s)); running it would erase that page and stop the file syncing. `purge --queue` skips it while the file is
published, and runs it if the policy refuses the file again; `~/.local/bin/agentsync purge path=<its path> --source
<its source>` erases it anyway``. `partition_purges` and `run_purge_queue` (through `_kept_queued`, formerly
`_kept_upstream_deletion`) apply it; DLP, erasure and operator entries are still never judged. The loop, status,
doctor and STATE.md print the kept entries through `governance.kept_lines(kept)`: one `<count> <note>` per reason,
`KEPT_PURGES` for upstream deletions and `KEPT_ESCALATIONS` for label escalations (``label-escalation purge(s) stay
queued while the label policy lets their file publish again: `~/.local/bin/agentsync purge --queue` skips them,
since running one would erase a current page; if the policy refuses the file again, they wait for it like any
queued purge``). A kept escalation is a note, never a wait. The setup report's Purge queue counts a kept
escalation with the kept upstream deletions, and its "still listed" line names both. Test:
`tests/test_review_fixes.py` (`test_a_label_escalation_purge_stays_queued_while_the_policy_publishes_its_file_again`).
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.139 V89 (by §16.131 U71): the note's count reads `N rows` (`1 row`).

**The lock-wait WARNING names no host, and the report keeps a fixed stage word** (G36). `lock._describe_holder`,
which LockHeldError, the cycle's `another sync is running (...)` WARNING and doctor print, no longer appends `on
<host>`: the lock is a local flock, so the holder is always this Mac, and the name reached the terminal and the
chat for nothing. The holder sidecar keeps `host`. The fixed stage words are `ops.lock.Stage` (`acquired`,
`secrets`, `curate`, `surface`, `land-gate`, `commit`, `retention`, `recordings`), which `beat` is called with;
`setup_report._scrub_item_paths` leaves a quoted value whole only when it is one of them right after `stage `.
A stage built from a source id (`source:<id>`, `work:<id>`, `fetch <id>`) is no fixed word and is still
`'<path>'`, and so is a fixed word quoted anywhere else (a folder named `commit`). Tests:
`tests/test_ops_lock.py` (`test_the_holder_description_names_no_host`), `tests/test_setup_report.py`
(`test_the_lock_wait_warning_keeps_a_fixed_stage_word_and_redacts_a_source_stage`).

**One label-escalation alarm per source** (G38). Each escalated file appended its own alarm, word for word the same
and naming no file, under a WARNING that printed the raw stable id and said "purge queued" even when the purge was
already queued. The source's accumulator now keeps a running tally (files, cached conversions removed, purges
queued) and one alarm, replaced in place: ``label escalation: N published file(s) now refused by the label policy;
R cached conversion(s) deleted; Q purge(s) queued[, A already queued] <_PURGE_QUEUE_STEPS>`` (the queued clause
is left out when Q is 0; the preview steps stay). The per-file line is INFO (`sync -v`), names the path and says
`purge queued` or `purge already queued`; the stable id is logged at DEBUG only. Test: `tests/test_review_fixes.py`
(`test_a_relabelled_folder_raises_one_label_escalation_alarm_that_counts_its_files`; `test_sg04`'s suffix now
reads `1 purge(s) queued (preview ...)`).

**The F35 re-screen count drops a condition that was always true** (G58). In `cycle._after_fetch`, `rescreen`
requires `not reread` and `again` is `reread and same`, so `if rescreen and not again:` was `if rescreen:`; it now
reads so, with the invariant in a comment. No behavior changes, so no test can fail without it
(`test_a_policy_rescreen_is_counted_apart_on_the_sync_line` pins the counts and passes before and after).

WAITING ON YOU line about <id> ...`; no count (the setup report) or more keeps `each`. Tests:

`test_status_points_the_heartbeat_at_a_wait_only_while_the_loop_has_it`.

flag and `counts_as_listed=listed`. F69's counter is unchanged. Test:

branch is removed; see the dated line under §16.57 F69. Test: `test_heartbeat_incomplete_fix_by_source_kind`.

Wave B13 round 6, lane RA: 19 items (`~/.cache/agentsync-bring-back/b13/round6/items/G<n>.md`, lanes in
`round6/lanes.json`), each built to its verifier's corrected fix with a test that fails without it, or left with a

**G3: the Redaction count line in two sentences.** Amends §16.40's count-line sentence (dated line there): "Numbered

**G41: a stored-as note that redacts to one form is shown once.** add-source's `(<typed>, stored as <path>)` note

**G51: an Attempt: line alone is not a header.** parse_friction's F23 rule (§16.58) reads a stated step 1 error as
another session's after a header (a Prompt:, Agent:, Outcome: or Run: line), whatever the gap; an `Attempt:` line
alone is not one, as install.sh's awk has it. The `cur["started"]` clause that said otherwise never fired (started
is set only by an Attempt: line, which clears the stated words the rule needs) and is gone; behaviour is unchanged,
