`test_an_attempt_line_alone_keeps_a_stated_step_1_error_in_its_attempt`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.86 L26: the error still stays in that attempt, and now states its words: an attempt with no
header reads them from its first stated step 1 error, wherever it sits.

**G56: the withheld legend names a .msg not on this Mac.** The same defect as lane E's G62 (§16.66), which landed
first in `1a37b7ec` with this item's fix (the legend, setup-feedback.md's Quarantine row, the `_LABEL_WITHHELD` and
`label_withheld_suffixes` docstrings); this lane builds nothing more for it. Test:
`test_a_msg_or_image_under_a_label_rule_is_withheld_not_missing_a_converter`.

**G12: the issue title names the attempt's own step.** `Outcome.title_label` is `Failed at step N (<the step's name
in the attempt's own prompt layout>)` for a failed step that layout has, else `form_label`; `build_issue_url` takes

report)` (KISS K16b), so old and new links stay valid options and triage counts stay in one bucket. v6 titles are

layout>)`, as its Summary does; its `outcome` field stays `Failed at step 1 (preflight)`.

later version with v7's layout until one adds an entry. A v5 title names v5's own step number and name too (its step 3 is `install and start`, which
the field files as step 2).

**G20: a newer copy's cause comes from the installer's fix column.** The Summary's prompt clause for a copy newer than
the installer no longer always blames the checkout. install.sh's error line says `this checkout is older than the
prompt` in every newer-copy case; only its fix column (`newer_copy_fix`) names the cause, and the report matches its
fixed words and shows its own: `(newer than the installer's vN: this Mac's checkout follows main, so the pasted copy
came from another branch or a fork)` for a checkout on the repository's main, `(newer than the installer's vN: this
Mac's checkout follows another remote or branch)` for a fix that starts `point this Mac's checkout at main of`, and
`(newer than the installer's vN)` otherwise (no upstream, an older installer, an empty column). The column itself is
never shown. Test: `test_an_attempt_a_stopped_copy_of_the_prompt_started_says_so_in_the_summary`.

**G23: an attempt that stopped for the folder answer is "stopped", not "failed".** `compute_outcome` gives kind
`stopped`, step 1, when the attempt has no install run, no error and no end line and every event is a step 1
`deviation`: the session stopped where the prompt says to wait. Its text is `stopped at step 1 (waiting for the folder
answer)` when a deviation's words mention the folder answer or waiting, else `stopped at step 1 (a deviation, no
install run and no error)`; its why is `no install.sh run and no error; step 1 logged only a deviation (F<n>)`. The
issue form has no such option, so `form_label` gives step 1's `Failed at step 1 (preflight)`. An error, an install
run, an end line or a later step keeps `failed`. Seen in the Summary's `- attempt: N of N (earlier: …)` and the
friction section's attempt lines. Test: `test_an_attempt_that_only_stopped_for_the_folder_answer_is_stopped_not_failed`.
Amended 2026-10-13, §16.69 H40: step 1 may also log `question`, `click`, `approval` and `prompt` lines beside its
deviation; the wait is read from the deviations alone, and the why then reads `step 1 logged a deviation (F<n>), <N
kind(s)> and nothing else`. Amended 2026-10-13, §16.69 H42: the issue title says `Stopped at step 1 (…)`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.92 M31: the Summary's line is `- attempt: N of N; earlier: …`, so an outcome's own note
bracket is the line's only one.

**G27: the origin/main clause dates the checkout's last fetch.** The run metadata's `install source` line ends `on
origin/main: <yes|no|unknown> (<fetch>)`, from one lstat of the checkout's FETCH_HEAD (no new network, no write):
`as of the checkout's last fetch, <UTC time>` when it holds data; `the checkout's last fetch, <UTC time>, failed;
origin/main is from an earlier fetch` when it is empty (git truncates it when a fetch or pull fails, and its time is
then the failed one's); `no fetch since the clone` when there is none (a clone writes none). A linked worktree has a
FETCH_HEAD of its own but shares origin/main, so it reads the newer of its own (`git rev-parse --git-path
FETCH_HEAD`) and the common one (`--git-common-dir`); one that cannot be read keeps `as of the checkout's last fetch`. The
friction log's step 1 error is not merged in: the empty file already carries that fact. Test:
`test_the_on_origin_main_line_dates_the_checkouts_last_fetch` (real `git pull`, against a missing path for the
failure).

**G32: the runs after the end line are not counted twice.** Amends §16.58 F37 (dated line there): the install line's
first count holds only the runs inside the attempt's end line, `N install run(s) (+L --list-folders) during this
attempt and K install run(s) [and J --list-folders run(s)] after its end line (<time>)`, or `no install run during
this attempt and …`; "the last exit" still names the last run overall, and the outcome, retry and time logic are
unchanged. Tests: `test_an_install_run_after_the_attempts_end_line_is_named_apart`,
`test_an_install_run_that_failed_before_the_one_that_ended_0_is_worked_with_help`.

**G34: one bracket in the first-sync clause.** Amends §16.58 F8, F32 (dated line there): the first-read clause
follows `read again R` after a colon and the unreadable/failed split after `; `, so the source tag stays the clause's
one trailing bracket, as on every other line: `converted 2, deferred 0 online-only, read again 2: 2 of them read for
the first time, also in the converted count; of the converted: 1 unreadable, 0 failed (install.log; the first-read
count and the unreadable/failed split: install.out)`; with no re-read, `online-only; of the converted: …`. Test:
`test_first_sync_clause_carries_the_read_again_count` (no `) (` in the line).

**G45, G46, G75: a context-mode organisation is a generic word, matched only after an app's name.** One defect from
three finders, built once. Amends §16.58 F42, F55 and F92 (dated lines there). F42's `context` mode matched after
any letter or digit and a hyphen, so an organisation named like a report word was replaced inside the report's own
hyphenated words (`~/agent-<org-1>/docs`, `first-<org-2>`, `--log-<org-2>`, `setup-<org-1>.md`) where anyone can
read it back, with no `Private only:`; and it covered all of `report_words()` (1,081 words; the shell's 863 code
tokens), so a tenant named like any of them (`Status`, `Probe`) printed bare in a sentence. Now:
- `context` mode is for a one-word organisation in `_CONTEXT_ORG_WORDS` only: data, docs, domain, files, folder,
  group, home, issue, link, links, report, shared, sync, team, work (generic words no plausible tenant uses as its
  whole name; not `_JOINED_WORDS`, which holds brand-like words such as shell, signal and origin). install.sh's
  `context_org_word` holds the same list and its organisation rule reads it instead of `report_word`; `report_word`
  stays for the joined-name rule (F93) and the shell's private-only rule.
- It matches after a CloudStorage app's name as a whole word (`(?<=(?<![A-Za-z0-9])OneDrive-)`, so `inbox-` is no
  `Box-`): the heads of this Mac's entries and configured sources (`Redactor.set_app_heads`, set where
  `r.provider_heads` is) with `_CONTEXT_HEADS` (OneDrive, SharedLibraries, Dropbox, Box, GoogleDrive, Egnyte). The
  `Drive - ` forms and the domain lookahead are unchanged.
- Any other one-word organisation is fuzzy, matched everywhere; one that is a report word (`Status`, `Context`,
  `Agent`) goes into `_word_named`, so the Redaction section says `Private only:` (F92), and its name never prints.
  `~/agent-context` then reads `~/agent-<org-N>` in that private report; that is the cost F42's verifier ranked
  below a leak.
  Amended 2026-10-13, §16.69 H74: agentsync's own path names after a slash (`agent-context`, `agent-context-sync`,
  case-sensitive, to a path boundary) are held whole, as the repository locator is, so `~/agent-context` stays;
  the organisation is replaced everywhere else and the report stays private only.
Known difference: a word that is only an install.sh code token (a local variable's name) is replaced everywhere in
both reports, but only the shell report adds `Private only:`, because its `report_word` reads every code token. Narrowing that vocabulary to
printed text would also change the joined-name rule (F93), which the verifier warned against; it over-warns and
leaks nothing, so it is not built. Tests:
`test_a_context_organisation_is_matched_only_after_an_app_name_and_only_for_a_generic_word`,
`test_a_report_word_organisation_never_prints_and_a_generic_one_keeps_the_reports_words`,
`test_the_shell_context_org_word_list_is_the_reports`,
`test_the_shell_report_replaces_a_one_word_organisation_outside_the_generic_list_everywhere`.

**G48: a configured generic folder leaves the report public.** Amends §16.58 F92: a one-word folder or library
value in `_GENERIC_FOLDERS` (Documents, Desktop, Downloads, Pictures, ...; exact case, as the listing path's
exemption) is still redacted, but never raises `Private only:`: every OneDrive or Google Drive has one, so reading
`<folder-N>` back as the name gives nothing away. install.sh's `fallback_redaction` skips a `<folder-N>` pair whose
value is a `generic_folder` the same way, so the two reports agree (before, Documents made only the Python report
private, Downloads only the shell's). An organisation is unaffected; `Status` stays private. Tests:
`test_a_configured_generic_folder_leaves_the_report_public`,
`test_the_shell_report_leaves_a_report_with_a_generic_folder_public`.
Amended 2026-10-13, §16.70 H39: the skip covers every pair that shares a generic folder's placeholder, its slug
id (G8) included.

**G49: OneDrive's organisation stays <org-1> beside a custom-domain tenant.** Amends §16.58 F42: the custom-domain
`graph.tenant` is registered whole after the organisations, not before them, so the first CloudStorage entry's
organisation keeps `<org-1>` (the comment's "OneDrive's first" rule) and the domain, when a line names it, takes the
next number; it still never prints, in any case or inside a URL. Test:
`test_a_custom_domain_tenant_leaves_onedrives_organisation_org_1`.

### 16.65 Round 6: installer and the shell report (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 6 lane RB)

Round 6 findings (`round6/items/G<n>.md` of the bring-back cache) built in `scripts/install.sh`, each with a test in
`tests/test_install_oneshot.py`.

- **The plist-absent line names the full path** (G74, G78, one defect). The shell report's Background runs line
  for a job loaded from this home's plist path whose file is gone reads ``(removed without `launchctl bootout`;
  `~/.local/bin/agentsync install-agent` repairs it)``, as the agentsync report's does: the bare `agentsync`
  fails where `~/.local/bin` is not on PATH. The backticks are escaped in the `say` line, so bash prints them;
  unescaped they would run both commands. `$AGENTSYNC` is not used: it is empty when the fallback runs before
  step 2. `test_the_shell_report_names_another_installs_job_as_not_this_setups`.
- **A stopped copy's closing line is its own paragraph** (G18). `stopped_report_note` holds each blank line back
  until a line that is kept follows, so the blank before the dropped issue link was never printed and Markdown
  read `Not for sending: ...` into the Redaction part. Its END prints a blank line first, whichever line the
  input ended on. `_sends_nothing` checks the gap for both writers.
- **An earlier run's NEXT line stays** (G14). The marker that stands for an earlier run's quoted `bring back: `
  and issue link lines read `(an earlier run's bring-back, issue link and NEXT lines are left out of this
  report)` while the earlier run's NEXT was the very next line: the clause that dropped a NEXT naming
  `bring-back.md and copy` matched only a `--report-only` run's, and `start_capture` never writes one of those
  into install.out. The clause is gone and the marker reads `(an earlier run's bring-back and issue link lines
  are left out of this report)`. Dropping step 2's real NEXT instead would contradict the Installer section's
  count of NEXT lines in install.out. `test_the_real_report_of_a_stopped_copy_invites_no_bring_back` seeds
  install.out with a full run's real end and checks the line after the marker is that run's `NEXT: stop:`.
  Amended 2026-10-17, §16.115 Q75 (by §16.105 O70): the marker now reads `(earlier runs' bring-back and issue
  link lines are left out of this report)`, since its lines can span runs.
- **The install.out embed says what it quotes** (G16, G17). `stopped_report_note` reads the report twice. The
  first read counts the lines it leaves out between the embed's `<details><summary>the last N line(s) of ...`
  line and `</details>` (every line it drops or turns into the marker), and the second writes the count into
  that summary line before its last ` (`: `the last 60 line(s) of ~/agent-context/setup/install.out, 2 of them
  left out (...)`. The count is of install.out lines, so N is the fence's lines, less the marker, plus K. A
  summary line in another wording is left as it is. A stopped copy stops before step 2 reinstalls agentsync, so
  the first one after an update is rendered by the agentsync from before, whose embed always ends `(what the
  agent saw)`. Where the report's own Summary has `- installer output: no run of this attempt in the last `
  (the renderer's own F20 condition), that suffix becomes F20's `(earlier attempts' install.sh output: this
  attempt ran no install.sh)` when the Summary also has `- install.sh: no run during this attempt` or `- install.sh:
  no run in the install log`, else `(... none of this attempt's runs is in it)`; with this attempt's run in the
  tail the label stays. The issue's "the most common field case" overstates it: since v11 a stop that names the
  prompt as not the installer's goes to no report, so this comes from copies v10 and older, an agent that
  strays, or a hand-run `--report-only`. Tests: `test_a_stopped_copys_embed_counts_the_lines_it_leaves_out`,
  `test_a_stopped_copy_rendered_by_an_older_agentsync_says_whose_install_out_it_quotes` (the agentsync stub
  copies `STUB_REPORT_FILE`), and `test_the_real_report_of_a_stopped_copy_invites_no_bring_back`.
  Amended 2026-10-16, §16.99 N22: the count now ends the renderer's bracket (`(...; 2 of them left out: the
  bring-back and issue link lines)`), not before it.
- **A stopped copy's note and NEXT read in order** (G9, G19, one defect). The first line reads `> This report
  is of an attempt started by a copy of the setup prompt that does not match this installer: do not send it or
  bring it back.` and the NEXT starts the same way (the subject, verb and object were split by a relative
  clause). A newer copy's NEXT ended `... came from another branch or a fork (this installer is for setup
  prompt v14) (<path> was not touched: ...)`: two brackets in a row, the first read as part of the clause before
  it. The version now follows the installer, `... does not match this installer, which is for setup prompt v14,
  so do not send it or bring it back: <fix>`, and only the bring-back bracket follows the fix, where
  bring-back.md exists. Any other fix keeps the copy-again sentence with the version inside its own brackets.
  `test_a_stopped_newer_copys_next_says_its_version_once_and_of_the_installer`,
  `test_a_copy_newer_than_the_checkout_is_told_what_fixes_it`.
  Amended 2026-10-13, §16.70 H18: the bring-back bracket no longer follows the fix; it follows "bring it back".
- **A checkout with no upstream is said to have none** (G21). `newer_copy_fix` said `(git could not say which
  branch it follows)` of a checkout whose branch has no upstream, though git answered: there is none. Whether
  `@{u}` is empty cannot tell that from a configured upstream whose remote ref is missing (a narrowed fetch
  refspec, where `git pull --ff-only` still works through FETCH_HEAD), so the wording reads git's config
  instead, inside the same developer-tools guard: `git symbolic-ref -q --short HEAD` and `git config --get
  branch.<b>.merge`. With a remote URL and no `@{u}`: no branch is `(it is on no branch)`, a branch with no
  merge setting `(it follows no upstream branch)`, and anything else (no developer tools, no URL, a merge
  setting git cannot resolve) keeps `(git could not say which branch it follows)`. A remote that is not the
  repository reads the same states as `<url> (no upstream branch)`, `<url> (on no branch)` and `<url> (git could
  not say which branch it follows)`. Step 1's own pull fails first in the no-upstream state, so only a hand-run
  `--log-start` reaches this text. `test_a_copy_newer_than_the_checkout_is_told_what_fixes_it` (the
  `--unset-upstream`, deleted-tracking-ref and detached-HEAD states).
- **The legend's proxy clause has a verb and the matcher's rule** (G4). `proxy hosts (one named like proxy or
  wpad only inside a URL)` read as a garden path and hid that a bare `proxy:8080` is replaced too. It reads
  `proxy hosts (a host that is just a common word, such as proxy or wpad, is replaced only where a URL or
  host:port names it)`, the paragraph is reflowed to 115 columns, and `Read the report before sending it:
  anything ...` stays on one line, which `stopped_report_note` rewrites. docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md's
  `<proxy-N>` row says the same for both reports (the agentsync report's rule is the URL alone).
  `test_the_shell_report_reads_past_a_dollar_quoted_install_log_word`.
  **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.73 H62:** the agentsync report's rule is not the URL alone: its url mode also matches
  such a host before `:<port>` (`proxy:8080 refused` reads `<proxy-1>:8080 refused`), so the row gives one rule
  for both reports, a URL or `host:port`. Only the port differs: the shell report matches the configured one, the
  agentsync report any number.
- **The shell report's private-only send advice is one line** (G50). The advice, `Send this report privately ...
  never as a public issue.`, ran on from the `Private only:` lines and survived in a stopped copy's report under
  its `do not send it` note. It is now one unwrapped line, `Send it: privately (docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md in the
  agentsync repository), never as a public issue. Nothing is sent automatically.`, as the agentsync report has it,
  and `stopped_report_note` drops it whole; wrapped, its second half would stay behind.
  `test_the_shell_report_sends_a_report_with_a_word_named_folder_privately` (now also through a stopped copy).
  Amended 2026-10-13, §16.70 H4: a report that is not private only has a `Send it: ` line too, naming the
  link and the private route.
- **G71 is not built: its premise was removed by §16.64 G46.** G71 found the loop's `<org-` branch dead, since F42
  and F55 registered a word-named organisation only in names and domains that hold `-` or `.`. Lane RA's G46
  (landed first) registers every one-word organisation that is not `context_org_word` bare, so an organisation
  named `Status` is now an `<org-N>` pair that is a `report_word` and must raise the lines
  (`test_install_oneshot.py`'s G46 test checks that). Removing the branch would leave that report public, so the
  branch and the words `folder or organisation` stay.
- **No line offers the public issue a private report rules out** (G47, G65, one defect). With F92's
  `Private only:` line in the report, `install.sh` still printed `issue link (review the report first): <link>`
  and `--report-only`'s NEXT read `... copy that one file back privately, or paste the setup report into the
  issue the link above opens`; `agentsync setup-report --out` printed the link as its last line too. The person
  reads those lines, not the Redaction part. `report_issue_link` now returns nothing for a report with a line that
  starts `Private only:` in its Redaction part (both writers write it there at column 0; a friction line that
  quotes one is not the flag), so `on_exit` prints no link line, on the install
  path as on `--report-only`, and the NEXT keeps its bring-back-only default. It reads the report's own text,
  so an agentsync older than the installer is covered. `_cmd_setup_report` prints no link line when
  `red.word_named_shown`. The shell report sets `PRIVATE_ONLY` where it prints its lines and then ends without
  the bare `ISSUE_URL` line; its `Send it:` line names no link. The agentsync report keeps its last-line link: its
  `Send it:` line says "not through the link on the last line", and that file is lane RA's, so G65's proposal to
  end it without the link (and reword that line) is not built. docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md section 3 says so;
  the README prompt's "its last lines are an issue link and a NEXT: line" is lane P's to word in v15.
  `test_the_shell_report_sends_a_report_with_a_word_named_folder_privately`,
  `test_an_agentsync_report_for_a_private_copy_gets_no_issue_link_line`,
  `test_a_word_named_folder_makes_the_redaction_section_advise_sending_privately` (tests/test_setup_report.py).
  Amended 2026-10-13, §16.69 H75: the agentsync report no longer keeps its last-line link: a private copy ends
  after its Redaction section, and its `Send it:` line says `never as a public issue`, as G65 proposed.
- **The shell report fences the friction log** (G6). The agentsync report fences it (`_fence`); the shell
  fallback printed it raw, so in a Markdown view its lines ran into one paragraph and a placeholder such as
  `<folder-1>` read as an HTML tag a renderer drops (the issue form wraps the paste in a code block, so the issue
  was unaffected). `fallback_body` writes `~~~text`, the log with `~~~` and three backticks broken up as `_fence`
  does, then `~~~`; no line numbers, which a read-back would number again. `friction_text`, which reads the log
  back from an earlier report when friction.md is gone (the finding's "stopped-copy awk" is this reader), leaves
  out lines that are exactly `~~~text`, `~~~` or `~~~<folder-N>` (a folder named `text` is redacted in the
  opener), so a fenced earlier report of either writer neither nests the
  new fence (an inner `~~~` would close it and leave every later section in an unclosed block) nor adds a pair a
  run. `test_the_shell_report_fences_the_friction_log_once`, `test_report_only_keeps_an_earlier_friction_log`.
  Amended 2026-10-13, §16.70 H41: the read-back leaves out every line that starts with `~~~`, and
  `redact_stream` no longer redacts the opener.
- **A cloud folder's id reads as its folder** (G8). The shell report gave each `[[source]]` id `<source-N>` by its
  table's place and nothing tied it to its folder, so `exclude-empty <source-1>` and the `--source-local
  .../<folder-1>` it is about read as two things; the Python report's fuzzy folder pair makes such an id the
  folder's placeholder (`_norm`). `redaction_pairs` records the number each folder part's pair has (a later
  part of the same bytes loses to the first, as `add_pair` does), and a source whose path is under CloudStorage
  takes `<folder-N>` when `id_key` of its id equals `id_key` of its path's last part (lower case, no blank, `_`,
  `\` or `-`: `_norm` for ASCII). Keyed on the id's spelling, not on the path: two `Reports` folders under two
  organisations share one `<folder-1>`, so `reports` reads as it and `reports-2` keeps `<source-2>`, as in the
  Python report. A user-chosen `--id`, inbox and non-cloud ids stay `<source-N>`, and the legend says so.
  Non-ASCII names do not match `id_key` (it strips no accents) and keep `<source-N>`, which hides nothing.
  `test_the_shell_report_redacts_a_configured_source_id`, `test_the_shell_report_keeps_a_deduplicated_ids_own_number`
  (tests/test_report_redaction.py).
  **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.73 H69:** `reports-2` keeps a `<source-N>` of its own, as in the Python report, but the
  number can differ: the shell report numbers an id by its table's place (`<source-2>`), and the Python report
  numbers only the ids no folder pair covers (`<source-1>`; measured with `Redactor`).
  Amended 2026-10-13, §16.70 H76: `id_key` also drops accents, as `_norm` does, so an accented folder's slug id
  reads as its `<folder-N>` here too.
- **A second Prompt: line opens an attempt in the shell readers too** (G81). `parse_friction` opens an attempt
  at a `Prompt:` line when the open one already has one, for any log version; `FRICTION_AWK`'s `track()` only set
  its header flag, so `friction_attempt_begin` dated the attempt from the first header (and the shell report's
  "no install run during this attempt" line, F30, disagreed with the agentsync report's), while
  `friction_attempt_stopped` and `friction_earlier_end` read the two as one. `track()` keeps `PS` (a `Prompt:`
  line in this attempt, cleared wherever an attempt opens: an `Attempt:` line, a line it reads as another
  session's, `restate`); at a second one it resets the attempt's words and time as a time-less `Attempt:` line
  would and sets `NH`, which each of the three readers takes right after `track()` as it takes an `Attempt:` line,
  and clears (`track()` returns 0 there: every reader's `q` branch reads a time from the line). Since v5
  `--log-start` writes `Attempt:` before every header, so this reaches v4 logs and repeated headers only. The
  awk's `Prompt:`/`Agent:` patterns stay case-sensitive and take no bold keys, a gap `_FRICTION_KEY_RE` does not
  have, left as it was. `test_the_installer_and_the_report_split_the_same_attempts_after_any_header` (two-`Prompt:`
  logs), `test_the_shell_report_only_says_the_last_install_run_was_before_this_attempt`.

### 16.66 Round 6: converters, stub re-render and speech (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 6 lane E)

Builds round 6's stub re-render, `.msg` and `.potx` stub, template and speech items (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`,
"B13 round 6"). G7 and G28 describe one defect and are built once; lane P's G69 is G62 and is built here, with
G69's words. Every line that corrects an older section is here, not in that section.

**One page is one change (G7, G28).** The one-time stub re-render rewrote a `no converter` stub whose name a
converter now claims, and the re-read in the same sync converted it, so one page was counted twice (commit subject
`0a 2m`, two `- M` CHANGELOG lines, `M` twice `converted` in the run record). `cycle._one_change_per_page` keeps
one added or modified change per page, at its first place, an add winning over a modify; it runs before the
end-of-run flush, so the manifest's run changes, CHANGELOG, the report, the run record and the commit see one.
Every stub is still re-rendered: skipping one the same run will read brings back §16.60 F63 under a label rule,
and leaves it on the old rendering for good when that read is deferred or fails. Pinned by
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_stub_rendered_again_and_read_in_one_sync_is_one_change` (a `.potx` and a `.msg`) and
`::test_a_stub_rendered_again_whose_read_fails_in_that_sync_is_one_change_and_rendered_once`.

**A withheld stub says so in `reason:` and `_sync/QUARANTINE.tsv` (G29).** A stub a label rule withholds (a
`.msg`, or an image OCR could read) shows `withheld by label rule: the label of a binary .msg, or of a .msg not on
this Mac, cannot be read` (an image: `the label of a <suffix> file cannot be read`) in its front matter's `reason:`
and its QUARANTINE.tsv row, which kept `no converter for <suffix>`. The stored reason is unchanged: re-reads, stub
identity, `mark_for_rescreen` and the setup report's class key on it. The text never starts `refused: `, which
`policy.is_refusal_reason` would read as a label refusal; an image on a Mac without OCR still says `no converter`.
`Publisher._withheld` is the one test `_plan_stub` and `write_quarantine` share; for an image it reads this run's
OCR state, as the page does when it is planned, so a run with no engine writes an image's TSV row as `no converter`. Pinned by
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_withheld_stub_says_so_in_its_reason_and_in_quarantine_tsv`. Amends §16.42 R33's
"only the words say why" and §16.60 F33: the stub's `reason:` is among those words.
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J73 (by §16.71 H52):** `write_quarantine` no longer reads this run's OCR state: for a
row a label rule may withhold it copies the `reason:` of the stub as published (`Publisher._stub_reason`), so a run
with no engine no longer rewrites an image's TSV row as `no converter`; the row says what the page says.

**`STUB_RENDER` is 4 (G29, G76, G77).** One bump for the three: a withheld stub's `reason:`, a redacted stub, and
the tombstone layout.
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J73 (by §16.71 H77):** `STUB_RENDER` is 5: H77's tombstone line bumped it once more, so
an install at 4 renders once more.
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.85 K70 (by §16.78 J74):** `STUB_RENDER` is 6: J74 widened the tombstone pass to the
sources deleted from sources.toml and kept 5, so an install that had run H77's build (at 5) never ran the wider pass
and kept those tombstones' title above the banner until they were reaped.

**A redacted stub is rendered again (G76; amends §16.51 Q75, §16.60 F94).** `Cycle._stub_again` no longer skips a
redacted item: the publisher redacts the re-plan from the stored redaction (`_shown_name`, `_shown_path`,
`_alloc_rel`), as it did the first page, and the secret scan's "survives redaction" check stands behind it. Its
title, `source_path` and `redacted-<hash>` page name stay. Pinned by
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_redacted_stub_from_an_older_rendering_is_rendered_again_once_and_stays_redacted`
(the made-up secret is in no commit, CHANGELOG or QUARANTINE.tsv).

**An old tombstone is rendered again (G77; amends §16.61 F88, §16.51 Q9).** `_rerender_stubs` also walks the
intact tombstone pages of every configured source, a retired one's too (`Cycle._rerender_tombstones`), and
`Publisher.rerender_tombstone` rebuilds each from its own front matter, as `unarchive_tombstone` does: the title (a
unit's or a subject, never the file name the repair path uses), `source_path` and redaction stay; only the
layout moves, banner first. The output row takes the new `page_sha256` and `rendered_sha256`, or the repair path
would see drift and retitle the page. A missing or changed page stays the repair path's, and one this run
reaps is only deleted (one `D`, not an `M` and a `D`). With G76, no stub or tombstone agentsync can rebuild keeps a
heading above the banner, so §16.61 F88's "an existing credential, path or redacted stub keep
the heading above the banner" and Q9's "Not built" re-render of old tombstones no longer hold;
`docs/deploy/data-governance.md` says every one is rendered again once. Pinned by
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_tombstone_from_before_the_banner_came_first_is_rendered_again_once_with_its_own_title`.
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.71 H77:** this rewrite also amends §16.60 F68, whose reason it had not answered: a row with
no `last_commit` takes the commit that holds its content before the page is rendered (§16.71).

**A `.msg` withheld by its name is read once the rule is lifted (G52).** `Manifest.mark_for_rescreen` takes
`withheld_suffixes`, and `_check_policy_change` passes `label_withheld_suffixes()`: a refused row whose reason is
`no converter for <suffix>` with one of them is marked for the re-screen too. A Graph `.msg` withheld under a rule
(§16.60 F73) was never pending work after the rule was lifted, since its hash had not moved and no re-read
downloads, so it kept the stub through reconcile. Under a rule `_no_converter` stubs it again with no download;
without one it is fetched and read. Marking happens only when the policy fingerprint moves. Measured: an online-only
local `.msg` was already read after a lift (the `no converter` re-read reaches it); only a Graph one was stuck.
Pinned by `tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_msg_withheld_by_its_name_is_read_once_the_label_rule_is_lifted` (a Graph
source; online-only as a guard).
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J73 (by §16.71 H47):** while the new policy keeps a label rule on, only such a row with
no byte read (no content hash) is marked (`mark_for_rescreen(..., unread_only=)`); once the rule is lifted every such
row is marked, as here.

**The deck emitter is 1.0.1 (G59; amends §16.60 F77).** F77's template rendering kept `pptx._EMITTER_VERSION` at
1.0.0, so the action key of bytes round 4 cached did not move: a copy under another name, a page the repair path
rebuilds or a label-only re-save got round 4's body back (a second table with no delimiter row). The bump moves
every deck's key, so a new conversion of those bytes gets the new rendering. It reads nothing again by itself
(`PptxConverter.outdated` is unchanged), so an existing page keeps round 4's rendering until its bytes change.
Pinned by `tests/test_convert_formats.py::test_a_template_round_4_cached_gets_the_whole_table_rendering_under_a_new_name`
and the `pptx-python-pptx@1.0.1+` pins in `tests/test_cycle.py`.
Amended 2026-10-15, §16.96 M65: the bump cures only a new conversion (a copy, a new name, a label-only re-save that
is converted again). A page the repair path rebuilds (`cycle._republish_from_cache`) is re-rendered from the round 4
entry its outputs row names, and keeps round 4's rendering until its bytes change.

**The template de-duplication is tested (G60).** `build_empty_template` puts the master's footer box on a second
layout and `build_table_template` puts the first table, whole, on a third, so the existing assertions fail when
`_template_lines` keeps a repeated block. No code changes.

**A `.msg` not on this Mac is named in every text of the class (G62, G69).** The setup report's legend under the
Quarantine table, setup-feedback.md's Quarantine row and the `_LABEL_WITHHELD` and `label_withheld_suffixes()`
docstrings now say a `.msg` not on this Mac (online-only, a Graph item, one the OS will not hydrate) is
`withheld by label rule` too, refused by its name unless `~/.local/bin/agentsync materialise PATH` names it (§16.60
F73). Pinned by `tests/test_setup_report.py` (the legend) and
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py::test_the_docs_state_the_msg_purge_and_banner_rules_of_round_4`.

**A repository-path proxy scope routes the clone, not the seed (G63; amends §16.60 F78).** git matches
`http.<url>.*` by path prefix, so a setting scoped to github.com or to a path `NEMO_URL` is under routes the seed,
and one scoped to FluidAudio's own repository routes only the clone; the `_GIT_URL` docstring said "as it does for
the clone". F78's test `test_a_proxy_git_scopes_to_fluidaudios_path_on_github_routes_the_seed`, as §16.60 names
it, is renamed `test_a_proxy_git_scopes_to_fluidinference_on_github_routes_the_seed`, and
`tests/test_speech.py::test_a_proxy_git_scopes_to_fluidaudios_own_repository_routes_the_clone_and_not_the_seed`
pins the repository case. Behavior is unchanged: the seed reads git's settings for the url its curl fetches.

### 16.67 Round 6: setup prompt v15 and docs (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 6 lane P)

The B13 round 6 items of lane P (specs `round6/items/G<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built). Eight need
prompt text (G5, G15, G24, G25, G26, G37, G67, G73), so the prompt is **setup prompt v15**: `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`,
`PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's `prompt v15` and `setup-prompt-compat 15`, the issue form's placeholder and the block's
digest move together; a saved v14 copy is stopped at step 1 like every older copy. v15 moves no step, so it has no
`PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry and is read with v7's rules. None adds a command, flag, installer option, config key or
friction kind. Dated lines in sections other than this one read `Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G<n>`, with
`(by §16.5N/§16.6N <item>)` where they record another round's change.

**The heading follows the section, and the reason comes first** (G5, G26; one sentence; dated lines at §16.43 H5
and §16.61 F26). "Write that heading even when this session asks for no change, unless step 3 skips its "## Not
used" section: that section goes under it" read as if the skipped section still went under the heading (G26), and
its exception named step 3's skip, which the folder wait and the version stop never reach with a checkout present
(G5). It now reads "Write that heading even when this session asks for no change, since step 3's "## Not used"
section goes under it; a session that asks for no change and adds no "## Not used" section (step 3 says when)
writes no heading", and step 3's list reads "Three cases have no report and no "## Not used" section". Rejected:
G26's finder's "when step 3 skips that section, write no heading", which drops the no-change scope, so a session
with no checkout that does write a fix request would write it under the last session's heading (H5's defect); and
G5's "unless this session ends with no report", which ties the heading to `--report-only`, a command that runs
after the section is written. Test: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py`
(`test_prompt_routes_changes_to_the_source_not_the_checkout`).

**The version stop passes on the installer's words** (G15, G67; dated line at §16.59 F17). Since F17 the installer
tells a newer copy's two causes apart, and when the checkout follows a fork or another branch its error says to
point the checkout at main, while the prompt's stop said "Tell me to copy the prompt again" and called the copy
older: two orders on one screen, and following the prompt's stops the same way. Step 1 now says "stop and run no
other step: this prompt is v15, and a copy that does not match the installer must not be used. If the command's
error says what to tell me, tell me that, in its words. Otherwise (--version printed another number and no such
error), tell me to copy the prompt again ..., and that if that copy stops here too, this Mac's checkout
(~/src/agent-context-sync) does not follow main of the Source: point it there, or move it aside so step 1 clones
it, then paste the prompt again." The fallback covers an installer old enough to print no such error. The relay is
in the chat only: the stderr names the checkout's path and remote, which the friction log keeps out on purpose
(`newer_copy_fix`), so the prompt asks for no log line of it. Test: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py`
(`test_readme_prompt_names_its_version_and_the_installer_compat_line`).
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J66 (by §16.72 H65):** since v16, unless the error's words already mention this Mac's checkout,
the agent also tells the person that a fresh copy stopping here too means the checkout does not follow main of the
Source: installers v8 to v14 say only "copy the prompt again", so the checkout sentence never came where it was meant.

**The git stop's hint names a URL rewrite and marks its commands** (G73, G24; dated lines at §16.61 F24). With
`url."https://<mirror>/".insteadOf = https://github.com/` git's error names the mirror ("Could not resolve host"),
and both proxy commands print nothing (measured, git 2.54, a throwaway home); `git config --get-regexp
'url\..*insteadof'` prints it, since git keeps key names in lower case. The hint now says git "was told to use that
host, either as a URL rewrite, which `git config --get-regexp 'url\..*insteadof'` prints, or as a proxy, set by
git's own setting, which `git config --get-urlmatch http.proxy https://github.com` prints and which wins over the
terminal's, or by the terminal's HTTPS_PROXY, https_proxy, ALL_PROXY or all_proxy, which `env | grep -i proxy`
shows". "Which wins" stays on the proxy setting: a rewrite is another mechanism. Each command is in code marks, as
the Xcode one is, so a person sees where it ends; both git queries are the person's, so the allow-rule list does not
cover them (`_agent_commands`). The hint stays read-only: it never tells the agent to change a rewrite. Test:
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py` (`test_readme_step1_is_one_command`).
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J66 (by §16.72 H21, H25):** since v16 the quote is sentences, the one action last ("Once git can
reach GitHub from a terminal, start a new session from that terminal and paste this prompt again"), and the rewrite
query is anchored, `git config --get-regexp '^url\..*\.insteadof$'`, which leaves out `pushinsteadof`.

**The report comes after a failure, except in three cases** (G25; dated lines at §16.36 and §16.49 R31). "Then
the report, always, even after a failure" came just before "Three cases have no report"; it now reads "Then the
report, even after a failure (except in the three cases below)". Test: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py`
(`test_readme_report_step_after_any_failure`).

**The first sync's own wait is named** (G37; dated line at §16.49's step 2). After step 2's reinstall wait ran
out, the first sync, an interactive one, waited for the same lock up to `cycle.INTERACTIVE_LOCK_WAIT_S` (600 s)
and said so only in agentsync's WARNING lines, which the prompt never named, so its friction rule had the agent
log a deviation; if the lock was still held then, the step was skipped (75). install.sh now prints
`<label>: another sync is still running; waiting for it to end, at most 10 minutes` before the sync when its lock
probe finds the lock held (the label is `first sync`, or `sync` where `sources.toml` existed), and the prompt adds
"its first sync then says "another sync is still running" and waits for that sync again, up to 10 more minutes,
and is skipped ("skipped, lock busy") if it is still running then. Both waits and that skip are expected, not
deviations: do not log them." A skipped first sync is still recorded (`skipped 75 lock-busy` in install.log). The
600 s cap stays: a first sync that did not wait would be skipped more often. Tests:
`tests/test_install_oneshot.py::test_a_sync_still_running_after_the_wait_leaves_the_reinstall_as_before` and
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py` (`test_readme_step2_is_the_one_install_command`).
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J66 (by §16.72 H66):** since v16 the first sync's wait is a sentence of its own, for every run, not
only a reinstall's: "If another sync is running when its first sync starts (that same one, or one that started
since, such as a background sync on a Mac that already syncs), it says "another sync is still running" and waits for
it, up to 10 minutes, and skips that sync ("skipped, lock busy") if it is still running then."

**Prompt words from another lane** (lane RB's G47 and G65, §16.65). A report that holds a `Private only:` line gets
no `issue link (review the report first):` line, and its `NEXT:` names `bring-back.md` alone, so step 3's "its last
lines are an issue link and a NEXT: line" now adds "(none when the report says it is for a private copy only)". Test:
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py` (`test_readme_report_step_after_any_failure`).

**Docs that lagged round 5's code** (G61, G64, G66, G68, G69, G70, G72). Docs and dated lines only; no behavior
changes:
- data-governance.md listed "a save that changes only the label ... is re-screened only when the content changes
  or the policy changes" under Known limits, while §16.60 F72 screens such a save under a label rule; the sentence
  leaves the limits and the labels item says what F72 does (G66).
- setup-feedback.md gave round 4's rule for a stated step 1 error, while F23 (§16.58) makes one after a header
  (a `Prompt:` or `Agent:` line) a new attempt at any gap; three passages now give F23's rule first and round 4's for a

  §16.73 H64:** the header is a `Prompt:`, `Agent:`, `Outcome:` or `Run:` line, as §16.64 G51 says, and the

  names the Configuration section's excludes line as a home of `(source N)`, which the shell report uses for

- Dated lines: §16.54 Q52 and Q77 by F78 and F77, and §16.60 F78 says what it amends (G61); §16.51 Q9's F88 line
  and §16.61 by F94, since credential and path stubs are rendered again (G68); §16.61's "every `.msg` is fetched"

- G69's Quarantine row in setup-feedback.md and the report's `withheld by label rule` legend are lane E's G62,

Tests: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py` (`test_the_docs_state_what_round_5_changed`,

`test_a_round_5_item_that_amends_another_has_a_dated_line_there`, which for each §16.60 item that says "amends

### 16.68 Round 7: sync, status and doctor (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 7 lane B)

Lane B's round 7 items: H12, H31, H32, H33, H34, H35, H37, H48, H49, H50, H51, H73, all built. H12 and H35 are one
defect from two finders, built once, in the same commit as H50 (all three are `loop._named`).

**H12, H35, H50: the waits name STATE.md first, and only the alarm names `sync -v` (`agentsync.loop`,
`agentsync.arm_local`, `agentsync.cli`).** The clear, collides and gone waits, both could-not-list waits and
exclude-empty's tail read `the alarm line a sync prints for <id>, also kept in <docs repo>/_sync/STATE.md, names
<what> (the first five; \`~/.local/bin/agentsync sync -v\` logs each one)`, even for one folder, and install.sh's
step 2 and `status` print no alarm line. They now read `<docs repo>/_sync/STATE.md keeps the alarm line for <id>,
which names <what> (a plain \`~/.local/bin/agentsync sync\` prints it too)` (`loop._named(config, ids, what)`, ids
a list). The five-name cap is applied in the alarm, so the alarm alone says `(+N more;
\`~/.local/bin/agentsync sync -v\` logs each one)`, only past five: a wait's own count is a part of the alarm's
(three empty and three held folders make two waits of three, and a sixth name the alarm holds back). Two or more
sources that could not be listed share one plural line: `a folder in each of <A and B> could not be listed (...):
... keeps the alarm lines for <A and B>, which name them (... prints them too); grant Files and Folders access, or
add each to its source's exclude in sources.toml`; one source's text is otherwise as before. install.sh's output is
unchanged (the first sync's alarm lines would put folder names below a source root into install.out). Tests:
`test_loop.py::test_one_empty_folder_is_never_sent_to_a_full_sync`,
`test_loop.py::test_the_sixth_folder_is_pointed_at_when_the_waits_split_the_folders`,
`test_loop.py::test_two_sources_that_cannot_be_listed_get_a_plural_wait`.

**H48: STATE.md keeps an alarm whole (`agentsync.publish`).** `write_state` wrote alarms at `_REASON_MAX` (300):
of five nested folder paths of about 65 characters it kept three and lost the `(+N more` tail. Alarm lines now
take `_ALARM_MAX` (6000: five relative paths at macOS's 1024-character limit fit); errors, skipped reasons and lint
messages keep 300. No name is cut: a tail cut makes sibling paths with a shared start identical. Tests:
`test_loop.py::test_state_md_keeps_the_five_long_folder_names_the_empty_folder_wait_points_at`,
`test_loop.py::test_state_md_keeps_the_five_long_folder_names_the_could_not_list_wait_points_at`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.102 N73: `_ALARM_MAX` is 16,000. Since §16.95 M5, M45 the mixed alarm names up to ten
folders, five it could not read, each with its reason, and five empty ones; at 6000 one with 1024-character names
lost its advice and its last names.

**H37: quoted text keeps its backticks, inside a fence they cannot close (`agentsync.publish`).** `_quoted`
turned every backtick into a single quote, so the command an alarm quotes in backticks read otherwise in STATE.md
than on the terminal. It now keeps them and opens and closes the code span with one backtick more than the longest
run in the text (padded with a space when the text starts or ends with one, or is empty), so no run inside can
close the span: third-party text stays inert data, the guarantee of SG13. Plain text keeps a single backtick. Every
`_quoted` caller (STATE.md alarms, errors, skipped reasons, lint findings, CHANGELOG paths) changes alike. Tests:
`test_review_fixes.py::test_quoted_text_keeps_its_backticks_and_stays_one_inert_span`,
`test_review_fixes.py::test_sg13_third_party_text_in_state_md_is_quoted_data`.
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.78 J50:** CHANGELOG lines written before H37 carry an apostrophe for each backtick of a
path; a purge matches that old form of a purged docs path only inside a single-backtick span of a non-JSON line, and
not where it is another item's live page. STATE.md, rewritten by every cycle, holds no such line after one cycle on
H37's build.

**H73: STATE.md keeps an unselected source's lines (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.publish`, `agentsync.model`).**
A `reconcile --source`, `sync --source` or `accept-deletions` of one source rewrote STATE.md without the other
sources' alarms, while their waits said STATE.md keeps them. Each cycle stores every selected source's raw alarm and
error lines with its run id in the manifest meta `state_md_lines` (`{id: [run, [alarms], [errors]]}`), keeps the
entries of sources it did not select, and drops sources no longer configured. `write_state(..., carried=)` shows
them under such a source as `alarm (run N): ...` and `error (run N): ...`, after any line this run has about it (a
rescan alarm, `not in this run`); quoting is at render time only. The keys are the sources the run reached (selected
and given an accumulator), not `report is None`: a selected source a failed cycle never reached keeps its stored
lines and shows them tagged. An unreadable store carries nothing and never fails the cycle. Test:
`test_loop.py::test_state_md_keeps_another_sources_alarm_after_a_one_source_run`.
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J51:** `sync --source` does not exist (KISS K13b deleted it on 2026-10-05, before this
text was written; `sync` refuses it with exit 2): the one-source runs are `reconcile --source` and
`accept-deletions`.

**H32: the sync line counts the files refused without a read (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.model`,
`agentsync.cli`).** A source line's `refused=` counts every refused stub, the closing split only those refused after
a read, so a file a rule withheld by its name (or a type with no converter) was in neither N nor the split.
`SourceReport.refused_unread` counts refusals `_publish(..., unread=True)` made with no byte read (no converter for
the name, `policy_refusal`, a withheld online-only `.msg`); a stub that stands or a page that is kept publishes
nothing and counts nothing. The line then ends `; Q refused without a read (no converter for the type, or a rule
that needs no bytes)`, only when Q > 0, with no bare `converted`, `deferred` or `read again` (install.sh's awk and
`setup_report._SPLIT_RE` read the line as before). It names no label rule: a type with no converter is refused the
same way. Amended 2026-10-14, §16.74 J39: the setup report's first-sync clause reads the count too, after the split
as on this line, and names it in its source tag. Tests: `test_cli.py::test_the_sync_line_counts_the_files_refused_without_a_read`,
`test_cli.py::test_a_type_with_no_converter_is_counted_refused_without_a_read_and_no_rule_is_named`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.77 J29: a refusal with no byte read whose stub says a label rule withheld it is counted
in `SourceReport.withheld_unread`, not `refused_unread`, and the line names the rule for those in a clause of its
own, `; W withheld unread by the label rule (its label cannot be read without the file)`, before this one.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.83 K33: its parenthesis reads `(a file whose label cannot be read: an image, a binary .msg
or a .msg not on this Mac)`.

**H49: an inbox duplicate is not in R (`agentsync.cycle`).** An inbox file whose bytes match a Graph file is read,
then quarantined (`duplicate-of ...`), yet `acc.refused` counted it, so the line said `1 refused` beside the source
line's `quarantined=1`. It stays in N and leaves R, as the name-and-size duplicate already did. Test:
`test_cycle.py::test_an_inbox_duplicate_by_its_bytes_is_quarantined_on_the_sync_line_too`.

**H31: install.sh's first sync waits for the lock quietly (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.cli`,
`scripts/install.sh`).** During the first sync's lock wait install.sh's wait line and ticker, a WARNING every 30 s
and three skip lines said the same news (about 65 lines over 800 s). `AGENTSYNC_QUIET_LOCK_WAIT=1`, which install.sh
sets for its first sync only (an environment variable, no flag: an older agentsync ignores it), makes
`_acquire_waiting` log its first WARNING and send the later beats to DEBUG, and the CLI drop its `skipped: lock held
by ...` WARNING, which the stderr line `skipped: lock held (...)` beside it carries with the holder's detail (that
line still shows the bare label, `pid N (poll) since ...`: it is `_describe_holder`'s, shared with doctor and the
lock-wait WARNING, which the setup report scrubs by its shape). Every other run keeps a beat each 30 s: without a
ticker it is the run's only sign of life. install.sh's 75 branch now says `<label>: skipped, lock busy`, without the
generic `rc_meaning` tail. The launchd jobs' `.err.log`, which the setup report reads, keeps its beats and its skip
WARNING (in H33's words). Tests:
`test_cli.py::test_the_quiet_lock_wait_logs_once_and_leaves_the_skip_to_its_stderr_line`,
`test_install_oneshot.py::test_first_sync_lock_busy_is_skipped_not_failed`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.83 K37: `_describe_holder` names a cycle's label as `pid N (a sync, its pass: poll) since
...`, so the stderr line, the lock-wait WARNING and doctor no longer show the bare label.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.85 K53 (by §16.77 J11): the stderr line H31 leans on now reads `skipped: lock held by
<full holder>` (from `LockHeldError.holder`), no longer `skipped: lock held (...)`; the holder is
`_describe_holder`'s, not the WARNING's `another sync (its pass: <label>)` (since §16.83 K37 it reads `pid N (a
sync, its pass: poll) since ...`).
Amended 2026-10-18, §16.125 T33: under the quiet wait the first beat is DEBUG too; install.sh's line announces it.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.131 U68, U69, U92, U105: install.sh's line announces the wait only when its lock probe found
the lock busy; a wait the probe missed gets one plain line from agentsync, in install.sh's words.
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.143 W14: the stderr line is `skipped: lock held by <holder>` from `cli._skip_holder`:
`LockHeldError.holder`, but an empty body in the wait line's words (`cycle.UNRECORDED_LOCK_HOLDER`), not as `an
unrecorded holder (...)`.

**H33: a terminal's sync is not called the background one (`scripts/install.sh`, `agentsync.cli`).** A sync typed
in a terminal holds the lock as `poll` or `reconcile`, as the job does, and the installer reads only the lock.
install.sh now says `agentsync: another sync is running (the background job, or one started in a terminal); the
reinstall waits for it to end (at most <N>s)`, ticks `agentsync: reinstalling after the other sync ends` and, when
the wait runs out, `agentsync: the other sync is still running after <N>s; reinstalling without waiting longer`.
The note `waited-for-a-background-sync` is a machine word the setup report reads, and stays. The skip WARNING
renders a cycle label as `another sync (its pass: <label>)` (`cli._lock_holder`); the unrecorded and unidentified
holders and the governance and exclude-empty labels are named as before (wrapping them would call install.sh's
reinstall a sync). Still one text per label, so Recent errors merges repeats. Tests:
`test_cli.py::test_lock_held_warning_names_the_holder_and_repeats_verbatim`, the reinstall pins in
`test_install_oneshot.py` (`REINSTALL_WAITS`, `REINSTALL_TICK`).
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.81 K35: the setup report renders that word as `waited for another sync to end`, in the
Summary and the Installer table; install.log keeps it.
Amended 2026-10-15, §16.93 M43, M60: since §16.87 (round 10 L73) the holder sidecar records who started a cycle;
install.sh names it from there for the lock body's own pid, and the either-or words read `the background job, or a
sync started another way`, not `one started in a terminal`.

**H34: a provider link keeps the form of the root that held it (`agentsync.paths`).** Under a home reached through
a link (`/tmp` is `/private/tmp`), a provider link whose absolute target is written in the unresolved form was read
through to that form, while the stored path and the real folder are resolved: add-source added the folder twice,
step 1 listed it unmarked, the overlap check said none. `provider_link_resolved` now returns the root that held the
path, joined with the target's name and the rest: one readlink still, nothing inside a domain read, no `resolve()`.
Test: `test_cli.py::test_a_cloud_link_written_in_a_linked_homes_other_form_is_the_same_folder`.

**H51: two doctor comments (`agentsync.ops.doctor`).** `_INCOMPLETE_RUNS` counts the heartbeat's
`consecutive_incomplete` (passes not counted as listed; a Graph delta resets it), and `_incomplete_fix`'s docstring
names exclude-empty, STATE.md's copy of the alarm and `sync -v` only past five. Comments only.

No command, flag or config key is added; no prompt words were needed (nothing sent to lane P).

### 16.69 Round 7: setup report (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 7 lane RA)

The setup report's items of B13 round 7 (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 7"). Each is built with a test
that fails without it, or names the measured reason it was not built.

**The Loop line names the docs repo's AGENTS.md and STATE.md in words** (H3, H36). `_eval_by_name` named the docs
repo's `_eval` folder "the docs repo's _eval folder" but cut its `AGENTS.md` to a bare `AGENTS.md` (rules 4, 6 and 8)
and its `_sync/STATE.md` to a bare `_sync/STATE.md` (the empty- and unlisted-folder waits), while `loop._baseline`
prints the path because a bare `AGENTS.md` is the agent's own project's when it runs from another folder. They now
read "the docs repo's AGENTS.md" and "the docs repo's _sync/STATE.md" (`_AGENTS_SHOWN`, `_STATE_SHOWN`); no path is
added, so K16b holds and `_NEXT_PATH_RE` (paths from `~` or `/`) leaves the words alone. Tests:
`tests/test_setup_report.py::test_the_loop_line_keeps_no_part_of_a_docs_repo_path_with_spaces`,
`tests/test_loop.py::test_the_empty_folder_wait_points_where_a_plain_sync_names_its_folders`.

**The first-sync source tag names refused when it printed it** (H46; dated line at §16.63 G35). After G35 added `, R
refused` to the split, the tag still read `the unreadable/failed split`; it now reads `the unreadable/failed/refused
split` when R is printed (R > 0), and keeps the old name otherwise, so it never names a count the line left out.
Test: `tests/test_setup_report.py::test_first_sync_clause_carries_the_read_again_count`.

**An open attempt's WARNING names the command that ends it, and its time takes in install.log** (H1, H2; dated lines
at §16.14). `setup-report` has no write path to the friction log, so the WARNING's "Run `agentsync setup-report`
again after step 3" left the WARNING in place. It now says the attempt ends, and the report is rewritten, when step
3's last command `install.sh --report-only` runs, and to run that command only if the session stopped early: telling
an agent mid-session to run it would end the attempt before the sync loop, time the end line wrong and leave later
friction lines after it (the verifier's measurement). The v5 branch keeps the agent's end line. Before the end line
the session span was the friction log's alone (6s beside a 4m13s install); it now spans the attempt's install.log
runs too, never those after the end line (round 5 F37), and says `so far` while the attempt is open; with the end
line the friction log's span usually covers the runs, so the final report reads as before, and a run that outlasts
the end line keeps the longer span without `so far`. Test:
`tests/test_setup_report.py::test_an_open_attempts_warning_names_the_command_that_ends_it_and_its_time_takes_in_install_log`.

**A stop for the folder answer may log approvals and questions, and its title says "Stopped"** (H40, H42; dated
lines at §16.64 G12 and G23). G23's gate required every event to be a step 1 deviation, so a session that did what
the prompt asks, logging the approval its tool asked for (step 1's clone or pull) and then waiting, read "failed at
step 1". `compute_outcome` now also allows step 1 `question`, `click`, `approval` and `prompt` lines (`_WAIT_OK_KINDS`)
beside at least one step 1 deviation; an error, an install run, an end line, a later step or an untyped line keeps
`failed`, and the "waiting for the folder answer" note is read from the deviations only, so an approval's own "wait"
does not set it. `Outcome.title_label` says `Stopped at step N (<the layout's step name>)` for a stopped attempt (v5:
`preflight and code`), so the title no longer contradicts the Summary; `form_label` keeps the Failed option, the
only one the form has. Test: `tests/test_setup_report.py::test_an_attempt_that_only_stopped_for_the_folder_answer_is_stopped_not_failed`.

**The Installer table shows the config step's folder counts** (H10). `_step_table` appended only the note, so a run
that kept 2 folders and added none read `config | done (add-source)`. When a step logs both `kept=` and `added=` as
digits, the row reads `done (add-source: kept 2, added 0)` (likewise `exists` and `created`); other steps and old
logs are unchanged. install.sh's `note=add-source` stays: `_first_sync_line` labels the sync `sync` from it, so
logging `note=kept` instead would relabel a re-run "first sync" (the verifier's measurement). Test:
`tests/test_setup_report.py::test_the_installer_table_shows_the_config_steps_folder_counts`.

**On origin/main says how far behind** (H22; dated line at §16.14 L10). `merge-base --is-ancestor` passes for any
ancestor, so a checkout 5 commits behind read `on origin/main: yes`, and in scenario D (a fetch that worked and a
merge that failed) that invites "current". `_checkout_facts` now runs one more read-only `rev-list --left-right
--count HEAD...origin/main` and reads `yes, 5 behind (…)` or `no, 1 ahead, 2 behind (…)`; the token stays first and
the dated fetch last, and a failed count prints none. The count is against the local origin/main, which the fetch
clause dates. Test: `tests/test_setup_report.py::test_install_source_names_origin_main_and_the_tree`.

**A private copy ends with no public issue link** (H75; dated lines at §16.58 F92 and §16.65 G47, G65). With
`red.word_named_shown`, the agentsync report's `Send it:` line said "not through the link on the last line" and the
report still ended with the prefilled link; round 6 kept it only because the file was another lane's. `build_report`
now ends such a report after its Redaction section, and the line reads `Send it: privately
(docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md in the agentsync repository), never as a public issue: it would show that name.
Nothing is sent automatically.`, the shell report's words. No reader needs the link: `issue_link`,
`report_issue_link` and `stopped_report_note` handle a report without one, and `setup-report --out` and install.sh
already print none for it. The README prompt already says "none when the report says it is for a private copy only".
Test: `tests/test_setup_report.py::test_a_word_named_folder_makes_the_redaction_section_advise_sending_privately`.
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J67:** not quite the shell report's words: its line (`fallback_redaction`) ends
`never as a public issue. Nothing is sent automatically.`, with no `: it would show that name`, and never had it.
The agentsync line is the shell report's words plus why; the shell report's own `Private only:` line, just above
its `Send it:` line, says why there.

**agentsync's own paths stay whole beside an organisation named like them** (H74; dated line at §16.64 G45). An
organisation `Context` or `Agent` is a report word, fuzzy and matched everywhere, so it cut `~/agent-context/setup/`
to `~/agent-<org-1>/setup/` and `~/src/agent-context-sync` to `~/src/<org-1>-context-sync`, and anyone who knows the
tool reads the name back; the shell report (a case-sensitive pair) kept them whole. `Redactor._compile` adds a held
alternative, `keep_path`, after the repository locator: `(?<=/)agent-context(?:-sync(?:\.git)?)?` with no word
character, hyphen or dotted suffix after it, case-sensitive, so an organisation spelled `Agent-Context` or a folder
`agent-context-partners` is still replaced, and a registered value that begins with those words and is longer
(`agent-context Contoso`) is tried first through a negative lookahead (`_HELD_PATH_NORMS`), so it is replaced too.
The path is the same on every Mac, so holding it reveals nothing;
`_word_named` is unchanged and the report stays `Private only:`. install.sh's case-sensitive pair is not changed
(lane RB's file; only a lowercase `context` organisation would cut it there). Test:
`tests/test_setup_report.py::test_an_organisation_named_like_agentsyncs_paths_leaves_them_whole`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.75 J71: that note was short: a lower-case `agent` organisation cut the paths there too, and
the word `agentsync` itself (`<org-1>sync`, `com.<org-1>sync.poll`). The shell's `redact_stream` now holds the same
path names, and `agentsync`, except where a longer pair covers them.

**A first sync that printed no counts borrows none** (H29). With no counts in its install.log note, the first-sync
line fell back to install.out's last `converted N, deferred M online-only` line, whichever run printed it, so a
`skipped 75 lock-busy` sync (which prints `sync: skipped, lock busy` and no counts) read `· converted 7, deferred 3
online-only (install.out)`, an earlier run's. `_installer_output` now records the run id of the last `# run=<id>`
header above that line (`_Facts.first_sync_run`), and `_first_sync_line` uses install.out's counts for the shown run
only when its step was not skipped and the line is in that run's output; an install.out with no header at all (an
older install.sh) keeps the old reading except for a skipped step. A skipped step's own words say what happened, so
no clause about who converts the files is added (for `no-sources` and `status-failed` no sync follows). The
borrowed path, already labelled "an earlier run's", is unchanged. Test:
`tests/test_setup_report.py::test_a_first_sync_that_printed_no_counts_borrows_none_from_an_earlier_run`.

**A prompt newer than the report's agentsync says so** (H23). On a scenario-D Mac the installed agentsync, older
than the pasted prompt, writes the report with its own step names and checks, and nothing said so. When the
attempt's prompt (header or stated) is above `PROMPT_VERSION` and the installer's own stop note
(`_prompt_copy_note`, unchanged) is absent, the prompt line adds `(newer than this report's agentsync, for prompt
vN)`. It names no cause: a header comes from `--log-start`, after a pull that worked (step 2 may have failed before
the reinstall), and a header-less step 1 error may be xcode-select's, before any pull (the verifier's measurement
of the finder's "its pull did not update it"). Amended 2026-10-14, §16.74 J40: the note reads `newer than this
report's agentsync, which is for prompt vN`, and every note after the version shares one bracket, joined by "; ". The run metadata's agentsync line names the build's prompt
(`agentsync: <version>, setup prompt vN (python …)`), so any report shows the comparison. The issue form's version and
the title keep the attempt's. Test: `tests/test_setup_report.py::test_a_prompt_newer_than_the_reports_agentsync_says_so`.

**A folder list that could not read the config is no expected turn** (H17 and H28, one defect from two finders,
built once; dated lines at §16.29). On a Mac that already synced 2 folders, step 1's list could not read the config
(the installed agentsync lacked a name install.sh's snippet imported, H7) and logged `note=listed-6` like a new
Mac's; the person was asked again, and the report said "fully one command" with the question as an expected turn.
install.sh's `list_folders` now sets a separate flag when `[ -f "$CONFIG" ]` and the marks could not be read (no
tool Python, a snippet failure, a timeout, bad output) and appends `${unread:+ synced=unreadable}` to every step
note, never through `$synced`, which `[ "${synced:-0}" -gt 0 ]` needs as a number. `synced_before` is unchanged
(`_count` reads `unreadable` as None, so the 2026-10-07 rule still counts the question as asked, human turns 1).
`unread_synced(runs)` gives the first install run's `kept=N` (that run's alone: a later run's can hold folders added
after the question) when the deciding list logged `synced=unreadable` and N > 0: `compute_outcome` adds the why `the folder question: step 1's list could not read the N folders this Mac
already syncs` ("worked with help", so the headline never says "fully one command" over the Item), the expected
turns say no question was due, and the Items list opens with `- install.sh · step 1 · the folder list could not
read the N folders this Mac already syncs[ (install.out has its warning)]; the folder question was a turn
agentsync caused`, beside the retried runs rather than as a friction event, whatever the outcome (the expected
turns point to it). A config with nothing synced (`kept=0`)
or no install run keeps today's wording; logs from before the flag are unchanged. The warning's wording is lane
RB's (H7). Tests: `tests/test_setup_report.py::test_a_finished_list_says_by_itself_whether_the_folder_question_was_asked`,
`tests/test_install_oneshot.py::test_list_folders_marks_nothing_when_the_config_cannot_be_read`,
`tests/test_install_oneshot.py::test_list_folders_keeps_a_set_up_mac_that_has_nothing_to_list`.

**The OCR part says "the early OCR build", and its all-zero re-read line reads in short sentences** (H5; dated lines
at §16.28 and §16.40 N37). "Field build" was defined only in CONTRACTS §16.27 and code, yet five report strings used
it. One constant, `_FIELD_BUILD = "the early OCR build"`, now names it in all of them (`_VERSION_WORDS[1]`, the
re-read table's `of them early OCR build` column, the counted kinds, the no-engine lead and the one-line bullet),
and `_ocr_part` adds `(an OCR build that was never released)` to the part's first mention, so one thing has one name.
`_reread_finished` keeps every fact of its one sentence (on this Mac, from the early OCR build or not, none failed,
none given up under any engine or version, none cut off by a dying cycle) in four short sentences, and its run
sentence says the run was chosen as the newest that records what its re-read looked for, then whether it had an
engine. The finder's wording was not built: "the newest run with an OCR engine" is not how `looked` is chosen, and
"nothing is left to read again" drops "on this Mac" and the dying-cycle fact (the verifier's measurement). Tests:
`tests/test_setup_report.py::test_an_all_zero_re_read_table_is_one_line`,
`tests/test_setup_report.py::test_ocr_part_counts_images_documents_rereads_and_time`.

**The issue form's step 3 option is the attempt's own** (H11; dated line at §16.64 G12). G12 named a v7 to v15
step 3 failure "sync loop and report" in the title and kept v6's "IT request and report" in the `outcome` field, a
step those people never had, and the field is the one a maintainer filters on. The form,
`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/setup-report.yml`, adds `Failed at step 3 (sync loop and report)` after v6's step 3 option, which stays so v6 and older
links stay valid, and its description says to count both for step 3. `FORM_OUTCOME_OPTIONS` names the options in
the form's order; `Outcome.form_label` returns the attempt's own step name when the form has it as an option and
maps through `form_step` to v6's otherwise (v5, and v7's step 2 `install`, which keeps `install and start`). The cost
is the one G12 avoided, two buckets for step 3, now stated in the form and in setup-feedback.md. Tests:
`tests/test_setup_report.py::test_prompt_layout_is_picked_by_explicit_version`,
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py::test_setup_report_form_outcomes_match_the_readme_prompt` (every layout's failed step is
an option) and `test_setup_report_form_has_a_run_type` (the options are `FORM_OUTCOME_OPTIONS`).
Amended 2026-10-18, §16.121 S67 (by §16.110 Q25): v7's step 2 is `install and start`, the form's own option, so
`form_label` returns it unmapped.

**A git URL rewrite's host and path are redacted, in both reports** (H20; dated line at §16.46 Proxies). v15's git
stop names a URL rewrite as a cause, and with `url."https://<mirror>/".insteadOf = https://github.com/` git's error
names the mirror (`Could not resolve host: <mirror>`), which both reports printed in clear: only proxies were
registered. Both readers now read `[url "<base>"]` sections with an `insteadOf` key (never `pushInsteadOf`) from the
files they read git's proxies from (`~/.gitconfig`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config`, `/etc/gitconfig`, the two
checkouts' repository configs), as files, with no git process: on a Mac without the developer tools `/usr/bin/git`
opens the install dialog, and that is the step 1 stop in which the report runs. Python: `_git_rewrite_bases`, sharing
`_git_config_names` with `_git_proxy_urls`; shell: `git_rewrite_bases`, sharing `git_config_files` with
`git_proxy_values`, every pipeline stage under `LC_ALL=C`. A base is a URL (`https://user@host:port/path/`) or git's
scp form (`git@host:path`); a base whose host is `github.com`, in any case and form, is skipped, so the repository
locator and the issue link stay whole (registering it would have made GitHub `<proxy-N>`). For each other base its
host is registered as a proxy host is (a dotless generic host only inside a URL), then the base after its scheme and
user, as the PAC value is, so a company word in its path goes too (`dev.example/<org>/` would otherwise read
`<proxy-1>/<org>/`), and for the scp form its path with the leading `:`: the Python redactor matches `user@host` as
an email address before any value, so a printed `git@host:path` kept its path otherwise. A URL base's path is not a
value of its own (its base value covers it), nor is an scp path of a server's generic words only (`git`, `scm`,
`repos`: `_GENERIC_PATH_WORDS`, and the report's own words in Python), which would cut `/usr/bin/git` and a
`github.com` link (a reviewer's measurement); the shell matches the path as a whole word (pair flag `w`). The shell
also adds each value's lower-case form, since its pairs are case-sensitive and a resolver error prints the host in
lower case, and registers the base before the host, as it does the PAC value, so its `<proxy-N>` numbers can differ
from the Python report's. All are `<proxy-N>`, registered after git's proxies and before the LaunchAgent's, so no
existing `<proxy-N>` is renumbered and no placeholder class or legend changes. The Environment line adds a count, `URL rewrite in git's config: set (N)` or `not set`. Tests:
`tests/test_setup_report.py::test_a_git_url_rewrite_host_and_path_are_redacted` (with no git on PATH),
`tests/test_install_oneshot.py::test_the_shell_report_redacts_a_git_url_rewrite_host_and_path`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.75 J37: the shell matches the scp path with an end boundary only (a new pair flag `e`: no
letter or digit after it, as Python's value ends; its leading `:` marks the start), in its written and lower-case forms, and skips the report's own words as Python does;
as a whole word it never matched, since a host's last letter comes before the `:`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.75 J78: the shell's `<proxy-N>` numbers are the Python report's: it registers the
environment's hosts, the system proxy's where its Enable flag is 1, the PAC URL's host and `[network] proxy`'s, then
the PAC value, git's proxies, each rewrite's host, value and path, and the LaunchAgent's, one number for a value in
any case, and none for a value that names no proxy (`direct`, `none`, `off`); a system proxy host whose flag is 0,
or a per-interface one or PAC URL, which Python never reads, comes last.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.74 J20: a URL base after its scheme is no longer a value, which gave the host a second
`<proxy-N>`; a URL path, like an scp path, is a value of its own only when it has a company word, both readers match
the path with flag `e` (§16.75 J37), and the `<proxy-N>` legend names a rewrite.

**Two round 6 tests pin what they claim** (H45; tests only). In
`test_a_context_organisation_is_matched_only_after_an_app_name_and_only_for_a_generic_word` the `word_named_shown`
