### 16.70 Round 7: installer and the shell report (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 7 lane RB)

Round 7 findings (`round7/items/H<n>.md` of the bring-back cache) built in `scripts/install.sh`, each with a test in
`tests/test_install_oneshot.py`.

- **Step 1's synced-folder reader runs on the agentsync an earlier setup left** (H7; H15, H27 and H38 are the
  same defect). `--list-folders` runs `synced_folders` through the installed agentsync's interpreter, and step 2
  is what updates that agentsync. Round 6 (§16.63 G39) had the reader import `agentsync.paths.provider_link_resolved`
  bare. No agentsync installed before 2026-10-13 has that name, so on every Mac set up earlier the import failed,
  no folder was marked, no `already synced on this Mac:` line was printed, and an unattended agent stopped at the
  folder question. The import now sits in `try` / `except ImportError`, and the fallback is the same single
  `readlink` of the provider entry written with `os` and `pathlib` alone: it uses no other agentsync name
  (`cloud_storage_roots` and `cloud_relative` date from 2026-10-12, so a fallback built on them would fail on a
  Mac set up between 2026-09-29 and then). Only ImportError is caught: a config that does not load still reaches
  the warning. Measured with the agentsync of `53824b3b` (2026-09-29), `4a42af93`, `cebf2775` and this build: the
  same marks from all four, a folder stored through a provider link included.
  **The rule for the next name:** the reader may import `load_config` and `canonical_source_root` from
  `agentsync.config` with no guard; any other agentsync name is imported in a `try` whose `except ImportError`
  defines it with the standard library alone. `test_the_synced_folder_reader_imports_no_agentsync_name_an_older_build_lacks`
  parses the reader and fails on an import outside that rule;
  `test_list_folders_marks_the_synced_folders_with_an_agentsync_from_before_round_6` runs the list with an
  agentsync that lacks the name.
- **The warning names its cause in fixed words** (H14 and H16, one defect; H27's half of H7). The line is
  `warning: could not read which folders <config> already syncs (<cause>), so none is marked below`, and the
  cause is one of four, checked in this order: `no agentsync is installed`; `the reader took over 10 s`; `the
  installed agentsync is older than this installer (it has no <name>)`, where `<name>` is the identifier from
  the reader's `cannot import name '<name>'` line; `the installed agentsync could not load it`. The reader's
  stderr was thrown away before, and the one text, "no installed agentsync loads it", was false on a Mac that
  has one. Nothing else of what the reader wrote is printed: an error line can quote the config, and an agent
  copies a warning into the friction log. The prefix and the suffix are unchanged.
  `test_list_folders_says_why_an_installed_agentsync_could_not_run_the_reader`,
  `test_list_folders_marks_nothing_when_the_config_cannot_be_read`.
  Amended 2026-10-14, §16.75 J27: `the installed agentsync is older than this installer: it has no <name>`; the
  report's note says `...older than the installer: it had no <name>` and `...could not load it: a <class>`.
- **The shell report that may be sent says how** (H4). Its Redaction part ended on the legend and the report on a
  bare link: no private route, no "Nothing is sent automatically", and no word that the form opens empty. After
  the legend's paragraph `fallback_redaction` now writes one unwrapped line, `Send it: the link on the last line
  opens a blank "Setup report" issue form; paste this report into its Setup report field, or send it privately
  (docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md in the agentsync repository). Nothing is sent automatically.`, the agentsync
  report's words for a link that fills no field. A private-only report keeps its own `Send it: privately ...`
  line and no link. One line at column 0, so `stopped_report_note` drops it whole, as it does G50's.
  `test_the_shell_report_says_how_to_send_it_before_its_link`.
- **A generic folder's id leaves the shell report public** (H39 and H57, one defect). G8 gave a cloud folder's
  slug id its folder's `<folder-N>`, and G48's skip went by each pair's own value: the id `downloads` of a
  configured Downloads is lower case, so no `generic_folder`, and it is a word install.sh prints, so the report
  turned private only again, with no link. `fallback_redaction` reads `redaction_pairs` once, collects the
  placeholder of every pair whose value is a `generic_folder`, and skips every pair with one of those
  placeholders: the folder's own name decides for whatever shares its placeholder, in any pair order.
  `generic_folder` stays exact case, equal to `_GENERIC_FOLDERS`. A report word's folder beside a generic one
  (`Status`) is still private only. `test_the_shell_report_stays_public_with_a_generic_folders_id`,
  `test_the_shell_report_is_private_with_a_report_words_folder_beside_a_generic_one`.
- **An accented folder's id reads as its folder in the shell report too** (H76). `id_key` kept accents, so the
  id `cafe-plans` of the cloud folder `Café Plans` was `<source-1>` in the shell report and `<folder-1>` in the
  Python one (`_norm` drops them). `id_key` now removes blanks, `_`, `\` and `-`, then the accents the way
  `add_forms` does (NFD through `iconv -t UTF-8-MAC`, combining marks U+0300 to U+036F dropped), then lowers
  case. Every value goes through iconv: a bash pattern that asks "is this ASCII" follows the shell's locale, and
  under a UTF-8 one `a-z` holds a precomposed é, so the review's first build left an NFC name's accent in place
  in an ordinary terminal. A value that is not UTF-8 keeps its bytes, so it shares no folder's placeholder. In
  either Unicode form of the name, under `C` and under `en_US.UTF-8`.
  `test_the_shell_report_reads_an_accented_folders_id_as_the_folder`.
- **The friction fence's opener is never a placeholder** (H41). The opener `~~~text` was written before
  `redact_stream`, so a source id `text` made it `~~~<source-1>` (G6 covered only a folder named `text`), the
  read-back kept that line, and the section grew by a line a run. `redact_stream` passes the exact line
  `~~~text` through, as it does a heading, and `friction_text` drops every line that starts with `~~~`: both
  writers break a `~~~` in the log up, so such a line is a fence, an earlier report's redacted opener included.
  `test_the_shell_report_fences_the_friction_log_once`.
- **A dead alternative is gone from the stopped copy's relabel** (H44). `stopped_report_note` set `norun` on
  `- install.sh: no run during this attempt` or on the exact line `- install.sh: no run in the install log`, and
  reads `norun` only under `noout` (the Summary's `- installer output: no run of this attempt in the last `
  line). The agentsync report prints the second line only when install.log has no run, and then
  `_attempt_out_start` is `unknown` and the output line is the whole-count one, in every renderer that has the
  `noout` line; the shell report prints neither. So the pair never occurs, and the alternative could match only
  a quoted line elsewhere in the report, where it would pick the wrong label. Behaviour is unchanged, so no test
  fails without it; the stopped-report label tests pass as before.
- **The stopped NEXT's bring-back bracket stands where it belongs** (H18). After the fix, `(<path> was not
  touched: ...)` read as part of the fix's last clause ("... then paste the prompt again (<path> was not
  touched ...)"). It now follows the words it is about: `... so do not send it or bring it back (<path> was not
  touched and still holds the report of the last attempt that was not stopped): <fix>`, with no colon inside it
  since the fix's colon follows, and not as a `;` clause, which two of the fix texts already have. The fix is
  the last thing before ` [setup report: ...]`. Only where bring-back.md exists, as before.
  `test_a_stopped_newer_copys_next_says_its_version_once_and_of_the_installer`,
  `test_the_report_of_a_stopped_copy_invites_no_bring_back`.
- **The shell report states the one outcome it can, and fills its link for it** (H24). A session whose step 1
  failed before agentsync was installed has a shell report whose friction line states the prompt version and
  the agent, but its Summary had neither and its link was bare, while setup-feedback.md says to copy the values
  from the Summary. The rule is narrow so that it cannot drift from `compute_outcome`: the friction log's latest
  attempt (`friction_attempt_begin`'s boundaries) has exactly one timed line besides its end line; that line is
  a step 1 error that states `prompt vN, <agent>:` (`stated()`), and is not the line `--log-start` writes for a
  copy it stopped; and the attempt has no install run (a `--report-only` run with no install log, no install
  run in it, or a last one that started before the attempt). Then the Summary's third line reads `- outcome:
  failed at step 1 (computed: no install.sh run; step 1 logged an error) · prompt: vN (from the step 1 error
  line) · agent: <agent>`, redacted with the rest of the body, and the report ends on `ISSUE_URL&title=Setup
  report: Failed at step 1 (preflight) · vN&outcome=Failed at step 1 (preflight)&prompt_version=vN&agent=<agent>`,
  encoded as `urllib.parse.quote` encodes it: the string `build_issue_url` returns for those values with no run
  type (the shell computes none). The agent is read back from the redacted Summary line, since the link is
  written after redaction, keeps `A-Za-z0-9_ .:/()+,@<>-` and at most 100 characters (the Python report also
  keeps letters outside ASCII), and is left out when nothing remains. The `Send it: ` line then names the fields
  the link fills, in the agentsync report's words. In every other case the line reads `- outcome: not computed
  (this shell fallback computes none for this attempt; the issue form's fields are left for you, from the
  friction log below)` and the link stays bare. A private-only report still has no link, and a stopped copy's
  report still drops link and send line (a titled link starts with `ISSUE_URL`).
  `test_the_shell_report_states_a_step_1_failure_and_fills_its_link`,
  `test_the_shell_report_computes_no_other_outcome`,
  `test_the_shell_report_computes_no_outcome_once_the_attempt_ran_install`.
  Amended 2026-10-14, §16.75 J22: the line has ` · run: Sandbox (computed: HOME is under a temporary folder)`
  or ` · run: Real Mac (computed: ...)` before its agent, by `paths.is_temporary`'s rule, and the link has the
  run type in its title and `run_type` field, as `build_issue_url` writes them.
  Amended 2026-10-14, §16.75 J21: a stated version above `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT` adds `; newer than this

  Amended 2026-10-14, §16.75 J77: the agent keeps letters and digits outside ASCII as well (UTF-8 classes,

  Amended 2026-10-14, §16.81 K14: not only a one-line attempt: every timed line but the end line is a step 1
  line, and the first is the stated error, whose version and agent are the only ones read.
  Amended 2026-10-14, §16.81 K8: not computed, the line reads `- outcome: not computed (this shell fallback

  type from the run line)`, and a `- run: <label> (computed: <why>)` line follows it.
- **A list that could not read the config: built once, by lane RA; this lane adds why** (H8, with H16's log
  note). H8 is the defect of H17 and H28: the log line of a list whose reader failed was a new Mac's, so the

### 16.71 Round 7: converters and the .msg re-read (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 7 lane E)

(`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 7"; specs `round7/items/H<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built).

it; H52's, H47's and H77's "is 4" now have theirs at §16.66 G29, G52 and the `STUB_RENDER` paragraph.

**A policy tweak that keeps the label rule reads no withheld `.msg` again (H47; corrects §16.66 G52).**
`Manifest.mark_for_rescreen` takes `unread_only`, and `_check_policy_change` sets it while the new policy has a label
rule on: a refused `no converter for <suffix>` row is marked only when no byte of it was read (no content hash). G52
marked every such row, a binary `.msg` read on this Mac under the rule included, so a tweak that kept the rule on
(a second label id) read each one again, and the sync line counted them as converted and refused but not as
re-screened. Once the rule is lifted every such row is marked, as G52 built, a read one that has since gone
online-only included; marking only unread rows always would leave that one's stub for good. Pinned by
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_policy_tweak_that_keeps_the_label_rule_reads_no_binary_msg_again` and
`test_a_binary_msg_read_under_the_rule_then_online_only_is_read_once_the_rule_is_lifted` (the guard against the
narrower fix); `test_under_a_label_rule_a_refused_image_is_not_read_and_without_the_rule_it_is` stays green.

**QUARANTINE.tsv copies the reason of the stub as published (H52; corrects §16.66 G29's last sentence).**
`write_quarantine` no longer reads this run's OCR state. For a refused row a label rule may withhold (a rule on,
its suffix in `label_withheld_suffixes()`, its stored reason `no converter for <suffix>`) it copies the `reason:` of
the row's page (`Publisher._stub_reason`) when it is one of the two wordings, and otherwise keeps the stored reason.
Whether an image's stub says `withheld by label rule` is decided by the run that planned it; the TSV, rewritten every
run, followed each run's engine, so a run whose engine missed its `--version` made a TSV-only commit contradicting
the page, and an engine that arrived after the stub left the two disagreeing for good. Re-planning stubs when the
engine flaps would turn each flap into a page commit, so it is not done. Pinned by
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_quarantine_tsv_keeps_the_wording_of_the_published_stub_whatever_this_runs_ocr` (engine
on, on, off, off, on; and off, then on: one commit, page and TSV equal after every run).
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.90 L54: the TSV writes the withheld reason whenever the page says withheld as
`policy.page_says_withheld` reads it (reason, summary or body), so a page from before G29 whose `reason:` says `no
converter` is withheld in the TSV as in the setup report; `_stub_reason` is `_stub_says`.

**The no-converter docstrings (H56).** `NO_CONVERTER_PREFIX` says its stub's stored reason keeps the prefix while a
withheld stub's page, `reason:` and TSV row show `withheld by label rule: ...`; `label_withheld_suffixes()` says an

only.

for` (§16.97 M79); the report goes by the probe there too.

**A re-rendered tombstone with no `last_commit` names the commit that holds its content (H77; amends §16.60 F68,
§16.66 G77).** Compaction leaves a tombstone row with no `last_commit` (its commit squashed; the page keeps the

**A timing test reads the load when it starts (H78).** `tests/conftest.py` skips a `timing` test in

### 16.72 Round 7: setup prompt v16 (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 7 lane P)

The B13 round 7 items of lane P (specs `round7/items/H<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built). All ten need
prompt text (H6, H9, H19, H21, H25, H26, H30, H65, H66, H70), so the prompt is **setup prompt v16**:
`SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, `PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's `prompt v16` and `setup-prompt-compat 16`, the issue form's
placeholder and the block's digest move together; a saved v15 copy is stopped at step 1 like every older copy. v16
moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry and is read with v7's rules. None adds an agentsync command, an
installer flag, a config key or a friction kind. This section amends the older sections it names here; the older
text stays as the record of its version.
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J66:** as §16.67 did for v15, each text this section amends now has a dated line,
`Amended 2026-10-14, §16.79 J66 (by §16.72 H<n>)`, also at the v15 lines that quoted the text v16 replaced. "§16.36
and §16.43's finish" below is §16.49's "The finish" (R11, R30): neither section has a finish paragraph.

**The finish's folder list is the config's** (H9 and H30, one defect, built once; amends §16.36 and §16.43's
finish). v15 listed "those step 1's list marked [synced] and those step 2 added", with `sources.toml` only for a
step 1 that stopped before its list. The list can run to its end and mark nothing (an installed agentsync too old
for the reader's import, §16.70; the reader's 10 s timeout; a config the installed tool cannot load), and step 2
then prints `folders: kept the N already synced (none added)`, so the literal answer was a false "none: this Mac
syncs no folder". The finish now reads "the kind = "local" sources in ~/agent-context/sources.toml that are not
paused or retired, read after step 2 or, if setup stopped before step 2, as they are (never the inbox or another
kind = "inbox" folder), saying which of them this session added: those for which a run of step 2 this session
printed an "added source" line; or, if sources.toml has no such kind = "local" source, "none: this Mac syncs no
folder"". "Added" is add-source's own per-folder line (`added source '<id>' to <config>:`, printed only when it
writes the folder), which step 2's `add_source_filter` passes on; the `folders:` line gives counts only, so H30's
"as many as step 2's folders: line says" could not name the paths. H9's verifier keyed on the absence of the
`already configured:` line instead; the lane's review measured that a re-run of step 2 (which the prompt allows)
prints that line for every folder the first run added, so the positive line is the one built. Rejected: making step

**The keep command keeps a local commit and moves main to the update** (H19; amends §16.30's "The bring-back sends
local work once"). A checkout with a local commit behind origin fails the pull with "Not possible to fast-forward",
which the prompt did not call local changes; v15's keep command then failed at its commit ("nothing to commit",
exit 1) and left the checkout on its new branch with no upstream, so every later paste's pull said "no tracking
information" and got the network message (measured, git 2.54, a throwaway home). Step 1 now names git's words for
both kinds ("would be overwritten", "Not possible to fast-forward"), and the command is `... switch -c
local-work-<time> && ... add -A && { ... diff --cached --quiet || ... commit ...; } && ... format-patch -q
origin/main.. -o ~/agent-context/setup/local-work && ... fetch origin && ... switch -C main origin/main`, led by
`... merge-base --is-ancestor main HEAD &&`: it commits only what is staged, writes one patch per commit the update
lacks, and resets main to the update only after the branch and the patches exist (the old tip stays on the branch).
The leading check is the lane review's: on a checkout that is not on main, with a commit on main the checked-out
branch lacks, the reset left that commit on no branch and in no patch (measured); the check stops the command
first, exit 1 with no output and nothing changed, and the prompt sends that case, with "no tracking information",
to `git switch main` and step 1 again, where the keep runs from main. When only the fetch or the switch failed, the
prompt names those two to run again; a checkout already left on a branch runs `git -C ~/src/agent-context-sync
switch main` first. The Rules line's exception reads "keeping local changes on a branch and moving main to the
update, as step 1 says, is none of these", since `-C` resets a branch. §16.30's "Not by file name" paragraph now
holds for the commit of uncommitted changes only: a local commit's patch is named `NNNN-<its subject>.patch`, and a
second keep overwrites a first keep's patch only where both get the same number and subject; the section 3 reader
loops over every `*.patch` in name order and decides by each one's mtime whether to send it, so nothing there
changes. Tests: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py` (`test_readme_keeps_a_local_commit_and_moves_main_to_the_update`,
`test_the_keep_command_leaves_a_main_with_commits_of_its_own_as_it_is`,
`test_a_checkout_a_v15_keep_left_on_its_branch_goes_back_to_main`,
`test_readme_keeps_local_work_then_runs_step_1_again`, `test_step1_keeps_local_changes_on_a_branch_and_updates`).
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.75 J65: such a patch starts with the commit's author's name and email; bring-back.md's
header and setup-feedback.md now say so.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.82 K28: since v18 each patch name carries its keep's branch, so a second keep overwrites no
earlier keep's patch.
**Amended 2026-10-14, §16.85 K65 (by §16.76 J7, J8):** since v17 "no tracking information" no longer goes to a
bare `git switch main`: step 1 keeps the branch's work on a new `local-work-<time>` branch, writes its patches
(`origin/main..`), switches to main, gives main `origin/main` as its upstream only when it has none, names both
branches to the person and runs step 1 again.

proxy setting, which `git config --get-urlmatch http.proxy https://github.com` prints and which wins over the

(measured: `git remote get-url origin` resolved to the insteadOf host, only `--push` to the pushInsteadOf one); git
lower-cases the key name, so the anchored query keeps every insteadOf, whatever its case. Test:

config's"). Step 1's `--list-folders` installs nothing, so at the folder wait, and at any stop before step 2 on a new

**The no-tracking path keeps the branch's work and goes back to main** (J7 and J8, one defect, built once; amends
§16.72's "The keep command keeps a local commit and moves main to the update", whose back-to-main step this
replaces). v16 answered "no tracking information", and a keep command that stops at its first step, with a bare
`git switch main`. On a branch with no upstream, one commit and an uncommitted edit to a file main changes, while
local main holds a commit the branch lacks, that switch exits 1 ("would be overwritten"), the keep command exits 1
at once, and the prompt sends that case back to the switch: step 1 looped (measured, git 2.54). That path also
copied none of the branch's commits to `local-work/` and told the person nothing. Step 1 now runs, in one command,
`git switch -c local-work-<time>`, `add -A`, a commit only when something is staged, `format-patch -q
origin/main.. -o ~/agent-context/setup/local-work`, `git switch main`, and `{ git config --get branch.main.merge ||
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/main main; }`, then tells the person the name of the branch they were on and of
the new local-work branch, and runs step 1 again. The person's branch is left as it was (the verifiers' correction of
the finders' fix, which committed onto it). Two corrections by measurement: the patch base is `origin/main..`, the
keep command's, not the verifiers' `main..`, which on a branch cut from an origin/main newer than local main also
wrote the update's own commit as a patch (`0001-v7.patch` beside the local one, a throwaway home); and the last step
gives main `origin/main` as its upstream only when it has none (the verifier's optional case). Without it a main
with no upstream still says "no tracking information" after the switch, so step 1 looped there too, and each loop of
the new command would add a branch; an upstream main already has is left as it is. The pull of the next step 1 sends
a main with commits of its own through the keep command as before. Tests:

`test_a_checkout_a_v15_keep_left_on_its_branch_goes_back_to_main`,

`test_readme_keeps_a_local_commit_and_moves_main_to_the_update`, `test_readme_step1_is_one_command`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.85 K80 (by §16.82 K12, K13): since v18, after `git switch main` the recovery prints the
count of commits the local-work branch keeps (`git rev-list --count origin/main..@{-1}`) and says what was kept by
that count, and its upstream test is `test -n "$(git config --get branch.main.merge)"`, which prints no bare ref.

**J26: agentsync's log lines carry their time in UTC (`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.setup_report`).** The stderr
handler, which is the terminal and the background job's launchd err.log, wrote `logging`'s default local time
with no zone (`2026-10-13 21:14:25,778`), while the lock holder's `since` inside the same line and the launcher's
lines beside it are UTC: one line showed two clocks a day apart, and the terminal and the setup report showed

"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"` and `default_msec_format = "%s.%03dZ"` (no `datefmt`, which would drop the milliseconds):
`2026-10-14T02:14:25.778Z WARNING ...`, byte for byte what `_utc_log_times` writes, so the report shows the same
time as the terminal. The timestamp stays: that handler is the background job's only log, and Recent errors

**J35: `already configured` says why another path is the same folder (`agentsync.cli`).** `add-source` matches a
folder a source already has by more than its bytes (`_same_folder`: a provider link read through to its real name,
case and Unicode folded, `samefile`), and its line printed only the stored path, so a folder typed by its real
name read back as a different path with no reason. When the typed path (made absolute as the `added source`
branch does) is not the stored one, the line ends `: <typed> is the same folder by another name or path`, after
the config path, so `has path <stored> in ` still holds. It names no cause: a link, a case or Unicode form and

only of the first. Typed as stored, the line is unchanged. Test: `tests/test_cli.py`
(`test_add_source_takes_a_cloud_folder_stored_through_a_link_as_the_same_folder`).

**J33: STATE.md points its waits at its own sections (`agentsync.loop`, `agentsync.publish`).** STATE.md's
`## Next` holds the loop's waits as the terminal prints them, so the empty-folder and unlisted-folder waits told
the reader of STATE.md that `<docs repo>/_sync/STATE.md keeps the alarm line for <id>`, the file they were reading;
and the alarm under `## <id>`, stored as the sync printed it, says its WAITING ON YOU line is "at the end of a
sync's output", while in STATE.md that line is above it. The two lines are fixed in different ways, since only the
wait is built when STATE.md is written. `loop.next_step` and `loop.next_lines` take a keyword `in_state: bool =
False`, passed to `_named`; `write_state` passes `True`, and the pointer reads `the alarm line under ## <id> below
names <what> (a plain \`~/.local/bin/agentsync sync\` prints it too)`, or for two or more ids `the alarm lines
under ## <A> and ## <B> below name ...`. The alarm's stored text is not rewritten: it is persisted, carried from
earlier runs (`alarm (run N):`) and quotes untrusted folder names, and a substitution would tie publish to
arm_local's wording. Instead `## Next` ends with one fixed line, `publish._STATE_WAIT_LEGEND` (`(In this file the
WAITING ON YOU lines are here, under ## Next, and each source's alarm lines are under its own ## <id> section
below: where an alarm puts that line at the end of a sync's output, it is here.)`), written only when the block
holds a `WAITING ON YOU:` line, so it never points at a wait that is not there (the placeholder when the loop
cannot be read, or a carried alarm that outlived its wait). The terminal, `status`, install.sh and the setup report
keep the STATE.md pointer. Tests: `tests/test_loop.py` (`test_state_md_points_its_waits_at_its_own_sections`,
`test_a_folder_a_sync_cannot_list_is_a_wait_and_reaches_rule_4`).
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.84 K38, K42: the legend now reads `(In this file the WAITING ON YOU lines are here, under ##
Next, and each source's alarm lines are under its own ## <id> section below. When an alarm says the WAITING ON YOU
line at the end of a sync's output says what to do, that is the line here, under ## Next.)`, and it is written only
when the block holds a wait and an alarm STATE.md holds, this run's or a carried one, says that phrase.

**J29: the sync line names the label rule for a file it withheld unread (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.publish`,
`agentsync.model`, `agentsync.cli`).** H32's one clause, `Q refused without a read (no converter for the type, or
a rule that needs no bytes)`, took in an image a label rule withheld: `_no_converter` refuses it by its name with
the stored reason `no converter for .png`, while its page says `withheld by label rule: the label of a .png file
cannot be read`, and OCR converts a .png. The count is now split by the predicate that writes the page:
`Publisher.withheld(reason, suffix)`, a public wrapper of `_withheld` (a label rule on, a suffix it may withhold,
and for an image `images_readable`). `_publish` adds a refused, unread file to `withheld_unread` when that holds
and to `refused_unread` otherwise; `_SourceAcc`, `SourceReport` and `report()` carry the new field. `_print_report`
prints `; W withheld unread by the label rule (its label cannot be read without the file)`, then H32's clause, each
only when its count is above 0, with no bare `converted`, `deferred` or `read again` (install.sh's awk and
`setup_report._SPLIT_RE` read the line as before); with both 0 the line is unchanged. An image under a label rule
on a Mac with no OCR engine keeps `no converter for .png` on its page, and so it is counted under H32's clause, not
as withheld: a split inferred from `labels_active` alone would mislabel it. Correction to the verifier's fix: it
also reworded H32's clause to `(no converter for the type, or a label refused before a download)`, which names a
label on a run with no label rule and breaks the test it asked to keep (a no-rule refusal never mentions
"label"); H32's words are kept, true for every refusal that clause still counts. Tests: `tests/test_cycle.py`
(`test_a_withheld_image_is_counted_apart_from_a_type_with_no_converter`,
`test_without_an_engine_an_image_under_a_label_rule_is_counted_with_no_converter`), `tests/test_cli.py`
(`test_the_sync_line_names_the_label_rule_for_a_file_it_withheld_unread`).
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.83 K33: the clause's parenthesis reads `(a file whose label cannot be read: an image, a
binary .msg or a .msg not on this Mac)`; K54: W and Q are disjoint, and R + W + Q add up to the sources' `refused=`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.89 L33, L50: `(a file whose label cannot be read: an image or a .msg not on this Mac)`;
a binary .msg on this Mac is read and counted in R, named by the split's `, K of them withheld by the label rule`.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.107 O34: `(a file whose label cannot be read: an image, or a .msg not on this Mac)`.

next `reconcile --source <other>` printed it again from the meta. agentsync's own ignored files (`_sync/STATE.md`,
`_manifest/cache/`) now take the log scrubber (a bare rel path, also as STATE.md quotes it: whitespace runs
collapsed); a user's ignored files keep the paired one. `_manifest_apply` marks each carried line that names a

stays, and a value it cannot read is deleted. Test:

`test_a_stopped_log_start_value_the_session_ran_again_is_a_rerun_not_a_failure` (1 s, 23 s and 2m01s rows).
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.86 L21: the bracket reads `failed at step 1 (an older copy, or a changed --log-start value;
the next attempt, 23s later, said v17)`.

**A git URL rewrite's path: one rule in both readers** (K10, K46; K77 not built; one code path; K72's dated line at §16.79 is

  shell's flag `e` redacted them. A value registered `keep_lead` (a rewrite path) gets the shell's end check: no
  letter or digit may follow. Every other `/` value keeps its rule.
- K10 is lane RB's K2 and K27, one defect, built once there (§16.81, `Redactor.add(keep_lead=True)` and
  install.sh's `${v:0:1}<proxy-N>`): the placeholder swallowed the path's separator, so a base read
  `https://<proxy-1><proxy-2>/...`, like a base written without its slash. This lane adds only an escaped form

  Registering the path without its separator (the finder's first fix) was not built: `gh` alone would redact

- K77, not built: a path that is no report word (`/gh`) still cuts `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh` to

  in exactly those places. A narrower rule (only after `bin`, `sbin` or `.config`) still leaks a company tool named
  like the path. The path is registered only when it holds a word that is neither generic nor a report word, which
  is usually the company's, so over-redacting a tool path is the cost kept. The finder's "only after its own host"
  was not built either: J37 redacts the path after any host on purpose.
Tests: `test_a_git_url_rewrite_host_and_path_are_redacted`, `test_the_shell_report_redacts_a_git_url_rewrite_host_and_path`,
`test_the_two_reports_number_each_proxy_value_alike` (numbers unchanged).

### 16.82 Round 9: setup prompt v18 (2026-10-14, wave B13 round 9 lane P)

The B13 round 9 items of lane P (specs `round9/items/K<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built). Nine need
prompt text (K9, K12, K19, K20, K25, K28, K31, K32, K78), so the prompt is **setup prompt v18**:
`SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, `PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's `prompt v18` and `setup-prompt-compat 18`, the issue form's
placeholder and the block's digest move together; a saved v17 copy is stopped at step 1 like every older copy. v18
moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry. K13 and K73 need no prompt text of their own and ship in it. No
other lane sent prompt words. None adds an agentsync command, an installer flag, a config key or a friction kind.
The older text this section amends stays as the record of its version; dated lines are where an item's spec asks.

**A folder list that could not read the config is not a wait** (K9, K20, K32, K73, K78: one defect, built once;
records the decision §16.75 J17 left to lane P, which §16.76 did not record: v17 kept only the "already synced on
this Mac:" exception). Where step 1's `--list-folders` could not read an existing `sources.toml` (no agentsync,
a reader timeout, an older build, a config that does not load), it marks nothing and prints no "already synced"
line, and its folder `NEXT:` ends "; this Mac has a config (<config>) whose folders could not be read: if it was
set up before, <install.sh> with no --source-local keeps whatever that config syncs, and each --source-local only
adds" (§16.75 J17), plus "; or re-run <install.sh> --list-folders to mark them" after a timeout. v17's agent that
could not ask logged a deviation and waited, and the report called the question "a turn agentsync caused" (round 9
rehearsals b, c, e). v18 step 1 has a second exception, keyed on those words and only on a list that printed
folders (the sign-in `NEXT:`s carry the same clause and keep v17's no-folder-paths rule): run the offered re-run
once; if no list marked a folder, say the list could not read them and that, if this Mac was set up before, step 2
with no `--source-local` keeps them, and ask only whether to add one; an agent that cannot ask adds none and runs
step 2 with no `--source-local`, which is not a deviation. The words do not claim folders are kept, since an
inbox-only config keeps none (the verifiers' correction): if step 2 then says no folder is synced yet, the Mac syncs
no folder after all, and step 1's folder question applies as on a new Mac (an agent that cannot ask
chooses none and waits). The README's intro says the same (K73).
`setup_report.unread_asked` gates the three uses of `unread_synced` (the outcome reason, the expected-turns line's
"so it was asked: see Items", the Item): from `UNREAD_GOES_ON` (18) the question is the expected "at most whether
to add one", the human turns count it as the already-synced case does, and the expected-turns line reads "no
folder question (N folders already synced; step 1's list could not read them, so it asked at most whether to add
one; not logged)". v17 and older, an attempt that states no version, and a v18 attempt that logged a step 1
deviation (its agent waited all the same: K9's verifier) keep v17's reading. Tests: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py`
(`test_a_folder_list_that_could_not_read_the_config_goes_on_unattended`,
`test_readme_prompt_asks_a_mac_already_set_up_for_no_folder`, `test_list_folders_is_step_1s_only_listing`),
`tests/test_setup_report.py` (`test_from_prompt_v18_a_list_that_could_not_read_the_config_costs_no_turn`).
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.86 L23: the line reads "... could not read them, so step 1 asks at most whether to add one;
not logged)": the step asks, not its list. Amended 2026-10-14, §16.86 L7: so does a v18 attempt whose install could
not count the folders either (its config step logged no `kept=`).

**The branch recovery says what it kept** (K12, K13; amends §16.76's J7 and J8 paragraph). On a main with no
upstream and nothing of its own, v17's recovery made an empty local-work branch and wrote no patch, while the
words after it said "my commits stay on my branch" and that the work was "copied as patches"; on a main with a
commit of its own the next keep's `switch -C main origin/main` moves main, so the first claim was false there too
(K12, measured in throwaway homes). After `git switch main` the command now runs `git rev-list --count
origin/main..@{-1}` (`@{-1}` is the local-work branch just made), which prints the number of commits that branch
keeps and no path; at 0 the agent says there was nothing to keep and that the person may delete that branch,
otherwise that all of the work is on it and copied as patches, and only for a branch other than main that the
person's commits also stay on it. `format-patch -q` stays quiet, since without `-q` it prints paths that hold the
login. Its upstream test is `test -n "$(git config --get branch.main.merge)"`, which prints nothing where main
already follows the Source; v17's bare `config --get` printed `refs/heads/main` there (K13: a branch with no
upstream while main tracks the Source; a main with no upstream printed git's "set up to track" line, as now). Test:
`test_the_branch_recovery_prints_what_it_kept_and_no_bare_ref`.

**The finish's folder-wait clause covers the folder wait only** (K19; dated lines at §16.43's H3 paragraph and
§16.72's H6 paragraph). "...; the folder list's NEXT: line is not a step for me" stood on its own after a
semicolon, so it also read as covering the list's exit-3 stops (OneDrive not signed in, no folders synced yet),
whose `NEXT:` is the person's step and the one the finish names. It now reads "(also "none: waiting for your
folder answer" while you wait for my folder answer in step 1: there, the NEXT: line that leaves the folders to
choose is not a step for me)". Test: `test_readme_step3_runs_the_loop_then_the_report`.

**A broken checkout goes to the clone's stop** (K25). Step 1 pulled whenever `~/src/agent-context-sync/.git`
was a folder, so an empty `.git`, or one with no `HEAD`, gave git's "not a git repository", which the prompt routed
to the proxy advice; and under a home that is itself a repository, git climbed to it, and "no tracking
information" sent the branch recovery to commit the whole home there (measured, git 2.54). Step 1 now tests
`[ -f ~/src/agent-context-sync/.git/HEAD ]` (the Claude Code allow rule too), so both go to the clone and its "already
exists and is not an empty directory" stop; a `.git` file keeps its route. As a second net, git's "not a git
repository" is the not-a-checkout stop, and "detected dubious ownership" is a stop of its own: the folder belongs to
another user account, the person moves it aside, and the agent does not run the `safe.directory` command git
suggests. Both are in the list of stops that log the failed command before the report. Tests:
`test_a_folder_at_the_checkouts_path_that_is_not_a_checkout_is_named`, `test_readme_step1_is_one_command`,
`test_readme_step1_command_clones_then_pulls`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.88 L61: the `[ -f .git/HEAD ]` test alone left one case open. A `.git` holding HEAD but no
objects or refs, or a HEAD that names no ref, passes it, and under a home that is a repository git still climbed
there, so "no tracking information" sent the recovery to commit the home (measured, git 2.54). Since v19 step 1's
command and each git recovery export `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES="$HOME/src"` (§16.88), and the two stops this
paragraph names run no installer and write no report.

**Each kept patch carries its keep's branch** (K28; dated lines at §16.30's "Not by file name" and §16.72's H19
paragraph). Two keeps, each with an uncommitted change, both wrote `0001-local-changes-kept-before-update.patch`,
so the second overwrote the first in the folder the person was told holds it; after a folder wait no report had
read the first. Both keep commands now run `format-patch -q --suffix=".$(git branch --show-current).patch"`
right after `switch -c local-work-<time>`, so each name ends `.<that branch>.patch` (git shortens the subject part).
Section 3 reads `local-work/*.patch` flat, as before; per-branch folders would need a second glob, as `/bin/bash`
3.2 has no `**`. Test: `test_a_second_keep_leaves_the_first_keeps_patch` (two keeps, both patches, both in
bring-back.md).
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.91 L65: not "right after" `switch -c local-work-<time>`. In both commands `format-patch` runs
after `add -A` and the commit (made only when something is staged), still on the new `local-work-<time>` branch, so
`branch --show-current` names it and the suffix is the same.

**The git stop's commands are the person's** (K31). The block opens with "Run each command yourself", and the git
stop's quote named three commands without saying whose they are. Run by the agent, `git config --get-urlmatch
http.proxy`, the `insteadof` query and `env | grep -i proxy` print proxy hosts, company paths and any stored
credential into the chat, where the report prints only yes or no (`install.sh` proxy lines). After the quote:
"(those three commands are mine to run in my own terminal: do not run them yourself)". The finder's other option,
the agent running the two git reads, would make things worse for that reason and is not built. Test:
`test_readme_step1_is_one_command`.

### 16.83 Round 9: sync, status, locks and doctor (2026-10-14, wave B13 round 9 lane B)

**K33: the sync line's withheld-unread clause names the cause its files share (`agentsync.cli`).** J29's clause
read `; W withheld unread by the label rule (its label cannot be read without the file)`. W holds an image on this
Mac while OCR could read it, whose stub says `the label of a .png file cannot be read`: having the file does not

share: `(a file whose label cannot be read: an image, a binary .msg or a .msg not on this Mac)`. The count and its
prefix `W withheld unread by the label rule` are unchanged, since `setup_report._WITHHELD_UNREAD_RE` reads only
that prefix and install.sh does not read the clause; there is still no bare `converted`, `deferred` or `read
again` in it. The count is not split into images and .msg files: that needs a new field across `model`, `cycle`
and `setup_report` and is not needed for a true line. Tests: `test_cycle.py::
test_the_sync_line_does_not_say_a_local_image_needs_the_file_for_its_label`, and the pins in
`test_cli.py::test_the_sync_line_names_the_label_rule_for_a_file_it_withheld_unread` and
`test_setup_report.py`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.89 L33, L50: the parenthesis reads `(a file whose label cannot be read: an image or a
.msg not on this Mac)`; a binary .msg on this Mac is read, so it is in R, and the split names it (`, K of them
withheld by the label rule`).

**K34: the first-read bracket after `read again R` no longer says both things of one file (`agentsync.cli`,

2 (2 of them read for the first time, also counted above)`. It now reads `read again 2 (2 of them a first read: a
stub whose bytes had never been read, now in the count above)`. `, read again R` stays byte for byte, with R right
after it and its meaning unchanged, because four readers take R from it: install.sh's awk (the note's
`-reread-R`), `_CONVERTED_LINE_RE`'s group `r`, `_CONVERTED_NOTE_RE`, and an older installed agentsync reading a
newer install.out. The finder's `re-read R for ...` is not built for that reason. The bracket has no bare
`converted`, `deferred` or `again`. `_FIRST_READ_RE` reads the new words and the old ones, so an older install.out
still gives the count, and the report's first-sync clause renders `read again R: F of them a first read, of a stub
whose bytes had never been read, also in the converted count`. Tests: `test_cli.py::
test_the_summary_line_counts_the_files_read_again_apart_from_those_converted`, `test_setup_report.py::
test_first_sync_clause_carries_the_read_again_count` (both wordings), `test_setup_report.py::
test_the_converted_line_parses_with_the_read_again_clause_in_either_form`, `test_install_oneshot.py::
test_first_sync_note_reads_the_read_again_count_past_the_first_read_bracket`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.89 L34: when F = R the head itself reads `, first read R (stubs whose bytes had never been
read, now in the count above)`, and every reader named above takes R from either head; the report drops the comma
before `of a stub`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.87 L16: both brackets end `so also counted as converted)`, not `now in the count above)`
(L34's head too). A bracket may hold `converted`, never as a field of its own (`converted)` is none), so never

**K37: a lock held by a sync reads as a sync and its pass (`agentsync.ops.lock`).** A sync typed in a terminal
holds the lock as `poll`, as the background job does, so `_describe_holder`'s `pid <n> (poll) since ...` read as
the job on the stderr skip line, the cycle's lock-wait WARNING and doctor. A `CycleMode` label now reads `pid <n>
(a sync, its pass: poll) since ...`, as H33's skip WARNING already says it; `governance` and `exclude-empty` are
printed as before. The lock body keeps its four fields: a fifth would make an older build's `LockInfo.parse`, which
install.sh imports, read a live holder as an unparseable body. `_holder_identity` (`LockHeldError.who`) keeps the
bare label, so the report's Recent errors still merge repeated skips. The verifier's optional `started_by` key in
the holder sidecar is not built: no reader asks which starter it was, and the run's pass is what the line must not
misname. Tests: `test_ops_lock.py::test_a_cycle_holder_reads_as_a_sync_and_its_pass`, and the pins in
`test_ops_lock.py`, `test_setup_report.py` and `test_cli.py`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.89 L73: the `started_by` key is built, from the environment (`launchd.in_our_job`), never
from the arguments; the line names `the background job` or `a sync not started by the background job` when the

**K40: an empty-folder wait no longer says the alarm names every folder (`agentsync.loop`).** With six empty
folders the exclude-empty wait said STATE.md's alarm line `names the folder(s)`, but the alarm names five and how

and `test_exclude_empty.py`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.89 L14, L36, L38: the words are `up to five, and past five how to list the
rest`; L48, L67: the unlisted-folder waits now say `one or more folders` and that the alarm names `what could not
be listed` with the same words.

**K41: the empty-folder alarm's "prints them" holds for one wait line (`agentsync.arm_local`).** With two or more
empty folders the alarm said each WAITING ON YOU line about the source says what to do, and that status `prints
them too`, though any number of plain empty folders makes one exclude-empty wait. It now ends `prints each one too`,
true for one line or three; one folder keeps the singular form. The plural is not computed from the arm's side:
which wait a folder lands on depends on the manifest rows, which the walk does not see. The comment now counts one

test_zero_child_cloud_dirs_log_at_info_and_the_scan_alarm_names_them` and the pin beside it.

**K54: the W and Q counts' docstrings (`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.model`).** `_print_report`'s docstring made W
part of Q (`counts those of them ...`) and said Q alone makes the line's refusals add up. W and Q are disjoint, and
R + W + Q add up to the sources' `refused=`. `SourceReport.withheld_unread`'s comment said `neither on this Mac`,
false for an image, which is withheld on this Mac too while OCR could read it; a .msg in W is one not on this Mac,
since a local .msg is read and a refused one counts in R. Words only, no code change, so no new test.

**K55: the UTC log test restores TZ before its `tzset` (`tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_cli.py`).** J26's test set
TZ with `monkeypatch`, deleted it and ran `tzset`; monkeypatch put the old TZ back after the test with no `tzset`
behind it, so `time`'s cached zone stayed the system's. `conftest.zone(name)` sets TZ, then restores the old value
(or removes it) and runs `tzset`; the test and the setup report's `mac_zone` fixture share it. Test:

**K57: J69's condition is one line (`agentsync.cli`).** ruff's formatter had wrapped `if red.private_only:` in

**K75: on status's path an inbox no wait names reads the install note (`agentsync.ops.doctor`).** J12 kept `sync

### 16.84 Round 9: stubs, front matter and purge (2026-10-14, wave B13 round 9 lane E)

Lane E's round 9 items: K38, K42, K50, K51, K52, K63, K74 built; K79 kept not built, with a test that pins it. K38
and K42 are one change.

**K38, K42: STATE.md's wait legend names the alarm's words, and only beside such an alarm (`agentsync.publish`,
`agentsync.model`, `agentsync.arm_local`).** Dated line at §16.77 J33. The legend's `where an alarm puts that line
... it is here` had no clear antecedent; it now quotes the alarm's phrase and says that line is the one under `##
Next`, keeping `## <id> section below`. It was written beside any wait, so a baseline draft wait with no alarm in
the file still explained alarm lines; it is written now only when an alarm STATE.md holds, this run's or a carried
one, says its wait is `at the end of a sync's output`. That phrase is one constant, `model.SYNC_OUTPUT_END`, which
the empty-cloud-folder alarm and the check share. Tests:
`test_loop.py::test_state_md_points_its_waits_at_its_own_sections`,
`test_loop.py::test_state_md_writes_its_wait_legend_only_when_an_alarm_there_names_the_wait`.

**K50: an online-only image a label rule refuses keeps its stub on a run with no engine (`agentsync.cycle`).** Such
an image is pending work every pass, and `_stub_stands` planned its stub with this run's OCR state, so a run whose
engine missed turned `withheld by label rule` into `no converter for .png` (page and QUARANTINE.tsv, a commit) and
the next run with an engine turned it back. On a run that cannot read images `_stub_stands` passes `plan_pages(...,
withheld=)` the page's own decision (`_page_withheld`, as §16.78 J47's re-render does), as §16.71 H52 says the run
that planned the stub decides; a run with an engine still upgrades a `no converter` page once, and a later run with
none does not revert it. Test:
`test_cycle.py::test_an_online_only_image_a_label_rule_refuses_keeps_its_stub_whatever_this_runs_ocr`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.90 L47: `_page_withheld` reads the page's `reason:` and `summary:` lines without a YAML
parse (`publish._withheld_on_page`), which cost about 1 s per 2000 such stubs on every poll with no engine.

**K51: a purge keeps another source's STATE.md line that names the same rel path (`agentsync.governance`).**
§16.78 J48 scrubbed STATE.md with the log scrubber, which cuts a bare rel path under any heading, so purging one
source's file also cut another source's line about its own file of that name, which J46 keeps in the carried meta.
`_reset_worktrees` scrubs STATE.md section by section: under the `## <id>` of a configured source a line goes when
the paired scrubber hits it or it names that source's purged file by its bare rel path (`own_line_hit`, as its
carried lines are scrubbed); under any other heading the log scrubber decides as before. Test:
`test_loop.py::test_a_purge_leaves_the_purged_files_name_in_neither_state_md_nor_its_carried_lines`.

**K52: `_STUB_RENDER_META` keeps its own docstring (`agentsync.cycle`).** J47's `_WITHHELD_BODY` and
`_WITHHELD_WORDS` sat between the constant and its attribute docstring; they move below it, no value changes. Test:
`test_cycle.py::test_the_stub_render_meta_keeps_its_own_docstring`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.91 L55 (by §16.80 K48): the two constants are no longer in `agentsync.cycle`. K48 moved them
to `agentsync.policy`, where `page_says_withheld` reads them, and dd3fa850 made them private:
`policy._WITHHELD_BODY` and `policy._WITHHELD_WORDS`. The K52 test still checks only that `_STUB_RENDER_META` is
followed by its own docstring.

**K63: the recording index's How to read defines `SAID vN:` and `SPEAKING:` (`agentsync.convert.recording_page`,
README).** Both fold into the existing `SCREEN:` and `TILE:` lines, as the sample index in the grammar tests shows:
N numbers a voice, not a person; `SPEAKING:` is the one label the meeting app lit, and with `TILE:` is on-screen
text, not proof of who spoke. The README's tag list names `SCREEN+:` and `SCREEN-:`. The recording
`_EMITTER_VERSION` is not bumped: it is part of every picture piece's key (`_picture_version`), so a bump would
read every frame of a recording again on its next conversion for a legend change; a page keeps the legend it has
until its recording is converted again. Tests:
`test_recording_grammar.py::test_how_to_read_defines_every_tag_a_window_line_carries`,
`test_deploy_pack.py::test_the_readme_says_what_a_recording_page_reads_of_speech_and_which_decks_get_ocr`.
Amended 2026-10-14, §16.90 L51: a page keeps the legend it has until its bytes, converter version or options
change; the index revision is in the options, so a new conversion of the same bytes (a copy, a repair rebuild)
gets the new legend from no cache entry.
Amended 2026-10-15, §16.96 M64, M65: the line above is wrong twice. A version or options change alone converts
nothing again, and a repair rebuild re-renders the cache entry under its outputs row's stored key, so a page keeps
the legend it has until its recording is converted again (new bytes, or a re-read: `outdated()`, or a capability or
converter it was read without, per `_lacks`). The index revision is in the options, so a new conversion of the same
bytes, such as a copy, no longer gets the cached index, and reads every frame and the sound again once the cycle
has deleted that recording's pieces.

**K74: a DEL or C1 character in a title or a file name is written as an escape (`agentsync.frontmatter`).**
`_render_scalar` wrote strings with `json.dumps`, which leaves DEL, U+0080-009F, U+FFFE/FFFF and lone surrogates
raw; YAML refuses them, so one mail subject or file name holding one made a page no reader parses, and the land
gate's repo-wide FRONTMATTER finding held every source's commit on every run. `_quote` writes each, and U+2028 and
U+2029, as `\uXXXX`, which YAML and the `reason:` line's JSON read both decode. A page whose `source_path` or
`part_name` holds U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029 re-renders once: those used to fold to a space on read. Tests:
`test_frontmatter.py::test_a_character_yaml_refuses_or_folds_reads_back_as_written`,
`test_frontmatter.py::test_a_plain_title_renders_as_it_did`,
`test_frontmatter.py::test_a_control_character_in_a_title_or_name_holds_no_sync`.

**K79: kept not built: an old-form CHANGELOG line a live file shares with a purged one (`agentsync.governance`).**
Dated line at §16.78 J50. ``q3-`plan`-x`` and a live ``q3-'plan`-x`` write one pre-H37 form, `q3-'plan'-x`, which is
neither's path now, so the line cannot be told apart and the purge scrubs it (R123's fail-closed rule); the live
item loses only its pre-H37 CHANGELOG line. Sparing it whenever a live twin exists would leave the purged file's
own old line in history, with the purge VERIFIED, when the twin never wrote one; sparing it per commit, where the
commit's tree holds the twin and not the purged page, fails the same way, since a month's CHANGELOG carries
earlier commits' lines forward. Test:
`test_review_fixes.py::test_a_purge_scrubs_an_old_form_line_a_live_file_shares_and_keeps_that_files_own_lines`.

**A Mac at `STUB_RENDER` 5 runs J74's wider tombstone pass** (K70; dated lines at §16.66's "`STUB_RENDER` is 4",

**The local-work line says only what it can know** (L8, L25, L40, L58; dated lines at §16.80 K30 and §16.75 J65).
`- local work kept by setup prompt step 1: 1 local-work branch(es) in the checkout, 0 patch file(s) ... (the

an earlier report carried by its hash, not its text (L8, L25); and a nested patch was counted though section 3
reads only `local-work/*.patch` (L8, L25). Both readers now read: with a patch, `- local work kept by setup prompt
step 1: N patch file(s) in the setup folder's local-work, newest written <UTC> (no patch text is in this report:
each patch goes once to the private bring-back.md section 3; one an earlier report already carried is listed there
by its hash); M local-work branch(es) in the checkout`; with branches and no patch, `- local-work branch(es) in
the checkout: M, no patch file in the setup folder's local-work (a keep with nothing to keep writes none)`; with
neither, no line. Patches are the top-level, non-hidden regular `*.patch` files (L40's verifier kept any depth;
L8's and L25's matching section 3 is built, since every keep command writes to the top). A branch whose sha (loose
file, else `packed-refs`, no git process) equals `refs/heads/main`'s or `refs/remotes/origin/main`'s is not
counted (L58's verifier; a branch cut from an older origin/main still counts). The bracket is

first and prints the header's author sentence only when section 3 sends a patch; when every patch was in an

### 16.88 Round 10: setup prompt v19 (2026-10-14, wave B13 round 10 lane P)

The B13 round 10 items of lane P (specs `round10/items/L<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built unless a
measurement below says otherwise). All ten need prompt text, so the prompt is **setup prompt v19**:
`SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, `PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's `prompt v19` and `setup-prompt-compat 19`, the issue form's
placeholder and the block's digest move together, and a saved v18 copy is stopped at step 1 like every older copy.
v19 moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry. Lane RB sent words for its L11, built here; no other lane
sent prompt words. None adds an agentsync command, an installer flag, a config key or a friction kind. Where this
section changes what §16.82 describes, §16.82 stays the record of v18; the one dated line is where L61's spec asks.
Amended 2026-10-15, §16.97 M81: that line is in §16.82's broken-checkout paragraph (L61; dated line at §16.82 K25).

**Git never searches above ~/src** (L6, L61: one defect, built once). In a home that is itself a git repository,
a checkout whose `.git` git does not accept (HEAD alone, or a HEAD that names no ref, even beside `objects/` and
`refs/`) passed v18's `[ -f .git/HEAD ]` test, git searched upward to the home, the pull said "no tracking
information", and the recovery for it switched the home's repository to a local-work branch and committed the home's
untracked files there (probe e4h, measured). Step 1's command and each of its three git recoveries now start with
`export GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES="$HOME/src" &&`, so such a checkout gives "not a git repository", the not-a-checkout
stop; the export also covers the git calls inside `$( )`, and installer and agentsync processes inherit it harmlessly
(their repositories are the checkout, below the ceiling, and `~/agent-context/docs`, outside it). A valid clone, one
under a symlinked `~/src` (git resolves the ceiling) and a `.git` file all still pull. L61's corrected fix,
`git --git-dir=.git pull`, is not built: an explicit git dir skips git's ownership check (measured with
`GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1`, git 2.54 and Apple git 2.50: "Already up to date." where discovery says
"detected dubious ownership"), so another account's checkout would pull, running its config and hooks, and the
ownership stop would never fire. Comparing `rev-parse --show-toplevel` with the path misroutes a symlinked `~/src`
(L61's verifier). The Claude Code allow list gains `Bash(export GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES="$HOME/src")` (an allow rule
matches a subcommand's whole text, and `export` is a subcommand of its own), and Copilot's list the same `shell(...)`.
Tests: `test_step1_and_its_recoveries_never_reach_a_repository_above_the_checkout` (runs v18's commands too, which
commit the home), `test_readme_pre_allow_rules_cover_every_command`.

**A checkout whose `.git` is a file pulls** (L27). `git clone --separate-git-dir` and a git worktree leave `.git` a
file, so v18 cloned onto a good checkout and told the person to move it aside. Step 1 tests `[ -f .git/HEAD ] || [ -f
.git ]`. An empty or junk `.git` file then reaches the pull, whose "invalid gitfile format" the not-a-checkout stop
now names beside "not a git repository" (a dangling `gitdir:` gives the latter). A second worktree of another
checkout also pulls; on a branch with no upstream, its no-tracking recovery cannot take main from the worktree that
has it out, and git's "is already used by worktree" (git 2.54 and Apple git 2.50; the CI runner's `/usr/bin/git`
resets that main instead, lossless under the ancestor test) is a not-a-checkout stop too, whose
words now read "not a checkout this setup can use" and name the local-work branch the recovery made (the lane's
review found that loop: v18 cloned onto such a folder instead). The allow list gains `Bash([ -f
~/src/agent-context-sync/.git ])`, so step 1 needs the first eight rules. Test:
`test_a_checkout_whose_git_is_a_file_pulls`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.94 M17, M69: "lossless under the ancestor test" covered only the local-work commits: the
runner's reset (Apple git 2.39.5's) moves the main another worktree has out under that checkout's files, which then
hold a staged revert of the update. Since v20 every recovery goes back with a plain `switch main`, which refuses there
on every git from 2.39.5 to 2.54, and the worktree case is a stop of its own that names both of git's phrases, the
person's branch, the local-work branch and `git worktree move`.

**A main the recovery keeps in full moves to the update** (L9). On a main with a commit of its own and no upstream,
v18's no-tracking recovery went back to main as it was; the next pull said "Not possible to fast-forward", and the
keep command kept the same commit again, on a second branch and in a second patch (probe G3c). The recovery's
`switch main` is now `{ if git merge-base --is-ancestor main HEAD; then git switch -C main origin/main; else git
switch main; fi; }`: HEAD is the new local-work branch there, so the test holds exactly when that branch keeps every
commit of main, and only then is the reset lossless. Where main has commits the branch lacks (the keep command's
exit-1 case), main stays as it was. `switch -C` from a remote-tracking branch sets the upstream, so git's "set up to
track" line comes before the count, and the upstream step is a no-op there. The optional `fetch` before format-patch
is not built: step 1's pull fetched before it failed. Tests: `test_the_branch_recovery_prints_what_it_kept_and_no_bare_ref`,
`test_a_checkout_a_v15_keep_left_on_its_branch_goes_back_to_main`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.94 M69, M83: since v20 the reset is `switch main && reset -q --keep origin/main`, which sets
no upstream, so git's "set up to track" line comes from the upstream step, after the count, and only where main had
none; a count of 0 also deletes the local-work branch, in the same chain.

**A kept patch's name keeps its subject** (L17, L30: one defect, built once). git counts `--suffix` inside
format-patch's 64-character file-name cap, so with the 33-character branch suffix a subject kept about 25 characters
("0001-local-changes-kept-before.<branch>.patch"). Both keep commands run `git -c format.filenameMaxLength=128
format-patch`. Not `--filename-max-length=128` (L17's finder): that option arrived in git 2.30, and an older git
would fail it after the keep's commit, with no patch written and main not restored; an unknown config key is ignored.
Test: `test_a_kept_patch_name_keeps_its_whole_subject` (v18's command cuts both subjects).

**Only this prompt's installer logs or reports at a step 1 stop** (L31). The not-a-checkout and ownership stops ran
`install.sh --log` and `--report-only` from whatever copy the folder held (a v14 archive's, measured), and the
ownership stop ran another account's script. Those two stops now run no `install.sh` command and write no report or
"## Not used" section. The Xcode and other-git-failure stops, where no pull ran, first run `install.sh --version`
(it checks for the developer tools before it calls git) and log and report only when it ends with this prompt's
number; otherwise they tell the person the code on the Mac is not this prompt's version and setup stopped before it
could be updated. The finish still applies after every one of these stops. Step 1's version check now reads "the
--version inside step 1's one command", so the Xcode and git stops' own `--version` is not taken for it. Step 3's
no-report cases are four. Test: `test_readme_step1_is_one_command`, `test_readme_report_step_after_any_failure`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.94 M16, M32: "where no pull ran" was so at the Xcode stop only; at the other-git-failure
stop the pull ran and failed. Since v20 the prompt says step 1 did not update that copy, and the stop with no report
also says the person has nothing more to do: the next paste tries the update first. Test:
`test_readme_step1_is_one_command`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.103 N68: the version check and the four no-report cases are v19's (this paragraph's own
text, as 93cedc51 wrote it); v20's line had been spliced in before them, so it read as if v20 made them.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.106 O27: since v22 "the code on this Mac is not this prompt's version" is said only when the
installer exists and its output does not end with this prompt's number; with no installer (the Xcode stop on a new
Mac, a first clone that failed) the agent runs nothing more and says setup stopped before the code was downloaded,
and that the next paste downloads it.

**The second exception follows the last list** (L62, L11). After a timed-out list, a re-run that read an inbox-only
config prints no unread clause, but v18's "if no list marked a folder" still told the person the config could not be

### 16.90 Round 10: stubs, OCR timing and recordings (2026-10-14, wave B13 round 10 lane E)

Lane E's round 10 items: L42, L47, L51, L54, L75 built. L47 and L54 are one change (one reader of a stub page's
lines); L75 is a test fix.

**L42: a running or crash-closed run is no earlier build's (`agentsync.setup_report`; amends §16.80 K6).** A run
still running has `counts_json` `{}` until `finish_run`, and crash recovery closes a run with `{}` as `aborted`, so
a report taken during a cycle said `(a run of an earlier build did not)` and `(a count that also holds for runs of
an earlier build)` on a Mac that only ran this build. `_UNFINISHED` holds `running` and `aborted`: only a finished
run without `converted` is an earlier build's. The OCR time bracket names what is there, joined by `; `: `a run of
an earlier build did not`, `a run still running has none yet`, `a run crash recovery closed has none`; the converter
cache line adds `; the newest run is still running, so its count can still grow` when it is. An aborted run of an
earlier build no longer counts as one; nothing could tell it from this build's (both are `{}`). Test:
`test_setup_report.py::test_a_running_or_crash_closed_run_is_no_earlier_builds`.

**L47, L54: a withheld stub is read from its own lines, by the one test (`agentsync.publish`, `agentsync.cycle`;
amends §16.84 K50 and §16.71 H52).** `publish._withheld_on_page` decodes a stub page's `reason:` and `summary:`
lines as `render_frontmatter` wrote them (one JSON string each) and gives them, with the body, to
`policy.page_says_withheld`; YAML parses only a page whose reason line is missing or a line does not decode.
`_reason_line` is that reader for `reason:` alone. L47: K50's `_page_withheld` ran `parse_mirror_page` for every
online-only image stub a label rule may withhold on each pass with no OCR engine, about 1 s per 2000 stubs a poll,
the cost §16.78 J55 had taken out of the TSV; it reads the lines first now (`_pages_intact` has matched the page to
its hash, so the validation the parse did is not needed). L54: `write_quarantine` read the `reason:` alone while the
cycle and the setup report read `page_says_withheld` (reason, summary or body), so a page from before §16.66 G29,
whose `reason:` still says `no converter for .png`, was `no converter` in the TSV and withheld in the report, for
good on a paused source, which the stub re-render never reaches. The TSV writes the withheld reason whenever the
page says withheld; `Publisher._stub_reason` is `_stub_says`, the reason and that verdict from one read. A Mac with
such a page makes one TSV-only commit the first time. Tests:
`test_cycle.py::test_a_run_with_no_engine_reads_an_online_only_images_stub_without_a_yaml_parse`,
`test_cycle.py::test_a_stub_pages_lines_say_withheld_as_its_yaml_parse_does`,
`test_cycle.py::test_quarantine_tsv_classes_a_page_from_before_its_reason_said_withheld_as_the_report_does`.
Amended 2026-10-15, §16.96 M62: `_reason_line` had no caller left and is removed; `_frontmatter_lines`, through
`_withheld_on_page`, is the reader. `_stub_says` returns the verdict alone (`bool | None`): `write_quarantine`, its
one caller, never read the reason.
Amended 2026-10-15, §16.97 M81: L54 also amends §16.78 J55's `_stub_reason`, where its second line is (L54; dated
line at §16.78 J55).
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.102 N60: `_withheld_on_page` returns the verdict alone (`bool | None`): both callers,
`_stub_says` and the cycle's `_page_withheld`, read only that. The tests read the decoded `reason:` through
`_frontmatter_lines`.

**L51: the recording index revision is in the cache options (`agentsync.convert.recording`; amends §16.84 K63).**
K63 changed How to read without moving the action key, so a copy of bytes converted under the old legend, or a
repair rebuild, was served the old index from the converter cache. `_INDEX_REVISION` (2) is in
`RecordingConverter.options()` only, never in `_picture_options()`: it moves the whole file's action key, while
`_key()`, `_speech_key`, `version()` and `outdated_key` stay, so no frame or speech is read again and no page is
re-read by itself, as §16.66 G59 did for the deck emitter. Raise it whenever a fixed wording of the index page
changes. Test: `test_convert_recording.py::test_a_copy_of_bytes_converted_under_an_older_legend_gets_the_new_one`.
Amended 2026-10-15, §16.96 M64, M65: "or a repair rebuild" and "no frame or speech is read again" were not so. A
page the repair path rebuilds (`_republish_from_cache`) still gets the old index: it re-renders the entry under its
row's stored action key. A new conversion of the same bytes is a read: once the cycle has finished a recording it
deletes its piece folder, so a copy reads every frame and the sound again, and even with its pieces stored the
keyframe stage (diff, pills, frames) runs again. Still true: `_key()`, `_speech_key`, `version()` and
`outdated_key` do not move, so no existing page is read again by itself. §16.96 M85 pins the wording beside the
revision.

**L75: the group-stop test's child takes SIGINT whatever pytest's launch ignored (`tests/test_ocr.py`).**
`test_a_stop_of_the_whole_process_group_leaves_no_compiler_running[SIGINT]` timed out at 120 s in a loaded gate.
The cause was not load: a pytest started with SIGINT ignored (a `cmd &` launch) passes SIG_IGN to the child, which
then ignored the group's SIGINT and waited out `_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S`. Under `trap '' INT` it failed every time at
120 s; §16.78 J80's raise from 30 s was for this. The child sets the default SIGINT handler before it builds; no
load skip is added.
