were its. `_first_sync_line` takes install.out's last sync line as the attempt's only when it sits under one of the
attempt's own `# run=` headers (an install.sh that printed a sync and logged no step); an earlier run's line keeps
its counts as `(install.out: the install run of <start>, before this attempt; ...)`, and a headerless install.out's
as `(install.out: which run printed it is not recorded; ...)`. The head reads `no install run of this attempt reached
its first sync (install.log: the last stopped at its <step> step)`, or for a list-only attempt `this attempt ran only
install.sh --list-folders, no first sync (install.log)`; when the counts sit under the attempt's own header, `no
install run of this attempt logged a first-sync step (install.log)`. The unscoped line, over the whole log's runs,
is as before. Test:
`test_an_attempt_whose_install_stopped_before_its_sync_shows_no_earlier_runs_counts_as_its_own`.

**The outcome names whose each exit code is, with one bracket** (M24, M41; dated line at §16.40 H14). `(computed:
install.sh exited 1 at its config step (rc 78))` reads `(computed: install.sh exited 1: its config step failed with
rc 78)`, or `... failed with no rc logged`, never `rc ?`; a run with no end line reads `install.sh has no end line
after its failed <step> step, <state>`: the step comes before the state's "a, b, or c", so it is never read as a
cause after the "or" (H14 C2), with no ";", which joins the outcome's reasons. A list-only outcome reads `only
install.sh --list-folders ran, in step 1`. Tests: `test_installer_failure_is_failed_at_step_3`,
`test_a_run_with_no_end_line_and_a_failed_step_keeps_the_two_apart`.

**A header-less attempt may start with step 1 lines before its error** (M30, M73; dated line at §16.86 L26).
`_headerless_kind` read only the first event, so the attempt L26 was built for, a step 1 deviation and then the
stated step 1 error, was labelled `since it is in the v4 format` (0 legacy lines), lost the Summary's note and
gained a stale WARNING naming `install.sh --report-only`. It reads the first step 1 error and accepts it when only
step 1 lines come before it; a later step's line first, or `F<n>` lines, still read v4. The Summary's note reads `It
holds a step 1 error (F<n>) logged ...` (`Its lines were logged ...` with none), never that the attempt starts at
it. Test: `test_a_step_1_line_before_the_stated_step_1_error_keeps_the_header_less_label`.

**A step 1 list that stopped asked no folder question** (M7; dated line at §16.86 L7). An attempt whose runs are
only step 1 lists, every one failed, counted the unlogged folder question. `_list_stopped` gives the last list's
note: after an exit 3 (`not-signed-in`, `no-folders`) nothing was listed, `human turns` counts no question and the
line reads `- expected turns: none (step 1's list stopped: OneDrive is not signed in, so no folder was listed: no
folder question and no Allow click)`; after an exit 4 (`denied`, `tcc-pending`, or an exit 3 after one) it reads
`no folder question (step 1's list ended on an Allow click, before the folder question)` and the click stays the
turn. A list that finished, an install run, or a Mac that already syncs keeps the usual rules. Test:
`test_a_step_1_list_that_stopped_on_a_sign_in_asked_no_folder_question`.

**The Configuration line's product-name clause says only what follows** (M2; dated line at §16.58 F4). `, so the
product name in the friction log's Agent: line stays as written` printed with no such folder, and beside an Agent
line that shares no word with one. It follows only when an Agent: line of the friction log (every attempt's: the
report embeds them all) has a word of a listed agent-word folder's name that is not configured; `N under
~/Library/CloudStorage` counts only those folders, since a configured one is redacted. Configured names never
decide the clause, which would hint that a redacted folder is named like the agent. Test:
`test_configuration_counts_the_folders_named_like_a_coding_agent`.

**Notes and counts in words** (M40, M82, M12; dated lines at §16.86 L35, §16.89 L33, §16.30's run table). M40: the
first-sync step's notes read as words in the Installer table and the Summary (`_first_sync_note`): `converted N,
deferred M online-only[, R read again or read for the first time][, after waiting for another sync to end]` (R is
neutral: install.sh adds the sync's "read again" and "first read" heads into it), `waited for another sync to end`,
`lock busy: another sync held the lock past the wait`, `no folder to sync in sources.toml`, `agentsync status
reported a failure, so no sync ran`, `this terminal app may not read the folders`; install.log keeps its tokens.
M82: `_SPLIT_RE` reads the CLI's `, K of them withheld by the label rule` after R, and the Summary prints it; an
older line parses as before. M12: the OCR part's re-read count names first reads (`reread_first`), as the CLI and
the Summary have since L34. Tests: `test_the_first_sync_steps_note_is_in_words_in_the_table_and_the_summary`,
`test_first_sync_clause_carries_the_read_again_count`, `test_the_ocr_part_calls_a_first_read_a_first_read`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.98 N14, N33: in the Summary a note follows a comma, not a bracket of its own: `skipped in
601s, rc 75, lock busy: another sync held the lock past the wait (install.log)`, `(uv 0s · agentsync 62s, waited for
another sync to end · config 1s)`; the Installer table keeps one bracket.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.98 N35: install.sh logs `-first-F` after `-reread-R` when F of the R were first reads, and
the row reads them as the Summary does (`first read R: ...`, `read again R: F of them a first read ...`); R stays
the sum, and a note with no `-first-` keeps the neutral words.

**The local-work line in a checkout whose `.git` is a file, and which branches are empty** (M49, M70, M54, M71;
dated lines at §16.86 L58 and §16.80 K30). v19 pulls a checkout whose `.git` is a file and keeps work there, but both readers
returned when `.git` was no folder, so the public report said nothing while bring-back.md section 3 sent the patch.
`_local_work_line` and `fallback_local_work_line` count the patches first, whatever the checkout is, and read the
branches from its common dir (`_checkout_git_dirs`, `checkout_git_dirs`, which the git-config readers now share).
M54: a branch at main's or origin/main's commit counts when a top-level patch is named for it (`.<branch>.patch`):
a keep whose fetch failed leaves its work there. M71: a branch at any commit origin/main's reflog names (both
columns, read as a file) is not counted; v19's recovery moves main on to origin/main, which left an empty keep's
branch counted. A commit only local main had still counts, and with no reflog the count errs toward counting. The
reflog skip of main's own (M71's finder) was not built: the most common keep's commit is in main's reflog. Test:
`test_both_readers_count_local_work_in_a_checkout_whose_git_is_a_file` (both readers, one line).

**Wording** (M19, M31, M34, M36, M44, M53; dated lines at §16.30's run table, §16.64 G23, §16.14, §16.22, §16.58
F92 and §16.40 H21). M19: the OCR run table's titles and Repeat conversions' `The last runs, newest first:` start
with a capital. M31: `- attempt: 2 of 2; earlier: attempt 1 failed at step 1 (...)`. M34: the `- friction (attempt
N)` line is left out when it would only repeat the agent-friction line. M36: "organization" and "capitalized" in
both reports and the guide. M44: `(this attempt's runs only; the Installer section also counts the <k> earlier
run(s) in the lines read)`. M53: `_STOPPED_COPY_WARN`'s docstring sits under it again, and `_STOPPED_COPY_BEYOND`
has its own; a test reads both with `ast`. M44's second half, one bracket on doctor's `[warn] heartbeat.<id>` line,
is not built: install.sh's `cleared_listings` finds the line by `(deletions held)`, and cli.py swaps the note by
equality, so a joined form would drop install.sh's "deletions are no longer held" line and the report's note swap.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.101 N17, N34, N74: that reason held only for the finder's `(deletions held; ...)`; the
second half is built as `... passes; deletions held (<note>)`, install.sh's anchor is `deletions held` (old and new
lines), and cli.py's swap compares the note, which is unchanged.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.103 N79 (by §16.92 M36): "organization" in the IT request draft's `<org>` note too, and in
docs/deploy/README.md and it-request.md's `<org>` row, which the person reads as well.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.98 N20: the closing `end | finished` line no longer prints the M34 line on its own, so a
clean attempt and a stopped copy print none.

### 16.93 Round 11: installer and the shell report (2026-10-15, wave B13 round 11 lane RB)

The installer's findings of the v19 rehearsal, the cross-lane review and the harvest (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`,
"B13 round 11"). Each item has a test that fails without it. Where an item changes what an older section states,
that section has a dated line (`Amended 2026-10-15, §16.93 M<n>`) and its text is otherwise as it was.

**bring-back.md's header says a section may name things** (M1; amends §16.87 L4). A dated line is also at the
bring-back paragraph that §16.75 J65 amended. The header said section 2 `names real folders and files`, though the prompt has the agent name
each folder, file or person by its role, and a section 2 of `No change requested.` and its `## Not used` lines names
none. The sentences read `Section N is not redacted: it may name a real folder, file or person, so review it
before sending.` and `Sections 2 and 3 are not redacted: they may name ...`; which one is printed is chosen as
before. docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md says so. Test: `test_the_bring_back_header_names_only_what_the_file_holds`.

**Step 1 promises no list it does not print** (M9; amends §16.29's "Every synced folder is printed"). With
nothing listed (OneDrive signed out, its folder still empty, the only provider denied) the first line read
`(marked [synced] below: first the 1 outside the list, then the list)` over the `[synced]` lines alone. The
long form is printed only when the list shows a folder. Tests:
`test_list_folders_keeps_a_set_up_mac_that_has_nothing_to_list`,
`test_list_folders_names_the_synced_folders_when_the_only_provider_was_denied`.

**One patch is not "each", nor "one" a count** (M18; amends §16.86 L25 and §16.75 J65). With one patch not repeated the header said "each was in an earlier report"; it reads `Section 3 sends no
patch this time: its one patch was in an earlier report and is listed by its hash.` (a counter in the skip branch,
not a grep). `LOCAL_WORK_WHERE` (install.sh and setup_report.py, one string) said `one an earlier report already
carried`, which beside `1 patch file(s)` read as a number; it says `any patch an earlier report already carried`.
docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md says both. Tests: `test_bring_back_names_patch_authors_only_when_section_3_sends_a_patch`
(one and two patches), `test_the_shell_report_says_step_1_kept_local_work_in_counts_only`.

**The stopped copy's Run metadata line has one bracket** (M27 and M52, one defect; amends §16.87 L24 (c)). L24 put
its clause in a bracket of its own right before the renderer's `(python X, <exe>)` one, two brackets in a row, the
form G9 and J23/J40 removed elsewhere. The clause opens inside the renderer's bracket and ends with `; `: `- agentsync:
0.1.0, setup prompt v18 (the installed agentsync, which renders this report; the checkout's installer, which stopped
this copy, is for setup prompt v19, and the fresh copy's step 2 reinstalls agentsync; python 3.11.9,
/usr/bin/python3)`. The interpreter path stays last, so a `; ` inside it cannot end the clause (M27's objection to
putting the clause after the path), and the `;` is kept (M27: a `:` would change the meaning). A line that holds the
clause already is left. Every renderer writes `setup prompt vN (python ...)`, so the bracket after vN is always the
python one. Test: `test_an_older_renderers_stopped_report_gives_both_reasons_and_whose_version`.

**A report writer that cannot finish leaves no temp file, and that is tested** (M84; amends §16.87 L4). L4's note said
bring-back.md's temp-file cleanup "cannot be forced in a sandbox"; a `mv` or `chmod` first on PATH that fails for the
temp file's name forces it. `stopped_report_note` and `write_fallback_report` ran a bare `mv -f "$tmp"
"$REPORT_PATH"`, so a failed one left `.stopped-report.*` or `.setup-report.*.tmp` beside the report; each now
removes its temp file and returns 1, the status it returned before. Tests:
`test_a_report_writer_that_cannot_finish_leaves_no_temp_file` (bring-back.md's mv and chmod, the shell report's mv),
`test_a_stopped_copy_note_that_cannot_finish_leaves_no_temp_file`.

**A helper not looked at is "not checked"** (M8; amends §16 OCR's "Who builds"). With a config that cannot be read,
step 2 printed `OCR helper: not built (the config cannot be read)`, and the same for media and speech, though all
three were built: the line is install.sh's relay of `ocr._entry`, shared by the three modules, which reads the
config before it looks at the helper. It prints `<label>: not checked (the config cannot be read)`, with the exit
code §16.96 M25 gives it (78, EX_CONFIG), and install.sh's own media and speech lines for that case, which M25 added,
say `not checked` too. Tests: `test_install_oneshot.py::test_helpers_step_is_skipped_when_the_config_cannot_be_read`,
`test_the_module_entry_point_builds_under_the_configured_cache_dir` (a built helper, then a broken config: the
line, and the helper still there).

**The sources line counts and names every inbox source** (M13; amends §16.56's list of bare commands). With hand-added
inbox sources beside the inbox (a Mac may hold them: `config.ensure_inbox`), `_ensure_setup` printed `sources: none
yet besides the inbox`. It reads `sources: no folder yet besides the inbox (run ~/.local/bin/agentsync add-source
<folder>)` for one, `sources: no folder yet besides 3 inbox sources (inbox, contoso-bridge, contoso-bridge-mail) (run
...)` for several, and `sources: none yet (run ...)` with none. The add-source pointer stays (KISS K05: it is the
line's purpose); the finder's `only inbox sources (4)` was not built, as it dropped the pointer and named no source.
The line is cli.py's (install.sh relays it unread). Tests: `test_init_counts_and_names_every_inbox_source`,
`test_status_with_no_folder_source_is_a_next_line_and_exit_0`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.101 N13: the names follow a colon and the pointer a `; `, `sources: no folder yet besides
3 inbox sources: inbox, contoso-bridge, contoso-bridge-mail; run ...`, so no two brackets sit side by side.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.115 Q59 (by §16.107 O17): under install.sh (`AGENTSYNC_NO_NEXT_HINT=1`) the line ends
before the pointer (`sources: no folder yet besides the inbox`), since the installer's NEXT line names its own
re-run with `--source-local`; a bare run keeps it.

**A config that does not load is the person's to fix** (M23 and M39, one defect). The config step ended through
`fail()`, whose NEXT `fix the error above, then re-run: install.sh` the prompt's step 2 rule ("do what NEXT: says only
if it is an install.sh or agentsync command or a click") reads two ways: re-run, which fails the same way, or edit
the person's sources.toml. When agentsync exits 78 (EX_CONFIG: `configuration error: ...`) on init or add-source and
the config was there before the run, `config_failed` sets the NEXT `the config <CONFIG> does not load with this
agentsync (the configuration error above; ~/.local/bin/agentsync status prints it again): fixing it is the person's,
not a step for the agent, so show them the error and go on to the report; once it loads, the next run is: <install.sh
and its arguments>`, which `fail()` writes in place of its own. Every other exit keeps the generic line: add-source's
own refusals of a folder the agent typed (no such folder, not a directory, inside the docs repo) exit 2, and a
config this run created is no config the person wrote. The finder's wording was not built as written: keyed on "a
config that exists" it told the agent its own typo was the person's to fix (M23's verifier). No prompt change: a
NEXT that names the fix as the person's is neither a command nor a click, so the rule sends the agent to the report.
Tests: `test_a_config_that_does_not_load_is_the_persons_to_fix` (init and add-source at 78; init at 1, add-source at
2), `test_a_failed_add_source_still_fails_the_run_through_the_filter` (a created config at 78: the generic line).
Amended 2026-10-18, §16.124 T1: the "does not load" NEXT is for a config the installed agentsync cannot load; an exit
78 on one it loads (a bad policy.toml or `[governance]` value) says `the config <CONFIG> loads, but agentsync refuses
it`, a created config included.

**Step 1 says step 2 reinstalls agentsync only when it will** (M37; amends §16.87 L11). For a config the installed
agentsync failed on, step 1's NEXT said `Step 2 reinstalls agentsync first, and if that version cannot load it
either, ...`, but step 2 skips the reinstall when the install stamp names this clean checkout's commit, the common
case for a config that is itself broken. Step 2's stamp test is one function, `install_is_current STAMP AGENTSYNC
SOURCE COMMIT`, and step 1 asks it through `checkout_is_installed`, which finds uv as step 1 does (`find_uv`, now
shared with `tool_python` and step 1 of the run), reads uv's tool folders with `uv tool dir` and `uv tool dir --bin`
as step 2 does, and reads this checkout's commit (`checkout_commit`; a changed tree never matches). When it holds,
the sentence after `status prints why.` reads `The installed agentsync is already this checkout's build (commit
<sha>), so step 2 (run from this checkout) does not reinstall it: step 2 stops at its config step, and nothing is kept
or added until the person fixes the config`; otherwise it is L11's. The clause's opening words, which the prompt's
step 1 exception reads, are unchanged. Test: `test_step_1_says_whether_step_2_reinstalls_before_a_config_it_cannot_load`
(this checkout's stamp, an older commit's, a changed tree; step 2's own `agentsync` step agrees each time).
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.99 N29: in that case the `NEXT:` no longer opens with `choose the folders`: it reads
`no folder can be added until the config is fixed: run <install.sh> with no --source-local, which shows the error`
before the same clause.

**Step 1 asks for the sign-in when synced folders are missing** (M4, the round's turn; amends §16.29's "A set-up
Mac with nothing to list"). On a Mac that syncs two OneDrive folders, with OneDrive signed out, step 1 printed the
two `[synced]` lines, exited 0 and said `a re-run keeps them`; step 2's doctor then failed on each missing folder
(`[FAIL] source.<id>.listable`, not a TCC line, so it blocks), and the report read `failed at step 2`, though step 1
already knew. `list_folders` counts the `[synced]` lines whose path is under `~/Library/CloudStorage` and not on disk;
when any is, it exits 3 with note `not-signed-in synced=N`, still prints the `already synced` line and every
`[synced]` path, and says `OneDrive is not signed in on this Mac, so it is missing M of the folders this Mac
already syncs: sign in to OneDrive (or let it finish setting up), then re-run: <install.sh> --list-folders; the
folders marked [synced] are kept`. It keys on missing folders, not on no provider, so a stale empty provider folder and another
provider being present take the same exit. A Mac whose synced folders are all there (one syncing only
`~/Documents/notes` too) keeps exit 0; a mixed Mac stops at step 1, where step 2 would have failed. The prompt half
(step 1's first exception: "If the list's NEXT: line asks me to sign in, tell me which folders are kept and that I
must sign in to OneDrive, and wait for me as for a click; once I say so, run --list-folders again and go by what it
prints.") is lane P's (§16.94). Test:
`test_list_folders_asks_for_the_sign_in_when_synced_folders_are_missing` (no CloudStorage, an empty one, an empty
provider folder, a notes folder beside them; signed in again, exit 0).
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.103 N64: the prompt half above quotes v20's words; it paraphrased them as "unless its NEXT
asks me to sign in", which reads the condition backwards.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.99 N41, N61: "keys on missing folders" was too wide. A missing folder counts only when its
app is signed out, decided by its provider folder as doctor decides it; the `NEXT:` names that app, not always
OneDrive. A folder renamed or deleted in a signed-in provider keeps exit 0 (note `gone=N`), and the `NEXT:` names it.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.112 Q15, Q73: since v23 the prompt half reads "If the list's NEXT: line asks me to sign in and
then re-run", the shape of these signed-out lines, so the other-account tail's "(sign in to that app with the account
it belongs to, ...)", which has no re-run, is not taken for a sign-in to wait for.

**The reinstall's wait line names who started the sync, when the sidecar says** (M43 and M60, one defect; amends
§16.68 H33). Since round 10 L73 the lock's holder sidecar (`<lock>.json`) records `started_by` (`launchd` or `other`)
and agentsync's skip line, doctor, status and the report name it, but install.sh still printed `another sync is
running (the background job, or one started in a terminal)`, and its comments said the lock cannot tell. A
terminal is one of several `other` starters (cron, an agent's shell), which L73 ruled out of every line. install.sh
records which lock the probe found busy, and `holder_words` reads that lock's body (`<pid> <boot> <iso> <label>`)
and, with an LC_ALL=C sed anchored on the sidecar's fixed layout (sorted keys, 2-space indent), the sidecar's `pid`
and `started_by`; it imports nothing (the installed build is the older one) and never reads the sidecar's host. When
the two pids are equal it prints `ops/lock.py`'s `_STARTED_BY` words, `the background job` or `a sync not started by
the background job`, with `, its pass: <label>` for `poll`, `reconcile` or `dry_run` as `_describe_holder` adds it;
otherwise (no sidecar, none of `started_by`, another pid, an empty body as lockf leaves it, anything unreadable)
`the background job, or a sync started another way`. The ticker, the timeout line and AGENTSYNC_NOTE are unchanged.
M43's verifier built the sidecar read and M60's the rewording alone; both are here, the rewording as the fallback.
The header's step 2 paragraph, the comments, setup-feedback.md and `setup_report._AGENTSYNC_NOTE_WORDS`'s docstring
say so. Tests: `test_the_reinstall_names_who_started_the_sync_it_waits_for` (other, launchd, no `started_by`, another
pid, an empty body; the host never printed), the `REINSTALL_WAITS` pins.
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.141 W31: an empty body no longer gets the either-or words; it has three lines of its own.

**The shell report computes a stopped copy's failure** (M14; amends §16.87 L2 and §16.81 K8). A copy `--log-start`
stopped writes a header (`Attempt:`, `Prompt: vN`, `Agent:`) and a stop line whose words state nothing, so
`friction_step1_stated` never matched and the shell said `not computed`, while the agentsync report computes `failed
at step 1 (computed: no install.sh run; step 1 logged an error)` with that prompt and agent. Round 10's L26 left the
stop mark out on purpose; the guards stay. The awk keeps the latest attempt's first `Prompt:` and `Agent:` header
values (reset with the attempt, as `friction_latest_said` does) and its first step 1 error; when the attempt has a
header, every timed line is step 1's and that first error is the stop line, it prints the header's version (less
its `v`; `7 or older` stays words, which no note reads) and agent with a third field `header`. The line then reads
`(from the attempt's Prompt line; older than the installer's vM: the pasted copy was not the current README, or the
--log-start value was changed)` for an older copy, the agentsync report's note, or the existing newer note for a newer
one, and leaves out ` · agent:` when the header has none. `OUTCOME_LINE_HEAD` is unchanged, so the link still reads
the line. A stopped attempt with a late line of another step stays uncomputed. Test:
`test_the_shell_report_computes_a_stopped_copys_failure` (v3, v99, no version, a late step 3 line).
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.99 N44: the note is now read from the stop line as `_prompt_copy_note` reads it, for
`7 or older` and a newer copy too, so the shell's clause is the agentsync report's word for word.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.105 O18: the bracket has no "from the attempt's Prompt line" label now; it is the agentsync
report's note alone.

**The uncomputed outcome names step lines only where there are some** (M15; amends §16.87 L2). With a friction log
of a header and an end line only, the line still said `the Outcome is yours to choose from the friction log's step
lines`. `friction_latest_has_step` reads, with the attempt boundaries the other readers take, whether the latest
attempt has a timed `<UTC> | step N |` line (`Attempt:`, `Prompt:`, `Agent:` and `| end | finished` are none). With
one, the line is as before; with none (or no friction log) it reads `- outcome: not computed (this shell fallback
computes none for this attempt, and the friction log has no step line for it; the Outcome is yours to choose; ...)`,
and `... to choose from the Installer section, which has this attempt's install runs; ...` when the attempt has an
install run (`attempt_ran_no_install` is false). The `- outcome: not computed (` prefix stays.
docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md says both. Tests: `test_an_uncomputed_outcome_names_step_lines_only_when_the_attempt_has_them`,
`test_the_shell_report_computes_no_other_outcome` (no friction log).

**The folder legend explains only the names its report shows** (M3; amends §16.87 L1). The shell legend's
`<folder-N>` item always gave four lines: step 1's list, the whole-word rule for a name every drive has, and the
list-only rule, whose example was the report's only `Copilot`, though the plain report kept no such name (round
10's L1/L5 pattern, inside one item). The item is built from clauses: the base (`... that --source-local,
sources.toml or install.log name`, with `, install.log or step 1's folder list in install.out name` when a name the
lists printed was registered); `; a name every OneDrive or Google Drive has, such as Documents, only where it stands
as a whole word` when a configured name every drive has (a pair of flag w) has its placeholder in the body; and the
list-only clause when a name only step 1's list gave, which `folder_parts` skips (every drive's name or coding-agent
product words), is in the body as a whole word in any case (`; not a name every ... nor one made of coding-agent
product words (Copilot, GitHub Copilot), where only step 1's list names it`, or after the whole-word clause its old
`, and neither such a name nor ...` form). The skipped names come from `listed_folder_names`, which reads install.out
as `redaction_pairs` does (both through `listed_folder_lines`), never through the pair stream. `say_item` wraps the
item at 115 columns with two-space continuation lines. `fallback_redaction` reads the body (its third argument)
before it writes the first legend line, and runs `redaction_pairs` once, as before. Test:
`test_the_folder_legend_explains_only_the_names_the_report_shows` (the plain state, a friction line quoting
`Copilot under Documents`, a configured `Documents`), and the `$'..'` folder case of the legend test.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.99 N45, N16: the list-only clause names only the kind of name the body shows (a name
every drive has, coding-agent words, or both), and the `<org-N>` item is built from clauses the same way.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.98 N3: the Python legend's `<folder-N>` item adds the list-only clause under the same test
(`; not a name every OneDrive has, such as Documents, nor one made of coding-agent product words, such as Copilot or
GitHub Copilot, where only a folder listing names it`), without "Google", which is no Python report word.

**An organisation is redacted inside a longer word** (M50; amends §16.87 L66). L66 made the shell match an
organisation as the Python report's fuzzy mode does, a whole word, so both reports printed it in `ContosoGroup`,
`Contoso2026`, `ContosoCorp.com` and `AcmeContoso`; the shell before L66 redacted them (and `Contosoft` too). An
organisation matched everywhere (not a context organisation, not one whose words spell a report word) gets pair flag
`o` in install.sh and literal mode `org` in `setup_report.Redactor`: also matched where a capital and a small letter
or a digit follow it, and where a small letter or a digit comes before a capital it starts with. Never inside a
word (`Contosoft`, `contosogroup`, `CONTOSOX`), and never where it and the CamelCase word beside it spell one of
agentsync's own identifiers, `_HELD_IDENTIFIERS` (`_CONTEXT_HEADS` with CloudStorage, SharePoint and GitHub; one list
in both readers; compared case for case, as written), so an organisation `Storage` leaves `CloudStorage` whole, and one
named `Box` is still cut out of `dropBox` but not out of `DropBox`. A `.` after it was already allowed. The
finder's "a capital next" alone was not built: it turned `OneDrive` into `<org-1>Drive` for an organisation `One`.
Folders, libraries, generic pairs, context organisations and joined (`j`) pairs stay whole-word. Tests:
`test_an_organisation_is_redacted_inside_a_longer_word` (both readers: Contoso, Storage, Box),
`test_both_readers_hold_the_same_identifiers_whole`, and L66's tests.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.134 V1: an organisation that spells a report word is cut out of a longer word too; only joined names and context organisations stay whole-word.

**A proxy host an earlier line names stays redacted once the proxy is unset** (M29; amends §16.75 J78). Both readers
registered only the proxies in force when the report ran, so a friction line from an attempt whose git stop named a
stale proxy (`... Could not resolve proxy: <host>`) printed that host once the person unset it, which is what the
stop asks; a host with no organisation word was not caught by any other pair. Two sources are registered after the
LaunchAgent's proxies, in the same order in both readers, so no shared `<proxy-N>` moves (J78, R68): (1) every host a
resolver message in the friction log names, `Could not resolve proxy: <host>`, `Could not resolve host: <host>` and
`Failed to connect to <host> port <n>` (with or without `via proxy` after it), in log order, lower case, less a
trailing dot or hyphen (`friction_proxy_hosts`, which also registers the host as written, since the shell matches it
byte for byte; `setup_report._resolver_hosts`), but none of the public hosts the
installer reaches (`PUBLIC_HOSTS`, `_PUBLIC_HOSTS`: github.com, api.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com,
release-assets.githubusercontent.com, astral.sh, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org; a test holds them equal), which
stay readable as diagnostics; this rule is stateless and also covers lines an older build logged; (2) the hosts in
`proxy-hosts` beside the friction log, which `--log-start` and `--log` now keep (`record_proxy_hosts`): the hosts of
the six proxy variables, git's proxies and git's rewrite bases (not github.com) in force at that moment, one a line,
lower case, never userinfo or a port, appended once each, mode 0600 (a symlinked file is left alone). git's proxy and
rewrite readers moved above the friction-log commands, which run before the rest of the script, and
`record_proxy_hosts` names the checkout holding the script itself, whose config they read too. Each host is
registered as any proxy host is (`_add_proxy_host`; a generic one only after `//` or `@` or before `:<port>`). The
finder's `407 from proxy` pattern was not built: curl's message names no host. The sidecar is no report section and
bring-back.md does not embed it. An installed agentsync older than this redacts neither (the installer runs its
report); the shell fallback reads both. Tests: `test_a_proxy_host_an_earlier_line_names_is_redacted_once_unset`
(both readers equal; github.com and astral.sh kept), `test_a_proxy_in_force_at_a_logged_line_is_redacted_after_it_is_unset`
(the sidecar's content and mode, the shell report, bring-back.md, the Python redactor),
`test_both_readers_keep_the_same_public_hosts`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.99 N42: `proxy-hosts` holds each host in lower case and then, where it differs, as
written, since the shell matches byte for byte; the shell reader takes both, under one number. §16.99 N69: the
deploy docs list the file.

**A checkout git cannot read takes no commit from a repository around it** (M51). In a home that is itself a git
repository, a checkout whose `.git` holds only `HEAD` (not a valid gitdir) made git search upward, so `install.sh
--version`, the shell report's `source commit`, install.log's start line (`read_commit "$SOURCE"`) and the agentsync
report's install source (`checkout ... @ <sha>`) all named the home's commit. v19's step 1 command exports a ceiling,
but only inside that one command. The read-only git helpers, `git_ro` (install.sh) and `_git_ro_err`
(setup_report.py), whose every caller reads a checkout, set `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` to the checkout's physical
parent (`cd -P`; `Path.resolve().parent`), and to nothing when that path holds a `:`, which would split git's list.
git still reads the checkout itself, so a healthy checkout and a linked worktree (`.git` a file) read as before, and
an unreadable `.git` falls to the existing words (`unknown`, `git cannot read its .git`). Tests:
`test_a_checkout_git_cannot_read_takes_no_commit_from_a_repository_around_it` (`--version`, the shell report, a
linked worktree), `test_the_install_source_reads_no_commit_from_a_repository_around_the_checkout`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.99 N75: `--version` gives the reason too (`unknown (git cannot read ~/.../.git)`), from
the same helper as the shell report.

### 16.94 Round 11: setup prompt v20 (2026-10-15, wave B13 round 11 lane P)

The B13 round 11 items of lane P (specs `round11/items/M<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built unless a
measurement below says otherwise): M16, M17, M21, M28, M32, M33, M35, M69, M74, M83. All need prompt text, so the
prompt is **setup prompt v20**: `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, `PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's `prompt v20` and
`setup-prompt-compat 20`, the issue form's placeholder and the block's digest move together, and a saved v19 copy is
stopped at step 1 like every older copy. v20 moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry. Lane RB sent words
for its M4, built here; no other lane sent prompt words. None adds an agentsync command, an installer flag, a config
key or a friction kind.

**A recovery leaves the other checkout's main alone** (M69; amends §16.88 L27 and L9). In a second worktree of
another checkout, v19's `switch -C main origin/main` runs on Apple git 2.39.5 (the Command Line Tools' git, and the
CI runner's) even when the other checkout has main out: behind origin/main, that main moved under the other checkout,
whose index then held a staged revert of the update (`D  b`, measured); diverged, git refused with "is already
checked out at", which v19 did not name, so the agent gave the proxy advice. Each of the three recoveries now goes
back with
`git -C ~/src/agent-context-sync switch -q main && git -C ~/src/agent-context-sync reset -q --keep origin/main`: a
plain `switch main` refuses a main checked out elsewhere on git 2.39.5, 2.50.1 and 2.54.0 (measured, behind, diverged
and level), and the tree is clean after the keep's commit, so `reset --keep` loses nothing. Where main is free (the
other checkout on another branch) the recovery still moves main to the update on all three; a blanket "linked
worktree" stop (M69's finder) would have stopped that case, which L27 made pull. The keep command and its retry say
"its last three steps (the fetch, the switch or the reset)". Not built: the verifier's allow rules for the reset. No
recovery is allow-listed (each runs only after a failed pull and asks first, `KEEP_LOCAL_WORK`'s docstring), so a
rule would cover no command of the block, which `test_readme_pre_allow_rules_cover_every_command` forbids, and would
let a bare reset run unasked. A main a keep command leaves without an upstream (only when the pull ran on another
branch with one) now gets it from the no-tracking recovery on the next paste, where `switch -C` set it. `-q` (the
lane's review): a plain switch prints "Your branch is behind ... by N commits" before the count, false once the reset
ran; git's refusal still prints. Tests: `test_a_recovery_in_a_second_worktree_leaves_the_other_checkouts_main`
(parametrized over this machine's gits; v19's reset as the control),
`test_the_branch_recovery_prints_what_it_kept_and_no_bare_ref`.

**Amended 2026-10-16, §16.100 N76:** since v21 the keep command and its retry end by giving main origin/main as its
upstream when it has none (the no-tracking recovery's own tail), so a keep from a branch with an upstream no longer
leaves the next pull "no tracking information" and a second, empty keep; they say "its last four steps (the fetch,
the switch, the reset or setting main's upstream)".

**The worktree stop says what is where and how to move it** (M17, M69; amends §16.88 L27). The not-a-checkout stop
named only the local-work branch. The worktree case is now a stop of its own, keyed on main "is already used by
worktree" or "is already checked out at" (git's version decides the words). It tells the person the branch they were
on (as it was, with its commits), the local-work branch (checked out in the folder, holding the work and copied as
patches), that the folder is a second worktree of the checkout at git's path, and to move it with
`git -C <that path> worktree move ~/src/agent-context-sync <new place>`, or `worktree repair` after a move by hand.
The lane's review found two more cases, both built. The same refusal comes when ~/src/agent-context-sync is the MAIN
checkout and a worktree of it elsewhere has main out; there `worktree move` fails ("is a main working tree", measured
on all three gits), so the stop splits on the `.git` test step 1 already has: for a folder, the person takes that
worktree off main (`git -C <that path> switch --detach`, for example) and runs
`git -C ~/src/agent-context-sync switch main`, and the next paste pulls. And the keep command's refusal sent the
agent to its retry and then the no-tracking recovery (each refusing the same way on 2.39.5, two local-work branches
and the same patch twice), so the stop covers the keep command and its retry and says to run no other recovery and
not step 1's command again. The verifier's reason, "can still use the local-work branch", is not the difference (the
other checkout cannot switch to it either way while the folder has it out); measured on all three gits: moved by
hand, the folder is a prunable entry, and a prune (which `git gc` also runs on its own after
`gc.worktreePruneExpire`) leaves the moved folder no checkout (status rc 128); after `move` or `repair` it stays one.
The stop says that. "Those three stops end there, with no report", and step 3's no-report case names "not-a-checkout,
worktree and ownership stops". Tests: `test_a_recovery_in_a_second_worktree_leaves_the_other_checkouts_main`,
`test_the_worktree_stops_commands_keep_a_moved_worktree`,
`test_a_recovery_in_the_main_checkout_whose_worktree_has_main_stops`.

**A count of 0 deletes the empty branch** (M83; amends §16.88 L9 and §16.86 L58). On a main behind origin/main with
no upstream and nothing of its own, v19's no-tracking recovery left `local-work-<time>` at the old main, a commit
neither reader's skip (main's or origin/main's sha) catches, so every later public report said "local-work branch(es)
in the checkout: 1". The count step is now
`n=$(git -C ~/src/agent-context-sync rev-list --count origin/main..@{-1}) && echo "$n" && { [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || git -C ~/src/agent-context-sync branch -D @{-1}; }`,
in the same chain right after the switch, where `@{-1}` is still the local-work branch. Lossless: 0 means origin/main
holds every commit of the branch, and an uncommitted change would have made it at least 1. `-D`: on the `switch main`
path the branch is an ancestor of origin/main, not of main. The words: "if it is 0, there was nothing to keep and the
command removed that empty branch, so say that", and only otherwise the local-work branch's name. The readers keep
their skip for branches earlier runs left. The block's Rules line, "do not delete, reset or stash anything", now
names the exception: "(keeping local changes on a branch, moving main to the update and removing a local-work branch
that kept nothing, as step 1 says, is none of these)" (the lane's review: the reset was covered by "moving main to
the update", the delete by nothing). Tests: `test_the_branch_recovery_prints_what_it_kept_and_no_bare_ref` (no branch
and `_local_work_line()` None at 0; the branch and the line stay at 1 and 2),
`test_an_empty_keep_on_the_way_back_to_a_main_of_its_own_is_deleted` (`-d` leaves the branch there, `-D` deletes it).

**The git stop's report entries** (M21, M33; amends §16.88 L74). The quote now reads "its `proxy in git's config` and
`URL rewrite in git's config` entries say whether each is set, never which host". M33: the labels stood unmarked, so
"its entries proxy in git's config" read as a broken sentence; code marks, as the quote's commands have, do not clash
with "git's", where single quotes would. M21: "only set or not set" was false, since both reports print "set (1)" and
"set (git uses it before HTTPS_PROXY)". The count (H20) and the bracket stay; dropping them (M21's finder's second
option) would reopen H20 and lose the precedence fact. No parenthesis enters the quote (H21). Test:
`test_readme_step1_is_one_command`.

**The Xcode and git stops say what step 1 did and what is left** (M16, M32; amends §16.88 L31). "no pull ran" was
false at the other-git-failure stop: the pull ran and failed (rc 1, `FETCH_HEAD` emptied, HEAD unchanged). It now
reads "step 1 did not update that copy (its pull did not run or did not finish)". At such a stop with an older
installer the person heard the stop's action, then a bare "not this prompt's version", which read as a second
problem; the stop now adds "and that this asks nothing more of me: once the Command Line Tools are installed (or git
can reach GitHub), the next paste of this prompt tries to update that code first". "Tries", not "updates" (M16's
verifier): local changes and a checkout off main have their own recoveries. Test: `test_readme_step1_is_one_command`.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.112 Q32: since v23 the stop says only its own cause ("once the cause of this stop is fixed,
the next paste of this prompt tries to update that code first (say only this stop's cause: ...)"): at the Xcode stop
git never ran, so "or git can reach GitHub" fixed nothing there.

**Amended 2026-10-16, §16.100 N27:** since v21 it reads "(its pull did not run, or failed)": at the other-git-failure
stop the pull ran to its end and failed, which "did not finish" read as cut off.

**The finish for a config that does not load** (M28; amends §16.72 H9 and §16.49 R11). A sources.toml that exists but
does not load (mode 000, bad TOML, a schema error; probe H) had no words: "read after step 2" could not be done or
parsed a file agentsync rejected, and the only other case, "none: this Mac syncs no folder", was false on a Mac that
synced 2 folders until its config broke. The finish adds: "or, if that file exists but does not load (the report's
Configuration section says "loads: no", or step 2 printed a "configuration error" for it), list no folders and do not
parse it yourself: say "unknown: ~/agent-context/sources.toml does not load", followed by the reason the report
gives". Keyed on "does not load", not "cannot be read" (the finder's), which missed a parse or schema failure; no
claim about the folders it held, which nobody can check. Not on "step 2 stopped at its config step" (the verifier's):
that step also stops on an add-source refusal ("no such folder", "must not contain each other") with a config that
loads (the lane's review, from install.sh's config step and cli.py's add-source). `- loads: no: <error>` is
`setup_report`'s line. Test: `test_readme_step3_runs_the_loop_then_the_report`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.99 N25: the shell report's Configuration section says `- loads: not checked (<reason>)`,
which the v21 finish reads as "unknown: ... was not checked".
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.106 O44, O28: since v22 this case keys on "loads: no:", with the colon, setup_report's own
form: the shell report's `- loads: not checked` starts with "loads: no". The not-checked case now comes first and
ends "list no folders and do not parse it yourself" too, and this one ends "(these two unknown cases come before the
others)".
Amended 2026-10-18, §16.118 S8, S55: since v24 this case keys on the report's "loads: no:" alone, not on "or step 2 printed a "configuration error" for it": the first sync's exit 78 (§16.111 Q22) prints one for a config that loads, which the report now gives as `- loads: yes, but ...` and the finish lists like any other, giving that line's reason
after the folders or the "none".

**bring-back.md's patches** (M35). The finish said the file holds "the patches of any work step 1 kept", false on a
re-run after an earlier report, whose section 3 holds only "not repeated:" lines. It now adds "a patch an earlier
report carried is not repeated, only listed by its hash", the header's own words, and claims nothing about what was
copied back. Test: `test_prompt_routes_changes_to_the_source_not_the_checkout`.

**Step 3 names the rule, not its place** (M74). "(also after step 2, as step 1's last sentence says)" pointed at the
add-source sentence; it reads "(also when step 2 says no folder is synced yet, as step 1 says)". Step 2's "as step
1's last sentences say, not its add-source" is accurate (the verifier) and stays. Test:
`test_readme_report_step_after_any_failure`.

**A signed-out OneDrive waits for the sign-in** (M4, lane RB's words; the installer half is §16.93's). On a Mac that
already syncs folders, a signed-out OneDrive left the `[synced]` folders missing, and step 1's first exception sent
an unattended agent on to a step 2 that fails. `--list-folders` now exits 3 there with a `NEXT:` that asks the person
to sign in, and the first exception, before its "add none and go on to step 2", reads: "If the list's NEXT: line asks
me to sign in, tell me which folders are kept and that I must sign in to OneDrive, and wait for me as for a click;
once I say so, run --list-folders again and go by what it prints." Test:
`test_readme_prompt_asks_a_mac_already_set_up_for_no_folder`.

**Amended 2026-10-16, §16.100 N32, N6, N5, N7:** since v21 the wait has a rule for nobody to ask ("do not wait and log
nothing for it: go to step 3's report"), the sign-in is no `click` line, and on a Mac that syncs no folder yet a
sign-in is no click to wait for; the person signs in to "the app that line names" (lane RB's N61, N41).

Register: `docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md` K44.

### 16.95 Round 11: waits, alarms, status and doctor (2026-10-15, wave B13 round 11 lane B)

Lane B's round 11 items: M5, M10, M11, M26, M42, M45, M46, M47, M48, M55, M56, M57, M58, M59, M63, all built. M5
and M45 are one defect from two finders, built once; so are M46 and M56. M5, M45, M42, M46, M47, M55 and M56
rewrite one alarm and are built together.

**M5, M45: each kind of unknown folder has its own clause in the alarm (`agentsync.arm_local`; amends §16.39
N27).** The alarm named the first five of one sorted list, so five empty folders hid an unreadable one in `+2
more`, while the could-not-be-listed wait says the alarm `names what could not be listed, up to five`. With both
kinds present it reads `N unknown dir(s) — F could not be read: 'X' (<reason>), ...; E empty cloud folder(s),
zero children in a cloud tree: 'A', ...; enumeration incomplete, no deletions this pass (for the folder(s) it
could not read, <fix>; for the empty one(s), <where>)`, each list capped at five with its own `(+k more;
`~/.local/bin/agentsync sync -v` logs each one)`. With one kind the single clause stays. The waits' words are
unchanged and now true of each kind. Tests: `test_arm_local.py::
test_an_unreadable_folder_behind_five_empty_ones_is_named_in_its_own_clause`, `test_arm_local.py::
test_unlistable_folders_log_at_info_and_one_warning_names_them_with_their_reason`.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.113 Q24, Q38, Q42, Q57: the head reads `1 unknown dir` / `N unknown dirs`, and the
empty-only cause `1 empty cloud folder` / `N empty cloud folders`, as the mixed form.

**M47, M42: the alarm names the reason and the fix for how a folder refused (`agentsync.arm_local`,
`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.loop`; amends §16.39 N27 and §16.45 R103).** With no empty folder the alarm gave
the three-way cause and offered to exclude an empty folder, and every refusal got the Files and Folders grant,
which cannot override a folder's own mode. The walk records each unknown folder's kind and reason:
`WalkStats.unknown_why`, a tuple of `UnknownDir(name, kind, reason)`, with `kind` one of `UNKNOWN_EMPTY`,
`UNKNOWN_PRIVACY` (EPERM: TCC), `UNKNOWN_MODE` (EACCES: the folder's owner, mode or ACL) and `UNKNOWN_OTHER`.
Only failed folders: `N unknown dir(s) — could not be read: 'X' (EACCES: Permission denied); enumeration
incomplete, no deletions this pass (<fix>)`. The fix by kind (`arm_local._read_advice`, no nested parentheses):
EPERM `grant the agent Files and Folders access`; EACCES `a folder's own permissions do not let this account read
it: check its owner and mode with `ls -ld`` (never a chmod: the folder may be another account's), with `, or
exclude it` only when no mirrored file is known below the folders (`LocalArm._mirrored_below` over `known_h0`)
and the root is not among them; anything else `check that each one opens in Finder and that its sync app is
running`, never a promised retry, since the wait says another sync does not clear it; several kinds name each.
An lstat failure's reason carries its errno code too (`lstat 'x': EACCES: Permission denied`). A folder with no recorded reason keeps the old text. `cycle._note_empty_dirs` stores the
kinds as manifest meta `unlisted_kinds:<id>` (`cycle._UNLISTED_KINDS_META`, a JSON object, "" when none, root as
"."), and `loop._access_fix` words the could-not-be-listed waits by them: EACCES only, `check the owner and mode of
each one with `ls -ld`, since a folder's own permissions keep this account out and no Files and Folders grant
overrides them`; a provider error, `check that each one opens in Finder and that its sync app is running`;
several kinds, each fix for its own (`for those refused with EPERM`, `of those refused with EACCES`, `the
others`); EPERM, and state from before this build, `grant Files and Folders access`. Sources share the plural line only when their fix is the same. A root refused with EACCES gets
`the folder of <id> itself could not be listed: its own permissions do not let this account read it (EACCES; no
Files and Folders grant overrides them, and another sync does not clear it): check its owner and mode with `ls
-ld`; to stop syncing it on purpose, set state = "paused" in [[source]] id = "<id>" in <config>`. Dated lines at
§16.39 N27, §16.45 R103 and §16.89 L68. Tests: `test_arm_local.py::
test_an_unreadable_folder_with_no_empty_cloud_folder_names_its_reason`, `test_arm_local.py::
test_a_walk_stats_with_no_recorded_reason_keeps_the_old_alarm`, `test_arm_local.py::
test_a_privacy_refusal_keeps_the_grant_and_a_mixed_one_names_both_fixes`, `test_loop.py::
test_a_could_not_list_wait_words_its_fix_by_how_the_folder_refused`, `test_loop.py::
test_a_source_root_a_sync_cannot_list_never_offers_an_exclude`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.101 N12, N38: the wait's bracket names the cause by the same kinds (`refused with EACCES`,
...), with `or a missing sentinel` only while one is set; N36, N37: the alarm's fixes take their number from the
folders of each kind, not from the number of kinds.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.115 Q80 (by §16.107 O49): `or a missing sentinel` only when the last walk stored
today's sentinel as missing (`sentinel_missing:<id>`), not whenever one is set.

**M46, M56: the alarm names the empty folders' wait by its subject (`agentsync.arm_local`; amends §16.89 L15).**
Since round 10 L68 a source with empty folders and one it cannot read gets two waits, and the alarm's `the
WAITING ON YOU line about <id>` fit both. It reads `the WAITING ON YOU line about the empty cloud folder(s) in
<id> at the end of a sync's output says what to do, and `~/.local/bin/agentsync status` prints it too` (plural:
`each WAITING ON YOU line about empty cloud folders in <id> ... prints each one too`), in the pure-empty form too.
`the`/`each` still counts only the empty-folder waits; counting the could-not-be-listed wait in would send the
reader to the wrong line. No numbered prefix is quoted: up to three empty-folder waits each start with their own
count. `SYNC_OUTPUT_END` stays in the text, so STATE.md's legend still applies. Dated line at §16.89 L15. Tests:
`test_arm_local.py::test_an_unreadable_folder_beside_an_empty_cloud_folder_offers_no_exclude`, `test_loop.py::
test_a_source_with_empty_folders_and_one_it_cannot_list_gets_both_waits`.

**M55: the alarm counts the waits over this walk's files too (`agentsync.arm_local`; amends §16.89 L15).** On a
first sync `known_h0` is empty, so the alarm said `the line` while the loop, reading the rows the cycle wrote for
this walk, printed a `[` collision wait beside the exclude-empty one. `LocalArm._empty_waits` counts over
`known_h0`'s files plus this walk's listed files; `known_h0` None still reads `each`. Dated line at §16.89 L15.
Test: `test_arm_local.py::test_the_alarm_counts_the_waits_over_the_files_this_walk_listed`.

**M57: the could-not-be-listed line follows its folder (`agentsync.loop`; amends §16.89 L68).** Beside a gone
folder it carried the whole missed count without `in all`, and the gone files alone gave it the safe words, so a
locked folder holding no mirrored file lost the plain exclude. Now, when the folder it could not read holds
mirrored files (`files_below` over the source's present rows), the line keeps the safe words and takes the count,
`in all, the last walk of <id> did not list N file(s) the mirror still has, the ones under the empty folders
above among them, and ...` when a gone folder is beside it; when it holds none, the line offers `add each one to
that source's exclude` and the count stays on the empty folders' line. The count is never split: it also holds
deletions held in readable folders. Dated line at §16.89 L68. Test: `test_loop.py::
test_a_gone_folder_beside_one_it_cannot_list_puts_the_count_where_it_belongs`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.101 N54: the same rule decides the wait with no empty folder and after exclude-empty, and a
count of deletions held elsewhere gets a clause of its own beside the plain exclude.

**M58: after exclude-empty the could-not-be-listed wait stays (`agentsync.loop`; amends §16.89 L68).** With every
stored empty folder excluded and no sync since, `next_step` asked for another sync (rule 3), which would not
complete the listing, while `unlisted_dirs:<id>` still held an unexcluded folder. That source now gets the
could-not-be-listed wait and its `heartbeat.<id>` check; rule 3's docstring and `empty_cloud_folders_held`'s say
so. Dated line at §16.89 L68. Test: `test_loop.py::
test_a_source_with_empty_folders_and_one_it_cannot_list_gets_both_waits`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.101 N52: with no empty folder stored, every stored folder excluded since is rule 3 too.

**M59: a walk incomplete only for its sentinel gets a sentinel wait (`agentsync.loop`; amends §16.89 L48, L67).**
A local source with a sentinel, no stored folder (raw `unlisted_dirs:<id>`, read before the exclude), no empty
folder and no unlisted root got `one or more folders in <id> could not be listed ...; grant Files and Folders
access, or add each one ...`, neither of which clears a sentinel. It reads `the sentinel set for <id> was
missing at its last sync, so its listing is incomplete and deletions in <id> are held (another sync does not clear
it): restore it in the folder of <id>, or change or remove sentinel in [[source]] id = "<id>" in <config>`, names
no file (a sentinel may be a folder) and adds `heartbeat.<id>`. A source with no sentinel, a stored folder, or a
last pass that failed (it stored nothing), keeps the folder wait. Dated line
at §16.89 L48. Tests: `test_loop.py::test_a_walk_incomplete_only_for_its_sentinel_gets_a_sentinel_wait`,
`test_loop.py::test_a_folder_a_sync_cannot_list_for_another_reason_points_at_sync_v` (a sentinel beside a folder),
`test_loop.py::test_two_sources_that_cannot_be_listed_get_a_plural_wait` (now two unreadable folders).
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.101 N51: the wait keys on the sentinel the walk stored as missed (`sentinel_missing:<id>`),
not on today's config; removed or changed since, the source is rule 3, and no stored miss keeps the folder wait.

**M63: one tuple of present-row states (`agentsync.model`, `agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.manifest`,
`agentsync.arm_local`).** `model.PRESENT_STATES` (live, dataless, quarantined, refused: all but a tombstone) is
`cycle._PRESENT` and `manifest._PRESENT_STATES`, and `arm_local._PRESENT_STATES` is its values as strings, so the
alarm's count of waits cannot drift from the loop's. Test: `test_arm_local.py::
test_the_alarm_counts_rows_by_the_one_present_state_tuple`.

**M10: doctor's fix for a missing source names what is missing (`agentsync.ops.doctor`).** Every missing source
read `fix path in [[source]] id = "<id>", or sign in to the sync client`. `doctor._missing_source_fix`, used by
the listable, volume and launcher-probe checks: its provider folder missing with no other folder of that app,
`sign in to <app> on this Mac, since <provider folder> is missing, then re-run`; missing beside another folder of
the app, `<provider folder> is missing while another <app> folder is there: sign in to <app> with the account it
belongs to, or fix path ...`; the provider folder there, `fix path ..., or sync that folder in <app>`; outside
~/Library/CloudStorage, `fix path ...` alone. No parenthesis. Dated line in the doctor fix table. Test:
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_missing_source_fix_names_the_sign_in_only_when_the_sign_in_is_the_cause`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.101 N53, N56: a `OneDrive-SharedLibraries-<org>` folder missing beside `OneDrive-<org>`
says to sync the library with Sync on its SharePoint page, or fix the path; the sign-in ends `then run
~/.local/bin/agentsync status again`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.99 N61: a provider folder there but showing nothing (hidden entries only) is stale, so
the fix is `sign in to <app> on this Mac or let it finish setting up, since <provider folder> is empty, then
run ~/.local/bin/agentsync status again`, the rule install.sh's list keys its sign-in exit on.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.107 O47, O52: the fix is computed only once the listing has answered, and reads the
provider folder within the listing's bound (unread, the path fix); an empty `OneDrive-SharedLibraries-<org>`
beside `OneDrive-<org>` reads `... is empty while OneDrive-<org> is there: sync the SharePoint library ..., or let
OneDrive finish setting it up, or fix path ...`, no sign-in.

**M11: one first-read stub is singular (`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.setup_report`; amends §16.89 L34).** `first
read 1 (a stub whose bytes had never been read, so also counted as converted)` and the report's `first read 1: a
stub whose bytes ...`; R > 1 stays plural. No parser reads these words. Dated line at §16.89 L34. Tests:
`test_cli.py::test_the_summary_line_counts_the_files_read_again_apart_from_those_converted`, the pins in
`test_setup_report.py`.

**M26: init loads the config before it says it uses it (`agentsync.cli`).** `using existing <config>` printed
before `load_config`, and in a pipe stdout is block-buffered, so it landed after the configuration error. init
loads first; `cli._err` also flushes stdout before it writes, for any command that prints and then fails (not a
guarantee in install.out, whose two streams go through separate tee processes). Test: `test_cli.py::
test_init_names_a_config_it_cannot_load_by_its_error_alone`.

**M48: a file is counted once, under its final verdict (`agentsync.cycle`).** Phase 1 counted a new file as
`created` and phase 2 as `changed`, so one new file read `changed=1, created=1`. `_SourceAcc.settle` moves a
file's phase-1 CREATED or MAYBE_CHANGED count (kept by stable id in `_SourceAcc.unsettled`) to the verdict a later
phase gives it (deferred, error, touched_not_changed, refused, output_unchanged, changed, quarantined).
Phase-1-only verdicts keep their counts. Test: `test_cli.py::test_a_new_file_is_counted_once_under_its_final_verdict`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.102 N30, N39, N50: `unsettled` is `counted_as`, the verdict each file is counted under
now: phase 1's for every file it counts, then each settle's, so a second settle in one cycle moves the count again.
A new file that converts reads `changed=1 (1 new)`.

### 16.96 Round 11: recordings, speech, OCR and stubs (2026-10-15, wave B13 round 11 lane E)

Lane E's round 11 items (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 11"; specs `round11/items/M<n>.md`, the
verifier's corrected fix built): M25, M62, M64, M65, M66, M67, M68 and M85. M64, M65, M67 and M85 are the
recording index's one defect from four finders, built in one commit: M64 and M65 as one change of text and tests,
M67 and M85 as one test.

**The helpers step is skipped when the config cannot be read (M25; `agentsync.convert.ocr`, `scripts/install.sh`).**
Each helper module printed `not built (the config cannot be read)` and exited 1, and `build_helper` threw the code
away (`|| true`), so install.log said `step=helpers rc=0 result=done` for builds never tried. `ocr._entry` exits 78
(EX_CONFIG) for an unreadable config; `build_helper` keeps the code, and on 78 from the OCR module the media and
speech modules, which read the same config, are not run: their lines say `not built (the config cannot be read)`
and the step ends `skipped 0 config-unreadable`, so the report's cell reads `skipped (config-unreadable)`. Any other
code is `done`, as before; an installed build older than this exits 1 there, which is `done`, as before. Dated lines
at §16.25's and §16.37's helpers text. Tests:
`test_install_oneshot.py::test_helpers_step_is_skipped_when_the_config_cannot_be_read`,
`test_ocr.py::test_the_module_entry_point_builds_under_the_configured_cache_dir`.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.98 N48: the cell reads `skipped (sources.toml could not be read, so no helper was built)`;
`no-devtools` and `no-interpreter` have words too.

Amended 2026-10-16, §16.103 N65 (by §16.93 M8): those media and speech lines, and the OCR module's own
(`ocr._entry`), read `not checked (the config cannot be read)`, not `not built`: the helpers may already be built.

**`_reason_line` is gone and `_stub_says` returns its verdict alone (M62; amends §16.90 L47, §16.78 J55).** After
L54 nothing in `src` called `publish._reason_line`, and `write_quarantine`, the one caller of `_stub_says`, read only
the verdict of the `(reason, verdict)` pair. `_reason_line` is removed and `_stub_says` returns `bool | None`; the
YAML fallback still yields None for a page with no reason. J55's test, which proved `_reason_line`, reads
`_withheld_on_page`, the reader production uses, and `setup_report._page_strings` names `_frontmatter_lines`. Test:
`test_cycle.py::test_quarantine_tsv_reads_a_withheld_stubs_reason_without_a_yaml_parse`. Code removal: the test
passes before the change as after it; it pins the reader production uses, where it pinned one production did not.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.102 N60: the same unread reason sat one level down, in `_withheld_on_page`, which now
returns the verdict alone (`bool | None`) as `_stub_says` does.

**A copy of a read recording is read again once the index revision rises; a repair rebuild keeps the old legend
(M64, M65; `agentsync.convert.recording`; amends §16.90 L51, §16.84 K63, §16.66 G59).** L51 said raising
`_INDEX_REVISION` reads no frame or speech again and gives a repair rebuild the new legend. Neither holds. The cycle
deletes a recording's piece folder once its read finishes, so the whole-file cache entry is all that spares a copy
of the same bytes a second read: once the revision rises, the copy reads every frame and the sound again, and even
with its pieces stored the keyframe stage (diff, pills, frames) runs again. `_republish_from_cache` re-renders the
entry under the outputs row's stored action key, so a page the repair path rebuilds keeps the old legend, as does an
existing page until its recording is converted again. The revision stays in the options (the finder's option (b),
taking it out, brings back the stale legend L51 fixed); the `_INDEX_REVISION` docstring, L51, K63's dated line, G59
and L51's test docstring say what happens. Tests:
`test_cycle.py::test_a_copy_of_a_finished_recording_is_read_again_in_full_once_the_index_revision_rises` (raised:
both pieces of the copy are read again; not raised: none) and
`test_convert_recording.py::test_a_second_conversion_with_its_pieces_stored_runs_the_keyframe_stage_again` (no scan,
the keyframe stage again). They pin the behaviour the corrected text states, which the code already had.

**The index wording and its revision move together (M85, M67; `tests/test_convert_recording.py`).** Only a
docstring asked anyone to raise `_INDEX_REVISION`, so a wording change without a raise (K63's defect) passed every
test once the grammar tests' copies were updated with it. `INDEX_WORDINGS` pins the SHA-256 of the fixed wording at
each revision, append only (1: before K63, 2: K63's), taken by rule: `recording_page`'s `_HOW_TO_READ`,
`_NOT_DETECTED`, `_TIMES_FACT` and every `_*_NOTE`, and `recording`'s every `_NOTE_*`, as sorted `module.name=value`
lines, a tuple joined by newlines. naming's notes are out: they reach the version through `NAMING_REVISION`. The
test fails when the digest moves without the revision, or when it equals an older revision's, with "raise
_INDEX_REVISION in recording.py and add <n+1>: <digest> to INDEX_WORDINGS". Test:
`test_convert_recording.py::test_the_index_wording_and_its_revision_move_together` (fails on a one-word edit of How
to read).

**The registry docstring says the TSV classes a row by the page (M66; amends §16.71 H56).**
`label_withheld_suffixes()` said `_sync/QUARANTINE.tsv` copies the page's `reason:`. Since §16.90 L54 the TSV and the
setup report class the row by the page as `policy.page_says_withheld` reads it (its reason, its summary or its body);
for a stub whose page it cannot read, the report goes by its own OCR probe and the TSV keeps the stored reason.
Docstring only: `test_cycle.py::test_quarantine_tsv_classes_a_page_from_before_its_reason_said_withheld_as_the_report_does`
already pins the behaviour.
Amended 2026-10-16, §16.102 N59: so does a stub whose page was read but says neither withheld nor `no converter
for` (§16.97 M79); the report goes by the probe there too.

**The speech seed reads git's config as clone does (M68; `agentsync.convert.speech`; amends §16.60 F78).**
`_git_config` ran `git config --get-urlmatch http` from `<cache>/speech/build`; with HOME itself a git repository,
git read that repository's `.git/config` there, which SwiftPM's `git clone` never reads, so the seed's curl could take
a proxy or CA the clone did not use (measured with Xcode's git 2.50.1). That one call runs with `GIT_DIR=/dev/null`:
system, global and XDG config only, url-scoped values and `~` expansion kept. It is not in `_build_env`, which swift
and the later `git -C` steps share. Test:
`test_speech.py::test_the_seed_never_reads_the_config_of_a_home_folder_that_is_a_git_repository`.

**The sign-in exit fires only when the folder's app is signed out** (N41, N61, one defect, the round's turn; amends
§16.93 M4 and §16.95 M10; dated line at §16.29's "A set-up Mac with nothing to list"). M4 counted every synced
folder under `~/Library/CloudStorage` that was not on disk as a signed-out OneDrive, so a folder renamed or deleted
in a signed-in OneDrive, or a missing Dropbox folder, gave exit 3 and `sign in to OneDrive`, and every re-run of the
list stopped the same way, with no report. `list_folders` now decides each such folder by its provider folder
(`signed_out`), as doctor does: gone with no other folder of that app (the name before its first `-`) beside it, or
there and showing nothing (hidden entries do not count: a stale one), is a signed-out app and keeps exit 3, note
`not-signed-in synced=N`, with `NEXT: <app> is not signed in on this Mac, so it is missing M of the folders this Mac
already syncs: sign in to <app> (or let it finish setting up), then re-run: ...` (`provider_label`; several apps
are listed in the list's order, `... are not signed in on this Mac, so this Mac is missing ...`). A symlinked
provider folder, dangling or not, is there, and one this account cannot read counts as signed in, as doctor's
`lexists` and `iterdir` read them. Any other missing folder keeps exit 0 and the usual `this Mac already syncs ...
a re-run keeps them` `NEXT:` (note `... gone=N`), which adds, for a provider folder that lists other folders, `; 1
of them is no longer on disk although its app is signed in (renamed, moved or deleted there): <path>. Step 2's
status fails on it and names the fix, and nothing syncs until the folder is back under that name or its [[source]]
path in <config> is fixed`, and for a provider folder gone while another folder of the app is there (another

there: <path>. Step 2's status fails on it and names the fix (sign in to that app with the account it belongs to,
or fix its [[source]] path in <config>), and nothing syncs until then`, doctor's two fixes. While a provider is
denied or still asking, no provider folder is read (exit 4 comes first, and a read could wait on the same prompt
past the list's cap). Not N41's exit 3 with a wait (N61's verifier):
step 2 runs, its doctor names the folder and its fix, and the report is written, as before M4; an exit 3 would

the same empty-folder rule, so the list and doctor agree. Tests:
