### 16.101 Round 12: waits, read advice, status and doctor (2026-10-16, wave B13 round 12 lane B)

Lane B's round 12 items: N12, N13, N17, N34, N36, N37, N38, N40, N51, N52, N53, N54, N56, N74, all built. N12 and
N38 are one defect from two finders, built once; so are N36 and N37, and N17, N34 and N74 (round 11 M44's second
half). N12, N38, N51, N52 and N54 rewrite the could-not-be-listed wait and are built together.

**N12, N38: the could-not-be-listed wait names its cause by the kinds the walk stored (`agentsync.loop`; amends
§16.95 M42).** The bracket was `(no access, or a missing folder or sentinel; another sync does not clear it)`
whatever was stored, beside an EACCES fix that rules out both, on a source with no sentinel.
`loop._unlisted_cause(kinds, sentinel)` builds it: `refused with EACCES`, `refused with EPERM`, `refused with EPERM
or EACCES`, `a sync-app error or a folder that vanished`, joined with `, or `; then `, or a missing sentinel` only
while sources.toml sets one, since a walk that also missed it lands in this wait, not the sentinel wait. No
stored kind, or one this build does not know, keeps `no access, or a missing folder or sentinel` (`_ANY_CAUSE`).
The verifier's "no access: a folder's own permissions refuse this account" was not built: the fix beside it says
that. Sources share the plural line only when cause and fix are both the same. Tests: `test_loop.py::
test_a_could_not_list_wait_words_its_fix_by_how_the_folder_refused` (each kind's cause; older state keeps every
cause), `test_loop.py::test_two_sources_with_one_fix_share_a_line_only_with_one_cause`, `test_loop.py::
test_a_folder_a_sync_cannot_list_for_another_reason_points_at_sync_v` (a missing sentinel beside an EACCES folder).
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.107 O49: `, or a missing sentinel` only when the last walk stored today's sentinel as
missing (`sentinel_missing:<id>`), not whenever one is set.

**N51: the sentinel wait keys on the sentinel the walk missed (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.loop`; amends §16.95
M59).** It keyed on today's sources.toml: removing the sentinel, as it says, turned it into `one or more folders
in <id> could not be listed ... another sync does not clear it` with a grant or an exclude as the fix, though no
such folder existed and one sync cleared it; changing it to a file that exists kept the sentinel wait; and a walk
from before round 10 L68 (no stored folder) with a sentinel set got the sentinel wait whatever the cause.
`cycle._Cycle._note_empty_dirs` stores manifest meta `sentinel_missing:<id>` (`cycle._SENTINEL_MISSING_META`): the
sentinel the walk looked for and did not find, "" otherwise. The sentinel wait needs it to equal today's
sentinel; removed or changed since, the source is rule 3 (sync again), and a changed sentinel still missing gets
its wait after that sync. No stored miss (state from before this build) falls to the folder wait, whose cause
keeps "or sentinel". A pass that failed after its walk keeps the folder wait, as before. Tests: `test_loop.py::
test_a_sentinel_removed_or_changed_after_a_miss_says_sync_again` (removed, and changed to a file that exists),
`test_loop.py::test_a_walk_from_before_the_stored_folders_never_blames_a_present_sentinel`.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.107 O53: that folder wait, with a sentinel set, offers the sentinel's fix beside the
folders' (restore it, or change or remove it in sources.toml); which cause it blames is unchanged.

**N52: a folder excluded since the walk that could not list it is rule 3 (`agentsync.loop`; amends §16.95
M58).** With no empty cloud folder stored, the folder wait stayed after the folder was added to the exclude, still
saying another sync does not clear it, its fix fallen back to the grant (and, mirrored first, the warning against
the exclude already made), though the next sync completed the listing. When the stored `unlisted_dirs:<id>` is not
empty and sources.toml excludes all of it, the source is rule 3, as M58's twin with empty folders is; rule 3's
docstring says so. Test: `test_loop.py::
test_a_folder_excluded_since_the_walk_that_could_not_list_it_says_sync_again` (unmirrored and mirrored first).

**N54: the held-below rule covers every branch (`agentsync.loop`; amends §16.95 M57).** With no empty folder, a
locked folder holding no mirrored file beside a deletion held elsewhere got `<fix> (the safe fix); the last walk of
<id> did not list N file(s) ... adding such a folder to that source's exclude retires the pages under it at once`,
while the walk's alarm offered `or exclude it`. `loop._mirrored_below` (M57's rule, true when no folder is known,
so it fails safe) now decides the M58 branch and the final one too: a folder holding none gets the plain `, or add
each one to that source's exclude in <config>` and, when files were missed, its own clause, `; the last walk of
<id> did not list N file(s) the mirror still has, and their deletion stays held until a sync lists <id> in full`,
on a line of its own. Tests: `test_loop.py::
test_a_folder_holding_no_mirrored_file_gets_the_plain_exclude_beside_a_held_deletion`, `test_loop.py::
test_a_folder_holding_mirrored_files_keeps_the_safe_words_beside_a_held_deletion`.

**N36, N37: the read advice takes its number from each kind's folders (`agentsync.arm_local`; amends §16.95
M42).** `_read_advice` chose singular or plural by the number of kinds, so two mode-000 folders read `a folder's
own permissions do not let this account read it` and one EACCES folder beside one EPERM folder `for those refused
with EACCES, ... them`. It takes a `Counter` of kinds: EACCES alone reads `a folder's own permissions ... it: check
its owner and mode with `ls -ld`[, or exclude it]` for one folder and `their own permissions do not let this
account read them: check their owner and mode with `ls -ld`[, or exclude them]` for several; beside another kind
`for the one refused with EACCES, its ...` or `for those refused with EACCES, their ...`; EPERM `grant the agent
Files and Folders access[ for the one|those refused with EPERM]`; other `check that it opens` / `each one opens`,
or beside another kind `the other one opens ... its sync app` / `the others open ... their sync app`. The mixed
alarm reads `for the folder|folders it could not read` and `1 empty cloud folder` / `N empty cloud folders`. No
reader parses the alarm. Tests: `test_arm_local.py::test_the_read_advice_follows_how_many_folders_have_each_kind`,
and the pins in `test_a_privacy_refusal_keeps_the_grant_and_a_mixed_one_names_both_fixes`,
`test_unlistable_folders_log_at_info_and_one_warning_names_them_with_their_reason`.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.107 O35, O37: one EACCES folder reads `its own permissions ...` after `for the folder it
could not read,` and `the folder's own permissions ...` in its alarm alone, never `a folder's`.

**N17, N34, N74: the incomplete-listing warn has one bracket (`agentsync.ops.doctor`, `scripts/install.sh`; amends
§16.92 M44).** It read `enumeration incomplete for N consecutive passes (deletions held) (held at its last walk:
...)`, and `(deletions held) (fix: ...)`. What the listing holds follows a `; ` now: `... passes; deletions held
(<note>)` and `... passes; deletions held (fix: ...)`, and a Graph source's `...; files missing from the listing
are kept while deletions Graph reports still apply (fix: ...)`. Of the three designs this is N17's: N34's
`(deletions held; <note>)` leaves the fix lines with two brackets, and N74's `(deletions held); <note>` keeps one
side by side with a clause. install.sh's `cleared_listings` anchors on `deletions held`, which matches the new
line and the bracketed one an older installed agentsync prints, and never a Graph line or the `[ok  ]` line
below the threshold. cli.py's report-note swap compares `r.note`, which is unchanged; the setup report's
`_yours_warn` reads a detail prefix. Tests: `test_ops_doctor.py::test_heartbeat_incomplete_fix_by_source_kind`,
`test_install_oneshot.py::test_a_listing_the_first_sync_cleared_is_said_and_never_inferred` (both forms),
`test_review_fixes.py::test_graph_delta_passes_leave_the_incomplete_count_and_doctor_at_ok`.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.107 O36: the notes begin `as of its last walk`, and the report's ends `still names it`, so
the line says `held` once; the swap and the anchor are unchanged.

**N53, N56: a missing SharePoint library is no sign-in, and the sign-in names its command (`agentsync.ops.doctor`;
amends §16.95 M10).** `_missing_source_fix` reduced `OneDrive-SharedLibraries-Contoso` and `OneDrive-Contoso` to
one app, so a library not synced on this Mac read `sign in to OneDrive with the account it belongs to`, an account
already signed in. Missing beside its own organization's `OneDrive-<org>` (`it_request.org_of`), it reads `<provider
folder> is missing while OneDrive-<org> is there: sync the SharePoint library to this Mac with Sync on its
SharePoint page, or fix path ...`; beside another organization's it keeps the sign-in or the path. Add shortcut to
My files was not offered: it puts the library under `OneDrive-<org>`, not the configured path. The sign-in fix
read `then re-run`, naming nothing; it reads `then run ~/.local/bin/agentsync status again`, and so does the
listing-timeout fix (`click Allow on the macOS prompt, then run ~/.local/bin/agentsync status again; if no prompt
shows: ...`). Tests: `test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_missing_source_fix_names_the_sign_in_only_when_the_sign_in_is_the_cause`,
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_cloud_source_listing_times_out_with_click_allow_hint`.

**N13: the no-folder sources line has one bracket at most (`agentsync.cli`; amends §16.93 M13).** With several
inbox sources it read `... besides 3 inbox sources (inbox, contoso-a, contoso-b) (run ...)`. It reads `sources: no
folder yet besides the inbox; run ~/.local/bin/agentsync add-source <folder>`, `... besides 3 inbox sources:
inbox, contoso-a, contoso-b; run ...`, and `sources: none yet; run ...`. The add-source pointer stays (§16.93's
KISS K05 ruling); the finder's `step 2 with --source-local adds one` was not built, as it ties a CLI line to the
setup prompt's step numbers, which mean nothing when install.sh is run by hand. Tests: `test_cli.py::
test_init_counts_and_names_every_inbox_source`, `test_cli.py::test_status_with_no_folder_source_is_a_next_line_and_exit_0`.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.107 O17: under install.sh (`AGENTSYNC_NO_NEXT_HINT=1`) the line ends before the pointer,
since the installer's NEXT line names its own re-run with `--source-local`.

**N40: exclude-empty names its folders by their count (`agentsync.cli`).** After excluding one folder it said `the
next sync lists <id> without them`, beside `files`. It reads `without that folder` or `without those folders`, and
the left-folders clause points at the alarm that `names it` for one folder. Tests: `test_exclude_empty.py::
test_every_empty_folder_is_excluded_once_and_the_listing_completes`, `test_exclude_empty.py::

### 16.102 Round 12: per-source counts, speech and stubs (2026-10-16, wave B13 round 12 lane E)

Lane E's round 12 items (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 12"; specs `round12/items/N<n>.md`, the
verifier's corrected fix built): N18, N30, N39, N50, N59, N60 and N73. N30, N39 and N50 are one defect, a file
counted twice, from three finders, built in one commit. A dated line this round writes reads `Amended 2026-10-16,
§16.102 N<n>`. No item needs prompt words, so none went to lane P.

**A file is counted once however many phases settle it, and a new one says so (N30, N39, N50; `agentsync.cycle`,
`agentsync.model`, `agentsync.cli`; amends §16.95 M48).** `_SourceAcc.settle` moved a file's phase-1 count only on
its first settle, so a second settle in the same cycle added a count: a new file settled `changed` and then refused,
failed or quarantined by `_publish` (a label rule, a file not the type its name says, a credential re-stub) read
`changed=1, refused=1` or `changed=1, quarantined=1`, and a new recording deferred and then read in the same poll
cycle read `changed=3, deferred=1` for three files. `_SourceAcc.counted_as` holds the verdict each stable id is
counted under now; phase 1 sets it for every file it counts and each settle moves the count from it, so the last
settle wins. A fetch the OS refused (`DatalessRefusedError`) set the row `deferred` but never settled it, so a new
file read `created=1`; it settles `deferred` now. `acc.deferred` and `deferred_online_only` still count events. The
moving count dropped the fact that a file was new (N39); `SourceReport.new` counts the files phase 1 counted
`created` whose final verdict is `changed`, and the sync line reads `changed=1 (1 new)`, never a bare `created=`.
The counts feed only the sync line, STATE.md's `this_run:` and the run record; no gate reads them. Tests:
`test_cycle.py::test_a_new_file_publish_settles_again_is_counted_once_under_that_verdict` (labelled, broken,
credential), `test_cycle.py::test_a_new_recording_read_in_the_cycle_that_deferred_it_is_counted_once`,
`test_cycle.py::test_a_new_file_the_os_will_not_hydrate_is_counted_deferred`,
`test_cli.py::test_a_new_file_is_counted_once_under_its_final_verdict` (an edited file reads `changed=1`, not new),
`test_cli.py::test_a_new_file_publish_quarantines_reads_quarantined_and_not_changed`.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.108 O50: `acc.deferred` and `deferred_online_only` count files, not events: a file deferred
and then read in the same cycle no longer reads `1 deferred` beside counts with no deferred entry.

**The speech build's flags keep `~/Library`, not the whole home (N18; `agentsync.convert.speech`; amends §16.48
R90).** R90 said the build wrote the real `~/Library` SwiftPM folders before it passed `--cache-path`,
`--config-path` and `--security-path`, which read as if nothing in the home is written now. On Swift 6.2.4 both
`swift package resolve` and `swift build` still re-create the real `~/.swiftpm/security` symlink, with
`--swift-sdks-path` too and whatever `HOME` says; `swift build --help` lists no other path flag (verifier's
measurement with a kill-on-write sandbox). The finder's lock is not in the home: `_Users_<login>_.swiftpm.lock` is
in `$TMPDIR`. On a person's Mac this re-creates the same symlink in their own home. Not built as code: wrapping
swift in an outer deny sandbox blocks the write but needs `--disable-sandbox`, which drops SwiftPM's own sandbox
around FluidAudio's manifest and plugin code, a security regression. `_compile`'s docstring points here. A rehearsal
tells a sandbox's own build by the lock files in its `$TMPDIR` and the `manifest.db.lock` under its own cache path,
never by `~/.swiftpm` mtimes, which every build on the Mac moves. Tests:
`test_speech.py::test_swiftpm_keeps_its_cache_config_and_security_beside_the_build_tree` (unchanged: the three
paths) and `test_speech.py::test_the_build_says_which_real_home_path_its_flags_do_not_cover`.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.108 O69: `CFFIXED_USER_HOME`, Foundation's own home override, which N18 never tried, does
move it: the swift steps get it set to `<cache>/speech/swiftpm/home`, so the `~/.swiftpm` links and the
`<home>_.swiftpm.lock` in `$TMPDIR` are the build's own, with SwiftPM's manifest sandbox on.

**A page read that says neither goes by the probe in every docstring (N59; `agentsync.convert.registry`,
`agentsync.setup_report`; amends §16.71 H56, §16.96 M66).** §16.97 M79 corrected the `_Mirror` comment and the
guide, and left the M66 sites saying the report uses its OCR probe only for a stub whose page it cannot read:
`label_withheld_suffixes()`, `quarantine_class`, `withheld_for` and the `pages_unread` comment now also name a page
read that says neither withheld nor `no converter`, and the registry sentence is one block again. The legend keeps
`could not be read`, as M79 pinned it. The recorded M66 text stands; dated lines follow it at §16.71 H56 and §16.96
M66. Test: `test_cycle.py::test_every_m66_site_names_a_page_read_that_says_neither`.

**`_withheld_on_page` returns the verdict alone (N60; `agentsync.publish`, `agentsync.cycle`; amends §16.90 L47,
§16.96 M62).** M62 took the unread reason out of `_stub_says`; it sat one level down, in `_withheld_on_page`'s
`(reason, verdict)`, whose two callers read only the verdict and whose only readers of the reason were tests. It
returns `bool | None` now; a missing or empty reason, or a line that does not decode, still gives None, which sends
the caller to the YAML parse. J55's test reads the decoded `reason:` through `_frontmatter_lines`, the L47/L54 test
and M79's test the verdict. Tests: `test_cycle.py::test_quarantine_tsv_reads_a_withheld_stubs_reason_without_a_yaml_parse`,
`test_cycle.py::test_a_stub_pages_lines_say_withheld_as_its_yaml_parse_does`,
`test_deploy_pack.py::test_a_page_read_that_says_neither_can_disagree_with_the_tsv`.

**STATE.md keeps the mixed unknown-folder alarm whole (N73; `agentsync.publish`; amends §16.68 H48).** `_ALARM_MAX`
was 6000, sized for five names, and since §16.95 M5, M45 the mixed alarm names up to ten: five folders it could not
read, each with its reason, which may name a 255-character child (`lstat '<child>': EACCES: ...`), and five empty
cloud folders. With 1024-character names STATE.md cut it inside the empty folders' names, so the advice and the
words the wait legend points at were gone. It is 16,000: ten such names with their reasons came to 12,257 characters
(the finder's 12,000 is too small). No test pinned 6000. Test:
`test_publish.py::test_state_md_keeps_a_mixed_unknown_folder_alarm_whole`.

**The sign-in stop logs its apps and how many folders are missing** (O5, the install.sh half; amends §16.99 N41).
`note=not-signed-in synced=N` named no app, and N is every synced folder, so both readers said "OneDrive is not
signed in" and called all N missing. The exit 3 logs `not-signed-in apps=<words> missing=M synced=N`: the words are
a fixed map of the provider label (`onedrive`, `googledrive`, `dropbox`, `box`, `egnyte`, else `other`; comma-joined
in the list's order, once each), never a folder's own text. They are built by lower-casing the label, since every
lower-case word on a line of install.sh that is not a comment is a report word, which redaction keeps in clear (a
literal `box` kept an organization named Box in clear). The no-provider stop logs `apps=onedrive`. The readers are
lane RA's (§16.104). Tests: `test_list_folders_asks_for_the_sign_in_when_synced_folders_are_missing`,

### 16.106 Round 13: setup prompt v22 (2026-10-17, wave B13 round 13 lane P)

The B13 round 13 items of lane P (specs `round13/items/O<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built unless a
measurement below says otherwise): O11, O15, O27, O28, O30, O44. All need prompt text, so the prompt is **setup prompt
v22**: `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, `PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's `prompt v22` and `setup-prompt-compat 22`, the issue form's
placeholder and the block's digest move together, and a saved v21 copy is stopped at step 1 like every older copy.
v22 moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry. None adds an agentsync command, an installer flag, a config
key or a friction kind.

**A [FAIL] whose fix is the person's sends the agent to the report** (O11, O30: one defect from two finders, built
once; amends §16.14 K02). A synced folder renamed in a signed-in OneDrive (probes RN and 52) failed step 2 with
`fix: fix path in [[source]] id = "<id>", or sync that folder in OneDrive` and `NEXT: fix the [FAIL] lines above
(each names its fix), then re-run: install.sh`. v21 named only `[warn]` and WAITING ON YOU: lines as the person's,
and let the agent follow a NEXT that is an install.sh command, so it could re-run to the same exit 1, or edit
sources.toml to the renamed folder, choosing a folder for the person. install.sh's `persons_fails` reads the first
words of each blocking `[FAIL]` line's fix (doctor's source checks and `_missing_source_fix`: `fix path in
[[source]]`, `point [[source]]`, `set path in the [[source]]`, `restore `, `sign in to `, `<provider> is missing
while ...`); when every one is the person's, step 2's NEXT reads `the [FAIL] lines above are the person's to fix
(each names its fix: a folder or file to put back or sync, a [[source]] path or a sign-in), not a step for the
agent, so show them those lines and go on to the report; once fixed, the next run is: <install.sh and its options>`,
shaped like the config error's (§16.93 M23, M39), and the closing status's `..., once fixed, run
~/.local/bin/agentsync sync and follow its NEXT line`. Exit 1 as before. Not for every `[FAIL]`, which both
finders' prompt sentence ("A [FAIL] line's fix is mine") would have done and the verifiers showed makes things

### 16.107 Round 13: status, waits, read advice and doctor (2026-10-17, wave B13 round 13 lane B)

Lane B's round 13 items: O16, O17, O34, O35, O36, O37, O47, O49, O51, O52, O53, all built. O16 and O35's third
part are one defect from two finders (the could-not-be-listed wait's count), built once; so are O35's fourth part
and O37 (the read advice for one folder beside empty ones). O52's install.sh half is lane RB's (§16.105, built with
its O41, O48 and O57 in `signed_out`); lane B built the doctor half.

**O16, O35: the could-not-be-listed wait and the empty-folder waits say how many folders (`agentsync.loop`,
`agentsync.arm_local`; amends §16.89 L48).** The walk's WARNING said `2 folder(s) could not be listed` and the
alarm `2 could not be read` while the wait said `one or more folders in <id>`, though the walk stores every name
(`unlisted_dirs:<id>`); and every known count kept `(s)`: `1 folder(s) could not be listed`, `1 empty cloud
folder(s) keep ... if the folder(s) are meant to be empty ... (it adds them ...)`. `cannot_list` keeps how many
folders are not excluded today and how many the walk stored (`loop._unlisted_stored`); the single-source line and
the safe-fix line read `1 folder in <id> could not be listed` or `N folders in <id> could not be listed`, with
`and is still not excluded` / `and are still not excluded` when some were excluded since, so a count below the
alarm's reads true; one folder takes `check its owner and mode with `ls -ld`, since its own permissions keep this
account out ...` and `check that it opens in Finder ...` (`_access_fix(kinds, one=True)`) and `or add it to that
source's exclude`. State that stored no folder keeps `one or more folders in <id>`, and so does the grouped line
for several sources, which has no one count. The exclude-empty, `[` collision and gone lines take noun, verb and
pronoun from their own count (`1 empty cloud folder keeps`, `has a [ in its name, so an exclude of it`, `remove
the empty folder`, `names the folder` / `it`); the walk's WARNING says `1 folder` / `N folders`, and the mixed
alarm's pointer `the WAITING ON YOU line about the empty cloud folder` / `folders`. Tests: `test_loop.py::
test_the_could_not_list_wait_counts_the_folders_the_walk_stored` (2, then 1 still not excluded, then none
stored), the updated pins in `test_loop.py`, `test_arm_local.py`, `test_exclude_empty.py` and `test_setup_report.py`.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.113 Q43, Q81: one folder reads `(it adds the folder to ...)`, and the file counts
`1 file` / `N files`, with the words that agree.

**O49: the cause names a sentinel only when the walk missed it (`agentsync.loop`; amends §16.101 N12).** With a
sentinel set, the bracket said `or a missing sentinel` though the walk had found it: the clause tested the config
alone. `cannot_list` passes `_unlisted_cause` today's sentinel only when `sentinel_missing:<id>` equals it, so a
sentinel found, or changed or removed since, adds nothing. State from before round 12 N51 stored no miss and
lacks the clause until its next sync; no stored kind keeps `_ANY_CAUSE`, which names the sentinel. Tests:
`test_loop.py::test_a_could_not_list_wait_names_a_sentinel_only_when_the_walk_missed_it`, `test_loop.py::
test_two_sources_with_one_fix_share_a_line_only_with_one_cause` (alpha's sentinel now one the walk misses),
`test_loop.py::test_a_folder_a_sync_cannot_list_for_another_reason_points_at_sync_v`.

**O53: with no stored cause, the wait offers the sentinel's fix too (`agentsync.loop`; amends §16.101 N51).** A
Mac upgraded from v20 has no `sentinel_missing:<id>` until its next sync, so a sentinel missed then got the folder
wait with a grant or an exclude as its whole fix. The finder's fallback (no key and a sentinel set means the
sentinel wait) was not built: the old builds write a key only when it changes, so an absent key cannot tell
"found" from "never stored", and it would blame a present sentinel beside a locked folder, round 12 N51's defect.
Which cause is blamed is unchanged; when nothing stored names it and sources.toml sets a sentinel, the line adds
`; if the sentinel set for <id> is what is missing, restore it in the folder of <id>, or change or remove sentinel
in [[source]] id = "<id>" in <config>` (on the safe-fix line, `<fix>, or, if the sentinel ... (the safe fixes)`).
Test: `test_loop.py::test_a_walk_that_stored_no_cause_offers_the_sentinel_fix_beside_the_folders`; the no-sentinel
case stays bare in `test_the_could_not_list_wait_counts_the_folders_the_walk_stored`.

**O35, O37: one unreadable folder's read advice names it once (`agentsync.arm_local`; amends §16.101 N36).**
Beside empty cloud folders the alarm read `for the folder it could not read, a folder's own permissions do not
let this account read it`. `_read_advice(..., named=True)`, passed by the mixed alarm, gives `its own permissions
do not let this account read it: check its owner and mode with `ls -ld`[, or exclude it]`; the alarm of that
folder alone says `the folder's own permissions ...`, never `a folder's` (O35's "the folder's" for both was not
built: after `for the folder it could not read,` it names the folder twice; O37's "keep a folder's alone" was not
either, since one folder is named there). Tests: `test_arm_local.py::
test_one_unreadable_folder_beside_an_empty_one_is_named_once` (excludable and not),
`test_arm_local.py::test_an_unreadable_folder_with_no_empty_cloud_folder_names_its_reason`.

**O36: the held-listing note dates the state, and the line says held once (`agentsync.ops.doctor`; amends §16.101
N17).** `deletions held (held at its last walk: ...)` used one word in two senses, and the report's note a third
time (`a WAITING ON YOU line still holds it`). The notes read `as of its last walk: the end of this run says
whether this run's sync cleared it` and `as of its last walk: the Summary's Loop line says whether a WAITING ON
YOU line still names it`. Nothing parses the note: cli.py swaps by comparing the constant, install.sh's
`cleared_listings` anchors on `deletions held` in the detail, and the setup report strips any trailing note.
Tests: `test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_held_listing_line_says_held_once`, `test_install_oneshot.py::
test_a_listing_the_first_sync_cleared_is_said_and_never_inferred` (the new note, the one before O36 and the one
before N17), `test_setup_report.py::test_a_wait_the_loop_names_is_yours_and_a_stopped_sync_stays_unexpected`.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.113 Q10, Q35: the install.sh note reads `as of its last walk: if this run's sync runs,
the end of this run says whether it cleared it`, or `doctor._LISTING_SKIPPED_NOTE` beside a [FAIL] that stops
that sync.

**O51: the incomplete-listing fix for a Graph source and an inbox has no bracket (`agentsync.ops.doctor`; amends
§16.57 F69 and §16.22).** `sync -v (a full pass that lists all of <id> clears this)` nested inside the line's
`(fix: ...)`. It reads `~/.local/bin/agentsync sync -v; a full pass that lists all of <id> clears this`, prose after
`; ` as the local fix's. The finder's `sync -v: a full pass ...` was not built: the CLI parser rejects `-v:` (`ignored
explicit argument ':'`), so it fails `assert_fix_parses` and would hand the person a command that does not run.
Tests: `test_review_fixes.py::test_graph_delta_passes_leave_the_incomplete_count_and_doctor_at_ok` (one `(` on the
rendered line), `test_ops_doctor.py::test_heartbeat_incomplete_fix_by_source_kind`.

**O47, O52: the missing-source fix reads the provider folder within the listing's bound, and an empty library is
no sign-in (`agentsync.ops.doctor`; amends §16.95 M10).** `_check_local_source` computed `_missing_source_fix` for
every live local or inbox source before its timed listing, and that fix lists the provider folder with no bound,
so a hidden Allow prompt holding reads under `OneDrive-<org>` held status there instead of giving the 10 s
click-Allow FAIL (measured 6.0 s against a 1 s bound). The fix is computed only in the missing branches, after
the listing has answered, and its provider read runs under `call_with_timeout` with the listing's bound (the
launcher probe calls it too, from the terminal); held or unreadable, it keeps the path fix. And an
`OneDrive-SharedLibraries-<org>` folder there but empty beside `OneDrive-<org>` read `sign in to OneDrive ...,
since ... is empty`: the empty-folder rule (round 12 N61) ran before the organization check (N53). It reads
`<provider folder> is empty while OneDrive-<org> is there: sync the SharePoint library to this Mac with Sync on
its SharePoint page, or let OneDrive finish setting it up, or fix path ...`; beside no `OneDrive-<org>` the
sign-in stays. Tests: `test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_held_provider_folder_never_holds_status_past_the_listing_bound`
(the folder there, and missing), `test_ops_doctor.py::
test_a_missing_source_fix_names_the_sign_in_only_when_the_sign_in_is_the_cause`.

**O17: under install.sh the no-folder sources line names no second command (`agentsync.cli`; amends §16.101
N13).** Step 2 printed `sources: no folder yet besides ...; run ~/.local/bin/agentsync add-source <folder>` beside
a NEXT line naming the installer's own re-run with `--source-local`, and the setup prompt says not to use
add-source. Under `AGENTSYNC_NO_NEXT_HINT=1`, which install.sh exports for every agentsync call, init included,
the line ends at what is synced (`sources: no folder yet besides the inbox`, `sources: none yet`); a bare init
keeps the pointer. The verifier's preferred form, an installer-set hint variable carrying the re-run command, was
not built: it adds an environment interface and an install.sh hunk for a command the NEXT line already gives.
Tests: `test_cli.py::test_init_under_the_installer_names_no_second_command_to_add_a_folder`, `test_cli.py::
test_init_counts_and_names_every_inbox_source`.

**O34: the withheld-unread bracket has its comma (`agentsync.cli`; amends §16.89 L33, L50 and §16.77 J29).** `(a
file whose label cannot be read: an image or a .msg not on this Mac)` read as an image not on this Mac too, false
for a local .png. It reads `(a file whose label cannot be read: an image, or a .msg not on this Mac)`;
`setup_report._WITHHELD_UNREAD_RE` reads only the count. Test: the pins in `test_cli.py::
test_the_sync_line_names_the_label_rule_for_a_file_it_withheld_unread`.

### 16.108 Round 13: deferred counts, speech, converters and policy (2026-10-17, wave B13 round 13 lane E)

Lane E's round 13 items (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 13"; specs `round13/items/O<n>.md`, the
verifier's corrected fix built): O50, O55, O56, O69 and O73. A dated line this round writes reads `Amended
2026-10-17, §16.108 O<n>`. No item needs prompt words, so none went to lane P.

**A file left for a later run is counted only while it still is (O50; `agentsync.cycle`; amends §16.102 N50).**
§16.102 N50 moved a file's count with its last settle but left `acc.deferred` and `deferred_online_only` counting
events, which no later settle undid. A new recording deferred and then read in the same poll cycle read `1 deferred
· cursor held · changed=3 (3 new)`: the bit `model.py` defines as items left for a later run, beside counts with no
deferred entry. `_SourceAcc` keeps `deferred_ids` and `deferred_online_ids`, filled at the three places that defer
(`_recording_defer`, a fetch the OS refused, `_defer`), and `deferred` and `deferred_online_only` are properties
that count the ids still settled `deferred`. A file deferred twice in one cycle counts once, and the count cannot
go negative. Only the sync line, the CHANGELOG line and the `deferred_online_only` sum read them; the cursor never
did. Tests: `test_cycle.py::test_a_new_recording_read_in_the_cycle_that_deferred_it_is_counted_once` (0 and 0),
`test_cycle.py::test_a_new_file_the_os_will_not_hydrate_is_counted_deferred` (1 and 1).

**§15's `Registry` stub has the code's signatures (O55; `agentsync.convert.registry`).** The stub in §15's module
reference still read `__init__(self, converters)`, `default(cls, cfg)` and eight converters, and had no `policy`,
`without_ocr`, `without_speech`, `screen`, `label_withheld_suffixes` or `sidecar_digest_lines`; it pointed at no §16
section. As the pandoc, pptx and pdf stubs above it are, it keeps the old signatures as `# SUPERSEDED (<date>,
§16.N)` comments, each change under its own date and section, and gives the current ones. It lists no converters: its `default`
docstring says which section added which (§7's routing, §16.26 the second `pandoc-gfm` and `image-ocr`, §16.34 and
§16.35 `recording-av` and `vtt-turns`, §16.42 and §16.48 `diagram-stdlib`, §16.42 and §16.54 `msg-olefile` or
`msg-mime`), and `Registry.default`'s own docstring stays the authority. Test:
`test_contracts.py::test_the_registry_stub_has_the_code_signatures` (every public member of the module and the
class, each with the code's parameter names, kinds and defaults).

**`page_says_withheld` names every reader (O56; `agentsync.policy`).** Its docstring named the cycle's re-render
and the setup report. `_sync/QUARANTINE.tsv` (`Publisher._stub_says`, round 10 L54) and the cycle's no-engine stub
read (`_Cycle._page_withheld`, round 9 K50) decide by it too: each reads the page's frontmatter lines with
`publish._withheld_on_page` first and calls it directly only on the YAML fallback. Test:
`test_policy.py::test_page_says_withheld_names_every_reader`, which walks `src/` for every function that calls it
or `_withheld_on_page` and fails on one the docstring does not name.

**The swift steps keep SwiftPM off the real `~/.swiftpm` (O69; `agentsync.convert.speech`; amends §16.102 N18,
§16.48 R90).** N18 found no flag that moves the `~/.swiftpm` links both swift steps re-create, since SwiftPM finds
them through Foundation, and built no code. Foundation's own override, `CFFIXED_USER_HOME`, was never tried: with
it, the links and SwiftPM's `<home>_.swiftpm.lock` in `$TMPDIR` move to the home it names. `_compile` makes
`<cache>/speech/swiftpm/home` (owner-only, under the folder its `finally` already makes owner-only) and runs
`swift package resolve` and `swift build` alone with `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` set to it; git and the seed's curl read
`HOME` and keep it. SwiftPM finds its default netrc through the same home, so the person's `~/.netrc`, when there
is one, is passed as `--netrc-file` beside the three path flags; with none, the fake home has none either, as
before. No sandbox is dropped. Measured on Swift 6.2.4 with SwiftPM's manifest sandbox on: the verifier's
one-dependency package built, and a full build of the speech helper from FluidAudio (701 s, its binary artifact
download included) exited 0, left the real `~/.swiftpm/security` link at the same inode and ctime, and its private
`$TMPDIR` held `..._speech_swiftpm_home_.swiftpm.lock` and no lock named for the real home. The fake home holds
the three links, empty `Library/org.swift.swiftpm` folders, and SwiftPM's `Library/Caches/swift-package` and
`Library/HTTPStorages` from the artifact download, which before went to the real `~/Library`. A rehearsal tells it
by that lock name, not by mtimes under `~/.swiftpm`. Tests:
`test_speech.py::test_the_swift_steps_alone_get_a_foundation_home_of_their_own`,
`test_speech.py::test_the_persons_netrc_reaches_both_swift_steps`,
`test_speech.py::test_the_build_says_which_real_home_path_its_flags_do_not_cover` (now: the docstring and both
dated lines).

**A build's time limit in the tests counts from the compiler's start (O73; tests only).** Under load (about 300)
`test_a_speech_build_out_of_time_leaves_no_compiler_running` failed: the 2 s covers the steps before `swift build`
too, and when they used it up the build raised before any compiler started, so `compiler_pid` waited 30 s for none.
A SIGINT inside the build step could also kill the stub's compiler before it wrote its pid, since `_run_build` waits
on the real clock. The speech test holds `speech._clock` at 0, so each step gets the whole 2 s, and
`test_ocr.compiling` first only notes a SIGINT, until its compiler has written its pid. Patching `ocr._clock` would
do nothing: `ocr._compile` passes its limit straight to `_run_build`. Measured: with the compiler's start 1 s late
and a SIGINT 0.3 s in, the old stub left no pid, the new one a pid and a compiler stopped. Nothing in the product
changed; the shared budget stays `test_the_build_gets_twenty_minutes_of_its_own`'s.
Amended 2026-10-17, §16.114 Q83: the measurement is two tests now, which fail on the stub's old body
("no compiler started"): `test_ocr.py::test_a_build_whose_compiler_starts_after_the_time_limit_is_stopped_too`
and `test_speech.py::test_a_speech_build_whose_compiler_starts_after_the_time_limit_is_stopped_too`.

`synced=2` reads `a sync app is not signed in`.

**A config step 2 cannot reinstall for adds no folder** (O61). Since §16.99 N29 a list whose installed agentsync is
this checkout's build and failed on the config ends on `no folder can be added until the config is fixed: run
<install.sh> with no --source-local, which shows the error`, and v21 asks nothing about folders there. The guide's
unreadable-config bullet quotes that `NEXT:` and v21's rule, and qualifies v18's "asks only whether to add one"; the
intro says the agent asks nothing about folders then. Tests: `test_the_guide_says_a_config_step_2_cannot_reinstall_for_adds_no_folder`,
`test_readme_prompt_asks_a_mac_already_set_up_for_no_folder`.

**The guide moves a late step 1 run at any gap** (O60). §16.98 N23 dropped the 10-minute test from `late_run`, and the
guide's first sentence on it changed, but the second still said each line must come "more than 10 minutes after the
earlier attempt's end line". Both now say the unbroken run of step 1 lines dated at or after the end line moves,
whatever the gap (the code's `>=`). Test: `test_the_guide_moves_a_late_step_1_run_at_any_gap`.

**Section 5 counts the sign-in step 1 waits for** (O64). The guide listed the OneDrive sign-in only as a precondition
at which "the prompt stops at step 1"; since v20 step 1 waits for it on a set-up Mac and the report counts it among the
expected turns (§16.98 N5). It is an unavoidable step now, with its evidence (K44, K45) and the unattended case on the
report side, and the precondition is a Mac that syncs no folder yet. Test:
`test_section_5_counts_the_sign_in_step_1_waits_for`.

**README's Install section gives the list's three exits** (O65). It said `--list-folders` "exits 3 when OneDrive is
not signed in or syncs no folder yet", round 10's rule: a set-up Mac also exits 3 when a folder under
`~/Library/CloudStorage` is missing because its app is signed out (§16.93 M4, §16.99 N41), and otherwise exits 0, even
with OneDrive signed out and nothing listed. docs/deploy/README.md's sentence is not copied: its "exits 3 when there are
none" leans on that guide's later set-up Mac paragraph. Test:
`test_the_deploy_guides_say_a_set_up_mac_with_a_missing_folder_exits_3`.

**§16.103 and §16.99 record what round 12's later commits changed** (O63; dated lines at §16.103 N9, N62, N67 and
§16.99 N41). §16.103 was written before lane RB's 42de9ecc and lane RA's N31: its N9 paragraph quoted the intro
without "(or the app it names)", its N62 paragraph said any missing synced folder gives exit 3, and its N66/N67
paragraph said `_list_stopped` runs `if not synced`. Each has a dated line, and §16.99's N41/N61 paragraph says the
README and both guides changed with it. The docstring of `test_the_guide_quotes_round_11s_installer_bracket_and_list_rule`
says what N67 was and that N31 has since removed the guard. Tests: the dated-line scan
(`test_every_dated_line_from_round_11_on_is_held_by_a_test`).

### 16.110 Round 14: setup report (2026-10-17, wave B13 round 14 lane RA)

The setup report's findings of the v22 rehearsals, the cross-lane review and the harvest (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`,
"B13 round 14"). Lane RA's round 14 items: Q3, Q4, Q12, Q13, Q14, Q17, Q18, Q21, Q25, Q28, Q36, Q37, Q46, Q47,
Q48, Q50, Q52, Q53, Q55, Q78 (round 14's Q ids, not round 4's). All are built; none was recorded as making things
worse. Q3, Q18 and Q36 are one defect, built once; so are Q14 and Q37, Q46 and Q55, and Q17 and Q78.

**A folder step 1 found not on disk has its own doctor bucket** (Q3, Q18, Q36; amends §16.39 N16, §16.104 O13).
Step 1's list logged `gone=1` and its NEXT said step 2's status fails on that folder, yet the Doctor line called the
folder's FAILs unexpected. `_gone_folder_fails` takes `source.<id>.listable` and `.volume` of a live source under
~/Library/CloudStorage whose own path is not on disk, by check name and path, never doctor's fix text, when the
attempt's last list logged `gone=N` (N at least 1) and was no sign-in exit. The provider folder may be gone too:
install.sh's `gone=` also counts the other-account and library cases. When more such sources are missing than N,
which went missing after step 1 cannot be told, so all stay unexpected. The line reads `from the folder step 1 found
not on disk 1: source.<id>.listable FAIL, source.<id>.volume FAIL` (N counts folders; `folders` for more than one;
the step is the layout's folder-question step), before `unexpected`, and never holds a sign-in stop's FAIL.
`_doctor_fails` and the outcome are unchanged; its docstring no longer says every FAIL is unexpected (Q52). Test:
`test_the_folders_step_1_found_not_on_disk_have_their_own_doctor_bucket`.

Amended 2026-10-18, §16.116 S12, S27: the number counts checks, like the other buckets; the label names the folder
count: `from the 1 synced folder step 1 found not on disk 2: source.<id>.listable FAIL, source.<id>.volume FAIL`.
Amended 2026-10-18, §16.122 T20, T34: the count is in a bracket with its unit, after the words: `from the 1 synced folder step 1
found not on disk (2 checks): ...`.

**The sign-in stop's bucket is install.sh's signed-out rule** (Q46, Q55; amends §16.104 O13). The bucket took a
source when its provider folder was not on disk. A stale provider folder holding only hidden entries is signed out
to install.sh's `signed_out` (rc 0), and its FAILs read as unexpected; a SharePoint library gone or empty beside its
`OneDrive-<org>` (rc 3) and a provider folder gone beside another folder of its app (rc 2) are no sign-in, yet their
FAILs landed in the bucket. doctor's classification is one function, `doctor.provider_state(provider)`:
`signed-out`, `other-account`, `library` or `signed-in`, the library check before the empty-folder one (O52), the
listing bounded by `_LISTING_TIMEOUT_S` (O47), an unreadable or held folder signed in (N61). `_missing_source_fix`
maps its states to the same fix texts as before, and `_sign_in_stop_fails` takes a source only when its own path is
not on disk (`_on_disk`, install.sh's `[ ! -e ]`: a dangling link is not on disk) and its provider folder is
`signed-out`. The report reads each provider folder once (`_Run.provider_states`), its listing bounded by
`_LISTING_S` and what is left of its budget, never doctor's 120 s; one that does not answer counts as signed in. The O13 test's
gone `OneDrive-<org>` sat beside its `OneDrive-SharedLibraries-<org>`, which install.sh reads as another account
(rc 2); it now uses a stale provider folder. Tests: `test_the_sign_in_stop_bucket_takes_the_folders_install_sh_calls_signed_out`,
`test_an_unattended_sign_in_stop_is_an_item_and_its_fails_are_the_stops`.

**A new Mac's step 1 stop goes to the report attended or not** (Q47; amends §16.104 O13). The stop item said `(not
logged: an unattended run goes to the report)` on every exit 3. From prompt v21 a sign-in on a Mac that syncs no
folder is no click, so every run goes to the report there. That reason stays only for the prompt's first exception,
a sign-in exit on a Mac that already syncs folders (`not-signed-in` with `synced=N`, N at least 1), where an
attended run waits; any other exit 3 (a `no-folders` exit, a sign-in with `synced=0` or none) reads `(not logged: on
this stop step 1 goes to the report)`. Test: `test_a_new_macs_step_1_stop_goes_to_the_report_attended_or_not`.

**Sign-in words for three apps, and the run table's stopped list** (Q48, Q13, Q52; amends §16.104 O1, O19).
Q48: `_signed_out` joins the sign-in's names as the stop's (`the OneDrive, Dropbox and Box sign-ins`, never `the
OneDrive and Dropbox and Box sign-ins`), and makes it plural whenever more than one app is named, `another sync app`

**The status step's notes** (Q4, Q50; amends §16.104 O3, O33). Q4: the Installer table's status row (`doctor` in
older logs) read `done, rc 1 (fail-lines)`; `_STATUS_NOTE_WORDS` words its notes: `agentsync status reported [FAIL]
lines`, `its only [FAIL] lines were a macOS Allow still to be clicked, which the wait step asks for` and `agentsync

`test_the_installer_table_puts_the_status_steps_note_in_words`, `test_sections_carry_the_facts`,
`test_the_outcome_of_a_status_fail_stop_names_the_status_step`, `test_a_status_that_fails_with_no_fail_line_logs_status_error`. Amended 2026-10-18, §16.117 S33, S58, S62: that run's
closing NEXT is no longer `fix the [FAIL] lines above ...` but `agentsync status exited <rc> (<meaning>) with no [FAIL]
line: ...`, which sends the agent to the report.

Amended 2026-10-18, §16.116 S35: the tcc-pending words read `its only [FAIL] lines were a macOS Allow still to be
clicked (the [FAIL] line names it)`, in both twins.

**The Summary's folders line** (Q17, Q78; amends §16.104 O9). The Installer row read `2 already synced, 1 of them
not on disk` while the Summary read `kept the 2 already synced (none added)`. `_folders_line` adds `step 1's list
found 1 synced folder not on disk: see Doctor`, in every branch (`(none added; ...)`, `1 added to the 2 already
synced (...)`), by the list's own `gone=` count, when the list run right before the last install run (no install
run between) finished with `gone=` at least 1 and no sign-in note, and this report's doctor FAILs a source's

on disk` is not built: without the doctor gate it claims a folder missing after it was fixed. Test:
`test_the_folders_line_says_step_1_found_a_synced_folder_not_on_disk`.

Amended 2026-10-18, §16.116 S9: the counts are the attempt's install runs', not the last run's alone; the
not-on-disk clause still follows the list run right before the last install run.

**A retried run's item** (Q12, Q21). Q12: Items said `the same command was run again and ended 0` of a run whose
re-run had other arguments; `_retry_line` now gets the attempt's first install run that ended 0 and compares the two

`--source-local` folders read `install.sh was run again with other folders and ended 0`; anything else (or quoting

run that ended 0 named none) or `with --source-local folders added` (the failed run named none); `other folders` is
for folders on both runs.

**Residue: an app's own provider folder** (Q14, Q37). `~/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/<folder-3>` flagged
`Dropbox`: only a provider folder naming an organisation was skipped (`provider_heads`). `residue()` skips an app
name (`_CONTEXT_HEADS`) only inside the provider folder right after `CloudStorage/` (`_PROVIDER_DIR_RE`: `Dropbox`,
both words of `Box-Box`, `GoogleDrive-<name>`, `Egnyte-<org-1>`); any other word there is still a hit (`Acme` in
`Dropbox-Acme-<org-1>`), and so is an app name anywhere else (`<folder-1> Box`, a project's leftover second word).
The names are not added to `_RESIDUE_IGNORED`. The finding's stated cause, `report_words()` skipping
`_SIGN_IN_APPS`, was not it: `residue()` never reads `report_words()`. Tests:
`test_an_app_name_is_no_residue_only_as_the_provider_folder`, `test_a_personal_dropbox_folder_leaves_no_residue_in_the_report`.

**The issue title's step 2** (Q25). The v7-and-later layout named step 2 `install`, so a v22 title read `Failed at
step 2 (install)` beside the field `Failed at step 2 (install and start)`; every prompt since v7 calls the step
"Install and start". The layout reads `install and start`, and setup-feedback.md's example of a title that differs
from its field is a v5 attempt's step 3 (`Failed at step 3 (install and start)` against `Failed at step 2 (install
and start)`). The older sections that quote v7's step 2 as `install` (§16.52, §16.58, §16.62) describe the layout
of their round. Test: `test_setup_feedback_states_the_report_rules_of_round_6`.

H43 and §16.79 J60, each with a dated line now; §16.52, §16.58 and §16.62 hold no such quote.

**Two sessions that each stop at step 1 within the gap are two attempts** (Q28). Probe prx: a finished attempt, then
two stated step 1 errors (`prompt v22, <agent>: ...`) 4m36s apart, read as one 4m36s session with the first stop as
friction and the second line's prefix kept. A session writes that prefix once, only before `--log-start`, at the
Xcode or git stop, then goes to its report, so after a header, or after a header-less attempt that already has
stated words, a stated step 1 error is another session's at any gap (after stated words, only a line in the awk's
strict `<stamp> | step 1 | error |` form, so both readers split a loosely written line alike). `parse_friction`'s `orphan()` and install.sh's
`track()` change together (the version, agent and gap comparisons of round 4 Q21 and `_agent_key` go), so the
installer's NEXT and the report judge the same attempts. Residual: an agent that logs its stated error twice gets a
second `failed at step 1` attempt; round 9 K14's twice-prefixed shell case now logs its second line without the
prefix. Tests: `test_two_sessions_that_each_stop_at_step_1_within_the_gap_are_two_attempts`,
`test_a_step_1_error_with_another_sessions_words_leaves_an_attempt_with_no_end_line`,
`test_the_installer_and_the_report_split_the_same_attempts_after_any_header`,
`test_the_shell_report_computes_a_step_1_failure_past_its_first_line`.

**The report's git lookup is inside its budget** (Q53). `_git_ro_err` looked git up (`xcrun --find git`, bounded
only by 10 s) before reading the budget, and a failed lookup was not kept, so each call asked again. The budget is
read first; `gitops.usr_bin_git(timeout=...)` is bounded by what is left of the budget (not the call's own 3 s,
so a slow but working xcrun still answers) and its answer, the `/usr/bin/git` fallback
included, is kept on the report's `_Run.git`; the time left is read again before git runs. gitops' per-process memo
still keeps successes only. Test: `test_the_reports_git_lookup_is_asked_once_within_its_time_budget`.

**Comments** (Q52). install.sh's `friction_latest_has_step` comment named `friction_step1_stated`'s attempt
boundaries, which O24 changed only for has_step; it names parse_friction's.

library ...` for a library folder that is there but empty, and `persons_fails` read only `is missing while`, so step 2

**bring-back.md's failures and missing patches name their remedy** (Q19, Q20, Q29, Q30; amends §16.105 O7, O25 and
§16.104 O23). Q19: every failure of `write_bring_back` sets `BACK_WHY`, which the warning names (`a folder, or a link
to a folder, is at that path; move it away`; a temporary file; a patch read cut short; `chmod or mv failed (its error
is above)`), since N71's NEXT says to fix the cause. Q20, Q29: with a kept patch this account cannot read, the
`--report-only` NEXT reads `<file> does not hold N kept patch file(s) this account cannot read (see the warning
above): make them readable (chmod u+r on the files in <setup>/local-work) and run this command again, then review
<file> and copy that one file back privately[, or paste ...] (nothing is sent for you)`; the header gives the remedy
beside a patch that was sent too; both readers' local-work line add `, U of them unreadable and not in bring-back.md

patch is listed in `local-work/.not-sent` (no `*.patch` glob reads it) by its identity (device, inode, time, size:
chmod changes none) and the report's time, and is sent whatever its time while the earlier attempt's end is not
after that record. Corrected by measurement: the verifier's rule, which rewrote the list from each run's unreadable
patches, dropped it again at a second report of the same later attempt; the record stays while the patch is
unchanged, and goes with it. Not ctime, which Finder, Spotlight and a moved folder change. Q30: the branches-only

`test_a_bring_back_file_that_cannot_be_written_is_not_named_as_the_one_to_review`,
`test_a_patch_unreadable_at_a_report_is_sent_once_it_is_readable` (with the issue link and without),

`test_deploy_pack.py::test_the_guide_names_the_late_listing_and_the_local_work_line`.

### 16.112 Round 14: setup prompt v23 (2026-10-17, wave B13 round 14 lane P)

The B13 round 14 items of lane P (specs `round14/items/Q<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built unless a
measurement below says otherwise): round 14 Q2, Q7, Q8, Q15, Q31, Q32, Q73. All need prompt text, so the prompt is

the issue form's placeholder and the block's digest move together, and a saved v22 copy is stopped at step 1 like
every older copy. v23 moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry. None adds an agentsync command, an
installer flag, a config key or a friction kind. Lanes that sent words: lane B (step 3's status sentence, for its
round 14 Q1, Q9, Q33).

**Status prints a sync's NEXT unless a check FAILs** (Q2; lane B's words). v22 step 3 said `agentsync status` "prints
the same NEXT: line without syncing", but with a check that FAILs, status's NEXT is rule 1's, which names that check
(after rule 1's own skill and sign-in checks, which a sync's NEXT gives as well), and it exits 1, where a sync's call (`loop.next_lines(config)`) goes on to the baseline. v23: "... prints the same NEXT:
line without syncing, unless one of its checks FAILs: then it exits 1, its NEXT: names that [FAIL] line, and a
[FAIL] fix that is mine (step 2) stays mine." Lane B's words, plus "it exits 1", so a non-zero status is not logged
as a failed command. Status's FAIL NEXT is not made a sync's (the finder's second option, which the verifier showed
makes things worse: it hides the check from the one read-only command meant to show it, and the setup report's Loop

### 16.114 Round 14: native pandoc, doctor's pandoc check and load-timing tests (2026-10-17, wave B13 round 14 lane E)

Lane E's round 14 items (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 14"; specs `round14/items/Q<n>.md`, the
verifier's corrected fix built): Q56, Q60, Q61, Q62, Q76 and Q83. Q56, Q60 and Q76 are one defect, built once;
Q62 and Q76's docs half are its CONTRACTS text. A dated line this round writes reads `Amended 2026-10-17, §16.114
Q<n>`. No item needs prompt words, so none went to lane P. Lane RB (round 14) agreed to lane E's edit of
`status_pandoc` in `scripts/install.sh`; it keeps `start_pandoc_once`.

**The native pandoc route (load root cause 2026-10-17 X26; `agentsync.convert.pandoc`).** On macOS only, with no
`[convert] pandoc_path`, the converters run `~/.local/share/agentsync/pandoc/<version>-arm64/bin/pandoc` when it is
an executable regular file (`~` read at each call). The operator installs it; agentsync never does. `<version>` is
the one `_WHEEL_PANDOC_VERSIONS` maps the sha256 to that the pypandoc_binary RECORD lists for
`pypandoc/files/pandoc` (what pip checked at install): the binary is never run or hashed for this. An unknown hash,
a missing RECORD, entry or copy, a size or path that does not match, or any other platform means the wheel's
binary. The copy is the same version with the same flags, so the same bytes come out; only the CPU architecture
changes (the wheel's binary is x86_64 and runs under Rosetta: about 0.16 s and 68 MB per run against 0.03 s and
30 MB, plus 10 to 67 s at the first start of each fresh copy). Tests: `tests/test_pandoc_native.py`.

**Doctor, the setup report and the installer check the pandoc the converters run (Q56, Q60, Q76;
`agentsync.convert.pandoc`, `agentsync.ops.doctor`, `agentsync.setup_report`, `scripts/install.sh`).** X26 changed
only the converters. Doctor's `_pandoc_path`, whose docstring said "the pandoc the converters will run", the
report's `pandoc` line and `status_pandoc` still named `pypandoc/files/pandoc`: with the copy installed a copy that
exits 137 read OK while every conversion failed, a Mac with the copy and no Rosetta read the EBADARCH FAIL while
conversions worked, and every install still paid Rosetta's first start of a binary nothing then ran. The rule now
lives in one place, `convert.pandoc.resolved_pandoc(pandoc_path) -> (path, kind)`, kind `configured`, `native` or
`wheel`, which `_PandocRunner.path` calls; it reads RECORD and runs nothing, and raises ConversionError for a
configured path that is not an absolute file and for a missing wheel binary. Doctor keeps `[convert] pandoc_path`
as written, for its own not-absolute and not-executable lines, and otherwise asks the resolver; a missing wheel
binary is still named, for its `missing or not executable` line and fix, not raised. Its OK line says which copy
ran: `pandoc 3.9 at <path> (native arm64 copy)` or `(bundled with pypandoc_binary)`. A native copy's FAIL line
says `(native arm64 copy)` after the path, and its fix is `replace or remove
~/'.local/share/agentsync/pandoc/<version>-arm64' (the converters run it instead of the bundled pandoc), or set
[convert] pandoc_path to an absolute pandoc`: not `uv sync`, which does not touch it, and no Rosetta words, which
are the wheel's binary's alone, as is the slow-first-start reason on a line that ran out of time. The report runs
the resolver's pandoc, adds ` (native arm64 copy)` for the copy and gives the resolver's reason for a missing
wheel binary. `status_pandoc` imports `resolved_pandoc` (and `agentsync.errors.ConversionError`) from the
installed tool; one older than that has no resolver and its status checks the wheel's pandoc, which is then the
one named, and a ConversionError names none. Tests: `test_ops_doctor.py::test_the_pandoc_check_runs_the_native_copy_the_converters_run`,
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_native_pandoc_that_fails_names_that_copy_and_not_rosetta`,
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_missing_bundled_pandoc_is_the_checks_fail_and_no_crash`,
`test_setup_report.py::test_the_pandoc_line_is_the_pandoc_the_converters_run`,
`test_install_oneshot.py::test_the_pandoc_the_installer_starts_is_the_one_the_converters_run` (the current tool,
an older one and a missing wheel binary, run by bash 3.2).
Amended 2026-10-18, §16.120 S47: the native copy's fix is the person's, `the native pandoc copy at <copy> is yours
to replace or remove (the converters run it instead of the bundled pandoc), or set [convert] pandoc_path to an

§16.116 S<n>`). No item needs prompt words.

**An Items line keeps the error after an exit code with no verb before it** (S1; extends §16.110 Q31). Q31's cut of
an error line longer than 220 characters starts the error where `_FAILED_EXIT_RE` matches, which needed `failed`,
`exited`, `returned` or `(exit` first; the shapes `<cmd> exit 1: <error>`, `exit code 1:`, `exit status 128:`, `rc=1:`
and `rc 1:` were cut inside the command, with no word of git's error. A second arm matches them; the leftmost match
is unchanged for the old shapes. Test: `test_a_logged_command_keeps_its_bars_and_its_error`.

**The folders line reads the attempt's install runs** (S9; amends §16.110 Q17). `_folders_line` took `kept`,
`added` and the named options from the last install run alone, so a run that added a folder and exited 1 at status,
then a re-run with no options, read `kept the 3 already synced (none added) · 0 named` while the prompt's finish
named the folder added (and, on a new Mac, `kept the 1 already synced`). Over the install runs inside the attempt's
end line whose config step logged both counts: kept is the first run's `kept`, what was synced before the attempt,
never a sum (2 + 3 would be 5); added is the sum of `added` over the `done` config steps (a config step that wrote
sources.toml before a status exit 1 still wrote it); named counts distinct folders (`_without_folders`, compared in
memory, never printed), so a retry with the same `--source-local` names one. An added count from a run that is not
the last names it: `1 added to the 2 already synced (by run <label>, which exited 1) · 1 named with --source-local
(install.log)`, or `1 added (none was synced before; by run <label>) · ...`. When the counts do not chain (a source
changed by hand between runs: first `kept` plus the sum is not the last run's `kept` plus its own), the line is the
last run's, with `(last run; install.log)`. One counted run, or a last run after the end line, reads as before; the
not-on-disk clause (`_gone_clause`) keeps the list run right before the last install run. Test:
`test_the_folders_line_counts_what_was_kept_added_and_named` (RT's two runs, a same-options retry, a run after the
end line, counts that do not chain).
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.134 V37: a last run after the end line whose config step added nothing (a retry confirming what an earlier run wrote) joins the chain; one that added a folder is still the last run's alone.

Amended 2026-10-18, §16.122 T44: only for an attempt with a begin time, as the install line scopes; with no friction log, or an attempt
with no begin time, the runs are the whole install.log, and the line is the last run's.

**A [FAIL] fix that is the person's is no hint for the agent** (S5). `instruction_counts` counted every `fix:` as an
instruction-like line, which the Installer section calls a hint the agent may act on, so a run whose six [FAIL]
fixes were the person's read `6 other instruction-like line(s) (6 fix:)` while that run's NEXT (`PERSONS_FAILS`)
said they are not a step for the agent. The lines are split at each `# run=` header and judged by run, as
install.sh's `persons_fails` does: a run whose stopping [FAIL] lines (TCC_PENDING ones left out, as `blocking_fails`
does) are there and all end in ` (fix: X)` with `doctor.is_persons_fix(X)` counts those lines' fixes as
`persons-fix` (`PERSONS_FIX`), outside `other_total`: `... and 0 other instruction-like line(s) and 6 fix: on [FAIL]
lines that are the person's (their run's NEXT says so; not hints for the agent) in the last ...`. A mixed run (a
person's fix beside a `chmod 700` [FAIL]) keeps both as `fix:`, since its NEXT says `fix the [FAIL] lines above`;
a fix on a [warn], [ok] or TCC_PENDING line stays `fix:`, and a NEXT holding `fix:` is still a `NEXT:`. Not per
line: a per-line split would call a mixed run's person's fix "not a hint" under a NEXT that asks the agent to act.
The Installer sentence says so. Test: `test_a_persons_fail_fix_is_not_counted_as_a_hint_for_the_agent`.

line(s) (6 fix:)` above is what the line read before S5.

### 16.117 Round 15: installer, the no-[FAIL] status NEXT and the unread patch (2026-10-18, wave B13 round 15 lane RB)

Installer items from the v23 rehearsal, the cross-lane review and the harvest (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`,
"B13 round 15"; specs `round15/items/S<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built). The S ids are round 15's. A dated
line this round writes reads `Amended 2026-10-18, §16.117 S<n>`.

**A status that exits non-zero with no `[FAIL]` line gets a NEXT of its own** (S33, S58, S62, one defect; amends
§16.110 Q50). Q50 logged `note=status-error` for it, but `DOCTOR_BLOCKS` still took the generic NEXT, `fix the [FAIL]
lines above (each names its fix), then re-run: ...`, with no `[FAIL]` line above it, and README step 2 has the agent
run that re-run into the same failure. Placed after the person's-fails arm and before the generic one, so a run with
a `[FAIL]` line keeps its NEXT, it reads `agentsync status exited <rc> (<meaning>) with no [FAIL] line: what it printed
above (its error, if it printed one; ~/.local/bin/agentsync status prints it again) is the person's to fix, not a step
for the agent, so show them those lines and go on to the report; once fixed, the next run is: <install.sh ...>`, the
config error's shape (§16.14 K02's O11 line). It promises no error, since a signal or a timeout prints none. Exit 1
and the skipped sync stay. Tests: `test_a_status_that_fails_with_no_fail_line_logs_status_error`,
`test_launcher.py::test_install_sh_doctor_failure_blocks_the_agent`.

**A known count needs no "(s)" in install.sh, doctor's heartbeat line or the vanished-source refusal** (S14; the
cluster lane RA's S26, S30 and S31 and lane B's S65 and S52 close in their files). install.sh's unread-patch lines
(section 3's `not sent:` line, both header sentences, the warning and the `--report-only` NEXT) read `1 patch file ...
make it readable` or `2 patch files ... make them readable`, set once where the count is known, as list_folders does;
doctor's `listing incomplete for the last 1 pass` / `2 passes`; the cycle's refusal `source 'x' (1 file) is mirrored`
or `sources 'x' (1 file), 'y' (3 files) are mirrored`. The Summary's `N patch file(s) in the setup folder's
local-work` line is left for a change of its own (setup_report, the guide's quote and its pin move together). Tests:
`test_a_patch_this_account_cannot_read_is_counted_not_sent`, `test_ops_doctor.py::test_heartbeat_states`,
`test_review_fixes.py::test_two_vanished_sources_are_named_with_counted_nouns`.

**Section 3's remedies name the command, and the branch remedy keeps the keep's file names** (S23, S25; amends
§16.104 O23). Section 3 is in a file the person reads, not command output, so `then run this command again` named
nothing, or read as the format-patch just before it; both section 3 lines (the unreadable patch's `not sent:` and the
branches-only remedy) now end `run ~/src/agent-context-sync/scripts/install.sh --report-only again`, the
`LOCAL_WORK_AGAIN` the Summary's local-work line already uses. The branches remedy had dropped the keep commands'
`-c format.filenameMaxLength=128`, so git's 64-character default (with the 33-character branch suffix) cut the
subject and one commit got a second file name (`0002-local-changes-kept-before.local-work-<stamp>.patch` beside the
keep's `...-before-update...`), sent twice if the original came back; the `-c` goes after `-C <path>`, as in the
README's keeps. The terminal NEXT lines, which are the command's own output, keep `run this command again`. Tests:
`test_a_patch_this_account_cannot_read_is_counted_not_sent`, the section 3 pin in
`test_the_shell_report_says_step_1_kept_local_work_in_counts_only`,
`test_section_3s_branch_remedy_names_a_commit_as_the_keep_does` (the remedy install.sh prints, run on a real branch),
`test_deploy_pack.py::test_the_guide_names_the_late_listing_and_the_local_work_line`.

Amended 2026-10-19, §16.136 V17, V79: one terminal NEXT names the command too, the `--report-only` NEXT for a kept
patch this account cannot read (`... and run ~/src/agent-context-sync/scripts/install.sh --report-only again, then
review ...`): an agent relays it to the person, where `this command` names none.

**The header's unread-patch sentence is two sentences, the second counted** (S24; amends §16.105 O25). With a patch
unread and the others listed by their hash it read `... could not be read: make them readable (chmod u+r) and run the
report again (install.sh --report-only); see its last line, and the others were in an earlier report and are listed
by their hash.`: two colons, and "the others ... their hash" of a single patch, since it keyed on there being any
skipped line and never read their count. It reads `Section 3 sends no patch: N patch file(s) could not be read; make
them readable (chmod u+r) and run the report again (install.sh --report-only), as its last line says.`, then `The one
other patch was in an earlier report and is listed by its hash.` or `The other N patches were in an earlier report and
are listed by their hash.`; with nothing sent, the others are exactly the patches listed by their hash. The arm beside
a patch that was sent drops its second colon the same way. (The counts above take S14's nouns.) Test:
`test_an_unreadable_patch_leaves_the_rest_of_section_3_right` (one and two listed by their hash).
Amended 2026-10-18, §16.123 T25: a report that sends a patch says the same counted sentence of the others.

**`.not-sent` lists only a patch the report would have sent, and lets go once the attempt that sent it ends** (S22,
S34; amends §16.111 Q29). S22 (probe bw3): a patch an earlier attempt's report carried, unreadable at a later report,
was listed, so once readable it was sent again. The unreadable branch now lists a patch only when the readable one
would send it: no earlier end, a listing at or after it, or a time unknown or after it. S34: `--report-only` writes the
end line before bring-back.md, so a listing is at or after its own attempt's end; made readable and reported again in
that attempt (Q20's remedy), the patch was sent and the listing kept, so the next attempt, whose earlier end is that
end line, sent it once more. A listed patch that a report sends now gets a third field, `<id> <listed> <begin>`, the
time its attempt began (`friction_attempt_begin`, parse_friction's boundaries; `-` when that cannot be told); while
that attempt lasts each report sends it (the same section 3), and once another attempt reports the listing goes and
the time rule lists the patch by its hash. A two-field listing is not sent yet. Corrected by measurement: the
verifier keyed the third field on the earlier attempt's end (`prev`), which every header-less attempt after the last
end line shares, so a patch sent in one would be forced again in the next; the attempt's begin tells them apart. Not
the finder's "drop the listing once sent": a third report in an attempt with an earlier end would then skip it by its
time, though no earlier report carried it. Tests:
`test_a_patch_made_readable_in_the_attempt_that_could_not_read_it_is_sent_once` (on the real clock, and with the end
and the listing 3 s apart), `test_a_patch_an_earlier_report_carried_is_not_listed_as_not_sent`,
`test_a_patch_unreadable_at_two_finished_reports_is_sent_once_readable`.
Amended 2026-10-18, §16.123 T24: a patch an earlier attempt's report carried and unreadable now is no unread patch:
it is a not-repeated line with no hash, and section 1 counts by the same rule.

**A report of an attempt with no header counts as carrying its patches** (S21; amends §16.111 Q29). An attempt step 1
stopped (Xcode, git) has no `Attempt:` line, so `friction_close_attempt` writes no end line for it and the time rule
(`friction_earlier_end`) never sees its report: Variant R's second session, 12 minutes after the first one's report,
embedded both patches again with no `not repeated:` line, and bw3 did the same after a finished headed attempt. Once
bring-back.md is in place, `local-work/.sent` (0600, skipped when it or local-work is a link, as `.not-sent` is) holds
one line per embedded patch, `<device:inode:mtime:size> <report time>`, keeping the first report's time while the
patch is unchanged; a patch gone or changed leaves it. A patch whose record is strictly before the current attempt's
begin (`friction_attempt_begin`) is listed `not repeated: a patch file an earlier attempt's report held (<time>): N
lines, sha256 <12 hex>; still in ~/agent-context/setup/local-work`; `.not-sent` keeps its priority, the time rule its
place, and an attempt that cannot be told (no friction log), a record of this attempt or a time that cannot be read
sends it. So a second report in one attempt still sends it (the same section 3), and header-less sessions that
parse_friction merges into one attempt (unstated words under 10 minutes apart) send it in each report. Not the
finder's "listed whatever the end lines say": the second report of the same attempt would then drop the patch from
the file that replaces the first. Not the alternative of an end line for a header-less attempt, which reverses the
tested "no end line for it" rule and how parse_friction reads the attempt. A patch `.sent` holds is not put in
`.not-sent` when it is unreadable (S22's rule). docs/deploy/README.md's setup/ row names `local-work/.sent`. Tests:
`test_a_report_of_an_attempt_with_no_header_is_counted_as_carrying_its_patches` (with no earlier attempt, and after a
finished one), `test_a_patch_unreadable_after_a_report_with_no_header_embedded_it_is_not_listed`,
`test_deploy_pack.py::test_the_guide_names_the_late_listing_and_the_local_work_line`.
Amended 2026-10-18, §16.123 T16, T26: `.sent`'s words come first; the time rule no longer clears it.

**The list counts a synced folder gone from disk apart from one outside it** (S10; amends §16.29). Every synced

Amended 2026-10-18, §16.123 T18, T43, T23, T84: the next wait is looked for after the whole count (a count of 10

**The two twins join the signed-out apps alike, and an unlogged step 2 stop is an item** (S40; amends §16.99 N41,
§16.104 O13 and §16.112 Q7). (a) Round 14 Q48 made the report say `OneDrive, Dropbox and Box are not signed in` and

install can take a minute; later ones are quick)` on every run, though a run stopped during the wait leaves the tool

**FRICTION_AWK keeps one flag for stated words, not a version and an agent** (S38). Since round 14 Q28 dropped the
