### 16.118 Round 15: setup prompt v24 (2026-10-18, wave B13 round 15 lane P)

The B13 round 15 items of lane P (specs `round15/items/S<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built unless a
measurement below says otherwise): round 15 S6, S8, S18, S55, S60. S8 and S55 are one defect from two finders (the
first sync's refused config), built once: S8's report half and S55's prompt half. All but S8's report half need
prompt text, so the prompt is **setup prompt v24**: `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, `PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's `prompt v24`
and `setup-prompt-compat 24`, the issue form's placeholder and the block's digest move together, and a saved v23
copy is stopped at step 1 like every older copy. v24 moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry. None adds
an agentsync command, an installer flag, a config key or a friction kind. Lanes that sent words: lane RB (step 2's
bracket, for its S33, S58, S62).

**A config the sync refuses is listed, with the report's reason** (S8, S55; amends §16.94 M28 and §16.112 Q8).
Round 14's Q22 (§16.111) made the first sync's exit 78 a stop the person owns; the sync prints `configuration error:
...` for a config that loads (a source deleted from sources.toml while its pages are mirrored, a policy.toml that
does not pass), and setup-report said `- loads: yes` with no reason. v23 keyed step 2's inbox skip and the finish's
does-not-load case on "configuration error", so the agent skipped a real inbox and said a file that loads "does not
load". `setup_report._configuration` now runs the sync's read-only refusal checks (`_live_refusal`: the manifest's
present rows against the configured ids, as `cycle._refuse_vanished_sources` reads them, then `policy.load_policy`
and `governance.load_governance`) and prints `- loads: yes, but a sync refuses it: <why>`: a source the config lacks
by place (`(not in the config, N)`, as `_Labels` names one), a table's error by its table, key and file only (its
words can quote a label or a host). A cause none of them reads comes from the latest attempt's last install run whose
first sync exited 78, its `configuration error:` line in install.out: `- loads: yes, but step 2's sync refused it
(run <id>): ...`; one they read and no longer find was fixed, and drops the line. Neither begins "loads: no" or
"loads: not". v24: step 2's inbox skip reads "unless its NEXT: line says the config does not load" (config_failed's
NEXT); the does-not-load case keys on "loads: no:" alone; and after the two unknown cases the finish adds "and,
outside those two cases, if the report's Configuration section says "loads: yes, but" (the file loads, but a sync
refused it: fixing that is mine), say so after the folders or the "none", followed by the error that line gives".
The two verifiers differed: S8's said "unknown: the sync refuses ...", listing no folders; S55's said the refused
config falls through to the folder list. The file loads and its folders are the ones the person chose, so they are
listed (or "none", when the deleted block was its last local folder), and S8's reason is given beside them. "A sync
refused it", since the install.out line names a cause the report cannot check again. The live check runs in the
sync's order (policy, `[governance]`, then the vanished sources), so it names the refusal `agentsync sync` prints;
policy.toml's own "cannot read the policy table" counts as a cause it reads; and with the manifest unreadable, the
install.out line's quoted source ids are named as `_Labels` names them. Step 2's person-owned clause is unchanged and routes both exit-78 stops. Tests:
`test_a_config_the_sync_refuses_loads_but_says_so`, `test_a_first_sync_refusal_is_no_config_that_does_not_load`,
`test_readme_step3_runs_the_loop_then_the_report` (`UNLOADED_CONFIG`, `REFUSED_CONFIG`),
`test_readme_prompt_carries_the_field_lines` (`INBOX_WHEN`).

Amended 2026-10-18, §16.122 T7, T15: a vanished source's count sits inside its label's bracket, `a source (not in the config, 1; 4
files) is mirrored ...`, on the live line and on step 2's install.out line; a table's refusal no longer names the
exception's class: `[policy] exclude_label_ids in policy.toml is not valid (the error's words are not shown here,
...)`.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.128 U22, U43: the refusal gives Doctor's words, only the file's path cut from their front, a
value a placeholder as in Doctor: `[policy] exclude_label_ids in policy.toml is not valid (a value in the error is a
placeholder here; `~/.local/bin/agentsync status` prints it in full): [policy]: exclude_label_ids: <label> is not a
label GUID`.

**Step 1 logs a failed command's error as printed, host names included** (S6; amends §16.112 Q31). Step 1's "log the
command that failed ... and its error" met the friction rule's "name ... my organization ... by its role, never by
its real name", and git's error can name a host that carries it; the rehearsal's agent logged it verbatim, and the
report showed `<proxy-1>`. v24: "and its error as the command printed it, host names included (the report replaces
the host of a proxy, of a URL rewrite and of a "Could not resolve" or "Failed to connect to" message; the role rule
is for your own words)". "As the command printed it", not the verifier's "as git printed it": the same sentence
logs xcode-select's error. Not the finder's "the report replaces host names", which claims more than the code does
(a host only in a 403 or TLS error is not replaced). Test: `test_readme_step1_is_one_command`.
Amended 2026-10-18, §16.123 T88: both readers now replace a git remote's host as well, so a 403 or TLS error on a
hand-set origin is replaced too.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.130 U97: since v26 the prompt's parenthesis names a git remote's host too.

**A failed step 2 run whose NEXT the agent follows is not logged** (S18). Step 2's middle branch (do what a non-zero
run's NEXT: says when it is an install.sh or agentsync command or a click) said nothing on logging, against the
friction rule's "error (a command failed ...)". The report already names a retried run (`_retry_line`), and a logged
line adds a second item and a friction count. v24 adds "A failed run whose NEXT: you follow this way is not logged
(the report names it once a later run ends 0)": `retried_runs` pairs a failed run only with a later one that ended
0 (the lane's review). Not the finder's alternative, "log it as a step 2 error, then run

**Each pandoc gets its own fix, and `uv sync` is gone (S29; `agentsync.ops.doctor`; dated lines at §16.32).** Every
pandoc FAIL but the native copy's named `uv sync (reinstalls pypandoc_binary) or set [convert] pandoc_path to an
absolute pandoc`, also for a `[convert] pandoc_path` that hangs or exits non-zero (rehearsal probe 60), where
pandoc_path already was an absolute pandoc, and a configured pandoc that ran out of time got the bundled one's
first-start sentence. `uv sync` syncs the project in the folder it runs in, never the uv tool environment install.sh
made, and install.sh sets `UV_NO_MODIFY_PATH`, so uv is often not on PATH. Re-running install.sh does not help
either: step 2 skips its reinstall when the stamp names this commit (`install_is_current`). Measured 2026-10-18 with
uv 0.12 on a tool environment of its own: `uv tool upgrade --reinstall-package <dep> <tool>` puts a deleted file of
the dependency back with the environment kept, and `uv tool install --force` makes a new environment. So the
bundled pandoc's fix is `reinstall pypandoc_binary in agentsync's tool environment: <uv> tool upgrade
--reinstall-package pypandoc_binary agentsync, or set [convert] pandoc_path to an absolute pandoc`, `<uv>` found as
install.sh's `find_uv` finds it (`doctor._uv_word`: on PATH, else `~/.local/bin/uv`); a configured pandoc's is
`check or replace the pandoc at [convert] pandoc_path ('<path>'), or remove that line to use the bundled pandoc or
its native arm64 copy`, its time-out line has no first-start sentence, and only a path that is not absolute keeps
`set [convert] pandoc_path to an absolute pandoc`. The python check's `uv python install 3.11 && uv sync` reads `run
scripts/install.sh again (it installs agentsync with uv's Python 3.11)`: a Python older than 3.11 is an environment
install.sh did not make, so its stamp does not match and step 2 reinstalls. Tests:
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_configured_pandoc_that_fails_names_that_pandoc_and_not_the_bundled_one` (exit 3, a

by three failures, and missing), `test_ops_doctor.py::test_the_uv_a_fix_names_is_the_one_install_sh_finds`,

has three outcomes: 0 green, 1 red (the id), 2 not read (a reason). gh's own exit status tells an error from an
answer; `gh run watch --exit-status` fails on red and on a network error alike, so the state is read with `gh run
view --json status,conclusion`, three tries; `success`, `skipped` and `neutral` are green, `failure`, `timed_out`
and `startup_failure` red, `cancelled` keeps the superseded-run rule (its own gh and fetch failures are not read),
a run not yet completed is watched again, and any other conclusion is not read. Every wait is bounded:
`SHIP_LAND_RUN_POLLS` (24) polls and re-watches, `SHIP_LAND_RUN_SLEEP` (5 s) apart, two minutes for runs to appear;
the two are for tests. Not read is exit 9: before the push `could not read trunk CI (<reason>); nothing pushed;
retry, or pass --no-ci to land without it` (`--allow-red-trunk` does not cover it, since not read is not red), after
it `LANDED <sha>, CI NOT READ: <reason>; read it back with the gh run watch loop in CLAUDE.md`. ci.yml runs on every
push to main, so no run for a pushed sha is never a green. Tests: `test_ship_land.py::
test_a_gh_that_answers_nothing_is_ci_not_read_and_pushes_nothing`,
`test_ship_land.py::test_a_run_whose_watch_and_view_fail_is_not_read_not_red`,
`test_ship_land.py::test_a_watch_that_breaks_off_reads_the_runs_state`,
`test_ship_land.py::test_a_pushed_sha_with_no_run_says_landed_and_ci_not_read`, and
`test_ship_land.py::test_a_red_trunk_stops_the_push_unless_allowed` (still 6, and 8 with `--allow-red-trunk`).

### 16.124 Round 16: setup prompt v25 and the config a sync refuses (2026-10-18, wave B13 round 16 lane P)

The B13 round 16 items of lane P (specs `round16/items/T<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built unless a
measurement below says otherwise): T1, T6, T10, T29, T30, T45, T67, T70, T72, T81. T1, T10, T29, T45, T67 and T81
are one defect from six finders (config_failed's "does not load" for a config that loads), built once; T6 and T30
are one (step 1 and a mirrored folder whose block is gone), built once. T6, T30, T70 and T72 need prompt text, so
the prompt is **setup prompt v25**: `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, `PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's `prompt v25` and
`setup-prompt-compat 25`, the issue form's placeholder and the block's digest move together, and a saved v24 copy is
stopped at step 1 like every older copy. v25 moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry. None adds an
agentsync command, an installer flag, a config key or a friction kind. Lanes that sent words: lane B (the person's
fixes, its T5 cluster, T2 and T9, folded into T70's sentence) and lane E (the bundled pandoc's fix is now an
install.sh re-run, its T54, T59, T60, T65: the re-run clause of T70's sentence, once).

**A config that loads but init or add-source refuses is no config that does not load** (T1, T10, T29, T45, T67,
T81; amends §16.93 M23). init and add-source also exit 78 on a config `load_config` reads: a policy.toml beside it
or a `[governance]` value that is not valid (`cli._ensure_setup` runs `governance.load_governance` and the policy
after `_ensure_inbox`, and add-source after it appended the folder's block). `config_failed` keyed on the exit code
alone and said `the config <CONFIG> does not load with this agentsync`, so the prompt's step 2 skipped the inbox the
config holds, and the report said `- loads: yes, but a sync refuses it`. It now asks the agentsync step 2 installed,
after the call, whether the config loads (`synced_count`, a number only when `load_config` reads it, within its
10 s bound): when it does, the NEXT is `the config <CONFIG> loads, but agentsync refuses it (the configuration error
above; ~/.local/bin/agentsync status prints it again): fixing it is the person's, not a step for the agent, so show
them the error and go on to the report; once it is fixed, the next run is: <install.sh and its arguments>`; when it
does not, or nothing can say (no installed interpreter, a dry run, the bound), the config that was there before keeps
the "does not load" NEXT. Never read off the error's words: a `[governance]` error names sources.toml, which loads
(T1's verifier). A config this run created that loads, with a bad policy.toml beside it, gets the "loads, but" NEXT
too (it had fail's generic "fix the error above", which let the agent edit the compliance-owned policy.toml); one
that does not load keeps the generic line. T29's verifier also proposed moving the governance check in front of
every write in cli.py, so a refused config is left unchanged; not built, as T67's verifier measured against it: the
inbox and the folder's block init and add-source wrote are valid blocks of a config that loads, the prompt's step 2
tells the person about that inbox and the finish lists that folder as added, both true once the NEXT stops saying
"does not load", and the re-run after the person's fix keeps them. No prompt words: v24's step 2 already keys the
inbox skip on "says the config does not load" and the finish on the report's "loads: yes, but". Tests:
`test_a_config_that_does_not_load_is_the_persons_to_fix` (an installed agentsync that loads the config, and one that
does not), `test_a_config_that_loads_but_agentsync_refuses_is_no_config_that_does_not_load` (the real agentsync:
policy.toml, `[governance] history_days`, `[governance] archive` through add-source, and a new config beside a bad
policy.toml), `test_a_first_sync_refusal_is_no_config_that_does_not_load`.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.130 U20: the "loads, but" NEXT reads `loads, but agentsync refuses a value in it or in
policy.toml beside it (the configuration error above names the file; ...)`.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.130 U40: a refused add-source that printed `added source` says the folder was added, and

**Step 1 names a mirrored folder whose [[source]] block is gone** (T6, T30). Step 1's list read the config alone,
so a folder whose block was deleted while its pages stay mirrored was listed unmarked and the NEXT said `(none is
needed)`, though step 2's status FAILs on it (`config.vanished_sources`, §16.119 S7) and every sync refuses the

--source-local "<folder>") or its [[source]] block is put back, as it was or retired` (N folders: "on each", "one

in the list above adds back is still mirrored but has no [[source]] block in <CONFIG>. Step 2's status fails on it

`test_the_vanished_source_reader_imports_no_agentsync_name_an_older_build_lacks`,
`test_a_mirrored_folder_whose_block_is_gone_is_named_in_step_1_and_added_back_in_step_2` (the real agentsync: step 2
with no folder stops on the [FAIL], and with the named one exits 0 with sources.toml byte for byte as before).
v25's step 1, after the folder question's wait and before its two exceptions, so the tail on either list reaches it:

**Step 2 names every kind of fix that is the person's** (T70, with lane B's words for its T5 cluster, T2 and T9;

### 16.125 Round 16: the person's fixes, the CLI's counts and WARNING lines (2026-10-18, wave B13 round 16 lane B)

**T12: a manifest that is no database fails status and stops setup on one line (`agentsync.ops.doctor`,
`agentsync.cli`, `scripts/install.sh`).** With manifest.sqlite overwritten by bytes that are no database, status
and doctor exited 0 with every check `[ok]` and `NEXT: cannot read the state: DatabaseError: ...`, and init,
add-source and sync ended on a traceback (exit 1), which install.sh turned into `fix the error above, then re-run`,
a re-run that fails the same way. Doctor's `state_dir.manifest` check opens the manifest read-only
(`doctor.manifest_unreadable`, `file:...?mode=ro`, reading `sqlite_master` as every open does, since a header can
be intact over a damaged schema page) and fails only on SQLITE_NOTADB (26) or SQLITE_CORRUPT (11)
(`doctor.MANIFEST_UNREADABLE_CODES`), extended codes included (`doctor.unreadable_code`); a locked, busy or unopenable manifest, an empty file and a healthy one print
nothing, and status scans no table (damage there shows when a command reads it). Its fix,
`doctor.MANIFEST_FIX`, is the person's (`the person decides, with a copy of it kept: restore it from a copy they
trust, or move it aside so the next sync starts a new one, which converts every file again ... and forgets the
deletions, holds and archive it recorded`), never a command for the agent. When the loop's state cannot be read
and a check failed, status's NEXT is rule 1's from the first fix (`cli._next_or_fix`), never `cannot read the
state`. `cli._state_readable` turns a NOTADB or CORRUPT error in init, add-source and sync (the manifest is the one
database they open) into
`state: <path> cannot be read: <error> (fix: <MANIFEST_FIX>)` (`cli.StateUnreadableError`) and exit 65 (EX_DATAERR, `cli.EXIT_STATE`, in the
help's exit codes); any other database error prints one `error:` line (the traceback at `-v`) and exits 1 as before.
install.sh's `config_failed` gives exit 65 the person's NEXT, `agentsync's state file cannot be read (the error
above, with its fix; ...): fixing it is the person's, not a step for the agent, so show them the error and go on to
the report; once it is fixed, the next run is: <install.sh command>`, whether or not this run wrote the config; any
other exit keeps fail's line. setup-report still writes its report over such a manifest (measured). Tests:
`test_cli.py::test_a_manifest_that_is_no_database_fails_status_and_stops_setup_on_one_line`,
`test_cli.py::test_a_manifest_a_sync_holds_is_no_fail`,
`test_install_oneshot.py::test_a_state_file_that_cannot_be_read_is_the_persons_to_fix`.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.131 U64, U95, U66, U72, U73: status classifies a NOTADB or CORRUPT error from its own read of
the loop's state as the `state_dir.manifest` FAIL, so damage under a table that read touches fails status; any
command's NOTADB or CORRUPT error exits 65 on the one line; only a locked or busy database is one `error:` line,
any other sqlite3 error keeps its traceback; MANIFEST_FIX ends `the deletion breaker's suspended removals and the
archive it recorded; legal holds are kept, in governance/holds.json`.

### 16.126 Round 16: the pandoc fix and wait, the CI flakes, converter counts (2026-10-18, wave B13 round 16 lane E)

Round 16's lane E items: doctor's pandoc time-out reason (T17, T77), the bundled pandoc's fix (T54, T59, T60, T65),
install.sh's traps and watchdogs, the causes of the Q40 pandoc and `--list-folders` CI flakes (T41, T79, T80), the
converters' last fixed plurals (T61) and the cache caveat about them (T62), the dead-function scan (T64) and the gate
journal (T90), landed after the other five lanes since every lane's gate loads that journal.

**Doctor's pandoc time-out gives the installer's reason (T17, T77; `agentsync.ops.doctor`; dated lines at §16.32 and
§16.117 S17).** The bundled pandoc's time-out line said `(the first start of a newly installed pandoc can take a
minute, and later ones take under a second)` on runs that installed nothing, the case §16.117 S17 measured at 110 s
on a busy Mac; S17 changed only install.sh's ticker. `_PANDOC_SLOW_START` is now the ticker's words, `a new copy's
first start can take a minute, and any start can on a busy Mac`, still for the bundled pandoc only. Tests:
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_pandoc_that_does_not_answer_in_time_names_the_rerun_and_is_no_crash`,
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_the_pandoc_slow_start_reason_is_the_installers_wait_line` (reads install.sh's line).
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.132 U104: not for the bundled pandoc only any more: a native or configured pandoc that
does not answer gives `(any start can take a minute on a busy Mac)`, the busy-Mac half; the first-start half is
Rosetta's and stays the bundled one's.

**The bundled pandoc's fix is install.sh's reinstall (T54, T59, T60, T65; `agentsync.ops.doctor`,
`scripts/install.sh`; dated lines at §16.32 and §16.120 S29).** The fix was `<uv> tool upgrade --reinstall-package
pypandoc_binary agentsync`. Measured with uv 0.12.17 in throwaway homes: it took none of the sync locks install.sh
holds around a reinstall, ran without the `UV_SYSTEM_CERTS=1` install.sh exports for networks that inspect TLS (uv
keeps no such setting in the receipt, and the command always reaches the index), rebuilt agentsync from the checkout
as it stood, and moved every dependency, the named one included, to its newest allowed version. Re-running install.sh
did not help, because step 2 skipped whenever the stamp named this commit. Now:
- `install_is_current` is `stamp_is_current` (the old test) and `bundled_pandoc_intact` of the tool environment:
  every file pypandoc_binary's RECORD lists under `pypandoc/` with a hash (the pandoc binary and the Python whose
  import doctor's `not importable` line reports) is there with RECORD's size and sha256 (urlsafe base64, unpadded;
  `openssl dgst`, about 0.1 s for the 119 MB binary), and the pandoc is executable. Nothing is run: a fresh copy's first start can take a minute, and step
  1's word on what step 2 will do reads the same test. A stamp that is current over a pandoc that is not whole
  prints `agentsync: the bundled pandoc in <tool dir> is missing or not the file pypandoc_binary installed;
  reinstalling`.
- A run stopped during the reinstall removes the constraints file in `on_exit`.
- Every reinstall passes the checkout's uv.lock versions as constraints when uv can export them (`uv export --project
  <checkout> --locked --no-hashes --no-emit-project --no-default-groups --quiet -o <tmp>`, then `uv tool install ... -c
  <tmp>`; uv keeps them in the receipt). Without them `uv tool install --force` resolves afresh, the same drift as
  the upgrade (this Mac's tool environment held charset-normalizer 3.5.2 and cryptography 50.0.2 against the lock's
  3.5.1 and 50.0.1). A checkout with no uv.lock, a wheel, a dry run, or a uv that cannot export installs as before.
- Doctor's bundled fix is `run scripts/install.sh again (it reinstalls agentsync when the bundled pandoc is missing or
  not the file pypandoc_binary installed), or set [convert] pandoc_path to an absolute pandoc`, the agent's step, as
  `_PYTHON_FIX` is; `_uv_word` has no caller left and is gone.
  Amended 2026-10-19, §16.132 U13, U30, U47, U78: the fix names the installer by its checkout path and ends `; if
  this line comes back after that, show the person this line: setting [convert] pandoc_path to an absolute pandoc
  is theirs`, so the re-run is the agent's and the edit the person's by the fix's own first words; under
  install.sh, a time-out that comes back names that person's line, not the same re-run again.
Not built: T65's `uv pip install --python <tool python> --reinstall --no-deps pypandoc_binary==<version>`, which
holds no sync lock (T54's verifier: the person's at best), and T60's `AGENTSYNC_FORCE_REINSTALL=1`, a new setting
the RECORD test makes unneeded. Tests: `test_install_oneshot.py::test_a_rerun_reinstalls_a_bundled_pandoc_that_is_not_the_one_pip_installed`
(whole, missing, changed, not executable, no RECORD, its Python changed),
`test_install_oneshot.py::test_the_reinstall_keeps_uv_locks_versions`,
`test_install_oneshot.py::test_step_1_says_whether_step_2_reinstalls_before_a_config_it_cannot_load` (a changed
pandoc), `test_ops_doctor.py::test_the_bundled_pandocs_fix_is_install_shs_reinstall_and_no_bare_uv` (and the guide's
quote).

**A lost or late TERM drops no line and holds no wait (T41, T79, T80; `scripts/install.sh`).** Under `set -e` the
pandoc ticker's trap `kill "$s" 2>/dev/null; exit $((said ? 3 : 0))` exited 1 when its sleep was already reaped, so
`pandoc: started after Ns` was not printed (the Q40 CI flake, ci 39132985876 attempt 1; 2 of 70 runs under load).
And `with_timeout`'s watchdog and the pandoc limit slept their whole limit in one sleep: bash 3.2 holds a TERM that
lands just before `wait` until the sleep ends, and drops one that lands in the child before its trap is set, so the
caller waited out the limit with nothing printed (21 of 16000 calls at a 5 s limit under load; the likely cause of
the `--list-folders` time-out in ci 39105995103). Every such trap reads `kill "$s" 2>/dev/null || :`, and each loop
clears `s` once its sleep is reaped, so a trap never kills a pid the system reused. One `watchdog LIMIT PID` serves
both limits: LIMIT 1 s slices, counted (a deadline on the whole-second `$SECONDS` could kill up to a second early),
while PID runs, ending once PID has. The pandoc ticker loops while pandoc runs and exits with
the status that says whether it printed. Not built: a 1 s cap on `with_progress`'s ticker sleep (optional; it already
ends with its command, and the cap would add a fork a second for every wait). Tests:
`test_install_oneshot.py::test_a_ticker_trap_whose_kill_fails_still_says_whether_it_printed` (each trap as written,
under set -euo pipefail), `test_install_oneshot.py::test_a_watchdog_whose_term_is_lost_ends_with_its_command`,
`test_install_oneshot.py::test_a_pandoc_ticker_whose_term_is_lost_ends_with_pandoc` (the callers' kills dropped),
`test_install_oneshot.py::test_the_wait_for_pandoc_forks_a_few_sleeps_not_five_a_second` (slices counted).

**Rows, columns and windows count at one (T61; `agentsync.convert`; dated lines at §16.39 N36 and §16.120 S52).**
S52 left fixed plurals in the same converters: a one-cell workbook's sheet page read `1 rows x 1 columns` beside its
index's `1 sheet`, a one-row CSV `1 data rows x 1 columns`, a recording under five minutes `1 windows` and `1
five-minute windows`. Rows, columns, non-empty and data rows, windows, screen states, keyframes, on-screen lines,
speech lines and voices take `plural` (xlsx, text and recording_page, the row-cap notes included), and a sheet's
`[no cached values: 1 of 1 formula cell carries ...]` its noun and verb from its counts; the recording
grammar's title rule takes `window` exactly at 1, and docs/design/meeting-video-spec.md says so. No emitter version
moved (Q39's rule). Not built: the carry-over NOTE's `N on-screen lines of sNNN left the screen`, whose wording is in
the index's fixed-wording digest: changing it raises `_INDEX_REVISION`, and a copy of every recording already read
is then read again in full for a count's noun (round 11 M64, M85; measured: the digest test fails). Tests:
`test_convert_formats.py::test_a_table_and_a_sheet_count_their_rows_and_columns_at_one`,
`test_convert_recording.py::test_a_recording_under_five_minutes_counts_one_window_as_one`.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.139 V69 (by §16.132 U76): the screen-limit NOTE's `N later changes not read (limit)` is the
second fixed plural kept for the same digest reason.

**A cached summary keeps its (s) for its bytes, not its page (T62; docs; dated lines at §16.24, §16.26, §16.54 Q77,
§16.111 Q39 and §16.120 S52).** The caveat "a page converted before keeps its `(s)` until it is converted again" was
wrong twice: `cache.action_key` holds no path, so a new page with the same bytes (a copy, a second synced folder, a
restored file before a reconcile's GC) gets the old summary from the cache, and converting the old page again changes
nothing while its key stays. Each site has a dated line with the right rule; no code changes, since an emitter bump
would read every cached file again, OCR and speech included. Test: the dated-line pins.

**The dead-function scan reads code (T64; tests; dated line at §16.120 S46).** The scan counted every textual match
of a private name across src, so a comment, a docstring, `self._x` or another module's same-named function hid a
dead one (67 private names are defined in more than one module). It now resolves each module-level private function
by (module, name): its name in its own module outside its own body, a from-import of it (relative ones resolved), or
an attribute of a name bound to its module, lazy imports included. Tests:
`test_contracts.py::test_no_private_function_in_src_is_left_for_the_tests_alone`,
`test_contracts.py::test_the_dead_function_scan_reads_code_not_text`.

**The gate journal keeps what a failure said (T90; `tests/_gate_journal.py`).** Round 15's pre-gate flake was an
xdist worker crash (`when: "???"`), and the journal kept only outcomes while the gate's output was overwritten. A
failed phase's record now keeps the last 20 lines of its report (`tail`) and the last 2000 characters of its
captured stderr (`stderr`), and
the controller appends `{"node_down": "gwN", "error": ...}` from xdist's `pytest_testnodedown` (an optional hook): a
crashed test's own report says only `worker 'gwN' crashed while running ...`, so the tail alone would not have
diagnosed it. Neither changes what a resume reads (`_last`). Not built: teeing the lane-mode pytest output to a file
(optional; scripts/gate.sh is every lane's). Tests: `test_gate_journal.py::test_the_journal_keeps_a_failures_text_and_a_lost_workers_error`
(a real worker crash), `test_gate_journal.py::test_the_journal_loads_without_xdist`.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.132 U106: the tee is built: a lane part that fails or is killed keeps its whole output, stderr
too, in `<tree>-<salt>.<part>.out` beside its journal (appended on a resume, removed when the part is green); being
every lane's file was a landing order, so it landed after the other five lanes.

**An earlier attempt that only listed the folders stopped** (U35). An attempt with an `Attempt:` line and nothing

Amended 2026-10-19, §16.134 V48: the label (`sync` or `first sync`) comes from the config note of the run whose sync the line shows, not the last run's, whose failed config step logs no note.

reaches. Test: `test_a_part_the_report_could_not_read_says_why_in_words_not_a_class_name`.
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.140 W64: a state file this account cannot open (sqlite's CANTOPEN, PERM or READONLY, or `errors.ManifestOpenError`) reads `the state file cannot be opened by this account: see Doctor's state_dir lines`; `state_dir.manifest` is named only for a file that is no database or a damaged one.

**The first report keeps its Doctor section: pandoc starts once, in Doctor** (U48; amends §16.114 Q60). All four
reports of a session's first act said `- pandoc: ... exited 124: timed out after 5.0s`, `Doctor: _This section
failed: TimeoutError: did not finish within 1.9s_` and `doctor: not run (see Doctor)`: the Environment section,
first in order, started pandoc with 5 s, and a slow start on a busy Mac (the wheel's Intel binary under Rosetta)
took those 5 s from the doctor's share of the 12 s budget, while the doctor's own pandoc check started it again.
With a doctor hook the Environment line is filled from that check after Doctor runs (its detail; a FAIL's or warn's
with its `(fix: ...)` left on Doctor's line and `(doctor's pandoc check: [FAIL]; its fix is in Doctor)`), or

resolver's pandoc as before, and a start past its limit reads `did not answer within 5.0s (a new copy's first
start can take a minute, and any start can on a busy Mac)`, doctor's `_PANDOC_SLOW_START`, never `exited 124`. A
doctor the time limit cuts off reads `- doctor: cut off by the report's time limit after N s (see Doctor)` and
still names install.sh's own doctor's warns and FAILs from install.out, which do not depend on this run's. Tests:
`test_the_reports_pandoc_line_is_the_doctors_check_and_never_starves_doctor`,
`test_a_doctor_the_time_limit_cuts_off_is_said_so_and_a_slow_pandoc_is_no_exit_code`,
`test_the_pandoc_line_is_the_pandoc_the_converters_run`.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.134 V3, V49, V4, V81: the cut-off seconds are the wait the doctor call was given, the one float Doctor's own line names (`did not finish within N s`), not what was left after the cut; the doctor gets at least `_DOCTOR_GRACE_S` (20 s), and one still cut off says so in Doctor and in the Summary with the advice to write the report again when the Mac is idle; with no doctor hook a start past its limit gives `_PANDOC_SLOW_START` for the bundled pandoc only and `_PANDOC_BUSY_START` for a native or configured one, as §16.132 U104 does.

**The bash 3.2 comment lint reads a braced substitution** (U108). `substitution_comment_apostrophes` opened a block
only at a line ending `$(` or `<(`, so a comment inside `done < <({ ... }` or `"$({ ... })"` (four such blocks in
the scripts, none with a comment today) went unread, though /bin/bash 3.2 passes `-n` on its apostrophe and then
fails at run time, dropping the block's input. Each open block keeps the closer it waits for: `)` for `$(`/`<(`, `}`
for `$({`/`<({`. The finder's close rule (a line starting `)` or a `}...)` line) was not built: the redaction
block's `}` line goes on in a pipe, so its `)` comes a line later, and that rule held the block open to the end of
install.sh (124 false hits). A comment between such a `}` line and its `)` is still not read; none exists. Test:
`test_deploy_pack.py::test_the_substitution_lint_finds_the_round_3_shape`.

**--report-only closes only the attempt the report reads as latest** (U33). `friction_close_attempt` closed the last
`Attempt:` with no end line, while `parse_friction` reads a step 1 error stating `prompt vN, <agent>:` after a header
as another session's header-less attempt (a git or Xcode stop before `--log-start`, while this session waits on its
folder answer): the end line went to the stopped session, its duration ran to the report's own end line, and the
report's note said `--report-only had no attempt to close`. The check now runs `FRICTION_AWK`'s `track()`, which
splits as the parser does, and closes nothing when the latest attempt is such a header-less one; an `Attempt:` line
alone (G51) and a stated line with no `<agent>:` open none, so their attempt is still closed once. `--log-end` reads
the same rule. Test: `test_report_only_closes_only_the_attempt_the_report_reads_as_latest`.

replaced (a bare number after "stop" read as a name), and its outcome rule kept v10's `ran (step 1)` before `; it
stopped:`; the test pinned both as the current words, so its round trip proved nothing. The bucket reads `from the

builds `S1_ITEM` as `_sign_in_stop_item` does (`- install.sh · step 1 · the folder list stopped: <clause> (not

**v10's friction and checkout words take the current ones** (U27; dated line at §16.123 T11). In both modes, outside
`<details>` and fences: the friction header's `run setup-report again` reads ``run `~/src/agent-context-sync/
scripts/install.sh --report-only` again`` (`REPORT_INSTALL_SH`, `setup_report.INSTALL_SH`); an attempt line's bits

### 16.132 Round 17: the pandoc fix's owner, converter counts and the gate (2026-10-19, wave B13 round 17 lane E)

Round 17's lane E items: whose step the bundled pandoc's [FAIL] is (U13, U47, U79, U80), the installer's path in
doctor's fixes (U30), a pandoc time-out's fallback (U78) and reason (U104), a converter missing at sync time (U3),
the converters' counts (U74, U75, U76), T62's cache caveat (U77), the CI flakes (U101, not built) and the gate's
lane-mode log (U106, landed after the other five lanes).

**A pandoc fix's first words say whose it is (U13, U47, U79, U80; `agentsync.ops.doctor`, `agentsync.cli`,
`scripts/install.sh`; dated lines at §16.106 O11 and §16.126 T54).** v25's step 2 made a [FAIL] whose fix "edits
sources.toml (... a [convert] line ...)" the person's, and the bundled pandoc's fix ended `, or set [convert]
pandoc_path to an absolute pandoc`, while status and install.sh handed the line to the agent (`PERSONS_FIX_RE` reads
the start of a fix). Its fix now reads `run ~/src/agent-context-sync/scripts/install.sh again (it reinstalls
agentsync when the bundled pandoc is missing or not the file pypandoc_binary installed); if this line comes back
after that, show the person this line: setting [convert] pandoc_path to an absolute pandoc is theirs`: the re-run
first, the agent's, then the edit, the person's, kept as their one lead when a re-run cannot restore the bundled
copy (U13's verifier). U47's fix with no [convert] text at all is not built: a missing file has no time-out
fallback to carry the edit, so the person would lose it. A configured pandoc_path's fix (`check or replace the
pandoc at [convert] pandoc_path ...`) and a not-absolute one's (`set [convert] pandoc_path to an absolute pandoc`)
are a [convert] edit only, which a re-run does not touch, so `PERSONS_FIX_RE` and install.sh's `persons_fails` read
both as the person's (alternatives `set \[convert\] pandoc_path ` and `check or replace the pandoc at \[convert\]
pandoc_path `), and `PERSONS_FAILS` and `PERSONS_KINDS` name `a [convert] pandoc_path`. A configured pandoc that
times out keeps the agent's re-run first. Lane P's v26 (§16.130) words step 2 to match: "A [FAIL] line whose fix
starts with an edit to sources.toml ... Otherwise, re-running the install.sh command its fix names is yours, once,
even when the fix goes on to name a [convert] edit for me (the bundled pandoc's), which stays mine". Tests:
`test_install_oneshot.py::test_doctors_persons_fix_words_are_install_shs` (every pandoc line's owner, through
`_pandoc_fail_lines`), `test_cli.py::test_status_names_the_pandoc_fix_that_is_the_persons_as_theirs` (configured,
not absolute, bundled), `test_ops_doctor.py::test_the_bundled_pandocs_fix_is_install_shs_reinstall_and_no_bare_uv`.

**Doctor's fixes name the installer by its path (U30, U47; `agentsync.ops.doctor`, `agentsync.cycle`,
`agentsync.ops.launchd`).** `scripts/install.sh` in a fix is a path inside a checkout the prompt never runs from: it
runs `~/src/agent-context-sync/scripts/install.sh` under `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, and its allow rule names that
path. Doctor's python, bundled pandoc, OCR, media, speech, launcher and Developer ID texts, the time-out's install.sh
re-run, the cycle's OCR and media alarms and launchd's launcher error now build it from `skill.INSTALL_SH`, and the
launcher's build script as `~/src/agent-context-sync/launcher/build.sh`. Tests: the pinned strings in
`test_ops_doctor.py`.
Amended 2026-10-19, §16.138 V68: the speech texts this listed were doctor's own; the three it relays from
`agentsync.convert` (the speech floor refusal and the two build sites' signal texts) named a bare
`scripts/install.sh`, and now build it from `skill.INSTALL_SH` too.

**A time-out under install.sh does not name the same re-run twice (U78; `agentsync.ops.doctor`).** `_again_fix`
gives `run the same <installer> command again ...; if this line comes back: <fallback>`, and the bundled pandoc's
fallback was its re-run: install.sh's step 2 has already found the bundled file whole (`install_is_current`) or
reinstalled it, so a second re-run repeated the first. Under install.sh (`AGENTSYNC_NO_NEXT_HINT=1`) the fallback is
`show the person this line: setting [convert] pandoc_path to an absolute pandoc is theirs (the bundled pandoc does
not answer on this Mac, and install.sh found its file whole)`; by hand it stays the re-run, which checks and repairs
the file. Not `_STILL_NO_ANSWER`, whose "no setup step clears that" setting pandoc_path contradicts. Tests:
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_pandoc_that_does_not_answer_in_time_names_the_rerun_and_is_no_crash`,
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_program_that_never_answers_is_told_what_to_do_when_the_line_comes_back`.
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.151 X68 (by §16.143 W19, W48): under install.sh `_again_fix` starts `run <install.sh> again
with the options of the run that installed agentsync (not --report-only, which builds nothing)`
(`doctor.AGAIN_UNDER_INSTALL_SH`), not `run the same <installer> command again ...`; the fallback above is unchanged.

**A native or configured pandoc's time-out gives the busy Mac's reason (U104; `agentsync.ops.doctor`; dated line
at §16.126 T17, T77).** It gave none, and round 16 left T77's optional part unrecorded. `_PANDOC_BUSY_START` is `any
start can take a minute on a busy Mac`; `_PANDOC_SLOW_START`, with Rosetta's first start, stays the bundled
pandoc's, so round 15 S29's guard (no "first start" on a configured line) holds. Tests:
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_native_pandoc_that_fails_names_that_copy_and_not_rosetta`,
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_configured_pandoc_that_fails_names_that_pandoc_and_not_the_bundled_one`.

**A failed conversion is tried again (U3; `agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.manifest`, `agentsync.convert`,
`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.setup_report`; dated line at §16.28).** Probe PD: a .docx added while pandoc could not
start got a `conversion failed: converter unavailable` stub and QUARANTINE row; once install.sh had restored pandoc
every sync settled it as unchanged, since the early cutoff of `_after_fetch` finds the same canonical hash behind
an intact stub, whatever "retried next cycle" said. Now:
- The cutoff converts a failed conversion's stub again (`_retries`) in up to `_CONVERT_RETRIES` = 2 later cycles
  per file and bytes (the source's `convert-retry:` meta), so a pandoc that timed out under load converts it and a
  converter that always fails on a file stops being run on it; new bytes count from zero, and a file that converts
  leaves the record.
- One whose converter could not start is not counted. While it still cannot (`_runs`), its row stays ERROR with its
  stub, QUARANTINE row and error line, and it is not fetched (`_converter_waits`, before any download); the first
  cycle in which the converter starts converts it.
- A stub an older build settled is read again by the re-read pass once its converter starts: `produced_by` and the
  re-read query include a `failed` stub of version `unavailable`, and `_reread_targets` and `_lacks` call it
  outdated while `_runs`. While it cannot start, the source's re-read record stays open (`_reread_waits`), so a
  later cycle with the same build and capabilities still looks.
  Amended 2026-10-19, §16.138 V65: the stub of an ordinary failed conversion that an older build settled gets the
  same bounded retries once, after the upgrade (`Manifest.retry_settled_failures`); a local online-only one
  waits for new bytes.
- A foreground sync whose cycle reported such an error, while the pandoc check fails, has rule 1's NEXT `the pandoc
  check failed (a file's converter could not start in this sync, so it is not converted yet): run
  ~/.local/bin/agentsync status, whose [FAIL] pandoc line names the fix` (`cli._unavailable_steps`). The convert
  logger's `converter ... unavailable` WARNING and the cycle's `cannot run` one carry `ECHOED_WHEN = "error"`: a
  foreground run holds them back while its error line says it, and a LaunchAgent's err.log keeps them.
- The report's Repeat conversions note and setup-feedback.md say a failed conversion is tried again, in up to 2
  later runs or once its converter starts.
- `agentsync.convert` exports `CONVERSION_FAILED` and `CONVERTER_UNAVAILABLE`, how a failed conversion's reason
  starts, which `agentsync.cycle` and `agentsync.cli` import; every other new name is private.
§16.28's "Whether a failed conversion should be tried again is older behavior and a separate decision" is that
decision. Tests: `test_cycle.py::test_a_conversion_that_failed_is_tried_again_a_bounded_number_of_times`,
`test_cycle.py::test_a_file_whose_converter_could_not_start_is_converted_once_it_starts`,
`test_cycle.py::test_a_stub_settled_before_the_retry_is_read_again_once_its_converter_starts`,
`test_cycle.py::test_a_foreground_sync_whose_converter_could_not_start_names_the_pandoc_check`, and
`test_setup_report.py`'s Repeat conversions note.

**The converters' counts (U74, U75, U76; `agentsync.convert.xlsx`, `agentsync.convert.recording_page`).** xlsx's
no-cached-values note said `those cells show` for one cell; it follows the uncached count now (`that cell shows`),
full and streamed. The workbook index said `(1 rarer terms omitted)`; it is `plural(dropped, 'rarer term')`. No
emitter version moves (Q39's rule, as T61). The recording's screen-limit NOTE keeps `N later changes` for the index
digest, as the carry-over NOTE keeps `N on-screen lines`; the spec and the code comment name both now, and no
wording moved, so neither the digest nor `_INDEX_REVISION` did. Tests:
`test_convert_formats.py::test_xlsx_uncached_note_and_term_index_take_their_noun_from_the_count`,
`test_convert_recording.py::test_every_note_that_keeps_a_fixed_plural_is_named_where_the_spec_says_why`.

**A copy's old wording waits for its key to move (U77; dated lines at §16.24, §16.26 (four), §16.54, §16.111 and
§16.120).** T62's lines said a cached summary lasts until its action key moves "or a reconcile's cache GC drops
it". `ConverterCache.gc` keeps every key `live_action_keys()` names, so beside its live original, or in a second
synced folder, a copy keeps the old wording until the key moves; only a restored file whose page was removed meets
the GC, and a purge or a label escalation deletes the entry too. Not built: U77's optional clause in T61's §16.126
paragraph, since that paragraph takes dated lines only and its pointer to Q39 already reaches T62's line there.
Test: `test_deploy_pack.py::test_round_11s_and_12s_lines_at_unlettered_paragraphs_are_there`
(`_ROUND_17_PARAGRAPH_AMENDS`).

**The CI flakes are not seen again (U101; not built).** Neither the Q40 pandoc line nor the `--list-folders` time-out
has failed attempt 1 of a `ci` run on main since a49acdba: 39224535079 (a49acdba), 39231001978 (3274f9a2) and
39290708602 (e5c5b0e2), each `4926 passed, 3 skipped` with neither test skip-gated. Three runs prove nothing fixed:
keep reading attempt 1, and reopen against 29876f26 if either comes back.

**A lane part that fails keeps its whole output (U106; `scripts/gate.sh`, `tests/_gate_journal.py`; landed after
the other five lanes).** Round 16 left T90's tee unbuilt because `scripts/gate.sh` is every lane's file, which is a
landing order, not a harm. In the lane modes pytest's output went only to the caller's terminal, and the journal
keeps a failure's last 20 lines cut to 2000 characters, so a crash or a long traceback was lost with the terminal.
`run_part` now runs a lane part as `step env PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 ... uv run --locked pytest ... 2>&1 | tee -a
<tree>-<salt>.<part>.out` beside its journal (pipefail keeps pytest's status): a fresh run empties the file, a
resume appends `== resumed by <pid>` after the killed run's text, and a green part removes it. Journals are never
removed, so nothing else is tied to them. Test:
`test_gate_journal.py::test_a_lane_part_that_fails_keeps_its_whole_output_beside_its_journal` (gate.sh's own
`run_part`, over a stand-in `uv`: failed, resumed, green).

### 16.133 Round 17: deploy docs and CONTRACTS cross-references (2026-10-19, wave B13 round 17 lane D)

Docs and dated lines that lagged round 16's code (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 17"; specs
`round17/items/U<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built). Lane D's round 17 items: U39, U82, U83, U84, U85, U90,
U91, U109 and U112. Every edit is outside the prompt block and no item needs prompt words, so none went to lane P. A
dated line this round writes reads `Amended 2026-10-19, §16.133 U<n>`, with `(by §16.NN T<n>)` when it records
round 16's change.

**The guide's `not repeated:` paragraph leads with the held form and routes a line with no hash** (U39, U82; dated
line at §16.127 T28). Since §16.123 T16 `local-work/.sent` is read first, and every report that embeds a patch adds
it there, so after any earlier report the line reads `not repeated: a patch file an earlier attempt's report held
(<time>)`; the guide gave the last-written time as the line's form and the held one only for an attempt that wrote
no end line, so a triager reading the usual line would think that attempt had stopped at step 1. The paragraph names
the held form first and the last-written form for a patch `.sent` lacks. Since T24 two of the four lines say `this
account cannot read it now, so no line count or hash`, and the guide's one route (send the patch whose hash starts
with the line's 12 digits) had nothing to match: such a line's patch is made readable and the report run again,
which sends nothing new and gives the hash. The T28 test read only the two hashed lines (`skipped="${skipped}...`)
and counted 2; it reads all four now. Lane RB's U60 names the same no-hash sentence; it is built once, here. Tests:
`test_the_guide_asks_for_a_not_repeated_patch_by_its_hash`, `test_prompt_routes_changes_to_the_source_not_the_checkout`
and the dated-line scan.

§16.125 T32 (295650c0) cli.py prints `tightened N paths ...: they hold tenant data` (`1 path ...: it holds` for
one). §16.29's "Who calls it." paragraph still quoted the `(s)` form with no dated line, and §16.127's T51 paragraph
said cli.py still prints it. Each gets a dated line; the landed sentences stay as the record. §16.29's
`N path(s) could not be made owner-only` is a log line (`cycle.py`) and keeps `(s)`. Tests:
`test_contracts_quote_the_tightened_line_as_cli_prints_it`, which finds every `(s)` quote of the line and its dated
line, the dated-line scan, and the §16.29 pin in `_ROUND_17_PARAGRAPH_AMENDS`.

**Exit 65 has its meaning in each exit-code list** (U84; dated line at §16.14). Since §16.125 T12 `cli._run`
wraps a cycle in `_state_readable`, so a sync, and a LaunchAgent's job, which the launcher passes through, ends on
65 when the manifest is no database or a damaged one. The CLI's `--help` named it; the deploy guide's "Exit codes
the jobs report", `setup_report.EXIT_MEANINGS` and install.sh's `rc_meaning` did not, so the report printed a bare
`65` and install.sh `exit 65`. Each names it now: the two maps' `the state file (manifest.sqlite) cannot be read:
the person's to fix` landed first with lane RB's U55, U65 (3bfef31c; it promises no `state_dir.manifest` line, which

prints the file and the fix again. Test: `test_every_exit_code_a_job_reports_has_its_meaning_everywhere`, which

...`.
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.143 W41: status's own probe now reads each table's first row, so damage under the cursors
table has the `state_dir.manifest` FAIL too.

**The guides say a git remote's host is redacted and kept** (U85). Since §16.123 T88 both readers redact the host of
a git remote's URL as a `<proxy-N>`, and `--log-start` and `--log` write it to `setup/proxy-hosts`
(`record_proxy_hosts` reads `git_remote_hosts`), but that commit changed no file under docs/: the deploy guide's

the rule's cases to `setup_report._remote_url_host`.

**A build with a damaged bundled pandoc is reinstalled, and the README and the guide say so** (U90). Since §16.126
T54 install.sh's `install_is_current` is `stamp_is_current` and `bundled_pandoc_intact`, and step 1's

**T76's test reads its dated line up to the next one** (U109). `test_contracts_quote_the_counted_unread_patch_lines`
read §16.127 T76's line in §16.116 S26's paragraph with a greedy `.*`, so it ran to the paragraph's end and passed

**CLAUDE.md gives `ci`'s measured time and its limit** (U112). CLAUDE.md said `ci` takes about 6 minutes, the

**The doctor's cut-off seconds are the limit it had, and a slow doctor gets a grace** (V3, V49, V4, V81; amends
§16.128 U48). The Summary's `cut off by the report's time limit after N s` was `min(limit, remaining)` read after
the cut, about 3.0 s whatever the budget (the Loop floor and the reserve), while Doctor's section named the call's
limit (`did not finish within 5.2s`). `_Run.call` records the wait it gave (`last_call_limit`), and both lines
format that one float; a doctor the budget never started reads `- doctor: not started: the report's time budget
was used up (see Doctor)`. On a busy Mac the setup's last report lost its Doctor section and the pandoc line (the
doctor's pandoc start alone can outlast what is left of `TIME_BUDGET_S`, 12 s): the doctor now gets at least
`_DOCTOR_GRACE_S` (20 s), the deadline moving by the difference so the Loop line and the late listing after it keep
their share, which makes the report at most about 35 s, inside install.sh's 120 s bound on it; `took` adds `, N s
more for a slow doctor`. A doctor still cut off has its own section, `Cut off: the doctor call did not finish within
N s, the report's time limit; write the report again when this Mac is idle (...) before sending it.`, and the
Summary's line ends with the same advice. V81: with no doctor hook the Environment's own pandoc start gave the
bundled copy's first-start reason for every kind; `_slow_start(kind)` gives `_PANDOC_SLOW_START` for the wheel's
copy only and `_PANDOC_BUSY_START` for a native or configured one, as doctor does. Tests:
`test_the_summarys_doctor_cut_off_seconds_are_the_limit_the_doctor_section_names`,
`test_a_slow_doctor_gets_a_bounded_grace_and_a_cut_off_one_asks_for_the_report_again`,
`test_the_reports_own_pandoc_time_out_gives_the_first_start_reason_for_the_bundled_copy_only`,
`test_a_doctor_the_time_limit_cuts_off_is_said_so_and_a_slow_pandoc_is_no_exit_code`.
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.140 W4: a doctor cut off past the grace reads `did not finish within N s, the wait the report gives a slow doctor (it moves its B s time limit for one; see Run metadata)`, and the Summary `cut off after N s, the wait the report gives a slow doctor`; `the report's time limit` names only a doctor that kept its own share.

- `state-table`, when `manifest_unreadable` reads the schema but a read-only `SELECT 1 FROM "<table>" LIMIT 1` of a
  table fails with an error `unreadable_code` accepts (SQLITE_CORRUPT or SQLITE_NOTADB). `manifest_unreadable` itself,
  which init's exit 65 and status share, is unchanged (V21's verifier). Init reads only the schema, so this passes the
  config step: the clause is its own, `; step 2 stops on agentsync's state file, part of which cannot be read (at its
  status or its first sync): fixing that is the person's, and the step that stops prints the error`. It catches a
  damaged first page of a table; damage deeper in a table still shows only at a read of it.
The log line adds `config_err=remote` or `config_err=state-table`; no host is in the NEXT or install.log. v27's step 1
reads a stop at step 2's config step, status or first sync alike (below). Test:
`test_list_folders_says_step_2_stops_on_a_config_it_refuses` (GR, TD, and a remote `[governance]` allows, which ends
`(none is needed)`).
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.142 W1, W10: `state-table` reads each table `NOT INDEXED` and each index `INDEXED BY`; a plain
`SELECT 1` from a table is answered from its smallest covering index, so the real schema's items page was not read.
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.151 X59 (by §16.143 W41): `manifest_unreadable` is no longer unchanged: it reads each
table's first row (`SELECT * FROM "<t>" NOT INDEXED LIMIT 1`), and `cli._state_readable` runs it before init,
add-source and sync, so init no longer passes the config step on a table page it cannot read. With an installed
build that has the probe, damage on a table's root or first-row page is `state`, and step 2 stops at its config
step (`agentsync's state file, which cannot be read`); `state-table` then names damage the probe does not read
(an index's root or first page) or a table's damage under an older installed build without the probe.

**An add-source that wrote the block says so on any exit, after its block** (V47, V26; amends §16.130 U40). U40's
branch read only exit 78, so an add-source that wrote the folder's block and then exited 1 on a docs-repo remote
`[governance]` does not allow (`_ensure_setup`'s `_refuse_remotes`, after the write) said `error: agentsync add-source
<folder> failed`, logged `step=config rc=1 result=failed` with no note, and the report dropped the add. The mark (the
call printed `added source `, which comes only after a validated write) now decides on any nonzero exit, and the code
only words the cause: exit 78, `but agentsync refuses the config (the configuration error just above)`; exit 1 with
`docs_remotes_refused` above 0, `but the docs repo has a git remote [governance] does not allow (the governance: line
above)`; any other, `but agentsync add-source failed after adding it (see the error above)`; each keeps `; the N
folder(s) after it were not added`. The log line is `step=config rc=<the code> result=failed
note=added-then-refused[ kept=K added=N]`; the report keys on the note. config_failed's NEXT, chosen by the code, is
unchanged. V26: install.sh's stdout and stderr go through two tees, and awk's piped stdout is held in a buffer until it
exits, so the call's `configuration error:` line reached the terminal before its `added source` block. The call's
stderr now goes to a file, printed once the pipeline ends, on success too (a `governance:` line), before the held lines
and the error; add-source writes only short lines to stderr and no ticker, so nothing a person watches is delayed. The
re-run still names every folder: an added one reads `already configured`, and naming only `$BASE_ARGS` would drop the
folders after the refused one (V26's verifier). Tests:
`test_a_docs_repo_remote_governance_does_not_allow_is_the_persons_to_settle` (add-source: the block stays, the log
line, the cause, no `add-source ... failed`), `test_a_folder_added_before_agentsync_refuses_the_config_is_no_failed_add`
(the new error words; in one stream, the block, then the configuration error, then the error line).
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.142 W39: a signal inside the call no longer loses the held stderr: on_exit prints it and
removes the file and the mark.

### 16.138 Round 18: the convert-retry record, converters and the gate (2026-10-19, wave B13 round 18 lane E)

Round 18's lane E items (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 18"; specs `round18/items/V<n>.md`, the
verifier's corrected fix built): U3's convert-retry record while a converter cannot start (V13, V57, V61, V64), an
older build's settled stub (V65), entries for deleted files (V63), the texts that still said a failed conversion is
never retried (V62, V67, V74), the installer's path in the texts `agentsync.convert` relays (V68), U74's pronoun pin
(V66) and the land gate's scanners (V93, landed after the other five lanes). No item needs prompt words. A dated
line this round writes reads `Amended 2026-10-19, §16.138 V<n>`, with `(by §16.132 U3)` where it records round
17's change.

**A file whose converter could not start is no conversion (V13; `agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.model`,
`agentsync.cli`).** Probe PD's sync printed `converted 1, ... (of the converted: 0 unreadable, 1 failed, 0
refused)` beside its NEXT's "so it is not converted yet", and the sync in which pandoc came back counted the same
file in `converted` again. A result whose converter version is `unavailable` now counts in
`SourceReport.converter_waiting` and the run record's `converter_waiting`, never in `converted`,
`conversion_failed` or `converted_failed`; its error line, stub and QUARANTINE row are as they were. The sync's
last line adds `; W waiting for its converter (it could not start; read once it does)` after the re-screen clause,
nothing at 0, with no bare "converted", "deferred" or "read again", so install.sh's awk and regex and setup_report's
`_CONVERTED_LINE_RE` still read `converted N, deferred M online-only`. Test:
`test_cycle.py::test_a_foreground_sync_whose_converter_could_not_start_names_the_pandoc_check` (the count line,
the record, and `converted 1` once in the sync after).
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.144 W2: a stub still waiting for its converter counts too, in every sync in which the
converter still cannot start, not only the one that first tried.

**A re-read that waits for its converter is no "sync again" (V57; `agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.loop`,
`agentsync.model`, `agentsync.cli`).** While a stub's converter could not start, `_reread_targets` left it out and
kept the source's record open, so the run had no `reread_left` and `loop._reread_notes` took its "not left" branch:
`sync again: ...` after every sync, which no sync cleared. `_reread_source` now counts those files
(`Manifest.reread_count` over the targets `_reread_targets` set aside) into the run record's `reread_waits`, kept
out of `reread_left`, and `_reread_notes` gives a run that read none and has `reread_waits` the `_REREAD_STUCK`
words ("... a converter or on-device OCR that cannot run ...: another sync does not clear it"), whether or not its
OCR time ran out. `CycleReport.converter_down` is True when a converter's version could not be read for a file in
the run, and `cli._unavailable_steps` gives rule 1's pandoc-check NEXT on it as on a `converter unavailable` error
line, so a stub an older build settled, which has no error line, points at the pandoc check too. Test:
`test_cycle.py::test_a_re_read_that_waits_for_its_converter_is_no_sync_again`.

**An unavailable stub's first read is a first read (V61; `agentsync.cycle`).** On the re-read path the stub of a
conversion whose converter could not start was "the same bytes, converted once more" (`again`), so the sync whose
pandoc came back read `converted 0, ..., read again 1` for a page no converter had read before, where the work
queue counts the same event as converted. `_unavailable_stub` (a quarantined row whose reason starts
`CONVERTER_UNAVAILABLE`) is now never `again` and is kept like a `no converter` stub: its first conversion is in N
and in R as a first read, and a read that fails keeps the stub. Since V65 moves an older build's stubs to the work
queue, this path is the one for a stub settled after the flag was written. Test:
`test_cycle.py::test_a_stub_whose_converter_could_not_start_is_a_first_read_on_the_re_read_path`.

**A converter that answers late is no OCR failure (V64; `agentsync.cycle`).** `_PandocRunner.version` keeps only a
success, so `convert_file`'s call can time out on a busy Mac and the cycle's next one answer: `_lacks` then called
the `unavailable` result one to read again, and `_tally_ocr` counted `ocr_failed` (or `ocr_without_budget` /
`ocr_without_down`) for an engine that never ran. `_tally_ocr` now returns, after its two cap-mark counts, for a
result of version `unavailable`; `_lacks` is unchanged, since the re-read's success test and its reopen need it.
Test: `test_cycle.py::test_a_converter_that_answers_after_failing_to_start_counts_no_ocr_failure`.

**The retry record forgets a file that is gone (V63; `agentsync.cycle`).** An entry of `convert-retry:<source>`
left only on a conversion that worked or on new bytes, so a file given up and then deleted upstream kept its entry
for good. `_retry_load`, which every source's run now calls once after its pass, keeps only the entries whose row
exists, is quarantined and has a reason starting `CONVERSION_FAILED` (the test `_retries` and `_retried` use) and
stores the record when it dropped one; a purge or `forget_item` is covered, their rows being gone. Not by LIVE
rows: every entry is a quarantined stub's, so that would drop the count it bounds and convert the file in every
cycle. Not built: the same prune for the re-read record's `failed` ids, which a new build or capability already
replaces with a record of its own. Test: `test_cycle.py::test_the_retry_record_drops_a_file_that_is_gone_and_keeps_a_stub`.
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.144 W75: built, keyed on the row's state: the re-read record drops the ids of tombstoned
or missing rows.

**An older build's settled failure is tried again once (V65; `agentsync.manifest`, `agentsync.cycle`; dated line
at §16.132 U3).** A build before U3 settled an ordinary failed conversion's stub as unchanged after one cycle (a
pandoc time-out under load), and the retry, reached only from the work queue's early cutoff, never saw it again,
while §16.132, the report's Repeat conversions note and setup-feedback.md say a failed conversion is tried again.
`Manifest.retry_settled_failures(reason_prefix, *, retried_meta, done_key) -> int` gives, once per manifest
(meta `convert-retry-legacy:done`, `_RETRY_LEGACY_META`, written in the same transaction), the ERROR verdict to
every quarantined file (not a folder) whose reason starts `CONVERSION_FAILED` and whose verdict is not ERROR, but
for one its source's `convert-retry:` record holds (a build with the retry tried it) and a local online-only one
(`dataless`), which waits for new bytes. A Graph file has no `dataless` flag: it is fetched again within the
run's download budget, as the retry fetches a failure of this build. The cycle runs it after the stub re-render, before any source's pass; the classifier carries each row as
pending and the early cutoff gives it the counted retries, or the uncounted wait-or-convert path for a `converter
unavailable` one. Each costs at most `_CONVERT_RETRIES` conversions, the cost every new failure has. Tests:
`test_cycle.py::test_a_failed_conversion_an_older_build_settled_gets_the_bounded_retries_once` (converter fixed:
live, one conversion, no QUARANTINE.tsv line; still failing: tried exactly `_CONVERT_RETRIES` times, then
settled).

**The texts that said a failed conversion is never retried (V62, V67, V74; `agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.convert`;
dated lines at §16.28, §16.48 R86).** `_run_tally`'s docstring, `convert_file`'s ("would be settled and never read
again", now "tried again in only `cycle._CONVERT_RETRIES` later runs and then settled, whether or not the engine
works by then") and two test comments are reworded; §16.28's `converted_failed` row and its Tests paragraph, and
§16.48 R86, carry dated lines. R86's says what V74's verifier measured, corrected by V65: a drawing that failed
on a build before U3 is converted again in the first syncs after the upgrade. Not added: a second pointer after
§16.28's not-retried bullet, which already carries U3's dated line. The `converted_unreadable` texts stay: an
UNREADABLE result does wait for new bytes.

**The installer by its path in the texts `agentsync.convert` relays (V68; `agentsync.convert.speech`,
`agentsync.convert.ocr`; dated lines at §16.35, §16.42, §16.48, §16.132 U30).** Doctor's speech check named the
installer two ways: `~/src/agent-context-sync/scripts/install.sh builds it` for no helper, `scripts/install.sh
rebuilds it` for the floor refusal. `speech._FLOOR_REFUSAL` and the two build sites' signal texts (`speech._step`,
`ocr`'s swiftc) now build it from `skill.INSTALL_SH` (skill imports only `agentsync.paths`, so no cycle). The
signal texts reach doctor through the `<helper>.failed` marker, which `ocr._failure` reads through `ocr._plain`,
which takes every path out: built alone, the fix would have read `...; <path>` with the rest of the line gone
(measured by `test_ocr.py::test_a_helper_or_compiler_killed_by_a_signal_says_so`). `_plain` now keeps that one
path, which names no one, and takes out every other. "or later" stays in the floor refusal: it states the floor
(spec C3), which `FLUIDAUDIO_PIN` equals today. Tests: `test_speech.py::test_a_build_step_killed_by_a_signal_says_so_and_is_tried_again`,
`test_ocr.py::test_a_helper_or_compiler_killed_by_a_signal_says_so` and `test_voice_naming.py`'s floor refusal,
each against `skill.INSTALL_SH`.
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.144 W67: "or later" is gone from the refusal, which names the pinned commit, since
probe's check is the exact pin, not the floor.

**U74's pronoun is pinned where the two counts disagree (V66; tests only).** Taking the pronoun from the formula
count passed every test, since the pins were 1 of 1, 2 of 2 and 4 of 4. 1 of 4 (D2, D3 and B4 cached, C4 not) is
the case where they differ; the full and the streamed call site are pinned on it. No code moved. Test:
`test_convert_formats.py::test_xlsx_one_uncached_cell_of_four_takes_the_pronoun_of_one`.

**The land gate runs its scanners first, and a killed gate is no green verdict (V93; `scripts/gate.sh`; landed
after the other five lanes).** All three red land gates of round 17 failed in `tests/test_contracts.py`, which ran
in the last part, after about 25 minutes of the rest, so each held the shared land lock 25 to 33 minutes.
`full_set` now runs a first part `scan` (`tests/test_contracts.py` and `tests/test_lints.py`, about 4 s together)
before `deploy_pack` and `rest`; the land gate's `set -e` stops at a red part, so a red scanner ends it in seconds.
`test_governance.py` (about a minute alone) stays in `rest`. `union_check` collects four sets: the ids of scan,
deploy_pack and rest must union to the full set's and their counts add up to its count, so no test runs twice or
not at all. CLAUDE.md's gate paragraph says so. And `gate.sh` traps HUP, INT and TERM to exit 129, 130 and 143:
under /bin/bash 3.2 a gate a SIGTERM ended while a pipeline ran entered its EXIT trap with `$?` 0, so
`gate-verdicts.log` recorded a killed run as `rc=0` (lane B's round 17 pre-gate of a73574af: rc=0 over a journal
with no summary line and a failed test). Not built: ship-land refusing a HEAD with no green `--affected` verdict,
which trusted that log. Tests: `test_gate_journal.py::test_a_gate_a_signal_ends_logs_a_failed_verdict`,
`test_gate_journal.py::test_the_scanners_run_first_and_every_test_runs_in_one_part` (gate.sh's own functions, over
a stand-in `uv`).

**A manifest this account cannot open fails a Doctor line, and the report points at it** (W64; amends §16.128 U21).
With manifest.sqlite at mode 0000 (or another account's, after a sudo sync) status exited 0 with `[ok]
state_dir.files — manifest.sqlite are 0600` and no state_dir.manifest line, since that check judges only sqlite's
NOTADB and CORRUPT, while the report said `the state file cannot be read: see Doctor's state_dir.manifest line`.

`chmod 600 <files>`; the loose-mode FAIL and its fix stay; and the ok line says `are 0600` only of mode 0600 (else

by name so the report works before it lands) `the state file cannot be opened by this account: see Doctor's

NEXT was the plain review line: nothing in the relayed line asked for it. install.sh reads the written report for
that phrase (`LC_ALL=C grep -qF`, so an older installed agentsync without it adds nothing) and puts an advisory

it off (its Summary says which): if this Mac was busy, run ~/src/agent-context-sync/scripts/install.sh
--report-only again once it is idle; either way, <the NEXT as before>`. The finder's `run --report-only again ...
before reviewing` was not built: a doctor that is always slow (a hung pandoc, which the probe simulated) would hold
the bring-back or loop an agent. The setup prompt's finish step still matches (it names bring-back.md, and keys
the patch remedy on `does not hold a kept patch`, which the NEXT still says), and it is still one NEXT line. Test:
`test_a_report_the_time_limit_cut_off_says_so_in_its_next_line_beside_the_review` (tests/test_install_oneshot.py,
with the stub's report, as the unreadable-patch NEXT tests).

**The shell report reads the re-add folder in the words the writer uses** (W34, W40, W56, W63: one defect from four

`$` and a backquote escaped (`cycle._shown_arg`), `shlex.quote`d for a name holding `!` or a character that does
not print. The parser read only ` add-source ` with a single-quoted or bare word, so the folder printed in clear
(and the bare branch registered a `"/…/Contoso` fragment). `redaction_pairs`' awk now reads each ` add-source ` and
` --source-local `, whichever comes first, and a double-quoted word up to its first unescaped `"` with the escapes
undone; the single-quoted branch stays for `shlex.quote` and older logs, the bare one for older logs.
`folder_value` also registers a value as those two quotings print it (escaped, or with each `'` as `'"'"'`) at the
same `<folder-N>`, where the Python report cuts the argument by structure (`_source_local_shown`). Test:
`test_the_shell_report_redacts_a_project_folder_and_a_vanished_sources_folder`, its lines built by

**The shell's install source line says a URL rewrite as the agentsync report does** (W7, W23: one defect from two

**The helpers note says "not ready", which a built helper that fails its probe is** (W38; amends §16.135 V6).
`ocr._entry` exits 1 when the probe after a good build answers `failed`, so install.sh notes `not-built-<names>`

**The shell's `<value>` cut keeps the words after a [governance] value** (W69; amends §16.135 V44). `gov_value_sed`
cut a type error's value to the first ` (fix: ` or the line's end, so a second refusal joined with `; ` and a
friction line's ` | ` fix column were lost where the Python report keeps them (V45's repr shape). The finder's fix,
Python's two-level shape as one alternation, makes things worse as written: BSD sed rejects a substitute pattern
over about 2048 bytes (measured: 2049 works, 2069 fails), the shape is about 3800, and the whole `sed -E -f` program
then prints nothing, which empties the report downstream; ERE's leftmost-longest alternation would also always take
the wide branch. Built instead: each value's start is marked (`\003`), then `_repr_shape(1)` (a quote-aware string,
a number, True, False, None, or one `[...]`, `{...}` or `(...)` of those, about 590 bytes a rule) is tried at the
line's end and before each delimiter in turn (a blank, a tab, `;`, `,`, `)`, `|`, the ` (fix: ` sentinel, and `.`
last, so `1.5;` is not cut at `1.`), the delimiter put back; a value still marked takes the old wide cut. A value
nested two levels or more (`[['x']]`) is the one divergence left: the shell cuts it to the line's end, more than
Python, never less. Tests: `test_a_policy_or_governance_value_is_redacted_alike_in_both_readers` (`; `, ` | `, a
string holding both, a number before `;`, a dict, and a two-level list),
`test_the_shell_governance_value_program_stays_under_bsd_seds_limit` (every rule under 2000 bytes; 9000 blanks
inside brackets cut at once).

**The git stop's one timestamp counts the attempt the renderer splits off** (W74; amends §16.135 V30).

step 2 line before its end line therefore kept the older build's session span beside an attempt that is the error
alone, and a step 1 line moved before a bare `Attempt:` line claimed one timestamp where the renderer has two lines.
The awk now resets its count at those splits and carries the moved run, as the verifier's prototype, and a gap
split restates the attempt as every other reader does (the lane's review: without it a stated error after an
unstated one read as another session's). A random differential against `parse_friction`, 4,500 logs, finds no

(a step 2 line before the end line: one timestamp; a step 1 line after it, and one moved before a bare `Attempt:`
line: the span kept).

**The older build's git-stop report names install.log's earlier first sync** (W21; amends §16.135 V16). V16's

(rehearsal D's oldr and oldr2 states, and none in install.log).

**The older build's report after a finished attempt says why its attempt holds both sessions** (W24; amends §16.135

**The older build's line-number line names F ids only when the Summary cites one** (W15). The v10 renderer always

**The older build's macOS line gives the version and build** (W16). A renderer from before c6c6a73b (round 12 N26)

**The older build's cut git-error item is rebuilt as the renderer cuts it** (W25). Round 18 V34 gave the renderer's
Items error line 320 characters, the command cut to 80, so git's reason stays; the v10 renderer cut it at 220 with

**A census test runs where gitleaks is missing, on a Mac that has it** (W78). Round 18's census passed here only
