### 16.142 Round 19: setup prompt v28 and step 1's damaged-table check (2026-10-20, wave B13 round 19 lane P)

The B13 round 19 items of lane P (specs `round19/items/W<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built unless a
measurement below says otherwise): W1, W8, W10, W12, W26, W28, W39. W1 and W10 are one defect, built once; W8 and W12
are one, built once (W12's words, which name the file by its path).

**Step 1's damaged-table check reads every table and every index** (W1, W10; amends §16.136 V21). `config_errors`
ran `SELECT 1 FROM "<table>" LIMIT 1` for each table. `SELECT 1` needs no column, so SQLite answers it from the
table's smallest covering index (`SCAN items USING COVERING INDEX items_by_canonical`) and never reads the table's own
b-tree: on agentsync's real schema a damaged items root page, which step 2's status stops on, read clean, and step 1's
NEXT ended `(none is needed)` (probe TD; round 18's test used a two-column items table with no index). It also read
no index but the one the planner picked, so a damaged `items_by_path` root was missed too. The reader now walks every
b-tree in `sqlite_master` (`rootpage > 0`): a table by `SELECT 1 FROM "<t>" NOT INDEXED LIMIT 1`, an index by `SELECT
1 FROM "<t>" INDEXED BY "<i>" LIMIT 1`, read only, names quoted with `""` doubling, under the same 5 s bound; an error
`unreadable_code` accepts (11 or 26) is `state-table` and ends the walk, any other (an older SQLite refusing `INDEXED
BY`) skips that b-tree. Not `PRAGMA quick_check(1)` (W1's verifier): it walks the whole file inside the 5 s bound,
whose timeout would drop the reader's other words with it, and flags damage no command reads (the freelist), which
predicts a stop that never comes. Not `NOT INDEXED` alone (W10's verifier): it drops the index damage the covering
read catches today. Standard library only, so an older installed build runs it too. Test:
`test_list_folders_says_step_2_stops_on_a_config_it_refuses` (`TD-items`, `TD-path`, which fail without it,
`TD-canonical`, which a `NOT INDEXED`-only reader fails, and `clean-real`, the same schema undamaged: `(none is
needed)`).
Amended 2026-10-20, §16.151 X59 (by §16.143 W41): `TD-items` no longer reaches this reader: the installed
`manifest_unreadable` reads the items table's first row and answers `state` first (as for `TD`). The cases that
fail without the W1/W10 reader are `TD-items-older` (an installed build without that probe) and `TD-path`;
`TD-canonical` is still the case a `NOT INDEXED`-only reader fails.

**Step 2's unreadable-patch line says where the patch goes, not that it is sent** (W8, W12; amends §16.136 V25).
Step 2's `WAITING ON YOU: 1 patch file in ~/agent-context/setup/local-work cannot be read by this account; make it
readable (chmod u+r), and the setup report at the end of this setup sends it` contradicted the report's own NEXT,
`(nothing is sent for you)`, and its send lines' `Nothing is sent automatically.`: the report only puts the patch in
bring-back.md, which the person copies back. The line now ends `... puts it in ~/agent-context/bring-back.md for you
to copy back` (`N patch files ... them`). The path is the one `write_bring_back` writes (`$out`, beside
`REPORT_PATH`), shortened to `~` as the local-work folder is, never a literal (W12's verifier:
`AGENTSYNC_SETUP_REPORT` moves it); still no file name. Section 3's `not sent:` label inside bring-back.md is left
as it is, where "sent" reads as "carried in this file". Test:
`test_step_2_says_a_patch_this_account_cannot_read_is_the_persons` (one patch at the default path, and two under a
report path of their own).

**A signal inside add-source keeps its held error** (W39; amends §16.136 V26). V26 holds add-source's stderr in
`ERRF` and prints it once the pipeline ends. Bash runs a trap only when the foreground pipeline ends, and
`on_signal` exits at once, so a run a signal ended inside the call (a coding tool's time-out sends SIGTERM) never
reached the `cat`: its `configuration error:` line was in none of stderr, install.out or the report (which reads
install.out for it), and the file, holding the error, stayed in TMPDIR beside the empty `MARK` file. `on_exit` now
prints a held `ERRF` that is not empty to stderr, right after the `PARSED` check, so before `step_end`, the report
and `stop_capture`, and removes `ERRF` and `MARK` (`${ERRF:-}`, `${MARK:-}`: both are unset when no folder is
given, under `set -u`). The loop empties `ERRF` once it has printed it, so a signal later in the iteration (inside
`synced_count` or `docs_remotes_refused`) prints nothing twice. The line follows `on_signal`'s `error: install.sh was
stopped by a signal ...`. Test: `test_a_signal_inside_add_source_keeps_its_held_error` (SIGTERM to the installer's
pid, and to its whole group: the error once, after the signal's error, in install.out, and TMPDIR empty).

**Setup prompt v28** (W26, W28; amends §16.136 V33). W26 and W28 need prompt text, so the prompt is **setup prompt
v28**: `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, `PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's `prompt v28` and `setup-prompt-compat 28`, the issue form's
placeholder, setup-feedback.md's version lists and the block's digest move together, and a saved v27 copy is stopped
at step 1 like every older copy. v28 moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry; it adds no agentsync
command, installer flag, config key or friction kind. Lanes that sent words: none (lanes RA, RB, B, E and D).
- Step 1's other-git-failure quote (W26): the first way's condition was `if ~/src/agent-context-sync exists` and its
  reason `since that leaves no folder`. Step 1 clones whenever `.git/HEAD` and `.git` are both missing, so into a
  folder that already exists and is empty too, and a clone that fails there (exit 128) leaves the folder; the
  person's query, run in their own terminal with no `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, then reads any repository above it (a
  dotfiles repo in ~) and prints its remote, a host that misdirects them to the mirror remote the quote rules out
  (probes b2, b3). It now reads `this checkout's own remote, if ~/src/agent-context-sync/.git exists, which `git -C
  ~/src/agent-context-sync config --get remote.origin.url` prints and which this setup expects to be
  https://github.com/renchris/agent-context-sync.git, never the cause after a clone that failed, since that leaves
  no checkout`: a failed clone leaves no `.git`, so the person skips the query; on the pull path the checkout's own
  config wins over any repository above it; a `.git` file (a second worktree) counts as existing. The query keeps no
  `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=` prefix (the verifier's optional hardening): the condition already keeps it from running
  where it would misread, and the pinned query and the person's command list stay as they are.
- Step 1's first exception (W28): `If you cannot ask me then, add none and go on to step 2.` came right after the
  not-on-disk sentence, so "then" could bind it to that case, and a Mac whose kept folders are all on disk would fall
  back to the rule for a new Mac (a logged deviation, a stop). Rounds 14 to 19's roles all read it the right way, so
  this is the wording's risk, not an observed misread. In place, not moved (W28's verifier: before the not-on-disk
  sentence, an unattended agent could go on to step 2 without telling the person which folders are off disk), it
  reads `Whether or not that line names such a folder, if you cannot ask me whether to add one, add none and go on to
  step 2, and still tell me in your final message any folder that line says is not on disk and its fix.`; the
  sentence after it is unchanged.
Tests: `test_the_prompt_text_changes_only_with_its_version` (`PROMPT` 28), `test_readme_step1_is_one_command`
(`GIT_REMOTE_QUERY`'s quote), `test_readme_prompt_asks_a_mac_already_set_up_for_no_folder` (`KEPT_UNASKED`, which
starts `Whether or not that line names such a folder, `), and the version lists in `test_setup_report.py` and
`test_install_oneshot.py`; register `docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md` K52.

### 16.143 Round 19: table damage, the lock-wait words and the speech fix (2026-10-20, wave B13 round 19 lane B)

Round 19's lane B items (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 19"), each the verifier's corrected fix.

**W13, W30: a foreground skip is said once (`agentsync.cli`; amends §16.39 N24).** A sync typed in a terminal
that gave up on the lock printed `skipped: lock held by ...` and then the same as a timestamped `WARNING
agentsync.cli:` line, which ended the output and reaches no store from a terminal. The handler logs the WARNING
only when `launchd.started_by_our_job` says the run is the background job's (its stderr is the err.log the
report's Recent errors reads), as `_alarms_in_the_report` does; a config that does not load counts as the job, so
the WARNING is kept on the error path. Any other run logs it at DEBUG (`-vv` shows it); install.sh's quiet first
sync still drops it (§16.68 H31). W30's "log file only" has no file to map onto and its DEBUG-for-every-run would
have emptied Recent errors of background skips, so neither is built. One defect from two finders, built once.
Tests: `test_cli.py::test_a_foreground_skip_is_said_once_in_the_wait_lines_words`, and
`test_lock_held_warning_names_the_holder_and_repeats_verbatim` under the job's `XPC_SERVICE_NAME`.

**W14, W30: the skip names an empty body as the wait did (`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.cycle`; amends §16.68 H31
and §16.137 V40).** The wait read `the lock is held by install.sh while it reinstalls agentsync, ...` and the skip
that ended it `skipped: lock held by an unrecorded holder (install.sh while ...); waited 600s`. One constant,
`cycle.UNRECORDED_LOCK_HOLDER`, builds `UNRECORDED_LOCK_WAIT`, and `cli._skip_holder` puts it in the skip line
for an empty body: `skipped: lock held by install.sh while it reinstalls agentsync, a status or doctor check, or
a cycle starting; waited 600s`, keeping the `skipped: lock held` opening the setup prompt and README quote.
`EMPTY_BODY_HOLDER`, `who`, the WARNING and doctor are unchanged, so Recent errors merges old and new skips.
Test: the W13 test's `no body` case.

**W29: the wait line's holder has one bracket level (`agentsync.ops.lock`, `agentsync.errors`, `agentsync.cycle`;
amends §16.137 V40).** A recorded holder read `another sync is running (pid N (a sync not started by the
background job, its pass: poll) since T, last beat T (0s ago), stage 'acquired'); ...`. `lock._wait_words` words
the same body and sidecar as `a sync not started by the background job, pass poll, pid N, active 0s ago`: no inner
bracket, no stage, `since T` only when it is not the beat `active` already gives. It rides on
`LockHeldError.wait_words` (default: `holder`), and `cycle._wait_beat` reads it. `_describe_holder` and `holder`
are unchanged: doctor, the skip line and the report keep pid, beat and stage. Test: the W29 lines of
`test_cli.py::test_the_clis_lock_wait_says_plain_lines_and_marks_a_wait_install_sh_did_not_announce`.

**W46: the quiet wait's DEBUG beats keep their elapsed time (`agentsync.cycle`).** Since §16.137 V40 every quiet
beat was `...; waiting for it to end, at most 10 minutes`, so a `-vv` log of install.sh's first sync repeated one
line every 30 s. `_acquire_waiting` logs the plain beat, `(Ns of at most Ms)`, on every DEBUG record and keeps the
quiet words for the one line it says. Test: the W46 lines of
`test_cli.py::test_the_quiet_lock_wait_logs_once_and_leaves_the_skip_to_its_stderr_line`.

**W19, W48: a fix under install.sh names install.sh by what it is (`agentsync.ops.doctor`; amends §16.32 and
§16.137 V5).** A check that ran out of time, and the speech helper build that did, said under install.sh
(`AGENTSYNC_NO_NEXT_HINT=1`) `run the same <install.sh> command again as it is (its NEXT line names it)`. A
warn makes no NEXT line name install.sh (only a [FAIL], a failed agent step or a stopped run does), and
`--report-only`, which sets the same variable and writes this fix into the report, builds nothing. Both fixes
(the helper builds' one is `_helper_again_fix` since §16.144 W49, for OCR and media too) now start
`doctor.AGAIN_UNDER_INSTALL_SH`, `run <install.sh> again with the options of the run that installed agentsync (not
--report-only, which builds nothing)`; `--list-folders` runs no doctor, so it is not named. Run by hand nothing
changes. One defect from two finders, built once; W48's corrected fix (both fixes, one phrase) is built over
W19's (the speech fix alone, plain words in both modes), since the plain `run <install.sh> again` is as wrong
under `--report-only`. Tests: `RUN_AGAIN_INSTALL` in `test_ops_doctor.py` and the W19 lines of
`test_a_speech_build_that_ran_out_of_time_has_a_fix_and_no_other_failure_gets_one`.

**W47: the run line's docstring gives the converter-waiting count its own letter (`agentsync.cli`).** Round 18's
V13 named it W in `_print_report`'s docstring, whose next sentences use W for the withheld-unread count ("with R
and W the line's refusals add up to the sources'"): read as the converter-waiting count, a false sum, since those
files are never refused. It is C; no output changes. Test:
`test_cli.py::test_the_run_lines_docstring_gives_each_count_its_own_letter`.

**W66: a gitleaks this account cannot reach is no gitleaks (`agentsync.lints`).** `_executable` called
`Path.is_file`, which in Python 3.11 raises PermissionError (EACCES, EPERM) for a file in a folder this account
cannot search or a sandbox hides, where install.sh's `[ -x ]` answers no. A recorded or fixed gitleaks there broke
`recorded_gitleaks`, `gitleaks_lookup`, `secret_rules_identity` (called outside any try in the cycle) and
`lint_secrets`, so a sync failed rather than falling back to the builtin patterns. An `OSError` there now counts
as not executable: the lookup goes on to PATH, the next place or none, as for a missing gitleaks, and a changed
identity re-screens as designed. Test:
`test_lints.py::test_a_gitleaks_in_a_folder_this_account_cannot_search_is_none` (skipped as root).

**W11: a listing warn over a state file the loop cannot read points at no WAITING ON YOU line (`agentsync.cli`,
`agentsync.ops.doctor`).** With the manifest damaged, the report's Doctor listing warn read `(as of its last walk:
the Summary's Loop line says whether a WAITING ON YOU line still names it)` under install.sh, and by hand `(fix:
each WAITING ON YOU line about <source> says ...)`, while the Loop line held only the state_dir.manifest FAIL's
NEXT and the Summary filed the warn as not judged. `cli._listings_unread`, run by the report's Doctor hook and by
status, gives each incomplete-listing heartbeat warn (`heartbeat.<id>` whose detail starts
`doctor.LISTING_INCOMPLETE`) the note `doctor.LISTING_STATE_UNREADABLE_NOTE`, `as of its last walk: the loop
cannot read the state file, so no line here says what keeps it incomplete; the state_dir.manifest [FAIL] line
says what to do first`, and drops its fix, when the loop's read raised SQLITE_NOTADB or SQLITE_CORRUPT or the
read-only probe finds the file so, the Summary's own test (a locked or busy manifest is not). A note, so the
Summary's buckets, keyed on the detail and the report's read, are unchanged; a readable state changes nothing.
Test: both cases of
`test_cli.py::test_the_setup_reports_doctor_fails_a_manifest_damaged_under_a_table_as_status_does`.

**W65: a manifest this account cannot open is one line, exit 1 (`agentsync.manifest`, `agentsync.errors`,
`agentsync.cli`).** `sync` and `curate` on a manifest this account cannot open (a root-owned file one sudo run
left, mode 000, a folder it cannot write when the file is not there yet) ended on a raw PermissionError traceback
from `manifest._connect`'s `os.open`: §16.137 V59 covered only sqlite's errors. `_connect` wraps its mkdir, open
and chmod and raises `ManifestOpenError` (an `AgentSyncError` and an `OSError`, so a caller that caught the raw
error still does; `errno` kept), and `cli._main` prints `error: state: <db> cannot be opened: <strerror> (fix:
give this account read and write access to the file and its folder, e.g. owner and mode 600; the file itself is
not damaged)` (`cli.MANIFEST_OPEN_FIX`), the traceback at `-vv`, and exits 1. Not 65 and not `MANIFEST_FIX`: those
mean a damaged database, and moving an intact manifest aside throws its history away; V59 already gives a file
sqlite will not open exit 1. Handled where it happens, not with a broad `OSError` arm that would hide code
defects. Status's owner and mode FAIL is lane RA's W64 (§16.140), which this line's words were sent to. Test:
`test_cli.py::test_a_manifest_this_account_cannot_open_is_one_line_and_kept` (file and folder; skipped as root).

**W41: damage under any table fails status and stops the sync (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.ops.doctor`,
`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.setup_report`; amends §16.131 U64, §16.129 U55 and §16.133 U84).** Damage under the cache or outputs table left
status at exit 0 with no FAIL while the report's evidence lines said `see Doctor's state_dir.manifest line`, and
the sync failed the source (exit 1, a traceback, `BLOCKING CYCLE -: cycle failed`, `NEXT: ... run sync again`):
`_run_source`'s and `run()`'s `except Exception` turned SQLITE_CORRUPT into a source's or the cycle's failure, so
`cli._state_readable` never saw it. Measured by the test below on the pre-fix source: 11 of the 14 tables (all but
meta, items and runs, which status's loop read already reached) and both last-leaf cases failed, 13 of the 16
cases. Five parts:
(1) `cycle._manifest_unreadable` (`doctor.unreadable_code` on a `sqlite3.DatabaseError`) re-raises out of
`_run_source`'s isolation; (2) `run()`'s handler, for the same error, discards pending and writes the run's end
best effort (logged at debug), then re-raises with no stack, so the CLI says `state: <db> cannot be read: ...
(fix: <MANIFEST_FIX>)` and exits 65; (3) `doctor.manifest_unreadable` reads each table's first row, `SELECT * FROM
"<table>" NOT INDEXED LIMIT 1` (one page per table: an index answers `SELECT 1`, `rowid` and `count(*)` and misses
a damaged cache root), and `cli._state_readable` runs it before the command, so damage under a table a sync never
reads (tombstones, depends) stops the sync as it FAILs status; (4) damage deeper than a first row, which only the
read that reaches it sees: an exit 65 writes `manifest-unreadable.json` beside the manifest
(`doctor.record_unreadable`), keyed to its device, inode, size and mtime, and `state_dir.manifest` FAILs from it
(`... (a sync read it)`, read by `doctor.recorded_unreadable`) while the file is the same; one moved aside, restored or written since drops it; (5) the setup
report keeps its evidence read's SQLITE_NOTADB or SQLITE_CORRUPT (`_Mirror.unreadable`), and its Doctor section
adds `doctor.manifest_damaged`'s FAIL when doctor printed none (`_with_evidence_damage`), so its `see Doctor's
state_dir.manifest line` names a line that is there, and the Summary files it as the state file that cannot be
read. The report's Loop line still reads the loop as it is (a read the damage does not reach). Lane D's round 19
W62 (§16.145, landed first) reworded round 18's V73 dated lines at §16.129 and §16.133, which say damage under the
cursors table passes status; it now FAILs status, and each has W41's dated line. Test:
`test_cli.py::test_damage_under_any_table_fails_status_and_stops_the_sync` (every table's root, and the last leaf
of cache and outputs, with the report before and after the sync), and the probe line of
`test_a_manifest_damaged_under_a_table_status_reads_fails_status`.

### 16.144 Round 19: the converter-waiting count, converters and recording tests (2026-10-20, wave B13 round 19 lane E)

Round 19's lane E items (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 19"; specs `round19/items/W<n>.md`, the
verifier's corrected fix built). A dated line this round writes reads `Amended 2026-10-20, §16.144 W<n>`.

**A converter that still cannot start counts its file in every sync (W2, W32, W42; `agentsync.cycle`; dated lines
at §16.138 V13 and §16.28).** A second sync with pandoc still gone printed the
same `conversion failed: converter unavailable` error line and the same pandoc-check NEXT as the first, but its
last line dropped `; 1 waiting for its converter (...)` and its run record had no `converter_waiting`: only the
first sync's conversion counted the file, and every later one reached `_converter_waits`, which counted nothing.
`_converter_waits` now counts the file in `SourceReport.converter_waiting` and the run tally where it gives the
error line, once per file and cycle (`_waiting_ids`, which also keeps the error line single); the first sync's
count on the convert path is unchanged, its row not being a stub yet. Three finders, one defect, built once. The
report's half (the Repeat conversions note on these runs) is lane RA's W68. Test:
`test_cycle.py::test_a_foreground_sync_whose_converter_could_not_start_names_the_pandoc_check` (a second sync
with pandoc gone prints the clause and records `converter_waiting` 1).

**A waiting stub's error line says why now (W51; `agentsync.cycle`).** `_converter_waits` printed the stub's stored
reason, the one of the cycle that first failed, so a cause that changed while the converter still could not
start (an older build's wording, another missing `pandoc_path`) stayed hidden until it started. `_runs` now keeps
the exception `conv.version()` raised (`_cannot_run_why`), and the error line is `<rel>: CONVERTER_UNAVAILABLE:
<this cycle's reason>`, the prefix `cli._printed` and `_unavailable_steps` match; the stub page, `state_reason`
and QUARANTINE.tsv keep the stored reason, as rewriting them each waiting cycle is git and manifest churn, and
the row is rewritten once the converter starts. Test:
`test_cycle.py::test_a_waiting_stubs_error_line_names_why_its_converter_cannot_start_now`.

**The upgrade's retry of an older build's failures says so (W18; `agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.model`,
`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.setup_report`; dated line at §16.28).** V65's one-time move of failures an older build
had settled logged its count at INFO, which a foreground sync does not print, so a conversion error settled long
ago came back in two syncs with nothing saying why. The count is now `CycleReport.legacy_retried` and the run
record's `legacy_retried`; the sync prints, before its last line and only when it is above 0, `  note: N
conversion(s) an older build gave up on is/are tried again, up to 2 times from this sync on; its error / their
errors may show again until then` (the count from `_CONVERT_RETRIES`, no bare "converted" for install.sh's
awk), and the report's Repeat conversions part adds `- tried again after an upgrade: run R, N files. ...`, since
the move may happen in a LaunchAgent cycle nobody reads, or in install.sh's first sync, whose screen shows only
the summary lines (`show_first_sync`). The INFO line stays for err.log and `-v`; a WARNING was
not used, as its logger prefix reads as an alarm. Tests:
`test_cycle.py::test_the_upgrades_retry_of_an_older_builds_failure_says_so_once`,
`test_setup_report.py::test_repeat_conversions_names_the_upgrades_retry_of_an_older_builds_failures`.

**The run tally's docstring names the wait (W53; `agentsync.cycle`).** `_Cycle._run_tally` still said "a later run
with none converted the file or gave it up", the sentence V75 corrected in the run record bullet, the report and
the guide. It now adds "or, while its converter still cannot start, left it unread, a wait that run counts in
`converter_waiting`" (W2 counts it), and names `legacy_retried` (W18). Docstring only. Test:
`test_cycle.py::test_the_run_tallys_words_on_a_later_run_name_the_wait_its_converter_leaves`.

**The re-read record forgets a file that is gone (W75; `agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.setup_report`; amends §16.138
V63).** V63 left the re-read record's `failed` and `tried` ids unpruned, so a file deleted upstream kept its count
until a second change of capabilities (the second record carries the first one's ids through one change). A
deleted file keeps its row as a tombstone (`publish` sets `RowState.TOMBSTONE`; `reap` removes only the
`tombstones` table's rows), so a prune by "row is gone" would never fire for an ordinary deletion. `_reread_load`
now drops, on its one load a cycle, every id of either record whose row is missing (a purge, a rekey) or a
tombstone, and stores the record when it dropped one (`_save_reread`'s `forget` takes an iterable). A restored
file keeps its stable id and so is read again, up to `_REREAD_ATTEMPTS` more times. The report's re-read lead
says a deleted file's count lasts only until the next sync; `_ROW_NOW`'s `deleted` stays for that window and for a
record an older build left. Tests: `test_cycle.py::test_the_re_read_record_drops_the_ids_of_files_that_are_gone`,
`test_setup_report.py` (the re-read lead).

**A blank diagram is a page (W27; `agentsync.convert.diagram`; dated line at §16.42).** What draw.io saves for a
new file (one page whose root holds only its two default cells) and an `<mxfile>` with no pages were the
`empty-output` stub, "agentsync could not convert this source", and a quarantine row of class "empty", while every
other converter writes a page for a valid empty file (`[empty presentation: no slides]`, `[empty document]`,
`[empty sheet]`). `DiagramConverter.convert` drops the `has_text` gate: a diagram with pages but no text reads
`## <page>` and `[no text on this page]` per page, as pptx does for a slide of pictures, and one with no pages
(no `<diagram>`, or a Visio `pages.xml` that lists none) reads `[empty diagram: no pages]`. `_EMITTER_VERSION` is
1.3.0. An unchanged file is never converted again, so the stub an older emitter left would stay: the converter's
`outdated(produced, reason)` is True for an `empty-output` stub below `_PAGE_FOR_NO_TEXT` (1.3.0), and its
`outdated_key` (`1.3.0<1.3.0`) changes what the re-read pass looks for, so that pass makes the page once. Files
that are no diagram still fail first (a `ConversionError`). Tests:
`test_convert_formats.py::test_a_diagram_that_cannot_be_read_fails_bounded`,
`test_cycle.py::test_a_blank_diagram_is_a_page_and_no_quarantine_row`,
`test_cycle.py::test_a_blank_diagrams_stub_an_older_build_left_is_read_again_into_a_page`.

**A missing bundled pandoc's error names the re-run (W33; `agentsync.convert.pandoc`; amends §16.137 V41).** With
the wheel's pandoc missing, the sync's per-file error line named only `set [convert] pandoc_path`, the person's
edit, while doctor's [FAIL] pandoc line for the same state names the agent's install.sh re-run first and gives
the person the edit only if the line comes back. `resolved_pandoc` now raises `bundled pandoc not found; run
<INSTALL_SH> again (it reinstalls agentsync with its pandoc); looked at <~/path>`: the action before the path
still (V41), so the 200-character cut falls in the path. The configured path's error (`[convert] pandoc_path is
not an absolute file`) is unchanged: that one is the person's. A stub that carries the old words keeps them, and
W51's error line shows the current ones while pandoc still cannot start. Tests:
`test_cli.py::test_a_missing_bundled_pandocs_error_keeps_its_action_whatever_the_home_folders_length`,
`test_cli.py::test_a_missing_bundled_pandocs_reason_names_the_re_run_and_not_the_persons_edit`.

**A crash's long line no longer cuts the retry clause (W50; `agentsync.convert.ocr`, `agentsync.convert.speech`;
dated line at §16.42).** A build step a signal stopped is stored as `<what> was stopped by SIGSEGV (signal 11):
<the crash line>; <INSTALL_SH> tries the build again on its next run`, and `ocr._failure` reads the marker back
through `_plain`, which keeps 200 characters: a crash line over about 49 characters (the OCR helper's swiftc) to
78 (`git`) cut the clause, and past about 90 to 116 the installer's path, the only fix doctor gives such a
failure. `ocr._signal_reason(head, returncode, stderr)`, used by `ocr._compile` and `speech._step`, gives
`_ended` the room that is left (`room=`), and `_ended` cuts the crash line with `…`, or drops it when not even its
start fits. The subject stays first, where doctor's `not working: <detail>` reads it; `_TIMED_OUT` and
`BUILD_TIMED_OUT` are unchanged, and a SIGKILL or SIGTERM reason, which has no crash line, reads as before. Tests:
`test_ocr.py::test_a_crashed_builds_long_line_leaves_the_retry_clause_whole`,
`test_speech.py::test_a_crashed_build_steps_long_line_leaves_the_retry_clause_whole`.

**The OCR and media helpers' builds that ran out of time are handled as speech's (W49; `agentsync.convert.ocr`,
`agentsync.ops.doctor`, `agentsync.setup_report`; amends §16.137 V5).** A swiftc build of the OCR or media helper
that ran out of time stored `swiftc ran out of time building the <helper>` with no retry clause, doctor's warn had
no fix (one only when the developer tools are missing), and the report's bucket read only speech's marker, so the
warn was `unexpected`. `ocr.BUILD_TIMED_OUT` (`swiftc ran out of time building the`) now starts that reason, which
ends `; <INSTALL_SH> tries the build again on its next run` (true: install.sh builds every helper on each run, and
the `.failed` marker blocks nothing), and `ocr.build_timed_out(cache_dir, kind)` reads a helper's marker by that
prefix and the helper's name, so a marker an older build wrote is recognised too. Doctor's `_speech_again_fix` is
`_helper_again_fix(detail, helper)`, used by `_check_ocr`, `_check_media` and `_check_speech`, keyed on
`doctor.helper_timed_out_words(helper)`: speech's 20 minutes and "the Mac and the network", the OCR and media
builds' 5 minutes (`ocr._BUILD_TIMEOUT_S`) and "the Mac", since they fetch nothing. The report's
`_helpers_timed_out` reads each helper's own marker and buckets a warn only when that helper's marker says so
and the warn's detail holds its words; the bucket reads `from a helper build that ran out of time (1 check): ...
(install.sh builds it again)`, plural for more. Tests:
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_an_ocr_or_media_build_that_ran_out_of_time_has_a_fix_and_no_other_failure_gets_one`,
`test_setup_report.py::test_an_ocr_or_media_build_that_ran_out_of_time_shares_the_helper_bucket`,
`test_ocr.py::test_a_build_that_hangs_is_stopped_and_recorded`.

**Doctor's speech time-out fix says the re-run once (W20; `agentsync.ops.doctor`; amends §16.137 V5).** The warn's
detail is the marker's reason, which already says `<install.sh> tries the build again on its next run`, and the
fix went on `again: it builds the speech helper again, within 20 minutes`, so one line said the retry twice and
read the build's limit as a promise. The fix is now `<again>; the build stops after 20 minutes, and if it stops
again, run it when the Mac and the network are less busy`. The marker's reason (`speech._TIMED_OUT`) is unchanged:
it is the only hint on the surfaces that read it without doctor, and tests pin it as a V68 promise. The `<again>`
head (`run <install.sh> again`, or under install.sh `_again_fix`'s words) is lane B's (W19, W48). Test:
`test_ops_doctor.py::test_a_speech_build_that_ran_out_of_time_has_a_fix_and_no_other_failure_gets_one`.

**The helper errors' docstrings name the one path they hold (W55; `agentsync.convert.speech`,
`agentsync.convert.media`).** `SpeechError` and `MediaError` said "Its text never holds a path", which V68 made
false: a build failure's text names `skill.INSTALL_SH` as its fix (the pin refusal, `_TIMED_OUT`, a signal's
reason). Both now say "Its text holds no path but the installer's (``skill.INSTALL_SH``), which a build failure
names as its fix", and §16.34's `MediaError` stub comment says the same. §16.34's answer-check errors, which hold
no path, are unchanged. Docstrings only. Test:
`test_speech.py::test_the_helper_errors_say_the_one_path_their_text_holds`.

**The pin refusal names the pin (W67; `agentsync.convert.speech`, `agentsync.ops.doctor`; amends §16.138 V68;
dated line at §16.35).** `_FLOOR_REFUSAL` said "not built from FluidAudio 04e363c or later", but `_open` raises it
whenever the helper's commit is not `FLUIDAUDIO_PIN`, an exact match; the floor (`merge-base --is-ancestor`) is
checked only at build time. V68's reason for keeping "or later" (it states the floor, which the pin equals today)
explained naming the floor, not the "or later". It is now `_PIN_REFUSAL`, built from the pin: `the speech helper
is not built from FluidAudio <pin[:7]>, the commit this agentsync pins; <INSTALL_SH> rebuilds it`; the module,
`probe` and doctor's `_check_speech` docstrings say the probe refuses any commit other than the pin. The case the
finder named, a downgraded agentsync opening a newer pin's helper, cannot happen: `ocr._helper_path` keys the
helper by the digest of `Package.swift`, which carries the `revision:`, so a different pin is a different path;
only a foreign helper at that path reaches the refusal. No reader matches the words. Test:
`test_voice_naming.py` (the refusal from the pin, and a helper reporting a later commit refused in the same
words).

**The recording tests' time limit holds under load (W70; tests only).** A recording's limit is wall time from
`recording._BASE_S` (60 s), and `media_kit.fake_media` runs each helper as a Python subprocess, so under a starved
land gate 3 of 3 runs of a state test read `0 of 60000 ms` and failed on a limit that is not their subject. A
file-level autouse fixture in `tests/test_convert_recording.py` sets `_BASE_S` to 600 s (ten times the field's,
which still bounds a hung fake helper well under the ci job's 40 minutes, `timeout-minutes` in ci.yml), unless
the test carries the new `real_limit`
marker (registered in `pyproject.toml`, not read by conftest's load guard): the two that measurably need the
field's 60 s (`test_the_time_limit_is_fixed_from_counts_before_the_frames_are_read`,
`test_a_speech_piece_past_its_deadline_waits_and_stores_nothing`, which relies on `_BASE_S + _SPEECH_S * 400 <
0`) and two more whose subject is the limit. Not the `timing` marker, which would skip them in every busy land
gate. Other files that drive recordings through `fake_media` keep the field's limit. Tests:
`test_convert_recording.py::test_a_recording_test_reads_under_the_wide_limit_unless_its_subject_is_the_limit`,
`test_convert_recording.py::test_a_test_marked_real_limit_keeps_the_fields_limit`.

### 16.145 Round 19: deploy docs, CONTRACTS cross-references and CLAUDE.md (2026-10-20, wave B13 round 19 lane D)

**V7's add-back is named where it is defined, and the older lines say what V7 changed** (W44, W59, W60, one
defect; dated lines at §16.131 U9 and §16.134 V18). §16.137 V7 named `cycle.vanished_readd_tail`, a name in no
source or test (the function is `cycle.vanished_add_back_tail`, the name lane B's merge kept); it is corrected in
place, since a name that resolves nowhere records no history. §16.131 U9 still said the add-back is the CLI's own
verb, not install.sh's, with `doctor._vanished_add_backs` as the rule, and its §16.134 V18 line that
`cycle.VANISHED_ADVICE`, the sync's refusal, is unchanged; since V7 the rule and the tail are cycle's, install.sh
gets its own `--source-local`, and the sync's exit-78 refusal ends with the same tail (the constant is unchanged).
The old lines stay; a dated line after V18's says what V7 changed, and one at V18's paragraph says its `doctor.`
names are imports of cycle's. W60's verifier proposed rewording V18's line in place; W44's kept it and added a
line, which is the repo's convention, so that is what is built. Tests:
`test_the_contract_calls_only_functions_the_code_has`, which reads every backticked `<module>.<name>(` from §16.68
on against the module (13 calls, all resolve once V7's is corrected), and
`test_the_vanished_add_back_lines_say_where_v7_moved_it`, which reads each claim from the code.

**V5's retry clause is quoted by its path** (W61; dated line at §16.137 V5). V5 quoted the speech marker's retry
clause as `; scripts/install.sh tries the build again on its next run`, the form before §16.138 V68 named
